[Lem 39 of arXiv:2609.03821, 'Condensation and Metastability in the Supercritical Two-Species Zero-Range Process via Res'] For fixed $k\ge1$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, as
$N\to\infty$,
\[
\sum_{\substack{p_{1},\dots,p_{k}\ge1:\\
p_{1}+\cdots+p_{k}=N
}
}\frac{1}{p^{\alpha}_{1}p^{\alpha}_{2}\cdots p^{\alpha}_{k}}\simeq\begin{cases}
k\bm{\zeta}(\alpha)^{k-1}N^{-\alpha} & \text{if}\quad\alpha>1,\\
\frac{k(\log N)^{k-1}}{N} & \text{if}\quad\alpha=1,\\
\frac{\bm{\Gamma}(1-\alpha)^{k}}{\bm{\Gamma}(k(1-\alpha))}N^{k(1-\alpha)-1} & \text{if}\quad\alpha<1.
\end{cases}
\]
Above, $\bm{\Gamma}(\cdot)$ and $\bm{\zeta}(\cdot)$ denote the usual
gamma and zeta functions, respectively.
title: Lem 39 of arXiv:2609.03821

[Corollary cor:depthprediction of arXiv:2608.30072, 'Learning Representations through Token Prediction: \\ Geometry, Approximation, and Downstr'] Suppose there exists a self-consistent and $\eta$-optimal population representation pair \((E^\ast,\Theta^\ast)\) such that
	$$
	\mathbb{E}_{X,j}\left[L\left(p_j(X);\hat{p}_{E^\ast}(\Theta^\ast_j(X))\right)\right]\le \mathcal L_p^\ast +\eta
	$$
	for some $\eta\ge 0$, and $\max_{v\in\mathcal V}\|E_v^\ast\|\le B_E$. Here, $\mathcal L_p^\ast$ is the  unrestricted population optimum
	$$
	\mathcal L_p^\ast=\inf_{\Theta,E}\mathbb{E}_{X,j}\left[L\left(p_j(X);\hat{p}_{E}(\Theta_j(X))\right)\right].
	$$
	Suppose further that $\Theta^\ast$ satisfies Assumption~(asp:rich of the paper) under the $L_2$ metric with contraction factor $\kappa_{\Theta^\ast}$ and block-approximation error $\delta_{\Theta^\ast}$. Then, 
	$$
		\inf_{\Theta\in \mathcal R^L(\mathcal G, \mathcal R^0), E} \mathbb{E}_{X,j}\left[L\left(p_j(X);\hat{p}_{E}(\Theta_j(X))\right)\right]\le \mathcal L_p^\ast+\eta+2B_E\left\{
		\kappa_{\Theta^\ast}^L\min_{\Psi^0\in \mathcal R^0 }D(\Psi^0,\Theta^\ast)+{1-\kappa_{\Theta^\ast}^L \over 1-\kappa_{\Theta^\ast}}\delta_{\Theta^\ast}\right\}.
	$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let X = (X_1, ..., X_n) be a random vector with INDEPENDENT, mean-zero, sub-Gaussian coordinates with sub-Gaussian norms bounded by K, and let A be an n by n real matrix. Then there is an absolute constant c > 0 such that for every t >= 0, P( | X^T A X - E[X^T A X] | > t ) <= 2 exp( - c min( t^2 / (K^4 ||A||_F^2) , t / (K^2 ||A||_op) ) ), where ||A||_F is the Frobenius norm and ||A||_op the spectral norm. The two regimes are the sub-Gaussian one governed by the Frobenius norm and the sub-exponential one governed by the operator norm; this is the quadratic-form analogue of Bernstein's inequality and reduces to it for diagonal A. The coordinates must be INDEPENDENT and sub-Gaussian: independence cannot be weakened to uncorrelatedness, and heavier tails change the shape of the bound. E[X^T A X] equals the trace of A when the coordinates have unit variance, but in general it is sum_i A_{ii} E[X_i^2]. A standard corollary is a concentration bound for the Euclidean norm of a random vector, ||BX||_2 concentrated around ||B||_F within K^2 ||B||_op scales. [Hanson and Wright (1971); modern proof in Rudelson and Vershynin, 'Hanson-Wright inequality and sub-gaussian concentration', arXiv:1306.2872]
coordinates of X independent, mean zero, sub-Gaussian with psi_2 norms at most K
A an arbitrary real n by n matrix; no symmetry is required
c is an absolute constant

body: [Lemma 35 of arXiv:2609.01190, 'Rough differential equations on manifolds via natural bundles'] Let $[S,T]\subseteq\Rsf$ be an interval, and let $n\in\Nsf$. Let $p\in [1,3)$, let $\omega$ be a control function on interval $[S,T]$, and let $X$ be an $n$-dimensional branched rough path on interval $[S,T]$ with regularity $p$ and control $\omega$. Let $M$ be a manifold and let $f:M\to R_n^2M$ be a compactly supported admissible rough velocity field. Then there exists $\varepsilon\in (0,\infty)$ such that for every $Y_0\in M$ and every $S_0\in [S,T]$, there exists an integral curve $Y: [S_0, (S_0+\varepsilon)\wedge t]\to M$ of $f$ driven by $X$ that satisfies $Y(S_0)=Y_0$.

body: [Theorem no feedback guessing strategy of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] Suppose a deck of $n$ cards is given a shelf shuffle with a single shelf. The player should follow the following (incomplete) guessing strategy. Card $1$ should be guessed in positions $1$, and $n$ and cards $2$ or $3$ should be guessed in positions $2$ and $n-1$. If $n$ is even, card $n-1$ or card $n$ should be guessed in positions $\frac{n}{2}$ and $\frac{n}{2}+1$. If $n$ is odd, card $n-1$ or card $n$ should be guessed in position $\frac{n+1}{2}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem no feedback guessing strategy of arXiv:2507.10294

\|a(u, \mu)\|\leq C_1, \text{ for all } x\in \mathbb R^2 \text{ and } \mu \in \mathfrak M.

  \mathfrak{p}(u_{3}^{s+1})=\mathfrak{p}(u_{4}^{s+1}),\, \xi(\mathfrak{p}(u_{1}^{s+1}))\le K,\;
  \xi(\mathfrak{p}(u_{3}^{s+1}))\le K\Big) \\
  =\,& \frac{(q_n(s))_{2}}{(q_n(s+1))_4}\,

[Theorem 36 (Euclidean and Sol long-time limits) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Let \(g(t)\), \(t\geq0\), be an immortal Ricci flow on the orientable total
space \(M\) of a \(\TT^2\)-bundle over \(S^1\), under the
\hyperref[par:working-cover-convention]{working-cover convention}.  Let
\(H\in\SL(2,\ZZ)\) be its monodromy, as
in Subsection~\ref{subsec:torus-bundle-conventions}.  Assume either that
\(H=I\), so that \(M\cong\TT^3\) is in the Euclidean case, or that \(H\) is
hyperbolic, so that \(M\) is in the Sol case.  Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If \(M\) has Euclidean type (equivalently, \(H=I\)), then for every
\(m\geq0\), \(g(t)\) converges
exponentially fast in the \(C^m\)-norm of any fixed smooth background metric,
as \(t\to\infty\), to a flat metric on \(M\).
\item If \(M\) has Sol type (equivalently, \(H\) is hyperbolic), then there
are constants \(0<c_-<C<\infty\) such that
\[
        c_-\sqrt t\leq \diam(M,g(t))\leq C\sqrt t,
\]
for all sufficiently large \(t\).  In addition, the Gromov--Hausdorff limit of
\((M,t^{-1}g(t))\) is a circle.  For every basepoint
\(\widetilde m\in\widetilde M\), the lifted blowdown flows
\[
        (\widetilde M,\widetilde m,s^{-1}\widetilde g(s\tau)),
        \qquad \tau>0,
\]
converge, as \(s\to\infty\), in the pointed Cheeger--Hamilton sense to a
pointed flow isometric to the Sol expanding soliton solution
\[
        (\RR^3,0,e^{-2z}dx^2+e^{2z}dy^2+4\tau\,dz^2),
        \qquad \tau>0.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Euclidean and Sol long-time limits

[Lemma 27 (Uniform moment bounds for the shifted process under tRLMC) of arXiv:2605.24937, '2605.24937'] Let $p\ge 2$ and define the shifted process $\widetilde Y_n := (1-\eta_n)Y_n' + \eta_n \bar Y_n$ for $n\ge0$. Under the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:P-moment-drift-RLMC} (with constants $q, C_p > 0$), and assuming $\bar M_p := \sup_{n\ge 0} \E\|\bar Y_n\|^p < \infty$, we have
\[
  \E\|\widetilde Y_n\|^p \le e^{-q\lambda n}\E\|\widetilde Y_0\|^p + \frac{C_p\lambda+\bar M_p}{1-e^{-q\lambda}},
\]
yielding the uniform bound $\sup_{n\ge 0} \E\|\widetilde Y_n\|^p \le \E\|\widetilde Y_0\|^p + \frac{C_p\lambda+\bar M_p}{1-e^{-q\lambda}} < \infty$.

[Proposition prop:fixed-box-distance-rec of arXiv:2608.25201, 'Recurrence of strong-decay inhomogeneous long-range percolation clusters'] Suppose that \(G\) is stationary, ergodic, and locally finite, that its degree
measure has finite intensity, and that for all $L \geq 0$ there exists \(\eta>0\) such that
\begin{equation}

  \mathbb{P}\big(\mathcal D(R)\big)\longrightarrow1
  \qquad\text{as }R\to\infty,
\end{equation}
where
\[
  \mathcal D(R)\coloneqq 
  \left\{
    \operatorname{d}_{G}(v,w)\ge\eta|v-w|
    \text{ for all }v\in V\cap Q_L(0),\
    w\in V\cap Q_R(0)^{\mathsf c}
  \right\}.
\]
Then almost surely every connected component of
\(G\) is recurrent.

[Corollary cor_Gab_conn of arXiv:2607.04002, 'Collisions of random walks in unimodular random graphs: applications to the random geometr'] Fix~$\mathbf z \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and~$i \in \{1,\dots,d\}$, and define
\begin{align*}
& \mathcal B(\mathbf z, i) := \{ B_{\mathbf z + \mathbf u}: \mathbf u \in \{0,1\}^d, \mathbf u \cdot \mathbf{e}_i = 0\}, \\[2mm]
& C(\mathbf z,i) := \mathrm{conv}( \{M(\mathbf z + \mathbf u): \mathbf u \in \{0,1\}^d, \mathbf u \cdot \mathbf e_i = 0 \} ), \\[2mm]
& \mathcal Q(\mathbf z,i) := \{ Q \text{ sub-box of side-length } M/\alpha: Q \text{ is contiguous to } Q', \; Q' \cap C(\mathbf z,i) \neq \varnothing  \}.
\end{align*}
Assume the boxes in~$\mathcal B(\mathbf z, i)$ are good. Let~$Q_1,Q_2 \in \mathcal Q(\mathbf z,i)$ be contiguous sub-boxes with~$Q_2 \cap C(\mathbf z,i) \neq \varnothing$, and~$x \in V(\mathcal G_\mathrm{Gab}) \cap Q_1$ and~$y \in V(\mathcal G_\mathrm{Gab}) \cap Q_2$. Then, there exists a path in~$\mathcal G_\mathrm{Gab}$ from~$x$ to~$y$ contained in~$\cup \{B: B \in \mathcal B(\mathbf z, i) \}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop coupling of arXiv:2607.28817, 'Limiting spectral distribution for the adjacency matrix of the Watts--Strogatz random grap'] Let $A_n$ be the adjacency matrix of $WS_n(K_n,p_n)$.  There is a coupling between $A_n$ and $(U_n, Z_n, \widetilde{U}_n)$ so that the following properties hold.
\begin{enumerate}[itemsep=0.3em]
    \item $A_n = Z_n+\widetilde{U}_n$. 
    \item  $Z_n$ and $U_n$ are independent and have the same distributions as stated in Theorem~(thm:coupling of the paper). 
    \item  We have
    \[
        \mathbb{E}\left[ \frac{1}{n} \tr \left( \frac{(Z_n+U_n) - (Z_n+\widetilde{U}_n)}{\sqrt{p_nK_n}} \right)^2 \right] \le 8\left(\frac{K_n}{n}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{p_nK_n}}\right).
    \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own-work draft; STATUS: proof (unaudited); novelty unestablished. Fix nu in (0,1] independently of feature scale e and width m. For 0<e<1/4 use n=4 stratified unit inputs x_(s,t)=(1,e s,e^2 t)/sqrt(1+e^2+e^4), s,t in {-1,1}, and test law uniform on this same support. The linear single-index teacher is g=(s+t)/4 and each label has independent plus/minus 1/2 noise. Train f=m^(-1/2) sum_j a_j ReLU(w_j.x) in BOTH layers by simultaneous GD of step 1/2 on squared residual norm divided by 8, using derivative zero at zero. Initialize w_j iid N(0,I_3) and a_j=nu epsilon_j with independent centered signs independent of label noise. Q is clean test MSE averaged over all sixteen training-noise patterns conditional on network initialization. The full limiting tangent kernel has entries [k(r)+nu^2 r kprime(r)]/4, where r=x_i.x_l and k(r)=[sqrt(1-r^2)+(pi-arccos r)r]/(2pi). Its Walsh eigenvalues satisfy lambda1~nu^2 e/(2pi), lambda2~lambda12~nu^2 e^2/(4pi), lambda0 tending to (1+nu^2)/2. Put b_h=-log(1-lambda_h/2), B=log(b1/b2). In the width-first then e-to-zero probability limit, four explicit ordered risk times in the proof have strict descent-rise-descent differences. Every maximizer on the integer interval from floor((B-1)/b1) to ceil((B+1)/b1) is interior and b1 k_peak-B tends to zero. Its leading peak time is (4pi/nu^2)e^(-1)log(2/e). The proof controls adaptive gate crossings with weighted initial margin bands and retains random initial output. SUBSTANTIVE RESTRICTION: the linear teacher vector has norm asymptotic to 1/(4e^2). With label noise unchanged, unit-normalizing it gives increasing limiting risks at the same four times: 1,5/4,2,20/9, divided by noise-mode variance 1/16. This obstructs the present witnesses, not double descent at all other times or in other models. No generic iid Gaussian-input theorem, bounded-teacher solution, high probability over label noise, practical width, macroscopic feature learning, novelty, or full Target 1 closure is claimed.
All explicit model definitions in proofs/FIXED_VARIANCE_NTK.md Section 1
n=4, stratified design containing each support input; uniform test law on same support
Linear single-index teacher, independent plus/minus 1/2 label noise; risk averaged over the sixteen label-noise patterns conditional on network initialization
IID Gaussian hidden weights, independent centered sign readouts of amplitude nu fixed across widths and feature scales, 0<nu<=1
Both layers updated simultaneously by GD at step 1/2; width tends to infinity before feature scale tends to zero
The displayed linear teacher vector depends on e and has norm asymptotic to 1/(4e^2); it is not uniformly norm bounded.

		Assume that $(X_n)$ is increasing, almost surely.

	\begin{equation}

	In particular, Assumption~(hyp: getting fast to classes of the paper) is satisfied and $(L_n)$ satisfies the weak LDP with rate function $I\equiv \infty$. The same conclusions hold if $(X_n)$ is strictly decreasing.

[Lemma lem:CMT of arXiv:2605.10617, 'Logarithmic scaling of selective sweep curves:\\ from tents to houses'] Let $(Z^N(t))_{t\geq 0}$ be a binary branching process with individual birth rate $\lambda_N \geq 0$ and individual death rate $\mu_N \geq 0$. Further, let $\varphi_N$ and $b\in[0,1)$ as in Definition~(def:moderate-selection of the paper) and denote $b_N=-\log_N\varphi_N$. Lastly, let $\beta_N\geq b_N$ for all $N$, assume that $\beta:=\lim_{N\to\infty}\beta_N$ exists and let the initial conditions satisfy $Z^N(0) = \lfloor N^{\beta_N} \rfloor$.
\begin{enumerate}[a)]
    \item \emph{(Slightly supercritical case.)}   
    Assume that $\lambda_N = 1+a \varphi_N$ for some $a>0$ and some sequence $(\varphi_N)_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ of positive numbers, and $\mu_N=1$.
   
    In case $\beta=b$ assume additionally that $N^{\beta_N}\gg \varphi_N^{-1}$. Then, for any $T,\delta>0$
    \[
      \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P} \Big(  \sup_{t \leq T} \Big| \log_N(Z^N(t \varphi_N^{-1} \log N) ) - (\beta+at) \Big| >\delta \Big)
        = 0,
    \]
    i.e.\ $(\log_N(Z^N(t \varphi_N^{-1} \log N) ))_{t\in[0,T]}$ converges uniformly in probability to $(\beta+at)_{t\in[0,T]}$.
    \item \emph{(Slightly subcritical case.)}  Assume that $\mu_N = 1+a \varphi_N$ for some $a>0$ and for some sequence $(\varphi_N)_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ of positive numbers, and $\lambda_N=1$.

    Let $\beta>b$ and $(\varepsilon_N)_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a non-negative sequence tending to 0 such that $N^{-\varepsilon_N}\to0$ as $N\to\infty$.
    Then, for  $T_N := \frac{\beta_N-b_N-\varepsilon_N}{a}$ and for any $\delta>0$,
    \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}  \mathbb{P} \Big(  \sup_{t \leq T_N} \Big| \log_N(Z^N(t \varphi_N^{-1} \log N) ) - (\beta-at) \Big| >\delta \Big)=0. \]
    In particular, for any $s<\frac{\beta-b}{a}$, $(\log_N(Z^N(t\varphi_N^{-1}\log N)))_{t\in [0,s]}$ converges uniformly in probability to $(\beta-at)_{t\in [0,s]}$ as $N\to\infty$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 47 (Uniform lifted Ricci--DeTurck continuous dependence) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Fix \(N\geq2\) and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\).  Let \(s(t)\), \(a\leq t\leq b\),
be a Ricci flow satisfying \(\PBG_N(s;\Lambda;[a,b])\) for some \(\Lambda\geq1\).
There are constants \(\eta_{\mathrm{cd}}>0\) and
\(C_{\mathrm{cd}}<\infty\), depending only on these data and an upper bound for
\(b-a\), with the following property.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Hypotheses.}
If \(v(a)\) is a smooth Riemannian metric and
\[
 \|v(a)-s(a)\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,s(a))}<\eta_{\mathrm{cd}},
\]

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Conclusion.}
Then the Ricci--DeTurck flow \(v(t)\) relative to \(s(t)\) exists on
\([a,b]\) and
\begin{equation}
 \|v-s\|_{X_s^N[a,b]}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{cd}}\|v(a)-s(a)\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,s(a))}.
\end{equation}
The constants are uniform under collapse of the quotient.

\leq \frac{9 n}{r}.
\]

AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. Let N,P,M be positive integers with M>=N+P+1. Let U in R^(N by M) and V in R^(P by M) have independent standard real Gaussian entries, independent of each other. B=UV^T/sqrt(N) has an everywhere finite, strictly positive log-concave density on R^(N by P). Indeed stack T=[U;V]; its Wishart Gram density is proportional to det(S)^((M-N-P-1)/2) exp(-tr(S)/2) on the positive-definite cone and is log-concave. B is its scaled off-diagonal block. Prekopa marginalization preserves log-concavity under this linear projection. Every B has a positive-definite completion with diagonal blocks tI for t>sqrt(N)||B||_op; the determinant-trace bound gives fiber integrability. This is a standard consequence recorded as an unaudited supporting lemma of claim w718-T287-013 version 3, not an established novelty claim.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:a5a73f91d74eab04d86aa89d295d5621aa4104345e879ce377b4a0f3ccec7f9a","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/a5/a5a73f91d74eab04d86aa89d295d5621aa4104345e879ce377b4a0f3ccec7f9a.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:235e82196ece14cc4302c0cd85fe5c21acc54bb11c4aacd75c90153e26068f72","bundle_entry_key":"gaussian-product-logconcavity-w718","bundle_id":"population.t287-gaussian-product-logconcavity-mmse-and-normalization-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian channels and extensive-rank matrix inference","draft":"w718/bundle_004.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.gaussian_channels:gaussian-product-logconcavity-w718","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Proof draft, unaudited; standard consequence, novelty not claimed.

## 2. The Gaussian product has a log-concave density

Put h=N+P and stack the factors into the h by M Gaussian matrix
T=[U_G; V_G]. Its Wishart Gram matrix S=T T^T has density proportional to

    det(S)^k exp[-tr(S)/2], S>0,
    k=(M-h-1)/2 >= 0.                                 (3)

The density is with respect to the h(h+1)/2 independent symmetric matrix
coordinates; only a positive normalization constant is omitted. Its domain
is the convex positive definite cone. Log det is concave there, as follows
from the second directional derivative

    -tr(S^(-1)H S^(-1)H)<=0, H symmetric.

Thus (3), extended by zero outside S>0, is log-concave. Its upper-right
block is exactly U_G V_G^T. Write the block coordinates as

    S = [ A, sqrt(N) B; sqrt(N) B^T, C ].              (4)

This is an invertible linear change between symmetric S and the independent
coordinates A in Sym_N, C in Sym_P, B in R^(N by P), with a constant
positive Jacobian. Prékopa's marginalization theorem, integrating A,C,
therefore makes the B density log-concave.

The marginal is positive for every B: the fiber contains the positive
definite block matrix with A=t I_N,C=t I_P whenever
t>sqrt(N)||B||_op, together with an open neighborhood in the fiber. It is
finite for every B as well. On the positive cone, A,C are positive
definite and det(S)^k is at most ((tr(A)+tr(C))/h)^(h*k). Hence its fiber
integral is bounded by a polynomial times exp[-(tr(A)+tr(C))/2] integrated
over the two positive definite cones. This is finite, since their traces
dominate their Frobenius norms. No regularity or integrability assertion
about the marginal is being inferred from a value on a null set.

The exact marginal theorem is recorded in Saumard-Wellner, arXiv:1404.5886,
Theorem 3.3, with two proofs following it; the result is due to Prékopa.

body: In probability theory, statistics and related fields, a Poisson point process is a type of mathematical object that consists of points randomly located on a mathematical space with the essential feature that the points occur independently of one another. The process's name derives from the fact that the number of points in any given finite region follows a Poisson distribution. The process and the distribution are named after French mathematician Siméon Denis Poisson. The process itself was discovered independently and repeatedly in several settings, including experiments on radioactive decay, telephone call arrivals and actuarial science.

On the uniform cube {-1, 1}^n let f be real, f^(S) = E[f chi_S] its Walsh coefficients and W_k = sum over |S| = k of f^(S)^2. For rho in [-1, 1], T_rho is the noise operator: T_rho f(x) = E[f(Y)] where the Y_i are independent with P(Y_i = x_i) = (1 + rho)/2, so T_rho chi_S = rho^|S| chi_S. D_rho(f) = <f, (I - T_rho) f> = (1/2) E[(f(X) - f(Y))^2] = sum_S (1 - rho^|S|) f^(S)^2 >= 0 for a rho-correlated pair. Its zero set: for -1 < rho < 1, D_rho(f) = 0 iff f is constant; at rho = 1, D_1 = 0 for every f; at rho = -1, D_{-1}(f) = 0 iff every odd-level coefficient vanishes, equivalently f(-x) = f(x). The loss of variance under noise is E[Var(f(Y) | X)] = ||f||^2 - ||T_rho f||^2 = sum_S (1 - rho^(2|S|)) f^(S)^2, which is 0 iff f is constant when |rho| < 1 and 0 for every f when |rho| = 1. For a parity character sigma = eps chi_R with |R| = r, D_rho(sigma) = 1 - rho^r, and the half-cube A = {chi_R = eps} has D_rho(1_A) = (1 - rho^r)/4 and P(1_A(X) != 1_A(Y)) = (1 - rho^r)/2.

	function $h:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}$ with bounded second partial
	derivatives, we have
	\[
	\left|
	\mathbb{E}h(F)-\mathbb{E}h(Z)
	\right|
	\leq
	\frac{1}{2}\|h''\|_{\infty}
	\sqrt{
		\sum_{i,j=1}^{m}
		\mathbb{E}\left[
		\left(
		C_{i,j}
		-
		\left\langle DF^{(i)},v^{(j)}\right\rangle_{\mathcal{H}}
		\right)^2
		\right]
	},
	\]
	where
	\[
	\|h''\|_{\infty}
	=
	\max_{1\leq i,j\leq m}
	\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^m}
	\left|
	\frac{\partial^2 h}{\partial x_i\partial x_j}(x)
	\right|.
	\]

[Lemma lem:couprLPP of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Let $I=\llbracket a,b\rrbracket$ for some $-\infty \le a < b \le \infty$. Take  $\{A_i,B_i\}_{i\in I}$ and $\{C_i,D_i\}_{i\in I}$ to be two families of independent random variables, such that either
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(1)] $A_i\sim \operatorname{Exp}(\gamma_0+\beta_i)$, $B_i\sim \operatorname{Exp}(\gamma_1+\beta_i)$, $C_i\sim \operatorname{Exp}(\gamma_1+\beta_i)$, $D_i\sim \operatorname{Exp}(\gamma_0+\beta_i)$, where $\gamma_0<\gamma_1$ and $\{\beta_i\}_{i\in I}$ are real parameters, such that $\gamma_0+\beta_i>0$ for each $i\in I$; or
    \item[(2)] $A_i\sim \operatorname{Geo}(\gamma_0\beta_i)$, $B_i\sim \operatorname{Geo}(\gamma_1\beta_i)$, $C_i\sim \operatorname{Geo}(\gamma_1\beta_i)$, $D_i\sim \operatorname{Geo}(\gamma_0\beta_i)$, where $\gamma_0>\gamma_1$ and $\{\beta_i\}_{i\in I}$ are positive parameters, such that $\gamma_0\beta_i\in (0,1)$ for each $i\in I$.
\end{itemize}
Then these two families of random variables can be coupled so that almost surely, for any $x\le y\in I$,
\[
\max_{j\in\llbracketx,y \rrbracket} \sum_{i=x}^j A_i + \sum_{i=j}^y B_i
=
\max_{j\in\llbracketx,y \rrbracket} \sum_{i=x}^j C_i + \sum_{i=j}^y D_i .
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:couprLPP of arXiv:2604.10020

Method: Critical moment condition for eventual stable-process unimodality structural calculation Result: A separated-atom counterexample of the source type cannot retain the critical moment while making its usual tail mechanism arbitrarily strong. If mu=sum_k w_k*delta_(a_k) and sum_k w_k*|a_k|^(2+alpha)<infinity, then w_k*|a_k|^(2+alpha) tends to0. Thus it cannot diverge along a subsequence, which is the condition used to make an isolated atom dominate the far-tail derivative of the main stable density. Check: Every term of a convergent nonnegative series tends to0. In the Cauchy case alpha=1, the derivative of the bulk kernel at a_k has order |a_k|^-3, while the local atom contributes order w_k at any fixed smoothing time; their ratio is of order w_k*|a_k|^3. This matches the critical exponent in the exact known construction. Obstruction: Failure of that counterexample mechanism is not a uniform derivative estimate for arbitrary initial laws. Asymmetric stable laws and the free cases still require global control.

body:
[Proposition p:covario-new of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Let $M=\{M(x)\}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}$ be a real-valued random field in $\mathbb{R}^d$ having fast $\mathbb{B} $-mixing correlations as in  Definition~(d.omegatmixing-field of the paper)(i.B-mixing-field of the paper)(i.mixing-field-fast of the paper).
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a simple point process on $\mathbb{R}^d$ having fast mixing correlations as in Definition~(d.omegamixing of the paper)(i.mixing-ground-fast of the paper), bounded reduced  Palm intensity function~(equation bdedreduced of the paper), and independent of the random field $M$.
Consider empirical covariogram $\sigma_{n}^{\gamma}$ of $M$ based on $\mathcal{P}$, as in (equation e.sigma-covariogram-new of the paper), for some value $h$ and tolerance $\delta>0$ .
\begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),labelindent=0pt]
\item 
If  $M$ has $p$-moment conditions for all $p>1$ (i.e., ~(equation e:M-p-moment of the paper) holds with  $\zeta(x,M(x))=M(x)$) then the central limit theorem holds  for
    $(\sigma_{n}^{\gamma}(f))_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$, i.e., as $n \to \infty$

\[   ({\rm Var} \, \sigma_{n}^{\gamma}(f) )^{-1/2}\Big( \sigma_{n}^{\gamma}(f) - \mathbb {E}  \, \sigma_{n}^{\gamma}(f) \Big) \stackrel{d}{\Rightarrow} Z
  \]
for $f\in\mathbb{B} (W_1)$, provided the random    ${\rm Var} \, \sigma_{n}^{\gamma}(f) = \Omega(n^{\nu})$ for some $\nu > 0$.

\item 
Further, if the random field $M$ and the point process $\mathcal{P}$ are  stationary (necessarily jointly so, due to their independence), with $\rho$ the intensity  of $\mathcal{P}$,
then the  expectation and variance asymptotics and multivariate central limit
theorem hold {\em mutatis mutandis} for 
$(\sigma_{n}^{\gamma}(f))_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$
as in Proposition~(expvar of the paper) and Theorem (t:multcltmarkedpp of the paper)
under $p=(2+\epsilon)-$ or $p=(4+\epsilon)$--~moment condition for $M$ i.e.,~~(equation e:M-p-moment of the paper) with $\zeta(x,M(x))=M(x)$, respectively.
Precisely, the limiting expectation takes the form $\rho \, \bar\gamma(h)$
of~(equation e:covario-mean of the paper)
and the covariance of the empirical covariogram at two values  
$\sigma_{n}^{\gamma(h)}(f)$ and $\sigma_{n}^{\gamma(h')}(f)$, with $h,h'\in\mathbb{R}^d$, (and for the simplicity, we assume  the same tolerance $\delta>0$ such that $\delta<\min\{|h|, |h'|, |h-h|', |h+h'|\}$) takes the form

$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac 1n {\rm Cov}(\sigma_{n}^{\gamma(h)}(f)),\sigma_{n}^{\gamma(h')}(f)))=
\sigma^2(h,h')\int_{W_1}f(x)^2\,\mathrm{d} x\in (-\infty,\infty),$$

 where 

\begin{align}  
&\sigma^2(h,h') :=\\
&\quad \frac{\rho}{16\theta^2_d \delta^{2d}} \int_{B_\delta(\0\pm h)}\int_{B_\delta(\0\pm h')}\mathbb {E} \big[(M(\0) - M(y))^2(M(\0) - M(y'))^2\big]\rho^{(3)}(\0, y,y')\, \mathrm{d} y \, \mathrm{d} y' \nonumber\\
&\quad +
\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\biggl(\frac1{16\theta^2_d \delta^{2d}}\int_{B_\delta(\0\pm h)\cap B_\delta(z\pm h')}\mathbb {E} \big[(M(\0) - M(y))^2(M(z) - M(y))^2\big] \rho^{(3)}(\0,z,y)\mathrm{d} y \nonumber\\
&\qquad +\frac1{16\theta^2_d \delta^{2d}}\int_{B_\delta(\0\pm h)}\int_{B_\delta(z\pm h')}\mathbb {E} \big[(M(\0) - M(y))^2(M(z) - M(y'))^2\big] \rho^{(4)}(\0,z,y,y') \, \mathrm{d} y \, \mathrm{d} y'  \nonumber\\
&\hspace{10cm} - \rho^2 \, \bar\gamma(h) \, \bar\gamma(h') 
\biggr) \mathrm{d} z \in (-\infty, \infty). \nonumber
\end{align}

\end{enumerate}
title: Limit theory for empirical covariogram

[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2603.26228, 'A local limit theorem for nonlattice multidimensional random walks in cones'] For any $\delta >0$ and   ${\bf x}\in \cC$,  there exist  positive  constants $C({\bf x},  \delta)$ such that  for all  $n\geq 1$ and ${\bf y}  \in \cC$, 
\begin{equation} 
  \bP(\tau({\bf x}) >n,  {\bf x}  +S(n) \in\llbracket {\bf y},  {\bf y}  +\delta {\bf 1}\rrbracket)
\quad \leq\quad {C({\bf x},  \delta)\over n^{p/2+d/2}}. 
\end{equation} 
There exist positive constants $c=c(\delta)$ and $C=C(\delta) $ such that  for every $n \geq 1,  t>0$,    and  $ {\bf x},  {\bf y}  \in \cC$,  
 
\begin{align}
 &(a)\  \bP( {\bf x} +S(n)\in\llbracket {\bf y},  {\bf y}  +\delta {\bf 1}\rrbracket) \leq {C \over n^{d/2}},  \notag
 \\
 &(b)\   \bP( {\bf x} +S(n)\in\llbracket {\bf y},  {\bf y}  +\delta {\bf 1}\rrbracket)
 \leq {C \over n^{d/2}} e^{-c t^2} \quad when \quad  \vert {\bf x}-{\bf y}\vert > t \sqrt{n}, 
\\
&(c)\ 
\bP(\tau({\bf x}) \leq n,  {\bf x}  +S(n) \in\llbracket {\bf y},  {\bf y}  +\delta {\bf 1}\rrbracket)
 \leq {C \over n^{d/2}} e^{-c t^2}\quad when \quad {\rm dist}({\bf x},  \partial \mathcal C),  {\rm dist}({\bf y},  \partial \mathcal C)> t \sqrt{n}.\notag
 \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 6 of arXiv:2603.26228

body: Thevenin (Vertices with fixed outdegrees in large Galton-Watson trees, Electron. J. Probab. 25 (2020), Section 6.2) conjectured that for a Galton-Watson tree T_n conditioned to have n vertices, the number N_A(n) of vertices whose outdegree lies in a fixed set A satisfies (N_A(n) - n mu_A)/sqrt(n) -> N(0, mu_A(1 - mu_A)) for every subcritical offspring law with no exponential moment and every critical offspring law with infinite variance. Both clauses are false, by a pair of explicit counterexamples (two lacunary offspring laws). Theorem 1.1: an explicit subcritical offspring law with finite third moment and no exponential moment (pi_1 = 1/4, rare atoms at H_r +- sqrt(n_r), n_1 = 256, n_{r+1} = n_r^4) for which (N_1(T_{n_r}) - n_r/4)/sqrt(n_r) converges to the Gaussian mixture (1/2)N(-a, v) + (1/2)N(a, v) with a = 0.99990793915708 and v = 1.7283757730977e-5. Theorem 1.2: a critical offspring law of infinite variance with limit (1/2)N(-1, 3/16) + (1/2)N(1, 3/16). The centering n mu_A and the scale sqrt(n) are the right ones and the limit exists along the subsequence; it is not Gaussian. Mechanism: by the cycle lemma the outdegrees are i.i.d. conditioned on their sum being n - 1, and for a lacunary tail the condensation vertex takes one of two values 2 sqrt(n) apart, each with probability tending to 1/2.

[Theorem 1 (Theta description of the $2$-division points) of arXiv:2609.03455, '2609.03455'] Define
\[\left\{ \ 
\begin{aligned}
 g_1(\tau)&=\phi_1(\tau)^2/\phi_1(2\tau),\\
 g_2(\tau)&=\phi_1(\tau)\phi_1(\tau/2)\phi_1(2\tau)
            -\phi_1(2\tau)/\phi_2(\tau),\\
 g_3(\tau)&=-\phi_1(\tau)\phi_1(\tau/2)\phi_1(2\tau)
            -\phi_1(\tau)^2\phi_2(\tau)/\phi_2(2\tau).
\end{aligned}
\right.
\]
Then the cubic equation \eqref{eq:main-cubic-intro} factors as follows:
\[
 P_{\u(\tau)}(T)
 =
 (T-g_1(\tau))(T-g_2(\tau))(T-g_3(\tau)).
\]

[Theorem 33 of arXiv:2605.02002, 'Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI'] Suppose the graph $G$ has $\alpha$-stretched-exponential growth and the RFIM $\mu_G$ satisfies $\operatorname{WSM}(C)$ for some $C>0$. [Lem 83 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For $0<\epsilon < 1/2$ and any $x\in\R$,
    \[
    2\epsilon^{1/2}
    +\frac{2(|x|-1)^2}{\epsilon^{1/2}} \ge x^2-1\,.
    \]
\begin{proof}
We can suppose without loss $x\ge0$, and make the change of variables $y=x-1$. Then the desired inequality rearranges to
    \[
    \bigg(\frac{2}{\epsilon^{1/2}}-1\bigg) y^2
    - 2y+2\epsilon^{1/2}\ge 0\,.
    \]
The left-hand side is a quadratic function of $y$ which is strictly positive at $y=0$ and has negative discriminant for the range of $\epsilon$ given in the statement of the lemma. It follows that the left-hand side never reaches zero, and the claim follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Lemma 20 of arXiv:2609.01574, 'A linear bound for Fujita's freeness conjecture'] Let $(R,\m)$ be a $d$-dimensional Cohen--Macaulay local ring with $d\geq1$ and infinite residue field. Let $c:=\edim R-d$. If $J$ is a minimal reduction of $\m$, set $A:=R/J$, $\mathfrak n:=\m/J$, and $h_k:=\ell_A(\mathfrak n^k/\mathfrak n^{k+1})$. Then $e_0(\m)=\sum_{k\geq0}h_k$, $h_0=1$, $h_1=c$, and $e_1(\m)\geq\sum_{k\geq1}kh_k$. If $c>0$, then $h_k\leq\binom{c+k-1}{k}$ for every $k\geq0$.

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); independent proof, priority and target-scope review pending. Let d>=1,N>=2d+1,n>=0,K>=2,1<=r<K and 0<=ell<=r be integers. Of N contexts with K candidate facts each, d disjoint pairs each contain exactly one arbitrary A and one systematic S context; other contexts are known S. All K candidates are true in S; each A has an independent uniform random r-subset true. The factual law chooses contexts uniformly then truths uniformly. The orientation class has VC dimension d. Observe n iid factual samples (context,candidate) WITH exact A/S tags. After training a verifier independently supplies a uniform ell-subset of truths in each variable context, including S contexts, certifying identities without new orientation labels. This verifies gamma=ell/r of arbitrary truths. Let U count untouched pairs,m=U/N,beta=r/K,kappa=1-beta,q=ell/K and alpha_j=(K-r)/(K-j),alpha=alpha_ell. For known A contexts let D_j count j DISTINCT identities in the union of observed candidates and verifier truths,ell<=j<=r. Define B_j=D_j*(r-j)/(N*r),T_j=sum_{h=j}^r B_h,M=m*(2-gamma-q). For arbitrary generators g and exact-level source calibration Mis_infinity(g,p)=TV(p_Pi,g), where Pi is determined by g probability levels and p_Pi is uniform coarsening, require calibration <=c in every compatible world. For c in [0,1], the exact worst-world false-mass frontier is V(c)=alpha*((T_ell+M-c)_+ +(T_ell-c)_+)/2 +sum_{j=ell+1}^r (alpha_j-alpha_{j-1})*(T_j-c)_+. The same conditional value holds for the uniform-compatible-world posterior-average game. Then V-O=alpha*((t+m*(1-q))_+ +(t-m*(1-gamma))_+ -2*t_+)/2, between zero and kappa*m/2. A polynomial-representation ERM-version-space generator, starting from the posterior mean factual law and removing mass in decreasing false-risk order to a known S reservoir, attains V in every world. {"artifact_digest":"sha256:0617927194536d9fb29dc79823884209783444351d0592763a143f303914f60d","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/06/0617927194536d9fb29dc79823884209783444351d0592763a143f303914f60d.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:e2d52e2418c8d31e00569395f67282223aeb3eca94c4913436867b6c0ba18a73","bundle_entry_key":"tagged-factual-vc-frontier","bundle_id":"population.t379-tagged-factual-histogram-frontier-20261020","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"statistical learning; calibrated generation; minimax decision theory","draft":"w709/bundle_004.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.calibration:tagged-factual-vc-frontier","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Tagged factual training plus partial truth verification

Candidate T379-C009 v2; Own-work draft, proof (unaudited).
Targets 1/2. This draft retains factual candidate identities in training,
but STILL REQUIRES partition tags. It does not solve untagged learning.
The hardest extension is removing those tags: then a sampled pair can
remain unoriented, and the density/risk ordering below need not hold.

## Experiment and conditional histogram

Integers d>=1,N>=2d+1,n>=0,K>=2,1<=r<K. There are d variable pairs
with exactly one arbitrary A and one systematic S context, plus N-2d
known S contexts. S has all K candidates true; A has an independent
uniform random r-subset true. A world's factual law p chooses a context
uniformly and then a true candidate uniformly. The orientation class has
VC dimension d. Observe n iid factual samples (context,candidate), EACH
WITH its true A/S tag. Thus every touched pair's orientation is known.

After training, a perfect verifier independently supplies a uniform
ell-subset of truths in EACH variable context, 0<=ell<=r. It certifies
identities only, including ell truths in paired S contexts, without
disclosing additional orientations. Its fraction of arbitrary truths is
gamma=ell/r. Set beta=r/K,kappa=1-beta,q=ell/K and
alpha_j=(K-r)/(K-j), for ell<=j<=r. No denominator vanishes since r<K.

Let U count pairs untouched by training, m=U/N. In every known A context
let j be the number of DISTINCT candidate identities certified by the
union of its factual observations and verifier output. Repeats count
once. Then ell<=j<=r. Let D_j count known A contexts with this j, so
sum_j D_j=d-U. Put

 B_j=D_j*(r-j)/(N*r),    T_j=sum_{h=j}^r B_h.

The unknown-pair uncertified group has posterior mass
M=m*(2-gamma-q). Define alpha=alpha_ell. The proposed exact robust
Mis_infinity hallucination frontier over ALL generators, conditional on
the observed samples/tags/verifier output, is

 V(c)=alpha/2*[(T_ell+M-c)_+ +(T_ell-c)_+]
      +sum_{j=ell+1}^r (alpha_j-alpha_{j-1})*(T_j-c)_+,
                                                        0<=c<=1.    (1)

Zero-mass risk groups and absent histogram entries contribute zero. The
same value holds in the specified uniform-compatible-world posterior
average game. The oracle given all orientations, but NO extra truths,
has exact value

 O(c)=alpha*(T_ell+m*(1-gamma)-c)_+
      +sum_{j=ell+1}^r (alpha_j-alpha_{j-1})*(T_j-c)_+.                (2)

For T=T_ell+m*(1-gamma)-c, the exact excess is

 V(c)-O(c)=alpha/2*[(T+m*(1-q))_+
                          +(T-m*(1-gamma))_+ -2*T_+].               (3)

In particular 0<=V-O<=kappa*m/2. The data-measurable calibration
threshold c_D=T_ell+m*(1-gamma) gives O(c_D)=0 and
V(c_D)=kappa*U/(2N). This budget is DATA DEPENDENT; it is not a claim
that some unspecified fixed c achieves that equality. When ell=r,
T_ell=0 and c_D=0 is fixed, and V(c)=(kappa*m-c)_+/2.

## Posterior under actual factual observations

Put the uniform prior on orientations and random A supports. A factual
sequence with q_x samples from a known A context has likelihood
(1/(Nr))^q_x if every distinct observed identity belongs to its support,
and zero otherwise. Verifier likelihood is 1/binom(r,ell) if its
certified subset is contained in that support. Thus the posterior support
is UNIFORM over r-subsets containing the UNION of all j certified truths.
No independent multiplication of candidate events is used.

An untouched pair has no factual samples in either context. Its verifier
sets have identical likelihood in both orientations: a uniform random
r-subset followed by a uniform ell-subset of truths produces a uniform
ell-subset of [K], exactly as in S. The untouched orientations remain
independent fair bits; the rest are determined by tags.

Let mu=E[p|data] and s(y)=P(y false|data). Uncertified atoms in a known
A context with j known truths have

 mu_j=(r-j)/(N*r*(K-j)),     s=alpha_j.

Their total mu mass at that j is B_j. The untouched-pair uncertified
atoms have density mu_M=(mu_ell+1/(NK))/2 and risk alpha/2; their total
mu mass is M. Certified atoms are safe with density 1/(Nr) in known A
and (1/(Nr)+1/(NK))/2 in unknown pairs. Known S atoms have density
1/(NK) and risk zero, regardless of observed identities. Since

 mu_j decreases as j grows, alpha_j increases as j grows,
 mu_j<=mu_ell<=mu_M<=1/(NK),

mu-density is nonincreasing with false risk. Equalities do not cause
problems, including ell=0 or j=r. The fixed S reservoir is nonempty.

## Lower bound with arbitrary mixed score bins

If E is any upper-risk threshold set, each inside atom has density at
most every outside atom. For every uniform coarsening Pi this implies
mu_Pi(E)>=mu(E). Proof: in each cell, the mean density inside is no
larger than outside, so averaging the entire cell cannot reduce its
inside mass. This is the l(L+H)/(l+h)>=L calculation in C008 and also
handles empty intersections.

For any arbitrary g, its score bins Pi(g) are fixed when worlds are
averaged. Linearity and finite triangle inequality give
TV(mu_Pi,g)<=E[Mis(g,p)]. Thus robust or stated posterior-average
feasibility at budget c forces g(E)>=(mu(E)-c)_+ for every upper-risk
threshold E. Express posterior false mass by the finite layer-cake
identity: a cost with risk levels 0<s1<...<sL has expectation
sum_t (s_t-s_{t-1})*g({s>=s_t}), with s0=0.

Here the lowest positive level is alpha/2 on unknown uncertified atoms,
then alpha on known-A uncertified atoms, then alpha_j as j increases.
Their posterior tail masses are T_ell+M, T_ell, and T_j. The resulting
lower bound is exactly (1). Worst-world H dominates this posterior
average. This bound covers all generators and all partitions of score
levels, with no purity, context-uniformity or plug-in restriction.

## Attainment and oracle

Begin with mu. Remove up to c mass from positive-risk groups in
DECREASING risk order, uniformly within each group; groups of zero mu
mass contribute no removal. This means known A groups in decreasing j,
then the unknown-pair uncertified group. Transfer removed mass uniformly
to the fixed S reservoir. This g is normalized, nonnegative and has
TV(mu,g) equal to removed mass, at most c. Finite layer cake or direct
piecewise mass removal gives posterior cost (1).

Every known-A context has two invariant-mass subgroups: its certified
j atoms of known p mass j/(Nr), and its remaining atoms with total
p mass (r-j)/(Nr). The construction is constant on each subgroup.
For each unknown pair, all its certified atoms have the SAME g value,
and all its uncertified atoms have the same g value, shared across
both siblings. Their pairwise p masses are fixed independently of
orientation/support. Known S context fibres stay uniform. Therefore each
exact g-level bin is a union of invariant-mass groups, even if levels
merge or vanish, and p_Pi=mu_Pi in every compatible world.

Since g_Pi=g, TV(p_Pi,g)=TV(mu_Pi,g_Pi)<=TV(mu,g)<=c. In each removed
risk group the fraction of atoms false is exactly its posterior risk
in EVERY world: (K-r)/(K-j) in a known A group, and alpha/2 in the
unknown group. All receive equal g within group. Thus actual H equals
(1) worldwise, not just after averaging. This proves attainment for
Mis_infinity. The finite-coarse-bin lower bound is valid; its matching
upper bound is not asserted, since g need not be constant in coarse bins.

For the oracle, each formerly unknown pair has a known A context with
exactly ell certified truths and no factual observations. It contributes
mass m*(1-gamma) to B_ell; higher B_j stay unchanged. The same argument
gives (2). Subtracting (2) gives (3); split T at -m*(1-q),0,
m*(1-gamma) to check its nonnegativity and maximum kappa*m/2.

## Expected minimax and learning error

For fixed c, algorithms robustly feasible conditional on each observed
outcome have exact minimax expected value E[V(c)]. A uniform world prior
gives the lower bound via conditional Bayes; worst >= average. For the
upper bound, the construction's worldwise H depends only on U and the
histogram D_j. The distribution of this histogram is the same in every
fixed world: permute sibling contexts to change orientations and rename
candidate labels within each A support to change supports. Uniform
context sampling, uniform within-truth sampling and the verifier are
invariant under those bijections. Thus E[V] is the same in every world,
and the constructed algorithm attains the Bayes lower bound globally.
This argument also applies to the explicitly data-measurable budget c_D.

The occupancy law E U=d*(1-2/N)^n is unchanged. The exact minimax
classification error of a fair consistent ERM is
R=d/N*(1-2/N)^n: only untouched pair bits are unknown, and neither
their nonexistent factual observations nor symmetric verifier sets label
them. The fair world prior proves the lower bound and fair ERM completion
attains it in every world. Hence E[V(c_D)]=kappa*R/2, and for every
fixed c the expected excess over the matching oracle is at most that.
For n,d>=1,N=4max(n,d), this data-adaptive-threshold value is between
(kappa/16)*min(1,d/n) and (kappa/8)*min(1,d/n); when ell=r the same
statement uses the fixed budget c=0. No such matching lower rate at an
arbitrary fixed budget is claimed.

The histogram has at most d occupied entries. Group sorting avoids
iterating up to a potentially enormous r; sample processing and exact
rational group sampling have polynomial complexity in n,d,explicit
verifier-output size, log K and input bit lengths. No NK table is needed.
P(U>0)<=d*(1-2/N)^n still gives the high-probability oracle-attainment
regime. No missing-event independence is assumed.

The source definition is Kalai--Vempala 2311.14648v3, Definitions 1--2,
pp.8--9. Random-subset posterior counting, TV event bounds and finite
layer cake are standard; their use here is not a novelty assertion. The
frontier is a proposed explicit candidate pending
independent mathematical, priority and target-scope audit. Ordinary
UNANNOTATED factual training remains outside this result.

Exact Fraction verification passed: 1350 arbitrary-generator/bin checks,
2677 attaining-world checks, 37 conditional histograms, 4380 actual
sample/verifier outcomes and 54 actual-sampling fixed-world laws. The
script also checks the four-sample untagged ordering failure described
in proofs/untagged_density_order_counterexample.md. These finite checks
supplement the general proof, not numerical extrapolation. No Lean

body: Under regularity (identifiability, smoothness of the log-likelihood, information positive and finite, true parameter interior), the maximum likelihood estimator from n iid observations is consistent and asymptotically normal: sqrt(n) (theta_hat - theta) converges to N(0, I(theta)^{-1}), attaining the Cramer-Rao variance asymptotically. Wilks' theorem is the testing companion: twice the log-likelihood ratio for a nested null of codimension k converges to chi-squared with k degrees of freedom.
title: Asymptotics of Maximum Likelihood

body: [Definition def:taylor-jet-comp of arXiv:2609.00698, 'Kinetic Wedge Layers and Diffusive Limit of Neutron Transport in Polygonal Domains'] Let $q\in\mathbb N_0$. The one-sided Taylor jet of degree $q$ of $F$ at $s=0$ is $\bigl(F(0+),\ldots,F^{(q)}(0+)\bigr)$, provided each $F^{(a)}(0+):=\lim_{s\downarrow0}\partial_s^aF(s)$, $0\le a\le q$, exists in $X$. Its Taylor-polynomial representative is $J_qF(s):=\sum_{a=0}^q(s^a/a!)F^{(a)}(0+)$, and $F=J_qF+\mathcal R_qF$ with $\mathcal R_qF=o_X(s^q)$, respectively $O_X(s^{q+\gamma})$ when $F\in C^{q,\gamma}$. The jet is one-sided because the side stops at the vertex.
title: Definition def:taylor-jet-comp of arXiv:2609.00698

[Proposition prop:Rfail of arXiv:2608.28007, 'Exact Risk Ratios for Weighted Data Selection in Linear Regression'] Let $\varepsilon=\frac1{100}$ and take the projective directions and masses
\[
\begin{aligned}
&d_0=(-1,-1,0,0),\qquad d_1=e_1,\qquad d_2=e_2,\\
&d_3=(0,0,-1,-1),\qquad d_4=e_3,\qquad d_5=e_4,\\
&d_6=-\varepsilon(e_1+e_3),\qquad d_7=-\varepsilon(e_2+e_4),
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
(s_0,\dots,s_7)=\tfrac1{2700}\,(399,400,401,399,400,401,100,200).
\]
Then $\sum_is_id_i=0$ and $M=\sum_is_id_id_i^{\top}\succ0$, so
Lemma~(lem:realize of the paper) realizes a whitened system in $\mathbb{R}^4$. It is a
rectangle system: its positive circuits are exactly
$\{0,1,2\}$, $\{3,4,5\}$, $\{1,4,6\}$, $\{2,5,7\}$, and no subset of at
most five directions positively spans. Its four circuit-plane energies are
$\frac49,\frac49,\frac13,\frac{167}{450}$, all below $\frac12$; and its
anchor costs satisfy
\[
\min_it_i=\tfrac{32003064046811}{144192302726400}\approx0.2219>\tfrac15,
\quad
\min_{i<j}t_{ij}\approx0.4439>\tfrac13,
\quad
\min_{i<j<k}t_{ijk}\approx1.1097>1 .
\]
Hence both branches of (equation eq:R of the paper) fail, and so do the single- and
triple-anchor variants. The system is nevertheless cheap for the selector:
the single point $0$ gives ratio about $1.2219$, and an explicit five-point
strictly convex objective on the support $\{0,4,5,6,7\}$ gives exact ratio
$\frac{2452861}{2000000}=1.2264\ldots<2$.

body:
[Proposition 5 of arXiv:2605.31344, 'Subcritical sharpness for real-valued spin models'] For any $\beta \geq 0$ and $a \geq 2 D \beta$, there exists $B > 0$ such that for any finite $\Lambda \subset V$, $\Lambda' \subset \Lambda$, $\psi \in \mathbb{R}^{\Lambda'}$, and any boundary conditions $\eta \in \mathbb{R}^{V}$,
    \begin{equation}
        
        \mathrm{d} \nu_{\Lambda, \beta, \rho}^{\eta}[\varphi|_{\Lambda'} = \psi] \leq \prod_{x \in \Lambda'} e^{BA(x, \Lambda, \eta, \beta, a)^2} \mathrm{d} \nu_{\Lambda', 0, \rho_{a}}^{0}[\psi].
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 5 of arXiv:2605.31344

[Theorem thm of arXiv:2412.01070, 'A note on Lévy-driven McKean-Vlasov SDEs under monotonicity'] Assume that
$({\bf H}_{1})$-$({\bf H}_{3})$ hold true, and suppose further
 $X_0\in L^\beta(\Omega\to\mathbb R^d,\mathscr F_0,\mathbb{P})$.
Then, (equation e of the paper) has a unique strong solution $(X_t)_{t\ge0}$ satisfying  that, for any $T>0,$ there exists a constant $C_T>0$ such that
\begin{align}
 \sup_{0\le t\le T}\mathbb{E}|X_t|^\beta \le C_T(1+\mathbb{E}|X_0|^\beta).

body:
[Lemma 32 of arXiv:2607.18104, '2607.18104'] Let $(\omega_v)_{v \in \Z^2}$ be an i.i.d.~environment. Fix $j\in \N$. Then there exist some constants $c,C>0$ and a coupling $\mathbf{P}_{\textup{full}}$ between the i.i.d. LPP environment $\Pfull$ and the family of environments  used to determine the last passage times $(\Tpat_{u,v})_{u,v \in \Z^2}$ such that for fixed $i\in \N$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf{P}_{\textup{full}}\Big( T_{u,v}= \Tpat_{u,v} \, \forall (u;v) \in (R_n^{i,j}\times R_n^{i,j}) \cap V^{N}_n, j\in \lbr n -1 \rbr \Big) \geq 1 - C \exp\big(-cn^{1/2}\big) 
\end{equation} for all $n\in \N$, and $N$ sufficiently large. 
Similarly, let $(\omega_v)_{v \in \Z^2}$ be an $(N,k)$-periodic environment and assume that \eqref{eq:NonDegeneratedEnvironment} holds. Then there exists a coupling $\mathbf{P}_{\per}$ between  $\big(\Tper_{u,v}\big)_{u,v \in \Z^2}$ and $\big(\Tpat_{u,v}\big)_{u,v \in \Z^2}$  such that for fixed $i\in \N$
\begin{equation}
\mathbf{P}_{\per}\Big( \Tper_{u,v}= \Tpat_{u,v} \, \forall (u;v) \in (R_n^{i}\times R_n^{i})  \cap V^{N}_n   \Big) \geq 1 - C \exp\big(-cn^{1/2}\big) 
\end{equation} for all $n\in \N$, and $N$ sufficiently large.

[Proposition 31 of arXiv:2605.11801, 'A non-local singular non-linear Fokker-Planck PDE'] \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(i)]  Let $0<\al<\be<1/2$ such that for $i =1,2$,
          $b^i\in C_T\shc^{-\al}$.
      
          
                  Let $v_0 \in \shc^{\be+}$, such that   $v_0$ is a non-negative function such that $\Vert v_0 \Vert_{L^1} \le 1.$
  
		For $i = 1,2$, let
                $v^i$
                
                be the (mild) solution of (\ref{eq:FPlim}) with $b=b^i$.
		Then there exists a increasing function $\ell:\R^+ \rightarrow \R^+$, depending
		$\beta, \alpha, T, C_{F, K}, \Vert v_0\Vert_{\shc^\beta}$,
                
                such that 
		\begin{equation}
			\|v^1-v^2\|_{C_T \shc^{\al}}\leq \ell(\|b^1\|_{C_T\shc^{-\alpha}}  \lor\|b^2\|_{C_T\shc^{-\alpha}})\|b^1-b^2\|_{C_T\shc^{-\alpha}},
		\end{equation}
		for all $t\in[0,T]$.
		\item[(ii)] Let $(b^n)$ be a sequence in $C_T\shc^{(-\be)+}$ and $v^n$ be the solution of (\ref{eq:PDEdm}) with $b=b^n$ and $v$ be the solution to (\ref{eq:FPlim}). If $b^n\to b$ in $C_T\shc^{(-\be)+}$ then $v^n \to v $ in $C_T\shc^\be$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 31 of arXiv:2605.11801

body:
A hyperbolic boost by rapidity $\phi$ in the $(x_0, x_1)$-plane fixing the spacelike $x_2$-axis is the linear isometry $R_h(\phi) = \begin{pmatrix} \cosh\phi & \sinh\phi & 0 \\ \sinh\phi & \cosh\phi & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$. It mixes the timelike direction $x_0$ and spacelike direction $x_1$ while preserving $-\Delta x_0^2 + \Delta x_1^2$.
\phi \in R is the rapidity parameter
Fixed axis is spacelike
title: Hyperbolic Boost in Lorentz-Minkowski 3-Space

body:
[Lemma 1 of arXiv:2506.10494, 'Geometric Jensen-Shannon Divergence Between Gaussian Measures On Hilbert Space'] Let $A,B \in \Sym^{++}(n)$, $m_1, m_2 \in \R^n$, $a, b \in \R_{+}$, with $a^2 + b^2 > 0$. Then
			\begin{align}
				&a\la (x-m_1), A(x-m_1)\ra + b\la (x-m_2), B(x-m_2)\ra 
				\\
				&= \la (x-m), C(x-m)\ra + D,
				
			\end{align}
			where
			\begin{align}
				C & = aA + bB,
				\\
				m& = (aA + bB)^{-1}(aAm_1 + bBm_2),
				\\
				D & = a\la m_1, Am_1\ra + b \la m_2, Bm_2\ra
				\nonumber
				\\
				& \quad - \la (aA + bB)^{-1}(aAm_1 + bBm_2), (aAm_1 + b Bm_2)\ra.
			\end{align}
title: Lemma 1 of arXiv:2506.10494

    Then for all $\ep>0$ and $p\geq 1$, there exists $C(d,\alpha,K,p, \ep,\delta)>0$ such that for all $y \in \T^d, N \in \N$,

[Thm 10 (Determination by resultant distributions) of arXiv:2608.06576, 'The Resultant Distribution Method: Universality for $p$-adic Random Matrices and Polynomia'] Let $P^S_1$ and $P^S_2$ be random elements of $\mathscr{P}^S$. Suppose that, for every fixed polynomial $Z\in\mathscr{P}^S$, we have
$$
\val\bigl(\Res(P^S_1,Z)\bigr)\overset{d}{=}\val\bigl(\Res(P^S_2,Z)\bigr).
$$
Then $P^S_1\overset{d}{=}P^S_2$ as random elements of $\mathscr{P}^S$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Determination by resultant distributions

[Proposition prop:parabolic-average of arXiv:2609.00777, 'Universal murmuration and Hecke augmentation'] Under the hypotheses of Theorem~(thm:scaled-murmuration of the paper), the following estimates hold for every $\varepsilon>0$ as $X\to\infty$.
Let
\[
\mathcal P_k
=
\frac{\zeta(2)\pi}{XY}
\sideset{}{'}\sum_{\substack{N\in[X,X+Y]\\P\nmid N}}
\frac12H_1(-4P^kN).
\]
If $k$ is even, then
\[
\mathcal P_k
=
\frac{AP^{k/2}}{\sqrt X}
+
O_{k,\varepsilon}\left(
(PXY)^\varepsilon
\left(
\frac{P^{k/2-1}}{\sqrt X}
+
\frac{P^{k/2+1/6}X^{1/12}}{Y^{5/6}}
+
\frac{P^{k/2}Y}{X^{3/2}}
\right)
\right).
\]
If $k$ is odd, then
\[
\mathcal P_k
=
\frac{AP^{k/2}}{\sqrt X}
+
O_{k,\varepsilon}\left(
(PXY)^\varepsilon
\left(
\frac{P^{k/2-1}}{\sqrt X}
+
\frac{P^{k/2+3/38}}{Y^{16/19}}
+
\frac{P^{k/2}Y}{X^{3/2}}
\right)
\right).
\]

[Proposition of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] We have $S_2\lesssim e^{-2}\cdot (2\pi)^{-1/2}\cdot (n- \sqrt{n})^{1/2}$.
    \begin{proof}
        From the uniform upper bound in Lemma $(upper bound for s2 summand of the paper)$, we have
        \[S_2\leq\frac{(\frac{n}{2}-m-1)\binom{n-2m-4}{\frac{n}{2}+m+1}}{2^{n-2m-4}}\]
        We check that
        \[\frac{\frac{n}{2}+m+1-\frac{n-2m-4}{2}}{\sqrt{(n-2m-4)(\frac{1}{4}})}\]
        \[\frac{4m+6}{\sqrt{(n-2m-4)}}=\frac{2\,O(\sqrt{n})}{O(\sqrt{n})}\to 2\]
        so the conditions of Lemma $(de Moivre-Laplace of the paper)$ are satisfied. This means
        \[\frac{(\frac{n}{2}-m-1)\binom{n-2m-4}{\frac{n}{2}+m+1}}{2^{n-2m-4}}\sim\frac{(\frac{n}{2}-m-1) (e^{-2})}{\sqrt{2\pi(n-2m-4)(\frac{1}{4}})}\]
        \[\sim e^{-2}\cdot (2\pi)^{-1/2}\cdot (n- \sqrt{n})^{1/2}\]
        which establishes asymptotic control over $S_2$.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered proposition of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'

[Proposition 63 (Discontinuity of exact support projectors) of arXiv:2608.12492, 'Weak Limits of Wiener Chaos: Primitive--Fock Classification and Hilbert--Stein Extraction'] Let $e,h$ be orthonormal, put $Z=I_1(h)$, and let $Y_n=I_n(y_n)$ be normalized with
\[
 y_n\propto\Sym(h\otimes e^{\otimes(n-1)}).
\]
For
\begin{equation}
 F_n=Z+e^{-n^2}Y_n,
 
\end{equation}
one has $F_n\to Z$ in every fixed analytic Fock norm
$\sum_q\rho^{2q}(1+q)^m\norm{P_qF}_2^2$.  Nevertheless
\begin{equation}
 h\in\cN_1(F_n)\quad\text{for every }n,
 \qquad
 \cN_1(Z)=\{0\}.
 
\end{equation}
Thus $P_{\cN_1(F_n)}h=h$ while $P_{\cN_1(Z)}h=0$.

Let $h_\delta$ be a GFF on $\delta\mathbf{D}$ with some boundary values that are bounded by $M$ and so that the flow lines $\eta^\delta_1$ (resp.\ $\eta^\delta_2$) with angles $\theta_1 = -\pi/2$ (resp.\ $\theta_2 = -\pi/2 - {\theta_{{\mathrm{dbl}}}}$) from $-i\delta$ to $i\delta$ are defined. Given $\eta^\delta_1,\eta^\delta_2$, let $\Gamma$ be a ${\rm CLE}_{\kappa'}${} independently in each connected component bounded between $\eta^\delta_1,\eta^\delta_2$. Let $E$ denote the event that there exist $x',x,y,y' \in \eta^\delta_1 \cap \eta^\delta_2$ such that $(x,y) \in \intptsapproxbubble{U_{x',y'}}{\epsilon}$ as in~(equation eq:intpts_bubble of the paper) and $U_{x',y'} \subseteq B(0,\delta^{1+a_1})$ and $\metapproxacres{\epsilon}{U_{x',y'}}{x}{y}{\Gamma} \ge \median{\epsilon}+\epsilon^{-a_0}\mathbf{a}_{\epsilon}$. Then $\mathbf{P}[E] = O(\delta^{{\alpha_{\mathrm{apr}}}})$ as $\delta\searrow 0$.

body: [Theorem mainthm2 of arXiv:2607.05418, 'On the Group Randomness of 0-1 Real Sequences from Binary Linear Codes'] Let $\{\mathcal{C}_n\}$ be a sequence of binary linear codes of length $n$ and dual distance $d_n^\bot$. Let $\widetilde{\Phi}_{\mathcal{C}_n}$ be the $p_n \times n$ 0-1 random matrix as constructed above, with $y:=p_n/n \in (0,1)$ fixed. Let $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_{\mathcal{C}_n}$ be the Gram matrix of $\frac{2}{\sqrt{n}}\widetilde{\Phi}_{\mathcal{C}_n}$, and $\tilde{\lambda}_1$ denote the largest eigenvalue of $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_{\mathcal{C}_n}$. If $d_n^\bot \geq 5$ for all $n$, then as $n \to \infty, \tilde{\lambda}_1-(p_n+1+y)$ converges in distribution to the Gaussian distribution with mean $0$ and variance $4y$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem mainthm2 of arXiv:2607.05418

PRIVATE SCAR, author-recorded. A tempting argument: quasi-multiplicativity alpha_4(1,R) asymp alpha_4(1,rho) alpha_4(rho,R) makes f(R) = -log alpha_4(1,R) approximately subadditive in log R, so lim f(R)/log R exists by the de Bruijn-Erdos approximate-subadditivity lemma, giving the four-arm exponent on Z^2. The step is invalid as written: approximate subadditivity needs alpha_4(rho,R) asymp alpha_4(1,R/rho), i.e. dependence on the ratio of radii up to constants (scale invariance up to constants), which on Z^2 is exactly as unproved as the exponent; on the triangular lattice it comes from the SLE(6) computation. What quasi-multiplicativity rigorously gives is alpha_4(1,2^n) asymp prod_{k<n} alpha_4(2^k,2^{k+1}) with each factor bounded between constants by RSW; the exponent exists iff the logarithms of the dyadic factors are Cesaro convergent, which is open. So both the existence and the value (conjecturally 5/4) of the four-arm exponent on Z^2 are open, as the Garban-Steif notes state. Route refuted for the existence claim; do not reuse.

RSW crossing estimates and quasi-multiplicativity hold on Z^2

Let m>=3 and q>=2 be integers satisfying q>=sqrt(m)/ln(m). Let Z have independent uniform coordinates in [q], and let K=|Unique(Z)|. Then E[K]=q*(1-(1-1/q)^m). With C=q*(1-exp(-m/q)), P(|K-C|>2*sqrt(m)*ln(m))<=2*exp(-(ln(m))^2). In particular, K lies between C-2*sqrt(m)*ln(m) and C+2*sqrt(m)*ln(m) with probability1-negl(m), where negligible means smaller than every inverse polynomial for sufficiently large m. The restrictions m>=3,q>=2 make the logarithms and the proof intermediates valid.
Integers m>=3,q>=2; q>=sqrt(m)/ln(m).
The length-m string consists of independent uniform alphabet symbols.

[Theorem 24 (Morikawa--Simpson criterion) of arXiv:2609.01570, 'A Proof of Fraenkel's Conjecture'] For \(0<p,s<q\), consider the two sets \(\B^q_{p,*}\) and
\(\B^q_{s,*}\), and set
\[
 g_p=(p,q),\quad A=q/g_p,\quad x=p/g_p,
 \qquad g_s=(s,q),\quad B=q/g_s,\quad y=s/g_s,
\]
and put \(d=(x,y)\), \(u=x/d\), \(v=y/d\).  Some translates of the two
rational Beatty sets are disjoint if and only if there exist positive
integers \(k,\ell\) such that
\begin{equation}
 ku+\ell v=(A,B)-2uv(d-1).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Morikawa--Simpson criterion

[Definition 4 (Weakly trace-majorizing) of arXiv:2608.29427, '\small Positive mass and rigidity \\ for asymptotically flat tangent bundles'] An AF metric $g$ on $M$ is called \emph{weakly trace-majorizing} if
	\[
	\fint_{\mathbb S_r}\tr_0g\,d\sigma_r\geq n
	\]
	for all sufficiently large $r$. If
	\[
	\fint_{\mathbb S_r}\tr_0g\,d\sigma_r=n
	\]
	for all sufficiently large $r$, we call $g$ \emph{weakly trace-rigid}.
title: Weakly trace-majorizing

[Corollary 10 of arXiv:2606.29512, '2606.29512'] Let Assumptions 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3 hold, and let $u$ be a solution to
$(2.1)$--$(2.2)$ such that almost surely 
\begin{equation}
                                                        
\int_0^T\Big( \int_{\cR}|u_s(x)|^p\,dx\Big)^{q/p}\,ds < \infty
\end{equation}
for some
\begin{equation}
                                                                  
d<p\le\infty,
\qquad
2\le q<\infty,
\end{equation}
satisfying the Ladyzhenskaya--Prodi--Serrin condition
\begin{equation}
                                                                   
\frac{d}{p}+\frac{2}{q}\le1.
\end{equation}
Then $u$ is an $\mathcal H$-solution. Moreover, if $v\in L_{p',q'}$ is a solution 
to $(2.1)$--$(2.2)$, such that $p',q'$ satisfy \eqref{LPS2}-\eqref{LPS3},  
then for its $\mathcal H$-valued c\`adl\`ag modification,
still denoted by $v$, we have 
$$
u_t=v_t\quad\text{almost surely for all } t\in[0,T]. 
$$

[Lemma l:NS_increased_viscosity of arXiv:2607.15140, 'On the absence of blow-up in the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with transport noise'] Let $p,q\in (2,\infty)$ be such that 
\begin{equation}

\frac{2}{p}+\frac{3}{q}<2.
\end{equation}
Then, for all $M\geq 1$, there exist constants $R_0,\mu_0>0$ for which the following assertion holds. For all $\mu\geq \mu_0$ and $u_0\in \mathbb{B}^{1-2/p}_{q,p}(\mathbb{T}^3)$ such that 
$$
\|u_0\|_{B^{1-2/p}_{q,p}(\mathbb{T}^3;{\mathbb R}^3)}\leq M,
$$
there exists a unique global-in-time $(p,q)$-solution $u_{{\rm det}}$ to the deterministic {{\normalfont{3D NSEs}}} with increased viscosity (equation eq:navier_stokes_cutoff_high_viscosity of the paper) such that 
$$
u_{{\rm det}}\in W^{1,p}_{{\rm loc}}([0,\infty);\mathbb{H}^{-1,q}(\mathbb{T}^3))\cap L^p_{{\rm loc}}([0,\infty);\mathbb{H}^{1,q}(\mathbb{T}^3)),$$ 
and it satisfies
\begin{align}

\|u_{{\rm det}}-\overline{u}_0\|_{L^{2p}({\mathbb R}_+;L^{2q}(\mathbb{T}^3;{\mathbb R}^3))}\leq R_0.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Global well-posedness of 3D NSEs with high viscosity

body:
Load-bearing hypothesis: 'the operator −Δ' or 'the Schrodinger operator H = −Δ + V' is not defined by its formula; the domain is part of the data, and essential self-adjointness on a chosen core is a theorem, not a convention. What fails without it: two different self-adjoint operators can agree on a common dense domain, with different spectra, different semigroups and different dynamics; semiboundedness does not select a unique extension either. Counterexamples. (1) −d²/dx² on C_c^∞(ℝ) is essentially self-adjoint with closure the operator on H²(ℝ); but −d²/dx² on C_c^∞(0, ∞) in L²(0, ∞) has deficiency indices (1, 1), and its self-adjoint extensions are the Dirichlet realization {f ∈ H²(0,∞) : f(0) = 0} and the Robin family {f ∈ H²(0,∞) : f'(0) = α f(0)}, α ∈ ℝ. All extend a nonnegative symmetric operator, yet for α < 0 the Robin extension has the eigenvalue −α² with eigenfunction e^{αx}: the lower bound 0 valid on C_c^∞(0,∞) is not inherited by every self-adjoint extension. The Friedrichs extension (here the Dirichlet realization) is the one that always inherits the lower bound; the Robin extensions with α ≥ 0 happen to stay nonnegative as well, so the lower bound alone singles out nothing. (2) −d²/dx² on C_c^∞(0, 1) has deficiency indices (2, 2); the Dirichlet, Neumann and periodic realizations are distinct self-adjoint extensions with eigenvalues {(kπ)² : k ≥ 1}, {(kπ)² : k ≥ 0} and {(2πk)² : k ∈ ℤ} respectively. (3) −Δ on C_c^∞(ℝⁿ ∖ {0}) is essentially self-adjoint if and only if n ≥ 4; for n ≤ 3 removing a single point changes the operator, and the extensions in n = 3 are the point-interaction ('delta potential') Hamiltonians. Audit rule: a claim 'H is self-adjoint' must name the domain or the core, and a claim that a computation on smooth compactly supported functions determines the operator must cite an essential self-adjointness theorem (Kato-Rellich, Faris-Lavine, Nelson's analytic vectors, or a limit-point analysis).
the operator is given by a differential expression on a domain with boundary or on a punctured space
essential self-adjointness on the chosen core is not verified

[Lem G_reg of arXiv:2603.29711, 'Strong Feller property, irreducibility,\\ and uniqueness of the invariant measure\\ for st'] Let $\gamma\geq2$ 
and $\delta > \frac d4$: then, 
there exists a positive constant $C$, depending on $\gamma, \sigma, \eta, \delta$, such that 
    \[
    \|G_\gamma(v)\|^2_{\mathscr{L}^2(H, H)} \le C
     \quad\forall\,
    v\in B_1^\infty.
    \]
Moreover, if $d\in\{1,2\}$, $\sigma\in[0,\frac12)\cap (\frac d4-\frac12,\frac12)$, $\delta>\frac d4+\sigma$,
and $\gamma\geq2d$, 
then for every $\eta\in(\sigma,1)\cap(\frac d4, \frac12+\sigma)$
the restriction
    \[
    G_\gamma: B_1^\infty \cap V_{2 \eta} \rightarrow \mathscr{L}^2(H,V_{2\sigma})
    \]
    is well defined, and 
    there exists a positive constant $C$, 
    depending on $\gamma, \sigma, \eta, \delta$, such that 
    \[
    \|G_\gamma(v)\|^2_{\mathscr{L}^2(H, V_{2\sigma})} \le C
    \|v\|_{V_{2\rho}}^{2(d-1)}
    \|v\|^2_{V_{2\eta}} \quad\forall\,
    v\in B_1^\infty \cap V_{2 \eta},
    \]
    where $\rho=0$ if $d=1$ and
    $\rho\in(1-\eta,\frac12)$ if $d=2$.
title: Lem G_reg of arXiv:2603.29711

[Definition def:scalimRW of arXiv:2607.09946, 'Statistics on Yau's conjecture: Variance asymptotics'] Let $M$ be either a compact Riemannian manifold of dimension $n$, or $M=\mathbb{R}^n$. Let $\dist \cdot \cdot$ denote the Riemannian distance function on $M\times M$.
Let $I_\ell\subset [0,+\infty)$ be an interval such that $\ell=\max I_\ell\in \mathbb{R}$ and let $\alpha\in [0,1]$.
We will refer to the following scaling bound for $\phi^M_{I_\ell}$ as the \emph{$\mathcal{C}^k$ Scaling Bound of Random Waves of type $\alpha$ in range $[\rho_\ell',\rho_\ell]$}:
\begin{gather}
E_{I_\ell}^M(x,y)=\ell^{n-1}{|I_\ell|} \left( 
{E^n_{\mathsf U(\alpha,1)}}\left( \ell\cdot \dist x y \right)
+
R_{\alpha,I_\ell}^{M}(x,y)
\right), \quad \text{and define}
\\
\sup_{ \rho_\ell'\le \mathrm{dist}(x,y)\le \rho_\ell}\sup_{|a|,|b|\le k} \frac{\| \nabla^a \nabla^b R_{\alpha,I_\ell}^{M}(x,y)\|}{\ell^{|a|+|b|}}\sqrt{n}^{|a|+|b|}=: \delta_{I_\ell}^{M}(\alpha,\mathcal{C}^k,[\rho_\ell',\rho_\ell])
    \end{gather} 
where $0\le\rho_\ell'\le \rho_\ell$ and $k\in \mathbb{N}$. We call the number $\delta_{I_\ell}^{M}(\alpha,\mathcal{C}^k,[\rho_\ell',\rho_\ell])$ the 
\emph{$\mathcal{C}^k$ Scaling error of Random Waves of type $\alpha$ in range $[\rho_\ell',\rho_\ell]$}. 

\textbf{Notation:} in what follows, to keep a lighter notation, we shall write $\delta_{I_\ell}^M \equiv \delta_{I_\ell}^{M}(\alpha,\mathcal{C}^k,[\rho_\ell',\rho_\ell])$.
title: Definition def:scalimRW of arXiv:2607.09946

[Theorem 15 (lower bound on the maximal solution) of arXiv:2606.07290, 'Boundary behaviour of the Volterra square-root process'] Suppose that $K$ is regularly varying of the form \eqref{eq: regularly varying} where $\alpha \in (1/2,1)$ and $\ell$ is slowly varying at zero. Then for each $\eta \in (0,1)$ there exists $t_0 > 0$ such that
    \[
        V_{\infty}(t) \geq (1-\eta)\frac{A_{\alpha}}{2\sigma^2} \frac{t^{-\alpha}}{\ell(t)}, \qquad t \in (0,t_0)
    \]
    where the constant $A_{\alpha}$ is given by
    \[
        A_{\alpha} = \frac{\Gamma(\alpha)}{B(\alpha, 2\alpha-1)} = \frac{\Gamma(3\alpha-1)}{\Gamma(2\alpha-1)}.
    \]

[Corollary cor:hard-lower-bound of arXiv:2510.06891, 'Multivariate CLT for L\'evy processes: convergence rates without moment assumptions'] Suppose $\bm{X}$ is in the domain of non-normal attraction of $\bm{Z}$. Then  for any measurable $\bm{A}:[1,\infty) \to \mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $\bm{B}:[1,\infty) \to \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$, such that $\bm{B}(t)$ is invertible for all sufficiently large $t$, we have $\bm{e}_j^\intercal \bm{B}(t)^\intercal \bm{B}(t)\bm{e}_j \to \infty$ and $\bm{B}(t)^{-1}\bm{B}(f(t))\to \bm{I}_d$ for all $j\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$ and non-decreasing functions $f$ with $f(t)/t\to 1$ as $t \to \infty$, respectively, it holds that
\[
t \mapsto t^{-1}d_\mathscr{K}(\bm{X}_t-\bm{A}(t),\bm{B}(t) \bm{Z} )\notin L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(+\infty).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary cor:hard-lower-bound of arXiv:2510.06891

[Corollary 4 of arXiv:2608.18557, 'Randomly Permuted Orthogonal Products and Fast Dimension Reduction'] Let \(A,B\in O(d)\), let \(D_\xi \in \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}\) be a Rademacher diagonal, and
	let \(\pi\) be an independent uniform permutation on \(S_d\). Let \(0<\eta<1/2\) and set $U=AD_\xi P_\pi B$. Suppose that
	\[
	\norm{A}_\infty\norm{B}_\infty
	\le
	\frac{1}{\sqrt{d \log(d/\eta)}}.
	\]
	Then, with probability at least \(1-\eta\),
	\[
	\norm{U}_\infty
	\le
	4\frac{\sqrt{\log(d/\eta)}}{\sqrt{d}}.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 4 of arXiv:2608.18557

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2609.01333, '2609.01333'] Let $\delta>0$, $\beta\in (0,1)$ and $\alpha\in (0,\beta)$. Define the set
\begin{align*}
\cB^\beta_\delta:=\{\varphi\in C^{1,\beta}(\R)\,:\, \varphi>\delta\}.
\end{align*}
Then
for every $w\in C^{0, \beta}(\R)$, the map
$\cJ_w:  \cB^\beta_\delta \to C^{0,\alpha}(\R)$
defined by
\begin{align*}

\cJ_w(\varphi)(t)
&=-\int_{\mathbb{S}^1}   \int_\R (w(t)- w(t-r  ))  \varphi(t-r) \overline{\cK}(\varphi,t,r, p_\theta) \mathrm{d}r  \mathrm{d}\theta   \nonumber\\

&\quad+\frac{w(t)}{2}\int_{\mathbb{S}^1}p_\theta^2 \int_\R    \varphi(t-rp_\theta) \cK(\varphi,t,r,p_\theta)  \mathrm{d}r \mathrm{d}\theta
\end{align*}
is of class $C^\infty$, where $p_\theta=|\theta-e_1|$.  Moreover, for every $k\in \N$, there exists a constant $c=c(\kappa,\delta,\alpha,\beta,k)>1$ such that
$$
\|D^k \cJ_w(\varphi)\|\leq c  \|w\|_{C^{0,\beta}(\R)}(1+\|\varphi\|_{C^{1,\beta}(\R)})^c.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 16 of arXiv:2609.01333

body: [Theorem thm:bound of arXiv:2609.00672, 'Deciding superellipticity and computing the Weierstrass normal form'] Let $C$ admit a cyclic cover of degree $n$ with a model (eq:model of the paper) in which $h$ is separable, and let $g\ge 2$. Then $n\le 2g+2$, and the bound is attained by $y^{2g+2}=x^2-1$. If $C$ is not hyperelliptic, then $n\le g+2$, and the bound is attained by $y^n=x^3-x$ with $3\mid n$, $n\ge 6$.

body:
[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2609.02850, 'Canonical-row Chern flow on Bott--Samelson towers:\\ realizable-volume models for Schubert'] Let
\[
 P(x,z)=\sum_{k=0}^{r}P_k(x)z^{r-k},
 \qquad \deg P_k=d+k,
\]
and suppose that $\Nrm_{x,z}(P)\in\RVC$.  Write
\[
 P_k(x)=\sum_{|\alpha|=d+k}c_{k,\alpha}x^\alpha.
\]
For $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)\in\mathbb R_{\geq0}^n$, define
\[
 M_k(\lambda)
 =(d+k)!\sum_{|\alpha|=d+k}
 \frac{c_{k,\alpha}}{\alpha!}\lambda^\alpha.
\]
Then
\[
 M_k(\lambda)^2\geq
 M_{k-1}(\lambda)M_{k+1}(\lambda)
\]
for every $k$, with out-of-range terms interpreted as zero.  The set of $k$ for which $M_k(\lambda)>0$ is empty or an interval of integers.

[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2608.15874, '2608.15874'] Fix $u>1$. For every $a\geq1$, writing $x=\log a$ and $c=\log u$,
\[
  \varpi([a,ua])=\frac{e+1}{2}\roundb[\bigg]{\frac{1}{e+\log(e+x)}-\frac{1}{e+\log(e+x+c)}}.
\]
The map $a\mapsto\Delta_\varpi(a,u)$ is nondecreasing on $[1,\infty)$. Moreover,
\[
  \Delta_\varpi(a,u)=\log\log a+2\log\log\log a+O_u(1), \qquad a\to\infty.
\]

[Lem flux of arXiv:2608.30847, 'An Almgren-type formula for planar $p$-harmonic functions'] Let $u$ be $p$-harmonic in $B_R(x_0)$.  For every $0<r<R$ for which the trace identity is valid,
$$
  D(r)=\int_{\partial B_r(x_0)} A v\partial_\nu u\,dS.
$$
In particular the identity holds for all small $r$ in the setting of Theorem (thm:main of the paper) below.

$$
  \operatorname{div}(AD u)=0
$$
pointwise, and the divergence theorem gives
$$
  0=\int_{B_r(x_0)} \operatorname{div}(vAD u)\,dx
    -\int_{B_r(x_0)} AD u\cdot D v\,dx.
$$
Since $D v=D u$, this is exactly the desired identity.

At a planar critical center, choose $r$ so small that $x_0$ is the only critical point in $B_r(x_0)$.  Apply the preceding smooth argument on the annulus
$$
  B_r(x_0)\setminus \overline{B_\varepsilon(x_0)}.
$$
The inner boundary contribution is
$$

[Lemma 17 (\citet{brezis2011functional}, Theorem~7.3) of arXiv:2608.22636, 'Q-Learning with Stable Infinite-Dimensional \\Linear Function Approximation'] Let $(E,\norm{\cd})$ be a Banach space and let $\cH:E\to E$ be globally Lipschitz; that is, there is
$L<\infty$ such that
$$
        \norm{\cH\theta-\cH\theta'}\le L\norm{\theta-\theta'},
        \qquad \theta,\theta'\in E.
$$
Then, for every $\theta_0\in E$, there exists a unique continuously differentiable function
$\vartheta:[0,\infty)\to E$ satisfying
$$
        \vartheta(t)=\theta_0+
        \int_0^t\cH\vartheta(s)ds,
        \qquad t\ge0 .
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let mu and nu be sigma-finite measures on a measurable space (X, Sigma) with nu absolutely continuous with respect to mu (nu(A)=0 whenever mu(A)=0, written nu << mu). Then there exists a non-negative measurable function f = dnu/dmu, unique mu-almost-everywhere, such that nu(A) = integral over A of f dmu for every A in Sigma. f is the Radon-Nikodym derivative; the theorem is the measure-theoretic foundation of conditional expectation and of probability densities.

[Theorem of arXiv:2506.09364, 'A collection of results relating the geometry of plane domains and the exit time of planar'] Suppose $D$ is a Jordan* domain with boundary given by a Jordan* curve $\hat C$, and with complementary Jordan* domain $\tilde D$. Define a new domain $U$ by $U:=D \cup \tilde D \cup V$, where $V$ is an open subset of $C$. Suppose there are closed sets $K \subset D, \tilde K \subset \tilde D$ with the following properties.

    \begin{itemize}
        \item $\sup\{E_a[T(K^c)^p] : a \in \tilde K\} < \infty$.
        \item $\sup\{E_a[T(\tilde K^c)^p] : a \in K\} < \infty$.
        \item $\inf\{P_a(T(U)<T(\tilde K^c)): a \in K\} > 0$ or $\inf\{P_a(T(U)<T(K^c)): a \in \tilde K\} > 0$.
    \end{itemize}

    Then $bh(U) = \min\{bh(D), bh(\tilde D)\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 9 (Block coefficients) of arXiv:2608.01674, '\textbf{Limit Theorems for Tempered Linear Processes with Innovations in the Domain of Att'] Let $0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_m\le T$.  For $1\le k\le m$ and
$j\in\Z$, set
\[
 C_{N,k}(j):=
 \sum_{n=(j+1)\vee(\floor{Nt_{k-1}}+1)}^{\floor{Nt_k}}
 b_{N,n-j},
\]
with an empty sum equal to zero.  For every $\delta>0$, when $N\to\infty$,
\begin{align}
 &\sup_{\floor{N(t_{k-1}+\delta)}\le j
          \le\floor{N(t_k-\delta)}}
 \left|\frac{C_{N,k}(j)}{Q_N}-1\right|
 \longrightarrow0,
 \\
 &\sup_{\floor{N(t_{k-1}+\delta)}\le j
          \le\floor{N(t_k-\delta)}}
 \frac{C_{N,i}(j)}{Q_N}
 \longrightarrow0,\qquad i>k.
 
\end{align}
Furthermore, the indices within distance $\delta N$ of the block
endpoints contribute at most $C\delta$ to the normalized empirical
$p$th powers, uniformly in $N$, for every $p>1$.

[Lemma lem:loop-approach-bound of arXiv:2607.18070, 'The Brownian loop-catcher'] Fix \(0<\varepsilon<T<\infty\) and \(\eta>0\).  Let
\(C_V^\delta,B_V^\delta\subset D^\delta\), with \(C_V^\delta\) connected,
and put \(C^\delta=\operatorname{Cell}_\delta(C_V^\delta)\).  Suppose that $\operatorname{diam} C^\delta\geq d$ and $\mathrm{dist}(C^\delta,B_V^\delta)\geq a$
for fixed \(a,d>0\).  If
\(0<\rho<(a\wedge d)/64\) and \(\delta<\rho/8\), then
\begin{align}
 m_\delta^{[\varepsilon,T],\eta}
 \{\ell:\mathrm{dist}(\ell,C^\delta)\leq2\rho,\
          \ell\cap C_V^\delta=\varnothing,\
          \ell\cap B_V^\delta\ne\varnothing\}\leq
 M_{\varepsilon,T}
 \left(\frac{\rho}{a\wedge d}\right)^{1/2}.
 
\end{align}
The constant is uniform in
\(\eta,\delta,C_V^\delta,B_V^\delta\).  The analogous Brownian loop estimate
holds for a connected compact \(C\) and compact \(B\) with
\(\operatorname{diam} C\geq d\) and \(\mathrm{dist}(C,B)\geq a\).

[Prop compactplanarlatching of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Assume that $\mathcal{F}$ is a $\Phi$-horizontal foliation on $M$, where $\Phi$ is nonwandering and $\aleph$-obstructed, and that $\mathcal{F}$ has finitely many compact planar leaves and no degeneracy $\mathbb{T}^2$-type planar minimal sets. Assume that the fine boundary multislope of $\mathcal{F}$ is of the form
    $$\big(\underset{k_\flat}{\underbrace{s_1^\flat, \dots, s_{k_\flat}^\flat}}, 
    \underset{k_\sharp}{\underbrace{t_1^\sharp, \dots, t^\sharp_{k_\sharp}}}, 
    \underset{k_\circ}{\underbrace{w^?_1, \dots, w^?_{k_\circ}}},
    \underset{k_\aleph}{\underbrace{\aleph, \dots, \aleph}}\big),$$
where
\begin{itemize}
    \item The first $k_\flat$ boundary components of $M$ are $\flat$-latching,
    \item The next $k_\sharp$ boundary components of $M$ are $\sharp$-latching,
    \item The next $k_\circ$ boundary components of $M$ are nonlatching and have unconstrained types,
    \item The last $k_\aleph$ boundary components of $M$ are of $\aleph$ type.
\end{itemize}
Then there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that
$$\prod_{i=1}^{k_\flat} \big(s_i - \varepsilon, s_i\big) \times \prod_{i=1}^{k_\sharp} (t_i, t_i+\varepsilon) \times \{(w_1, \dots, w_{k_\circ})\} \times \mathbb{R}^{k_\aleph} \subset \mathcal{Z}(\Phi).$$
title: Prop compactplanarlatching of arXiv:2608.30031

body:
[Defn 5 (discrete R\'enyi and Tsallis entropies) of arXiv:2607.17576, 'How much randomness is needed to symmetrize a random variable?'] Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the probability mass function $\{f(k)\}_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}$. For $\alpha\in (0, 1)\cup (1, \infty)$, the R\'enyi entropy $H_\alpha(X)$ of order $\alpha$ is defined by
$$
H_\alpha(X) = \frac{1}{1-\alpha}\log \sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}f(k)^\alpha
$$
and the Tsallis entropy $T_\alpha(X)$ of order $\alpha$ is defined by
$$
T_\alpha(X) = \frac{1}{1-\alpha}\left(\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}f(k)^\alpha-1\right).
$$
Taking the limit $\alpha\to 1$, both entropies are reduced to Shannon entropy 
$$
H(X)=-\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}f(k)\log f(k).
$$
title: discrete R\'enyi and Tsallis entropies

[Theorem Szarek of arXiv:2605.05193, 'Grokability in five inequalities'] Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\) be even and \(n\ge 4\). Let \(x\) be distributed uniformly on
\[
\Omega_n:=\Bigl\{x\in\{-1,1\}^n:\sum_{i=1}^n x_i=0\Bigr\},
\]
and let \(a=(a_1,\dots,a_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Then
\[
c_n \sqrt{\mathbb{E}\Big|\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\Big|^2}
\le
\mathbb{E}\Big|\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\Big|,
\]
where
\[
c_n=\sqrt{\frac{n-2}{2(n-1)}}
\]
is optimal. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Balanced Szarek's inequality
