body: [campaign status: candidate_full_solution - author-checked, unrefereed] Lyons and Peres, Probability on Trees and Networks (version 19 August 2026), Question 17.18 (p. 575) asks whether a consistent equivariant flow rule admitting a stationary measure EQUIVALENT to Galton-Watson measure must induce an ergodic Markov chain; their Proposition 17.17 proves it when all child weights are strictly positive, and Exercise 17.22 gives a non-ergodic example whose stationary measure is only absolutely continuous, so equivalence is the point of the question. Our result (id P0033, 2026-09-08): NO. Take Galton-Watson with P(D=2) = 3/5, P(D=3) = 2/5 (mean 12/5) and an isomorphism-invariant colour in {0,1} defined by AND at two-child vertices and OR at three-child vertices; both preserve unanimity, so every vertex has at least one child of its own colour, and the flow chooses uniformly among those. Galton-Watson measure is stationary, the root colour is invariant along the chain and takes each value with probability 1/2 - a non-constant invariant function, hence no ergodicity - and the stationary measure equals Galton-Watson measure, trivially equivalent to it. The colour exists because F(p) = (3/5) p^2 + (2/5)[1 - (1-p)^3] fixes 1/2, and r_n = E[q_n^2] satisfies r_{n+1} = 3/10 + (3/5) r^2 + (2/5) r^3 whose increment factors as (r - 1/2)[(2/5) r^2 + (4/5) r - 3/5], driving r_n from r_0 = 1/4 up to 1/2 and giving E[q(1-q)] = 0. Verification as the source words it: the step the proof leaves implicit, and which was checked, is that Galton-Watson really is stationary - it holds because, conditioned on the children's colours, the child subtrees are independent, each distributed as Galton-Watson conditioned on its own colour, so the chosen subtree is exactly GW given colour = c, the uniform choice adds no bias, and mixing over c returns GW. Prior art unchecked; the tree-automaton and factor-of-iid literature is where to look. Galton-Watson with P(D=2) = 3/5, P(D=3) = 2/5 consistent equivariant flow rule choosing uniformly among same-coloured children

body:
[Theorem permuton_convergence_thm of arXiv:2412.07258, 'Permuton limit of a generalization of the Mallows and $k$-card-minimum models'] Given $g$ and $\sigma_n \sim \mathrm{PERM}(g,n)$ as in Definition (def_gen_perm_model of the paper), let $F_{\sigma_n}$ denote the (random) c.d.f.\ of the (random) permuton corresponding to $\sigma_n$ (cf.\ Definition (def_permutation_permuton of the paper)). We have
    \begin{align}
        F_{\sigma_n}(x,y) \stackrel{\mathbb{P}}{\longrightarrow} F_{g}(x,y), \quad n \to \infty, \quad x,y \in [0,1].
    \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Law of large numbers in permuton space

body:
[Lemma backward estimate of arXiv:2605.03151, 'Giants through Higher-Order paths in Random Simplicial Complexes'] Let $k \geq 0$ and $v$ be a vertex that can create a backward $d$-dimensional simplex a $(d-1)$-simplex $\sigma^k$ that is being explored at Step $k$. Then, the probability that $\sigma^k \cup \{v\}$ appears at Step $k$ is lower bounded by
\[  \tag{3.2.18}
p_k^B := \bigg( 1- \sum_{\ell = 1}^{d-1} \sum_{\substack{\rho \subseteq \sigma^k, \\ \dim(\rho) = \ell-1}} \deg_{\ell-1, d-1}^{\mathcal{X}_{k-1}}(\rho) p_{d, \ell} \bigg) \left( \frac{\lambda}{n} + o(1) \right).
\]
In particular, if the given MRSC model is the Linial-Meshulam model, the probability is exactly $\lambda/n + o(1)$.
title: Lemma backward estimate of arXiv:2605.03151

[Lemma lem:later-conflict of arXiv:2609.02845, 'Degeneracy bounds, stability, and a sharp gap for $B$-colorings'] Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, and let $G$ be a $d$-degenerate graph with degeneracy ordering $v_1,\ldots,v_n$.  Order $E(G)$ by increasing index of the earlier endpoint, breaking ties arbitrarily.  For an edge $e=v_i u_1$, where $u_1$ is later than $v_i$, let $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ be the later neighbors of $v_i$.  Then the number of edges following $e$ in this ordering that $B$-conflict with $e$ is at most
\[
  d_G(u_1)-1+
  \sum_{j=2}^{r}|N_G(u_1)\cap N_G(u_j)|.
\]

Chain rule (Stampacchia): if $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ is open and $u \in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$, $1 \leq p \leq \infty$, then $T_k(u) \in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ with $
abla T_k(u) = 
abla u \cdot \mathbf{1}_{\{|u| < k\}}$ almost everywhere; if $u \in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$ then $T_k(u) \in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$, and $|T_k(u)| \leq \min(|u|, k)$. In particular $
abla u = 0$ a.e. on every level set $\{u = c\}$. Companion functions: the positive part $u^+ = \max(u,0)$ and $G_k(u) = u - T_k(u)$ (the part of $u$ beyond level $k$); all such compositions satisfy the same chain rule $
abla(\phi \circ u) = \phi'(u)
abla u$ a.e. for piecewise $C^1$ Lipschitz $\phi$ with finitely many corners (with $\phi(0) = 0$ to stay in $W_0^{1,p}$). The truncation method uses $T_k(u)$ (or $G_k(u)$) as a test function in a weak formulation; because it is bounded by $k$ it is admissible against $L^1$ right-hand sides, and $\int_\Omega |
abla T_k(u)|^p$ measures the energy of $u$ on the set where $|u| < k$. Sharp edges: the chain rule needs $\phi$ Lipschitz (a merely continuous or unbounded-derivative $\phi$ can leave $W^{1,p}$); for a function that is only in $L^1_{loc}$ with no Sobolev regularity, $T_k(u) \in W_0^{1,p}$ for all $k$ is a genuine extra hypothesis, and this is exactly the class in which entropy solutions of $L^1$-data problems live.

body:
[Lemma lem:plane-blind-ricci-packet of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Fix a complete orthogonal-Weingarten atom $(p,q,r)$ before opening any
packet front.  Let $P$ be an external $q$-component assigned wholly to
one aggregate-Ricci root time, and suppose its $s$ coefficient
occurrences all carry
\[
 \mathsf C_i=|a_i\rangle\langle a_i|-N^{-1}I_W.
\]
The aggregate-Ricci passive boundary has no $q$-dart, so the coefficient
contraction of $P$ is a closed scalar, denoted $Z_{P,q}(i)$.  It satisfies
\[
 \boxed{Z_{P,q}(i)=z_{P,q}\quad\hbox{for every coordinate plane }i,
 \qquad |z_{P,q}|\le4^s.}
\tag{3.3.1w$_{6b}$}
\]
If $P$ has one occurrence, then $z_{P,q}=0$.  If it is nonzero and has
at least two occurrences, then $c=c^{\!*}(P)\ge2$, and replacing its bare
carrier $n^c$ by the closed scalar costs at most
\[
 A^s n^{-c}
\tag{3.3.1w$_{6c}$}
\]
relative to the bare Euler majorant.

Let X be a locally compact Hausdorff space and mu a regular Borel measure on X (the case X = [a,b] with Lebesgue measure is the usual one). Let f be a real-valued function in L^1(mu) and let eps > 0. Then there exist functions u and v on X with u <= f <= v, u upper semicontinuous and bounded above, v lower semicontinuous and bounded below, and integral_X (v - u) dmu < eps. In particular an integrable function is squeezed between an upper semicontinuous minorant and a lower semicontinuous majorant whose integrals differ by as little as one likes.
mu regular Borel on a locally compact Hausdorff space;
f real-valued and mu-integrable.
The upper semicontinuous minorant need only be bounded above and the lower semicontinuous majorant bounded below - neither is claimed continuous.

[Lemma 14 (Normalized Gaussian scale mixture) of arXiv:2605.11451, '2605.11451'] Let $1\le p<2$, and let $Z$ have density $g_p(x)=e^{-|x|^p}/(2\Gamma(1+1/p))$. Then there is a positive non-degenerate random variable $V$ such that
\[
 Z\mid V\sim N(0,V).
\]
Equivalently,
\begin{equation}
 g_p(x)=\E\left[\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi V}}\exp\left(-\frac{x^2}{2V}\right)\right].

This classifies possible scalar curvature LIMITS. It does not assert that a

Let f(x)=lambda x^2/2, lambda,eta,epsilon>0, 0<b<1, 0<d<1. Use ordinary
uncorrected Adam or ordinary separate bias corrections, epsilon outside sqrt.
Let D_t=sqrt(v_(t+1))+epsilon (uncorrected) or sqrt(vhat_(t+1))+epsilon
(corrected), C_t=lambda/D_t. Suppose C_t->C_infinity exists and is positive.
Then one of the following holds:
 (i) C_infinity=lambda/epsilon and x_t,m_t,v_t ->0;
 (ii) eta*C_infinity=2(1+b)/(1-b), |x_t|->a>0, and signs eventually
      alternate. The state approaches the known two-cycle, with
      a=eta*(1-b)/(2(1+b))-epsilon/lambda.

x_t^2->0. Then m_t->0 by a stable linear recursion.
Otherwise v_t tends to a strictly positive value lambda^2*a^2; subtracting
d v_t from v_(t+1) gives x_t^2->a^2, so x_t is nonzero eventually.

Write the actual x update as x_(t+1)=x_t-alpha_t*m_(t+1), where
alpha_t=eta/D_t (uncorrected) or eta/[(1-b^(t+1))*D_t] (corrected).
Then alpha_t->alpha=eta*C_infinity/lambda>0 and alpha_t/alpha_(t-1)->1.
Eliminating m_t using the preceding update gives exactly
 x_(t+1)=[1+b alpha_t/alpha_(t-1)-alpha_t(1-b)lambda]x_t
          -b alpha_t/alpha_(t-1)*x_(t-1).
Thus with s_t=sign(x_t), A=1+b-alpha(1-b)lambda<1+b,
 s_(t+1)=A s_t-b s_(t-1)+o(1).                                (1)
There are only finitely many sign quadruples (s0,s1,s2,s3) in {+1,-1}^4.
Any quadruple occurring arbitrarily late must satisfy BOTH limiting equations

If s0*s2=-1 the right side is 1-2b, strictly between -1 and 1, impossible.
So s0=s2 and s1=s3. The two remaining possibilities are constant signs, with A=1+b, and alternating signs, with A=-(1+b). The former contradicts
A<1+b. Since finitely many words can occur, every sufficiently late word
is alternating, and A=-(1+b). It follows that alpha(1-b)lambda=2(1+b),

body:
[Theorem thm:main1 of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Let $D$ be a simply-connected domain and $z_1 \neq z_2 \in D$. Let $E^{\rm nest}_\varepsilon(z_1,z_2)$ denote the event that there is a nested CLE$_4$ gasket that comes $\varepsilon_1$-close to both $z_1$ and $\varepsilon_2$-close to $z_2$. Then we have
$$\lim_{\max(\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2) \to 0}\varepsilon_1^{-1/8}\varepsilon_2^{-1/8}\mathbb{P}(E^{\rm nest}_\varepsilon(z_1,z_2)) = C_0\CR(z_1,D)^{-1/8}\CR(z_2,D)^{-1/8}\exp\left(\frac{\pi}{2}G_D(z_1,z_2)\right),$$
where $C_0$ is an absolute constant \footnote{Both here and in the next statements these absolute constants are explicit up to a term depending on SLE$_4$ loop measure (that we think does not have an explicit expression). This term would disappeaer when using conformal radii instead of actual radii, or when normalising the two-point function by product of one-point functions. We prefer to keep this dependence and remark here that some duality arguments are nicer using the Euclidean normalisation, although the conformal radii one would also follow from the same techniques.}.
Further, this two-point function also equals,
up to an absolute constant,
$$\Big\langle:\exp\Big(i\sqrt\frac{\pi}{2}\Phi_D(z_1)\Big):~
:\exp\Big(-i\sqrt\frac{\pi}{2}\Phi_D(z_2)\Big):
\Big\rangle .$$
Here the GFF $\Phi_D$ in $D$ is normalized to have covariance $G_D$, and we consider the usual imaginary multiplicative chaos. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Two-point correlations of nested CLE$_4$

body:
[Proposition prop: exact ruin brownian motion for collective model of arXiv:2606.28031, 'Insurance risk models in a heterogeneous time-dependent population: scaling limits and rui'] Let $X$ and $Y$ be two independent arithmetic Brownian motions. We assume the existence of $\rho$ and $\eta$ defined in Assumptions~(A:hyp LLN for V of the paper) and (A:hyp CLT for V of the paper). Set $\alpha_*:=2\frac{\rho {\mathrm c}_X+(1-\rho){\mathrm c}_Y}{\sigma_X^2\eta^2+\sigma_Y^2\left(\eta^2+1-2\rho\right)}$. 

Under the net profit condition $\rho{\mathrm c}_X+(1-\rho){\mathrm c}_Y>0$, for any $\alpha>\alpha_*$,
\begin{equation}
p(u)=\frac{{\mathrm e}^{-\alpha u}}{\mathbb{E}\left[{\mathrm e}^{-k_{\alpha}(\tau(u))}\,\big|\,\tau(u)<\infty\right]}.
\end{equation}
Moreover, when $F$ is deterministic, the decay rate of $p(u)$ is $\alpha_*$:
\[
\lim_{u\to \infty}\frac{1}{u}\log p(u)= -\alpha_*.

body:
[Lemma upper bound for s2 summand of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] We have
    \[\max_{1\leq j\leq\frac{n}{2}-m-1}\frac{\binom{2j-2}{n-j}}{2^{2j-2}}=\frac{\binom{n-2m-4}{\frac{n}{2}+m+1}}{2^{n-2m-4}}\]
    \begin{proof}
        Denote 
        \[a_j=\frac{\binom{2j-2}{n-j}}{2^{2j-2}}\]
        First notice that $a_j>0$ if and only if $j\geq\frac{n+2}{3}$. Fix $n\geq 5$. We will apply the ratioing method from the proof of Proposition $(middle terms strategy of the paper)$. We have
        \[\frac{a_{j+1}}{a_j}=\frac{(2j)(2j-1)(n-j)}{4(3j-n+1)(3j-n)(3j-n-1)}:=f_n(j)\]
        We sketch the rest of the proof. One can show by differentiation that when $n\geq 5$ is fixed, $f$ is decreasing on $j\geq\frac{n+2}{3}$, which is precisely in the nonzero terms of $S_2$. By direct computation, we have $f(\frac{n}{2})<1$ and $f(\frac{n}{2}-1)>1$. Since $f$ is decreasing, this implies 
        \begin{equation}
        
        f_n(j)>1\;\;\;\; \text{for all}\;\;\;\; \frac{n+2}{3}\leq j\leq\frac{n}{2}-1. 
        \end{equation}
        In particular, since $\frac{n}{2}-m-1<\frac{n}{2}-1$ when $n\geq 5$, equation $(s2 ratio equation of the paper)$ holds for all $\frac{n+2}{3}\leq j\leq\frac{n}{2}-m-1$. We deduce that $a_j$ is maximized at $j=\frac{n}{2}-m-1$.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma upper bound for s2 summand of arXiv:2507.10294

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). The lace expansion writes the two-point function of self-avoiding walk, Bernoulli percolation, oriented percolation or lattice trees as a renormalised random-walk Green function plus a correction series: for SAW, c_n(x) = sum_y D(y) c_{n-1}(x - y) + sum_{m=2}^{n} sum_y pi_m(y) c_{n-m}(x - y), with pi_m the alternating-sign lace coefficients obtained by inclusion-exclusion over self-intersections (for percolation the analogous expansion is in terms of pivotal bonds and sausages). The expansion is an exact identity; its use requires a bootstrap showing the coefficients are small in a norm controlled by a random-walk diagram: the bubble diagram for SAW (finite for d > 4), the triangle diagram for percolation (finite for d > 6) and the square diagram for lattice trees (d > 8). Proved regimes: nearest-neighbour SAW for d >= 5 (Hara-Slade), spread-out SAW for d > 4, nearest-neighbour percolation for d >= 11 (Fitzner-van der Hofstad) and spread-out percolation for d > 6 (Hara-Slade). Conclusions there: mean-field exponents (gamma = 1, eta = 0, beta = 1 and delta = 2 in bounded-ratio senses), Gaussian or super-Brownian scaling limits, and asymptotic expansions of critical points. It gives nothing at or below the upper critical dimension, and for nearest-neighbour percolation in 7 <= d <= 10 there is no small parameter, so the expansion holds only as an identity, not as a bound. Typical failure: Applying the expansion's mean-field conclusions (eta=0, Gaussian or super-Brownian scaling limit) to a model at or below its upper critical dimension without re-verifying the triangle or bubble condition; the coefficients pi_m are not shown small there, the bootstrap can fail to close, and the diagrammatic control silently assumed at the outset is exactly the open problem, which is why four-dimensional nearest-neighbor percolation mean-field behavior remains open despite the spread-out and high-dimension cases being resolved. Canonical reference: Hara and Slade, 1990, Communications in Mathematical Physics; Madras and Slade, The Self-Avoiding Walk, 1993, Birkhauser.
A small parameter: bubble (SAW), triangle (percolation) or square (lattice trees) diagram small at criticality
Above the upper critical dimension: d > 4 (SAW), d > 6 (percolation), d > 8 (lattice trees)
Nearest-neighbour models need d >= 5 (SAW) or d >= 11 (percolation) with current methods
title: Technique: Lace Expansion

Let Phi be a stationary simple locally finite planar point process with finite positive intensity, bounded Voronoi cells, finite nonempty edge-neighbor sets, no four cocircular points, no three collinear points, and almost surely unique nearest nuclei p_x at deterministic observation points. Define F6(x) as the mean of ((q-p_x)/|q-p_x|)^6 over its Delaunay edge-neighbors. Put C6(x,y)=E[F6(x)conjugate(F6(y))]-E[F6(x)]E[conjugate(F6(y))], V(t)=P(Phi intersect B(0,t) is empty), and alpha(A,B)=sup |P(E intersect H)-P(E)P(H)| over events of the restrictions to A and B. Then for every r>0 and deterministic x,y, |C6(x,y)| <=16alpha(B(x,3r),B(y,3r))+28V(r/32). No independence of empty-disk events is needed.

[Theorem 20 of arXiv:2606.16164, 'A Low-Regularity Semigroup Sewing Lemma via Quotient Structures'] Let $\gamma\in(0,1]$, $\alpha\in\mathbb R$ and $h\in Z\hat C^{\gamma}(\Delta^3_T;B_\alpha)$.  Then, for every $\tau\in[0,T]$, if $\gamma\in(0,1)$, one has
\[
r_{\mathrm d}^\tau(h)\in C^{\gamma}(\Delta^2_\tau;B_\alpha), \quad \delta r_{\mathrm d}^\tau(h)=h^\tau
\]
and the uniform estimate $\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}\|r_{\mathrm d}^\tau(h)\|_{\gamma,\alpha;\tau}\le C_\gamma M_{\alpha,T}\|h\|_{\gamma,\alpha}$; if $\gamma=1$, one has
\[
r_{\mathrm d}^\tau(h)\in C^{1}_{\mathrm{log}}(\Delta^2_\tau;B_\alpha), \quad \delta r_{\mathrm d}^\tau(h)=h^\tau
\]
and the uniform estimates $$\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}\|r_{\mathrm d}^\tau(h)\|_{1,\log;\tau,\alpha}\le C_{1,T} M_{\alpha,T}\|h\|_{1,\alpha},$$ 
as well as, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, $$\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}\|r_{\mathrm d}^\tau(h)\|_{1-\varepsilon,\alpha;\tau}\le C_{\varepsilon,T} M_{\alpha,T}\|h\|_{1,\alpha}.$$

[Definition def:bracketprod of arXiv:2411.06827, 'The Exponential Lie Series and a Chen--Strichartz Formula for L{\'e}vy Processes'] We define a commutative associative product $[\cdot , \cdot ]$  on the vector space over ${\mathbb R}$ generated by the alphabet ${\mathbb A}$ as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
\item if $i=0$ then $[i, j]:=\mathbf{0}$ for all $j\in {\mathbb A}$, 
\item 
$[i, i]:=i^{(2)}$ and $[i, i^{(2)}]:=\mathbf{0}$ for all $i=1, \ldots , d$, 
\item $[i^{(l)}, i^{(k)} ]:=i^{(l+k)}$ for all $l, k\ge 1$ and for all  $i=d+1, \ldots ,\ell$, and
\item $[i^{(l)}, j^{(k)} ]:=\mathbf{0}$ for $i\not=j$ and all $l, k\ge 1$.
\end{enumerate}
We extend this definition to the vector space generated by
 ${\mathbb A}$ linearily. Here $\mathbf{0}$ denotes
the zero in $\mathbb R$ to distinguish it from the letter $0$ in ${\mathbb A}$.
For  letters $a_i$ in ${\mathbb A}$, iterated products are denoted by 
$$
	[a_1,\dots,a_n]:=[a_1,[a_2,\dots,a_n]].
$$

[Definition def:c4-witness-block of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] In this section a root, or candidate root, is a right vertex $j_\star\in J$.
Its first left layer is
\[
I_\star:=N_G(j_\star).
\]
For $i\in I_\star$, an $L$-\hyperref[def:c4-witness-block]{\textcolor{PineGreen}{\emph{reservoir}}}{} at $i$ is a set
\[
\mathcal R_i\subseteq N_G(i)\setminus\{j_\star\}
\]
of auxiliary right vertices with $|\mathcal R_i|\ge L$. 
After choosing, for each $i\in I_\star$, an $L$-\hyperref[def:c4-witness-block]{\textcolor{PineGreen}{\emph{reservoir}}}{} $\mathcal R_i$,
the associated $L$-\hyperref[def:c4-witness-block]{\textcolor{PineGreen}{\emph{witness block}}}{} at $j_\star$ is the subset of right vertices
\[
{\mathcal W}(j_\star):=\{j_\star\}\cup\bigcup_{i\in I_\star}\mathcal R_i.
\]
The \hyperref[def:c4-witness-block]{\textcolor{PineGreen}{\emph{reservoir}}}{}s $\mathcal R_i$, $i\in I_\star$, witness this block.
title: Roots, reservoirs, and witness blocks

[Theorem thm_HKp of arXiv:2606.28067, 'Ergodic approximation for the invariant distribution: An abstract framework for law-depend'] Let $p\ge 1$. Let $f,g:{\mathbb{R}}^d \to {\mathbb{R}}_+$ be
		probability density functions such that $\int_{{\mathbb{R}}^{d}}\left\vert
		x\right\vert ^{p}f(x)dx+\int_{{\mathbb{R}}^{d}}\left\vert x\right\vert
		^{p}g(x)dx<\infty$. Then, we have 
		\begin{equation}
			W_{p}^{p}(f(x)dx,g(x)dx)\leq 2^{p-1} \int_{{\mathbb{R}}^{d}}\left\vert
			x\right\vert ^{p}\left\vert f(x)-g(x)\right\vert dx.  
		\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm_HKp of arXiv:2606.28067

	C\sqrt{\frac{\log d}{d}}.

[Lemma lemsimpole of arXiv:2605.01878, '\Large Random trade timing and power-law tails in realized prices'] Let $\mathbb{A}(z)$ be an $N\times N$ complex matrix-valued holomorphic function on an open connected set $\Omega \subset \mathbb C$. Suppose that $\mathbb{A}(z)$ is invertible for some $z \in \Omega$, and that $\mathbb{A}(z_0)$ has rank $r<N$ for some $z_0 \in \Omega$. Then the following conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), ref=(\roman*)]
    \item  $\mathbb{A}(z)^{-1}$ has a simple pole at $z=z_0$.
    \item  There exist $N \times (N-r)$ matrices $x$ and $y$ of full column rank such that $\mathbb{A}(z_0)x = 0$, $y^\top \mathbb{A}(z_0) = 0$, and $y^\top \mathbb{A}^{(1)}(z_0)x$ is invertible.
\end{enumerate}
Under either condition, the residue of $\mathbb{A}(z)^{-1}$ at $z=z_0$ is
\[
x \left(y^\top \mathbb{A}^{(1)}(z_0) x\right)^{-1} y^\top.
\]
title: Simple-pole criterion

Let (X, mu) and (Y, nu) be sigma-finite measure spaces and K: X x Y -> C measurable for the product sigma-algebra. (a) Unweighted form: suppose A = sup_{x in X} int_Y |K(x,y)| dnu(y) < infinity and B = sup_{y in Y} int_X |K(x,y)| dmu(x) < infinity (suprema may be essential suprema). Then for every 1 <= p <= infinity and f in L^p(nu), (Tf)(x) = int_Y K(x,y) f(y) dnu(y) converges absolutely for mu-a.e. x and ||Tf||_{L^p(mu)} <= A^{1 - 1/p} B^{1/p} ||f||_{L^p(nu)}. In particular ||T|| <= sqrt(A B) on L^2. (b) Weighted form: let 1 < p < infinity, p' = p/(p-1), and suppose there exist measurable h_1 > 0 on X and h_2 > 0 on Y and constants C_1, C_2 with int_Y |K(x,y)| h_2(y)^{p'} dnu(y) <= C_1 h_1(x)^{p'} for a.e. x, and int_X |K(x,y)| h_1(x)^p dmu(x) <= C_2 h_2(y)^p for a.e. y. Then ||T||_{L^p(nu) -> L^p(mu)} <= C_1^{1/p'} C_2^{1/p}.
(X, mu), (Y, nu) sigma-finite (needed for Tonelli)
K measurable for the product sigma-algebra
both kernel bounds hold (one alone is not enough except at the endpoints p = 1, infinity)

There are at least three other characterizations of Dedekind domains that are sometimes taken as the definition: see below.

Let F:R^d->R be locally Lipschitz and admit the chain rule: for every locally absolutely continuous arc z, (F composed with z)'(t)=<h,z'(t)> for every h in partial^C F(z(t)), for almost every t. Suppose F(a x)=a^k F(x) for every x and every a>0, with fixed degree k. Then partial^C F(a x)=a^(k-1) partial^C F(x) for every a>0, and <x,h>=k F(x) for every x and every h in partial^C F(x). Here partial^C is the Clarke subdifferential, and multiplying a set means multiplying each element. This is a nonsmooth chain-rule result; no differentiability of F at x is assumed.
F locally Lipschitz on R^d
F admits the stated chain rule for all locally absolutely continuous arcs
Homogeneity F(a x)=a^k F(x) for all x and a>0

[Lemma 147 of arXiv:2605.03236, 'Stochastic It\^o Equations and Parabolic Second-Order Equations with singular Drift'] Let $x_{\cdot}$   be a solution  of
 \eqref{3.24,1} with $(t,x)=(0,0)$
and let $\tau$ be a stopping time
such that $(t,x_{t})\in C_{R}$ for $t\leq \tau$ and some
$R\in(0,\infty)$. Assume that

(a) for any  
  Borel nonnegative $f$ on $\bR^{d+1}$
\begin{equation}
                             
E\int_{0}^{\tau }f(s,x_{s})\,ds\leq N\|f\|_{E_{q,p,\beta }},
\end{equation}
where $N$ is independent of $f$. Then

(b) (It\^o's formula)  for
\index{$S$@Miscelenea!It\^o's formula}
 any    $u\in E^{1,2}_{q,p,\beta  } $, 
 with probability one for all $t\geq0$,
\begin{equation}
                                
u(t\wedge\tau ,x_{t\wedge\tau })
=u( 0)+\int_{0}^{t\wedge\tau }D_{i}u 
\sigma^{ik} (s,x_{s})\,dw^{k}_{s}
+\int_{0}^{t\wedge\tau }\cL u (s,x_{s})\,ds
\end{equation}
and the stochastic integral above is a 
square-integrable
martingale. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemm l:abs12 of arXiv:2607.18194, 'Temperature chaos in directed polymers'] Fix $k\in\mathbb{N}$.
    Let $\{X_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ and $\{Y_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be sequences of $k$-dimensional random vectors on the same probability space, such that the pair $(X_n,Y_n)$ jointly converges weakly to some $(X,Y)$ as $n\to\infty$.
    Suppose that for every $\varepsilon>0$, there exist sequences of random vectors $\{W_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ and $\{Z_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ such that $Z_n$ and $W_n$ are independent for every $n$, and such that
    \begin{align*}
        \limsup_{n\to\infty} \mathbb{E}\left[
            \left\lVertX_n - Z_n\right\rVert_2^2
        \right] 
        \leqslant \varepsilon,
        \qquad\text{and}\qquad
        \left\lVertY_n - W_n\right\rVert_2
        \xrightarrow{\,p\,} 0
        \text{ as $n\to\infty$.}
    \end{align*}
    Then $X$ and $Y$ are independent.

body:
[Ppn 22 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recall $F^{\rii}$ from \eqref{e:F.rii}
    and $F^{\riii}$ from \eqref{e:F.iii}. 
    For sufficiently large $N$, for all $t\in \R$,
    \[
        \P(F^{\rii}(k) \ge t)
        \le \P
        \bigg(
        F^{\riii}(k,\hat{\cB}(\bG,\omega))
         + \frac{\epsilon'}{5} \ge t
        \bigg) + e^{-cN} \,.
    \]
That is, $F^{\riii}(k)$ approximately stochastically dominates
$F^{\rii}(k)$.

\begin{proof} Condition on any realization of $\bG$. Recall that
$F^\rii(k)$ is defined by \eqref{e:F.rii}
as the average of $F^\ri$ over $k$ orthogonal replicas, maximized over $S_\perp(k)$. Recall moreover that $F^\ri$ is defined by summing \eqref{e:F.B}--\eqref{e:F.w}, where we rewrote \eqref{e:F.B} and \eqref{e:F.U} in \eqref{e:F.B.rewrite} and \eqref{e:F.U.rewrite} above.
\begin{itemize}
\item Considering \eqref{e:F.U.rewrite}, 
note that $\bXi^\ell \hat{\bx} / \sqrt{N}$ is a standard gaussian in $\R^M$, independent of the gaussian process $\{\bXi^\ell \by^\ell : (\hat{\bx}, \by^\ell) = 0\}$.
Thus, the quantity inside
the maximum defining $F^\rii(k)$
(see \eqref{e:F.rii}),
as a process indexed by $\by^{1:k}$, remains distributionally unchanged if we replace each $\bXi^\ell \hat{\bx} / \sqrt{N}$ with $\bz^\ell$, which corresponds to replacing $F_U$ with $\bar{F}_U$. 
\item Considering \eqref{e:F.B.rewrite}, we can set
     \[
        \tbmeta^j
        = \frac{1}{|B_j|^{1/2}}
        \sum_{a\in B_j}
        \bmeta^{\ell,a}\,,
    \]
and note that the $\tbmeta^j$ are i.i.d.\ standard gaussian vectors in $\R^N$.
\end{itemize}
This shows that
    \begin{align*}
    F^{\rii}(k)&
       \stackrel{d}{=}
       \sup\bigg\{
       \frac{1}{k} \sum_{\ell=1}^k
     \bigg[
       \bar{F}_B(\tbmeta^\ell,\by^\ell,\hat{\cB}(\bG,\omega))
       +F_v(\bG,\by^\ell,\hat{\cB}(\bG,\omega)) \\
 &\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad 
       +\frac{\|\bar{\bx}\|^2}{N}
       \bar{F}_U(\bG,\bz^\ell,\by^\ell,\hat{\cB}(\bG,\omega))
       +F_w(\by^\ell,\hat{\cB}(\bG,\omega)) \bigg]
        : \by^{1:k}
    \in S_\perp(k)
       \bigg\} \,.
    \end{align*}
Enlarging the domain from $S_\perp(k)$ to $S_+(k)$ can only decrease the above supremum. Finally, the difference between the quantity inside the above supremum, versus the quantity inside the supremum \eqref{e:F.iii} (with $\cB = \hat{\cB}(\bG,\omega)$),
is upper bounded by
    \baln
        &\lt|\frac{\|\bar{\bx}\|^2}{N} - 1 \rt|
        \frac{1}{k}
        \sum_{\ell=1}^k
        \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{\hU_j}{MN|B_j|}
        \bigg(
            \sum_{a\in B_j}
            (\bz^\ell)_a \barbg^a,
            \by^\ell
        \bigg)^2 \\
        &\le \bigg|\frac{\|\bar{\bx}\|^2}{N} - 1 \bigg|
        \frac{1}{k}
        \sum_{\ell=1}^k
        \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{\hU_j}{MN|B_j|}
        \|\bz^\ell(B_j)\|^2
        \|\bG^{B_j}\|_{\op}^2
        \|\by^\ell\|^2\,.
    \ealn
    By standard estimates, we have $\|{\bz^\ell(B_j)}\|^2 \le 2|B_j|$ with probability at least $1-e^{-cN}$.
    Combined with the estimate $\|\bG^{B_j}\|_{\op} \le C\sqrt{N}$ from \eqref{e:wishart.bound.repeated}, and $\|\by^\ell\| = \sqrt{N}$, we find that the last display is
        \[
    \le O(1)
    \bigg|\frac{\|\bar{\bx}\|^2}{N} - 1 \bigg|
    \le \frac{\epsilon'}{5}\,,
    \]
where the last inequality holds with probability at least $1-e^{-cN}$ by
 Lemma~\ref{l:fp-gc}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem disintegrated deviation bds of arXiv:2411.14350, 'Randomized Geodesic Flow on Hyperbolic Groups'] Let $(Y_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a random walk started at $o$ with step distribution $\mu$. For any $D\geq 0$ and $n\geq 0$ sufficiently large, there exists $C_D>1$ such that for all $\xi\in \partial G$
\[ C_D^{-1} {\rm e} ^{-D} \leq \mathbb{P}_{o}\big[d_{{\mathcal G}}\big(Y_n, [o,\xi)\big)\geq D\big \vert \xi \big]\leq C_D {\rm e} ^{-D}.\]
The constants $C_D$ are bounded in $D$ and do not depend on $\xi$.

[Lemma lem.peakednessl2 of arXiv:2603.11043, 'An asymptotically optimal bound for the concentration function of a sum of independent int'] Let $\epsilon \in (0, \frac 1 2)$ and define $V_0 = V_0(\epsilon) := \frac{320 \cdot 2^{\frac{1}{3}}}{\epsilon^{2}}$. 
    Let $X \sim \mu_X$, $Y \sim \mu_Y$ be indepedent random variables on integers.
    Let $X' \sim \mu_X'$ and $Y' \sim \mu_Y'$ be independent symmetric log-concave integer random variables. 
    
    If
    \[
        \mu_X \preccurlyeq_\epsilon \mu_X', \quad \mu_Y \preccurlyeq_\epsilon \mu_Y', \quad {\mathrm{Var}}\, X' \ge V_0 \quad\mbox{and}\quad {\mathrm{Var}}\, Y' \ge V_0
    \]
    then
    \[
        \mathcal{Q}(X+Y) \le (1+20\epsilon)\mathcal{Q}(X'+Y').
    \]

Own-work draft: proof (unaudited); no independent C009 PASS. Instance and hypotheses: n>=2; K>=1; T=nK; 0<mu<=L; f_i(x,y)=mu*x^2/2+L*y^2/2+b_i*x+c_i*y; sum b_i=sum c_i=0; s_mu=mean b_i^2, s_L=mean c_i^2; deterministic x0!=0,y0; s_mu+s_L>0; fresh independent uniform permutations each epoch; shared permutation across coordinates allowed; all parameters fixed as K tends to infinity; global step minimization over eta>=0 or a fixed positive capped interval. Under C001 fixed-instance hypotheses, candidate refinement mu*T*eta=(3/2)log(T)-log(log(T))+(1/2)log(8*A0/(27*D))+o(1), with A0=mu*x0^2/2 for L>mu and A0=mu*(x0^2+y0^2)/2 for L=mu. Natural logarithms; all global minimizers intended.

metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:da704187e683c75687c34cba5425d7b2187b3aa1316235bc6bfddc8a4981bc63","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/da/da704187e683c75687c34cba5425d7b2187b3aa1316235bc6bfddc8a4981bc63.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:9afa88a3c3a646433088a5648a4f7494552195796931a76422c1e2673e285e46","bundle_entry_key":"second-order-optimal-step-common-hessian","bundle_id":"population.t362-second-order-optimal-step-008","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"optimization; random reshuffling; optimal constant step; second-order asymptotic","draft":"w732/bundle_008.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.randomreshuffling:common-hessian-random-reshuffling-second-order-optimal-constant-step","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C009 v2: second-order optimal step, fixed instance

Kind: special. Target: 1, reviewer-requested refinement of C001.
Status: proof (unaudited). This does not alter the approved C001/C002 proof files.
Prior campaign work is credited in PRIOR_WORK_ATTRIBUTION.md. No novelty is asserted.

Use exactly the instance and fixed-parameter asymptotic hypotheses of C001:
n>=2, 0<mu<=L, x0!=0, s_mu+s_L>0, fresh independent uniform
epoch permutations, deterministic initialization, and T=nK tending to infinity.
Let eta_T be ANY global minimizing constant step, either unrestricted over
eta>=0 or subject to a fixed cap H>0. Put

    t_T = mu*T*eta_T,
    D = n*(n+1)*(mu^2*s_mu+L^2*s_L)/(48*mu^3),
    A0 = mu*x0^2/2                       if L>mu,
    A0 = mu*(x0^2+y0^2)/2               if L=mu.

Then D>0 and A0>0. All logarithms below are natural. The refinement is

    t_T = (3/2)*log(T) - log(log(T))
          + (1/2)*log(8*A0/(27*D)) + o(1).                 (R)

Constants and convergence rates may depend on the fixed instance, including
the positive gap L/mu-1 when L>mu. There is no uniform-in-kappa claim.

## 1. A common window for all minimizers

The approved C001 v1 proves t_T/log(T)->3/2 for every minimizing sequence,
and eventually every minimizer is interior and eta_T<1/L. Therefore eventually
ALL minimizers belong to

    I_T = [(7/5)*log(T), (8/5)*log(T)]

in the t coordinate. Otherwise selecting one outside this interval on an
infinite subsequence would contradict C001. This uses its all-minimizer
statement, not uniqueness. For a fixed capped interval, eta_T->0 makes the
upper cap inactive eventually.

## 2. Exact differentiated decomposition

Index the two coordinates separately even when their curvatures agree.
For a coordinate h in {mu,L}, define k_h=h/mu, a_h=1-k_h*t/T,
r_h=a_h^(2T), A_h=h*u_h^2/2. On I_T, eventually 0<a_h<1. Set

    B_h(eta)=(h/2)*eta^2*V_h(eta)/(1-(1-h*eta)^(2n)).

The denominator has a simple zero at eta=0, while V_h is a polynomial
with a double zero there. Its canceled expression extends analytically
through eta=0. By the finite polynomial expansion already used in C001,

    B_h(eta)=C_h*eta^3+O(eta^4),
    B_h'(eta)=3*C_h*eta^2+O(eta^3),
    C_h=s_h*h^2*n*(n+1)/48.

Differentiation is valid because of this analytic extension. It does not
differentiate an unspecified asymptotic remainder. If s_h=0, B_h and both
displayed terms are identically zero. Also sum_h C_h=mu^3*D.

With a dot denoting differentiation in t at fixed T, the exact objective is

    Q_T(t)=sum_h [A_h*r_h+B_h(t/(mu*T))*(1-r_h)],
    dot r_h=-2*k_h*a_h^(2T-1),
    Q_T'(t)=sum_h [A_h*dot r_h+dot B_h*(1-r_h)-B_h*dot r_h].  (1)

No division by r_h or zero variance is needed.

## 3. Uniform variance-derivative estimate

All estimates in this section hold uniformly for t in I_T. Since t=O(log T),
eta=t/(mu*T)->0 uniformly. The analytic expansions give

    sum_h dot B_h = 3*D*t^2/T^3 + O(t^3/T^4),
    sum_h |dot B_h| = O(t^2/T^3),
    sum_h |B_h| = O(t^3/T^3).

Indeed dot B_h=B_h'(eta)/(mu*T), including the chain-rule factor.
For large T, a_h>=1/2, and log(1-z)<=-z gives

    0<r_h<=exp(-2*k_h*t)<=exp(-2*t),
    |dot r_h|=2*k_h*r_h/a_h<=4*k_h*exp(-2*t).

The two corrective sums in the variance derivative from (1) therefore have
absolute magnitude at most

    C*(t^2+t^3)*exp(-2*t)/T^3.

Since D>0, division by 3*D*t^2/T^3 is legitimate on I_T. Thus

    sum_h [dot B_h*(1-r_h)-B_h*dot r_h]
      = 3*D*t^2/T^3 * (1+epsilon_2(T,t)),
    sup_{t in I_T}|epsilon_2(T,t)|
      <= C*[log(T)/T+(1+log(T))*T^(-14/5)] -> 0.          (2)

The exponent 14/5 is twice the lower window endpoint 7/5. Zero noise
in either coordinate is permitted: only the sum D must be positive.

## 4. Uniform deterministic-derivative estimate

For fixed k_h>=1, the Taylor estimate of log(1-k_h*t/T) yields

    (2T-1)*log(a_h)=-2*k_h*t+O((t+t^2)/T).

The remainder tends to zero uniformly on I_T. Hence

    A_h*dot r_h=-2*k_h*A_h*exp(-2*k_h*t)
                *[1+O((t+t^2)/T)].

When L=mu, both terms have k_h=1 and combine into amplitude A0.
When L>mu, the flat term has A_mu=A0>0 and the stiff term divided
by 2*A0*exp(-2*t) is bounded in magnitude by

    C*exp(-2*(L/mu-1)*t)
      <= C*T^(-(14/5)*(L/mu-1)) -> 0.

If y0=0 this term vanishes identically. Consequently in both cases

    sum_h A_h*dot r_h=-2*A0*exp(-2*t)*(1+epsilon_1(T,t)),
    sup_{t in I_T}|epsilon_1(T,t)| -> 0.                  (3)

The equal-curvature case cannot be handled by discarding the stiff
initial displacement; that is why A0 is defined piecewise.

## 5. Stationarity and the constant

Every minimizer is eventually interior. Equations (1)-(3), evaluated there,
give

    2*A0*exp(-2*t_T)*(1+epsilon_1)
       = 3*D*t_T^2/T^3*(1+epsilon_2).

Both error factors are positive for large T. Taking logarithms is valid,
and uniform smallness makes log(1+epsilon_j)=o(1). Therefore

    2*t_T=3*log(T)-2*log(t_T)+log(2*A0/(3*D))+o(1).

C001 gives log(t_T)=log(log(T))+log(3/2)+o(1). Substitution yields (R),
because

    (1/2)*log(2*A0/(3*D))-log(3/2)
      = (1/2)*log(8*A0/(27*D)).

All log arguments are positive. The constant combines a derivative factor
3 with the squared leading step factor (3/2)^2; balancing function values
instead of derivatives would give a different, unjustified log-log term.

## Checks and limits

The 48 Decimal cases in logs/second_order_numerics.json test stationary
derivatives and slow convergence, not global minimality or asymptotic proof.
The finite exact derivative-identity checks are recorded separately.
Formal arithmetic checking, if available, concerns only the displayed
rational factor identity; it does not certify this analytic proof.

[Lemma Euclidean spherical condenser of arXiv:2606.23025, 'Spectral-Capacitary Bounds for Homological Recovery from Reflected Brownian Trajectories'] Let
\(0 < \varepsilon < R\), and let \(u\) be the capacitary
potential of the spherical condenser
\(\left( \overline{B(0,\varepsilon)},\,\mathbb{R}^{d}\backslash B(0,R) \right)\),
that is, the harmonic function on
\(B(0,R)\backslash\overline{B(0,\varepsilon)}\) with \(u = 1\)
on \(\partial B(0,\varepsilon)\) and \(u = 0\) on
\(\partial B(0,R)\). Then

\[\int_{B(0,R)\backslash B(0,\varepsilon)}^{}|\nabla u|^{2}\, dx = \left\{ \begin{matrix}
\frac{2\pi}{\log(R/\varepsilon)}, & d = 2, \\
\frac{(d - 2)\,\omega_{d - 1}}{\varepsilon^{2 - d} - R^{2 - d}}, & d \geq 3.
\end{matrix} \right.\ \]

In particular, for \(d \geq 3\) the Newtonian capacity of a
ball is
\(cap\left( B(0,\varepsilon) \right) = (d - 2)\,\omega_{d - 1}\,\varepsilon^{d - 2}\),
and for every fixed \(R > 0\) one has, as
\(\varepsilon \rightarrow 0\),
\(\int|\nabla u|^{2}\, dx = (d - 2)\,\omega_{d - 1}\,\varepsilon^{d - 2}\left( 1 + O\left( (\varepsilon/R)^{d - 2} \right) \right)\)
for \(d \geq 3\) and
\(2\pi/\log(1/\varepsilon)\,\left( 1 + O\left( 1/\log(1/\varepsilon) \right) \right)\)
for \(d = 2\).

[Proposition prop:diffusion_mixed_tail of arXiv:2609.01576, '\normalfont Pointwise Majorization for sub-Weibull and Mixed Tail Processes with Applicati'] Under Assumptions (ass:diffusion_coefficients of the paper) and
(ass:diffusion_index_class of the paper), $d_1$ and $d_2$ are finite-valued
pseudo-metrics and $(\cF,d_1+d_2)$ is separable. The map
$(\omega,f)\mapsto Z_\tau(f)(\omega)$ is jointly measurable, its sample
paths are almost surely $(d_1+d_2)$-continuous, and $Z_\tau(0)=0$ almost
surely. Moreover, for every $f,h\in\cF$ and $u\ge0$,
\begin{align}
\PP_\pi\cbr{
|Z_\tau(f)-Z_\tau(h)|
>
u\,d_1(f,h)+\sqrt u\,d_2(f,h)
}
\le2e^{-u}.

\end{align}
Consequently, $\cbr{Z_\tau(f)}_{f\in\cF}$ is an anchored two-metric
mixed-tail process of orders $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)=(1,2)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Its two end directions are +e1 and -e1 because f(k)/abs(k) tends to zero, but neither tail lies eventually in any finite horizontal strip because f is unbounded at both ends. [Thm 5 of arXiv:2604.11489, '2604.11489'] Fix $0< \delta< \frac{1}{2}$. Let $\{X_n, n\ge 1\}$ be a sequence of independent and identically distributed random variables with a common nonuniform distribution $\{p_i, i\ge 1\}$ satisfying $\ee|\ln p(X_1)|^{2+\delta} < \infty$. Assume that there exists an integer valued function $K(n)$ such that,
\beq
K(n)\le n^{\frac{1}{2}-\delta},\ \ n^{\frac{1}{2}+\delta}\ln n\sum_{i=K(n)}^{\infty}p_i \leq C
\ \ \text{and}\ \ -n^{\frac{1}{2}+\delta}\sum_{i=K(n)}^{\infty}p_i\ln p_i\leq C,
\deq
then we have
\beq
\sup\limits_x\left|\pp\left(\frac{\sqrt{n}(\hat H_n-H)}{\sigma}<x\right)-\Phi(x)\right|
 \leq Cn^{-\frac{\delta}{2}},
\deq
where $\Phi$ denotes the standard normal distribution function and $\sigma^2=\Var(\ln p(X_1))$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Cor cornegbin of arXiv:2605.01878, '\Large Random trade timing and power-law tails in realized prices'] Maintain the assumptions on $X$ and the type distribution, and Assumption (asshol of the paper), in Proposition (propmain of the paper), but replace the conditional geometric law of $T$ by the negative-binomial law (equation eqnbinom of the paper). Suppose that there exists $\alpha>0$ such that $r_D(A(-\alpha))=-\log(1-p_1)$. Then $\alpha$ is unique, and there exist constants $0<C_1\le C_2<\infty$ such that, for all sufficiently large $y$,
\[
\widetilde M_n C_1 \le (\log y)^{-(n-1)}y^\alpha \mathbb{P}(P_T>y) \le \widetilde M_n C_2,
\]
where $\widetilde M_n>0$ is given by
\[
\widetilde M_n = q_1\left(\frac{p_1}{1-p_1}\right)^{n}\bigl(-\,y_{p}' B^{(1)}(-\alpha)x_{p}\bigr)^{-n}(y_p'x_p)^{n-1}(w_0'x_p)(y_p'1_N),
\]
with $B(s) = e^{\log(1-p_{1})I+A(s)}$, $B^{(1)}(s) = \frac{d}{ds}B(s)$, and $x_p$, $y_p$ right and left eigenvectors of $B(-\alpha)$ associated with the unit eigenvalue. In particular, the negative-binomial IIM has the same Pareto exponent as the geometric IIM, but for $n\ge 2$ the tail carries a logarithmic correction of order $n-1$.

body: The heat (diffusion) equation is the parabolic PDE u_t = k Laplacian(u) with diffusivity k > 0, modelling the diffusion of heat or concentration. On all of R^n, initial data f evolves by convolution with the heat kernel (4 pi k t)^(-n/2) exp(-|x|^2 / (4kt)), the Gaussian fundamental solution; the equation smooths arbitrary initial data at once (infinite propagation speed) and satisfies the maximum principle: on a space-time cylinder a solution attains its maximum and minimum on the parabolic boundary (the initial time or the lateral boundary).

body:
[Thm algebraic_local_sewing of arXiv:2606.21049, '\textsc{Locality of rough path lifts}'] \begin{enumerate*}[label=(\roman*)]
\item  There exists a linear map \(\Lambda \colon E[0,1] \to \mathbb{R}^{\triangle}\)
such that $\delta_2\Lambda=\mathbbm 1$ and $\Lambda$ is strongly local (cf.\ (rem:timeloc of the paper)) in the sense that, for all \(\tau\geq 0\) and $(s,t) \in \triangle$ such that \(t+\tau\leq 1\) and \(\Xi,\Xi'\in E [0,1] \) such that $\Xi_{a,b,c} = \Xi'_{a+\tau,b+\tau,c+\tau}$ for all $(a,b,c)\in\triangle^3[s,t]$,
one has
\(
(\Lambda\Xi)_{s,t}=(\Lambda\Xi')_{s+\tau,t+\tau}
\).
\medskip
\\

\item  There exists a linear map \(\Lambda \colon F[0,1] \to \mathbb{R}^{\triangle}
\)
such that $\delta_2\Lambda =\mathbbm 1$ 
and which is local in the sense that, for all $(s,t) \in \triangle$ and \(\Xi,\Xi'\in F [0,1] \) such that $\Xi|_{\triangle^3[s,t]}= \Xi'|_{\triangle^3[s,t]}$,
one has
\(
(\Lambda\Xi)_{s,t}=(\Lambda\Xi')_{s,t}
\).
\medskip
\\

\item  There does not exist a map
\(
\Lambda \colon F[0,1] \to \mathbb{R}^{\triangle}
\)
such that 
\(
\delta_2\Lambda=\mathbbm 1
\)
and which is time translation--invariant in the sense of (def:weak_sewing of the paper)(pt:time_translation_def of the paper).

In fact, there exists \(\Xi\in F[0,1]\) which is translation-invariant in the sense that $\Xi_{s,u,t} = \Xi_{s+\tau,u+\tau,t+\tau}$ for all $(s,u,t),(s+\tau,u+\tau,t+\tau)\in\triangle^3$
and for which there exists no \(A\in \mathbb{R}^{\triangle}\) with $\delta_2A=\Xi$ and which is translation-invariant in the sense that \(A_{s,t} = A_{s+\tau,t+\tau}\) for all $(s,t),(s+\tau,t+\tau)\in\triangle$.
\end{enumerate*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm algebraic_local_sewing of arXiv:2606.21049

body:
[Theorem thm:certified-music-landscape of arXiv:2609.03264, 'Certified Spherical MUSIC for 3D Localization under Adversarial Subspace Perturbations'] Let
		$$
		X=\{\bm{x}_1,\dots,\bm{x}_s\},\quad s\ge 2
		$$
		be an  $s$-point cloud and 
			\[
	\delta_X:=\min_{j\ne k}\abs{\bm{x}_j-\bm{x}_k}
	\]
	be its minimum separation.  
	

Suppose		$$
		\bigcup_{j=1}^s\overline{B_\rho(\bm{x}_j)}
		\subset B_1(\bm{0})\subset\mathbb R^3, \quad\rho\le \frac{\delta_X}{2}.	$$
 Define two  fundamental dimensionless constants:
		\begin{eqnarray}
		
	\gamma:=\rho{\kappa}, \qquad \mu_X
		:=
		\frac{9}{2}
		\frac{s^{2/3}}{\kappa\delta_X}<1
\end{eqnarray}
with  $\kappa>0$ 
	and four other derived constants
	\begin{eqnarray}
\nu_X
		&:=&
	 \frac{64c_\nu^2}{27}
\frac{\mu_X^2}{s} = 	48c_\nu^2
		\frac{s^{1/3}}{\kappa^2\delta_X^2} ,\qquad c_\nu:=\sup_{t>0}\left|t\cos t -\sin t\right|/t \,\,\approx 1.0631,\\
				\nonumber	C_1&:=&
			\frac{\gamma^2}{9}
			+
			\nu_X+\sqrt{1+\nu_X}
			\sqrt{				\left(
				\frac{1}{3}+\frac{\gamma^2}{10}
				\right)^2
				+
				4\nu_X
			}\\
			\nonumber 	C_2&:=& \frac{8}{15} \gamma^2 +6\nu_X+ \frac{2\mu_X}{1-\mu_X} C_1.
\end{eqnarray}
Let \(\widetilde{\mathcal U}\) be any $s$-dimensional subspace of $\mathcal{H}$ 
satisfying
\[
    \|P_{\widetilde{\mathcal U}}-P_{\mathcal U_X}\|_2 =\varepsilon_{\rm sub}.
\]
Assume 
\begin{eqnarray}
 
 A_\gamma& :=& \frac{b_\gamma-\mu_X-\nu_X}{1-\mu_X}>0,\quad b_\gamma
		:=
		1-\sup_{t\ge \gamma} \operatorname{sinc}^2(t)
 \end{eqnarray}
			and 	\begin{eqnarray} C_2<\frac23,\qquad
\varepsilon_{\rm sub}
	< \min\left\{ \frac{\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\gamma
            \left(\frac23-C_2\right)
       }{1+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\gamma \left(\frac{2}{\sqrt5}+\frac23\right)},\,\,   \sin\left(
        \frac12\arcsin\sqrt{A_\gamma}.
    \right)\right\},
		\end{eqnarray}
		Define
\begin{eqnarray}

\tau_0:=\varepsilon_{\rm sub}^2,\qquad    \tau_1
    :=
    \sin^2\left(
        \arcsin\sqrt{A_\gamma}-\arcsin\varepsilon_{\rm sub}
    \right).
\end{eqnarray}
Then  \(\tau_0<\tau_1\) and:

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item
For every \(j\),
\begin{eqnarray}

    C_0^-\kappa^2I_3
    \preceq
    \nabla^2\widetilde q({\bm z})
    \preceq
    C_0^+\kappa^2I_3,
    \qquad
    {\bm z}\in\overline{B_\rho({\bm x}_j)}
\end{eqnarray}
where
\begin{eqnarray}
C^-_0&:=&	\frac23
			-
			C_2
			-
			\left(
			\frac{2}{\sqrt5}+\frac23\right) 	\varepsilon_{\rm sub} > \frac{
            \frac23-C_2
       }{1+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\gamma \left(\frac{2}{\sqrt5}+\frac23\right)},\\
    C_0^+
    &:=&\frac23+C_2
      +\left(\frac2{\sqrt5}+\frac23\right)\varepsilon_{\rm sub}.
\end{eqnarray}

\item
Every point outside the certified wells satisfies
\begin{eqnarray}
    \widetilde q({\bm z})\geq\tau_1,
    \qquad
    {\bm z}\in
    B_1(0)\setminus
    \bigcup_{j=1}^sB_\rho({\bm x}_j).
\end{eqnarray}
\item
Each \(B_\rho({\bm x}_j)\) contains exactly one critical point
\(\widetilde{\bm x}_j\), which is its unique minimizer, and
\begin{eqnarray}

    |\widetilde{\bm x}_j-{\bm x}_j|   \le  \frac{2\varepsilon_{\rm sub}}{\sqrt3\,C_0^-\kappa}<\rho,
    \qquad
    \widetilde q(\widetilde{\bm x}_j)\leq\tau_0.
\end{eqnarray}

\item 	If the  fill distance of  a finite set \(G\subset B_1(0)\)
	\begin{equation}
	
		{\rm mesh}_{B_1}(G)
		:=
		\sup_{{\bm z}\in B_1(0)}
		\min_{\bm g\in G}|{\bm z}-\bm g|
	\end{equation}
 satisfies
\[
    \operatorname{mesh}_{B_1}(G)
    <
    \min\left\{
        \rho- \frac{2\varepsilon_{\rm sub}}{\sqrt3\,C_0^-\kappa},
        \,
        \frac{\sqrt3}{2\kappa}(\tau_1-\tau_0)
    \right\},
\]
then
\[
    G_{\tau_1}:=
    \{{\bm g}\in G:\widetilde q({\bm g})<\tau_1\}
\]
contains at least one point in every certified well and no point
outside their union.

\item
For
\[
    0<h\leq
    \frac{2}{(C_0^-+C_0^+)\kappa^2}
    =
    \frac{3}{2\kappa^2},
\]
the gradient map
\[
    T_h({\bm z}):={\bm z}-h\nabla\widetilde q({\bm z})
\]
maps every \(\overline{B_\rho({\bm x}_j)}\) into \(B_\rho({\bm x}_j)\) and is
a contraction there with factor
\[
    r_h:=1-hC_0^-\kappa^2<1.
\]
Consequently, every accepted initialization converges geometrically
to the unique minimizer in its well. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

support contained in $[n]$.

let $Q_{i,k} = \mathbb{P}(A_i = k)$.
For all $k \in [n]$, let 
$a_k = |\{i \in [m] \colon A_i = k\}|$. Then $\overline{a}=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ is a   generalised multinomial  random variable with parameter~$Q$.

body: [Lm Ohlin \cite{Ohlin} of arXiv:2607.08869, 'Inequalities for convex functions of random points inside and on the boundary of convex bo'] Let $X$ and $Y$ be integrable random variables with $\mathbb E X = \mathbb E Y$. If their distribution functions $F_X$ and $F_Y$ cross exactly once, with $F_X \leqslant F_Y$ to the left of the crossing point and $F_X \geqslant F_Y$ to the right, then $\mathbb E f(X) \leqslant \mathbb E f(Y)$ for every convex $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem AdDecomp of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] Let $S(\gamma)$ be the signature of $\gamma$.
Then one has
\begin{equation}
S(\gamma)=\big(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\int_{0<t_{1}<\cdots<t_{n}<1}e^{x_{t_{1}}{\rm ad}_{{\rm e}_{1}}}({\rm e}_{2})\otimes\cdots\otimes e^{x_{t_{n}}{\rm ad}_{{\rm e}_{1}}}({\rm e}_{2})dy_{t_{1}}\cdots dy_{t_{n}}\big)\otimes e^{{\rm e}_{1}},
\end{equation}
where 
\[
e^{{\rm ad}_{\xi}}(\eta)\triangleq\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}\frac{({\rm ad}_{\xi})^{m}}{m!}(\eta).
\]
In particular, 
\[
\tilde{L}(\gamma)\triangleq\log\big(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\int_{0<t_{1}<\cdots<t_{n}<1}e^{x_{t_{1}}{\rm ad}_{{\rm e}_{1}}}({\rm e}_{2})\otimes\cdots\otimes e^{x_{t_{n}}{\rm ad}_{{\rm e}_{1}}}({\rm e}_{2})dy_{t_{1}}\cdots dy_{t_{n}}\big)
\]
is a Lie series.

body: In probability theory, in particular in the study of stochastic processes, a stopping time is a specific type of "random time": a random variable whose value is interpreted as the time at which a given stochastic process exhibits a certain behavior of interest. A stopping time is often defined by a stopping rule, a mechanism for deciding whether to continue or stop a process on the basis of the present position and past events, and which will almost always lead to a decision to stop at some finite time.

(Thm 1.1) Let 1 <= k < n and E a k-dimensional subspace of R^n. There are gamma_1,...,gamma_n in [0,1] with sum gamma_i = k (depending only on E) such that for all bounded probability densities f_1,...,f_n on R, the product f(x) = prod f_i(x_i) satisfies ||pi_E(f)||_{L^inf(E)} <= min{ (n/(n-k))^{(n-k)/2}, 2^{k/2} } prod ||f_i||_inf^{gamma_i}, where pi_E(f)(x) = int_{E^perp + x} f is the marginal density on E. In particular, if X has independent coordinates with densities <= 1, then P_E X has density <= min{ (n/(n-k))^{(n-k)/2}, 2^{k/2} } <= 2^{k/2}. For the uniform cube the first bound is attained when n-k divides n and 2^{k/2} when k <= n/2; for those k the cube is the worst case over all such X and all E.

Assumes: independent coordinates (product density); coordinate densities bounded by 1 (in general the bound carries the weight prod ||f_i||_inf^{gamma_i}); 1 <= k < n

[Prop inv of 231 avoiding permutation of arXiv:2604.23751, 'Large deviation principles for pattern-avoiding permutations, and limit shapes for constra'] If $\sigma$ is a $231$-avoiding permutation then
    \[\inv(\sigma) = \binom{n}{2} - \sum_{x=0}^{n-1} F_\sigma(x).\]
    Therefore,
    \[ \inv(\sigma)
    = \binom{n}{2} - n^2 \int_0^1 f_\sigma(x) \mathrm{d}x 
    = \frac{-n}{2} + 2 n^2 \int_0^1 \varphi_\sigma(x) \mathrm{d}x  .\]
title: Prop inv of 231 avoiding permutation of arXiv:2604.23751

[Cor 2 of arXiv:2608.24552, 'Asymptotic Rounding Laws for Optimal Thresholds in Secretary Problems'] If \(\ell\) is irrational, then every sufficiently large
continued-fraction convergent \(p/q\) of \(\ell\) gives the unique optimal
threshold \(p\) for \(\mathcal F_q\). If \(\ell=a/b\) is rational in lowest
terms, then, for every sufficiently large \(m\), the threshold \(am\) is the
unique optimal threshold for \(\mathcal F_{bm}\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop 11 of arXiv:2509.01797, 'Relation between Wick powers and excursion clusters of the 2D GFF'] The composition law $\odot$ is associative,
but it is not commutative.
The monomial sequence $(x^{n})_{n\geq 0}$
is the unique left-neutral and the unique right-neutral element for $\odot$.
Endowed with this composition law, $(\mathtt{S}_{\R},\odot)$ forms a group,
and in particular every element of $\mathtt{S}_{\R}$ has an inverse for $\odot$.

body:
[Corollary 2 of arXiv:2604.10051, 'Ergodicity of the voter model with dynamic anti-voter bonds'] Let~$(\xi_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a Feller process on a metric space~$\mathcal C$. Let~$I$ be an index set and, for each~$i \in I$, let~$(Z^i_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a Markov chain with countable state space~$\mathcal S_i$ and~$Q$-matrix satisfying~$\eqref{eq_q_finite}$. Suppose that, for every~$i \in I$, the processes~$(\xi_t)$ and~$(Z^i_t)$ are dual with respect to~$D_i:\mathcal C \times \mathcal S_i \to [0,\infty)$, which satisfies conditions~$(i)$ and~$(ii)$ of Lemma~\ref{lemma_uniqueness_1} for all~$z \in \mathcal S_i$.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(1)] If, in addition, the family of functions~$\xi \mapsto D_i(\xi,z)$, indexed by~$i \in I$ and~$z \in \mathcal S_i$, is measure-determining (that is, two probability measures coincide whenever their integrals against all these functions coincide), then every measure in~$\mathscr{I}_\infty$ is stationary for~$(\xi_t)_t$.
    \item[(2)] If, furthermore, the metric space~$\mathcal C$ is compact and~$(\xi_t)_t$ admits a unique stationary measure, then $(\xi_t)_t$ is ergodic.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 2 of arXiv:2604.10051

[Theorem thm:intro-scaling-limit of arXiv:2512.20338, 'Up-down chains and scaling limits: \\ application to permuton- and graphon-valued diffusio'] Let $ \iota  $ denote the map from $   \mathbb S   $ to $  E  $.
Suppose that \orange{$ \{  X _n \}_{ n \ge 0 } $ are up-down chains satisfying}
Assumptions (assumption finite state spaces of the paper) and (assumption:commutation of the paper)
(or more generally, \orange{Markov chains satisfying (assumption finite state spaces of the paper)--(assumption intertwining of the paper)}), and that (assumption state space approximation of the paper)--(assumption continuous density functions are limits of the paper) are satisfied.
Suppose also that $  c _n \to \infty $ and
that the distributions of $  \iota (  X _n( 0 ) ) $ converge to $\mu$, a distribution on $  E  $.

Then the following statements hold.
 \begin{enumerate}
   \item
    There exists a Feller process $  F  $ in $  E  $ with initial distribution $ \mu $
    such that the convergence
	$$
		\big(
			 \iota (  X _n (  \lfloor   c _n t  \rfloor  ) )
		\big)_{ t \ge 0 }
			\Longrightarrow
        		\big(
        				 F ( t )
        		\big)_{ t \ge 0 }
	$$
	holds in distribution in the Skorokhod space $ D([0,\infty), E )$.
	\item 
	The transition semigroup $ \{   \mathcal T  (t) \}_{ t \ge 0 } $ of $  F  $ admits the diagonal description
	$$
		  \mathcal T  (t) h_s^o 
			= 
				e^{ -t  c _{ k-1 } } 
				h_s^o
			,
				\qquad
				s \in   \mathbb S  _k, 
				\,
				k \ge 0,
				\,
				t \ge 0
			.
	$$ 

  \item The process $  F $ is ergodic with a unique stationary measure $M$,
	which is the weak limit of the stationary measures $M_n$ of $X_n$
	(or, more precisely, of their push-forwards on $  E $).
 \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:intro-scaling-limit of arXiv:2512.20338

[Proposition 6 (Quasi-multiplicativity) of arXiv:2605.30030, 'Critical exponents for planar random-cluster model with cluster-weight~$q=4$'] For every~$1\leq r\leq \rho\leq R$, 
\begin{align}
    \pi_1(r,R)&\asymp \pi_1(r,\rho)\pi_1(\rho,R), \\
     \pi_2(r,R)&\asymp \pi_2(r,\rho)\pi_2(\rho,R), \\
 \Delta(r,R)&\asymp  \Delta(r,\rho)\Delta(\rho,R). 

\end{align}
Moreover,~$\pi_1(R) \asymp \pi_1(1,R)$,~$\pi_2(R) \asymp \pi_2(1,R)$ and~$\Delta(R) \asymp \Delta(1,R)$.

Finally, there exists $c > 0$ such that, for any $1\leq r \leq R$, $\pi_2(r,R)  \leq \pi_1(r,R)^2\leq \pi_1(r,R)\big(\frac{r}R\big)^c$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 7 (Early-time tracking from a zero output layer) of arXiv:2608.24007, '2608.24007'] Initialize
\[
    a_j(0)=0,
    \qquad
    w_j(0)=\varepsilon {\omega_j^0},
    \qquad
    {\omega_j^0}\in\mathbb S^{d-1}.
\]
Let $(\bar u_j,{\bar\omega_j})$ solve the self-selected teacher-only system
\[
    \dot{\bar u}_j
    =
    \Phi({\bar\omega_j}),
    \qquad
    {\dot{\bar\omega}_j}
    =
    \tanh(\bar u_j)
    \nabla_{\mathbb S^{d-1}}\Phi({\bar\omega_j}),
\]
with
\[
    (\bar u_j(0),{\bar\omega_j(0)})
    =
    (0,{\omega_j^0}).
\]
For every fixed $T<\infty$, there are constants $L_T<\infty$ and
$\varepsilon_T>0$ such that, for $0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_T$,
\[
    \sup_{0\leq t\leq T}
    \left(
        |u_j(t)-\bar u_j(t)|
        +
        \|{\omega_j(t)-\bar\omega_j(t)}\|_2
    \right)
    \leq
    L_Tm\varepsilon^2,
\]
where
\[
    a_j(t)=\varepsilon\sinh(u_j(t)),
    \qquad
    {\omega_j(t)}=\frac{w_j(t)}{\|w_j(t)\|_2}.
\]

body:
Let $T: X \to X$ be a continuous map of a COMPACT metric space and let $M(X, T)$ be the (nonempty, by Krylov-Bogolyubov) set of $T$-invariant Borel probability measures. Then
$$h_{top}(T) = \sup\{ h_\mu(T) : \mu \in M(X, T) \},$$
and the supremum may be restricted to ERGODIC invariant measures. The inequality $h_\mu(T) \le h_{top}(T)$ for every invariant $\mu$ is Goodwyn's half; the existence, for every $c < h_{top}(T)$, of an invariant $\mu$ with $h_\mu(T) > c$ is the Dinaburg-Goodman half (Misiurewicz's proof below). Both sides may be $+\infty$. A measure attaining the supremum is a measure of maximal entropy; it need NOT exist for a general continuous $T$ (there are continuous maps, and even homeomorphisms, with $h_{top} < \infty$ and no measure of maximal entropy), but it exists whenever $\mu \mapsto h_\mu(T)$ is upper semicontinuous, e.g. for expansive maps and for $C^\infty$ maps of compact manifolds. The variational principle is the case $\varphi = 0$ of the variational principle for topological pressure, $P(T, \varphi) = \sup_\mu \{ h_\mu(T) + \int \varphi\,d\mu \}$.

WHERE IT FAILS OR NEEDS CARE. (1) Non-compact $X$: the statement depends on which notion of topological entropy is used; for the Bowen metric entropy on a non-compact space the supremum over invariant measures can be strictly smaller, and $M(X,T)$ may be empty (translation on $\mathbb{R}$). (2) The supremum need not be a maximum (see above). (3) Restricting to a non-invariant measure is meaningless: $h_\mu(T)$ is defined only for invariant $\mu$. (4) The principle relates ENTROPY to entropy; it does not say that a generic point has orbit-growth rate $h_{top}$, nor that the measure of maximal entropy is unique (uniqueness = intrinsic ergodicity, a much stronger property that holds e.g. for topologically mixing shifts of finite type but fails for many systems).
X is a compact metric space
T is continuous
the supremum is over T-invariant Borel probability measures; it need not be attained

[Definition 19 (Skorohod integral) of arXiv:2606.08776, 'Approximation of certain stochastic integrals with anticipating integrands'] \
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
            \item We let $\dom(\delta)$ be the set of $u \in L_2([0,1]\times\Omega)$ such that
            \[
                  \left|\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{1} D_tF u_tdt\right|^2 \leq C_u \E |F|^2
            \]
            for all $F \in \mathbb{D}_{1,2}$, where $C_u\ge 0$ is a constant depending on $u$.

            \item If $u\in \dom(\delta)$, then $\delta(u)$ is the element of $L_2(\Omega)$ characterized by
            \[
            \mathbb{E}(F\delta(u)) = \mathbb{E}\int_0^1 (D_t F) u_t dt \sptext{1}{for}{1} F \in \mathbb{D}_{1,2}.
            \]
           
      \end{enumerate}
The operator $\delta$ is called the {\normalfont divergence operator} and the divergence $\delta(u)$ is called the {\it Skorohod integral} of the process $u$, denoted by
      \[
            \delta(u) = \int_0^1 u_t \delta W_t.
      \]
title: Skorohod integral

body: [Proposition 117 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mf A$ be an HTM, $\mf B$ be a topological submonoid of $\mf A$. Suppose $f(k)\in\mf B$ for all $k\in K$. If $\sm{\mf B}{k\in K}{f(k)}$, then $\sm{\mf A}{k\in K}{f(k)}$ and $\sum^{\mf A}_{k\in K} f(k) = \sum^{\mf B}_{k\in K}f(k)$. If $\sm{\mf A}{k\in K}{f(k)}$ and $\sum^{\mf A}_{k\in K} f(k)$ belongs to $\mf B$, then $\sm{\mf B}{k\in K}{f(k)}$.

[Definition def:weighted-bipartite-graph of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] Let $G=(I,J,M)$ be a weighted bipartite graph, where
\[
M\in\mathbb R^{I\times J}.
\]
We call $I$ the left vertex set and $J$ the right vertex set. We declare that
\begin{align}
  
(i,j) \in I\times J \mbox{ is an edge}
\quad
\Leftrightarrow
\quad
M_{ij}\ne0
\end{align}
and, when $(i,j)$ is an edge, its weight is $M_{ij}$.
With this convention, we define the support of $G$ to be the set of edges
\[
E_M:=\{(i,j)\in I\times J:M_{ij}\ne0\}.
\]
By the support graph of $G$ we mean the unweighted bipartite graph $(I,J,E_M)$.
title: Weighted bipartite graph and support graph

[Theorem 1 (Uniform Laplace principle of bridges) of arXiv:2511.14757, 'A weak convergence approach to the large deviations of the dynamic Schr\"odinger problem'] Under Assumptions \ref{ass:b-sigma-local-properties}--\ref{ass:log-gradient-convergence}, for any compact set $K \Subset D$,
    \begin{equation}
        \lim_{\eta \downarrow 0} \sup_{x,y \in K} \left|-\eta \log \bE\left[\exp - \frac{1}{\eta} F(X^{\eta, xy}) \right] - \inf_{\varphi \in \calC_1} \left[F(\varphi) + I_B^{xy}(\varphi)\right]\right| = 0,
    \end{equation}
    where $X^{\eta, xy}$ is given by the dynamics \ref{eq:R-SDE-main-results}, conditioned on starting in $x$ at $t=0$ and ending in $y$ at $t=1$.
    The good rate function $I_B$ is given by
    \[ I_B(\varphi) = \inf_{\nu \in U^{xy}_\varphi} \frac{1}{2} \int_0^1 |\nu(t)|^2 dt,\]
    where $U^{xy}_\varphi \coloneq \{\nu \in L^2([0,1]:\bR^d): \varphi(\cdot) = \int_0^{\cdot} (b(s, \varphi(s) + \sigma(s, \varphi(s))\nu_s)ds\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm mr3 of arXiv:2411.06571, 'Moment-based approach for two erratic KPZ scaling limits'] Let $\eta$ be a space-time white noise on $\Bbb R_+\times\Bbb R$, and let $\eta^\epsilon:= \varphi_\epsilon *\eta$ where the convolution is in space only, and where $  \varphi_\epsilon (y):= \epsilon^{-1} \varphi(\epsilon^{-1}y)$ for some fixed smooth even mollifier $\varphi \in C_c^\infty(\Bbb R)$ such that $\|\varphi\|_{L^2(\Bbb R)}<1$ (equivalently $\sup_{x\in \Bbb R} \varphi*\varphi(x)<1$). 
    
    Denote by $\mathcal Z^\epsilon_{s,t}(x,y)$ the propagators given by the It\^o-Walsh solution of the SPDE \begin{equation}\tag{aSHE}\partial_t u(t,y) = \frac12 \partial_y^2 u(t,y) + u(t,y)\eta^\epsilon(t,y) + \epsilon^{1/2}\partial_y\big(u(t,y)\eta^\epsilon(t,y)\big),\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\; t\ge 0,y\in\Bbb R.
    \end{equation}
Then $\mathcal Z^\epsilon$ converges in law as $\epsilon\to 0$ to the family of propagators given by the It\^o-Walsh solution of $$\partial_t \mathcal U(t,y) = \tfrac12 \partial_y^2 \mathcal U(t,y) +  \gamma_{\mathrm{ext}} \mathcal U(t,y) \xi(t,y), \;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\gamma_{\mathrm{ext}}^2 := \int_\mathbb R\frac{\varphi*\varphi(a)}{1- \varphi*\varphi(a)}da.$$ Here $\xi$ is another space-time white noise. The convergence is in the sense of finite-dimensional laws $(\mathcal Z^\epsilon_{s_1,t_1},...,\mathcal Z^\epsilon_{s_m,t_m}),$ where each coordinate has the topology of $\mathcal M(\Bbb R^2)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

   We call $Y$ the {\em reduced center} of the weighted blowup.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Conservation, explicit coupling reduction, exact law comparison or spectral calculation Result: The exactly solvable one-particle sector provides a dilute check. On the cycle of length L, waking a particle runs rate-one simple random walk until an independent Exp(lambda) sleep time. For $\theta=2\pi/L$, its first Fourier multiplier is $r_L=\lambda/(\lambda+1-\cos\theta)$. After k wakes, a point start has cosine expectation $r_L^k$, whereas stationarity is uniform with expectation zero. Hence TV is at least $r_L^k/2$, and reaching TV<=1/4 requires $k\ge\log2/(-\log r_L)\sim\lambda\log2\,L^2/(2\pi^2)$. Check: The multiplier is the integral of lambda*exp(-lambda*t)*exp(-(1-cos(theta))*t) over positive t. Equivalently it is the resolvent eigenvalue of the walk generator. For zero particles the state space is a singleton and mixing takes zero steps. Obstruction: One particle has density tending to zero, so this does not prove the positive-fixed-density lower bound or the supercritical upper bound. Neither is claimed solved.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0387-slow-to-one-step-mixing-transition-of-the-arw-wake-chain

NOVELTY: UNCHECKED (priority is not assessed; the argument is an elementary finite-chain escape calculation).
Status: proof (unaudited).

## Statement

Let A be a nonempty finite vertex subset of a connected infinite graph of maximum degree at most three. A discrete-time simple random walk killed on exit from A has, at every vertex x in A, exponentially bounded survival and diagonal kernel. In particular, for any fixed finite comb rectangle A, constants c>0 and beta>0, an inequality p_{2 floor(n/2)}^A(x,x)>=c n^(-beta) cannot hold for every sufficiently large integer n.

This shows that the unrestricted-time statement of source Lemma 4.8, (4.68), arXiv:2609.05343v1, p.28, needs an upper-time restriction. It does not refute a lower bound on a bounded macroscopic window, and does not refute source Lemma 4.9 or the accepted conditional I0012 theorem.

## Proof

For each y in A, connectedness to the infinite exterior gives a simple path from y to a vertex outside A, stopping on its first exit. No vertex before the exit is repeated, so its length is at most |A|. Fix J=|A|+1. The walk follows this path with probability at least 3^(-J), because every step has probability at least 1/3 and at most J steps are used. Thus, with epsilon=3^(-J)>0,

    inf_{y in A} P_y(tau_{A^c}<=J) >= epsilon.

At each deterministic multiple of J, conditional on survival to that time, the current vertex is in A and the same escape estimate applies. The ordinary Markov property therefore gives

    P_x(tau_{A^c}>kJ) <= (1-epsilon)^k

for every nonnegative integer k. At any time t,

    p_t^A(x,x) = P_x(X_t=x, tau_{A^c}>t)/deg(x)
               <= (1-epsilon)^(floor(t/J)),

since deg(x)>=1. With t=2 floor(n/2), this upper bound is exponentially small in n. For any c,beta>0 it is eventually smaller than c n^(-beta), because an exponential dominates every positive power. This contradicts the claimed all-time polynomial lower bound in a fixed box.

For a fixed environment of the finite-tooth comb and fixed N,b, the rectangle in (4.68) is finite and satisfies all these hypotheses. At gamma=1/3 its purported exponent is beta=2/3. Therefore the contradiction applies exactly to the displayed critical specialization, as well as to every gamma in (0,1).

## Scope

No gamma>1/3 requirement is inferred. The defect is time/box quantification, rather than a critical exponent. A corrected range such as n<=constant*N^(4/(1+gamma)) is compatible with exponential late-time decay; its constant and containment must be proved separately.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:7eb1c3de89ebff6970233fcf997d1d41bd3bff3ab5fc125d337afc30020b63f3","revision_digest":"sha256:95e3936149632e097b28dee910cbf0a9dfaff7c6071f4e630385724cda5abed3","source_id":"own-work:w664:I0012-U1:v1","source_revision":"version 1; w667 and w668 PASS; novelty UNCHECKED","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

Let $\Theta=(0,v)$ with $v$ defined above.
Then, for every $t\in[0,T]$, $X_t\in W^{1,p}_\Theta$ and the directional derivative $D_\Theta X$ admits a c\`adl\`ag version satisfying
\begin{equation}
D_\Theta X_t
=\int_0^t \partial_x b(s,X_s)\,D_\Theta X_s\,\dd s
+\int_0^t\int_{\R_0}\kappa(s)\,v(s,z)\,N(\dd s,\dd z),\qquad D_\Theta X_0=0.

CANDIDATE COUNTEREXAMPLE, AUTHOR CHECKED; NOVELTY UNVERIFIED. Rational Weyl clock-shift pairs converge strongly to an irrational rotation pair, whereas every selected sum is nilpotent and the limiting sum has Haar-circle Brown measure. Strong convergence includes all fixed matrix-coefficient amplifications. The matrices may share a Haar conjugation and are dependent. This addresses the literal unrestricted family question, not independent-entry or free-limit subclasses. The parent supplied matrix amplification and trace/norm proof arguments, so its review does not independently certify the amended proof.
Irrational limiting rotation parameter
Primitive rational approximants
Dependent random matrix family is permitted
Fang-Jiang-Lin-Xu Theorem12.2 supplies the limiting Brown measure

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:801cd94b91360bdb765994754a3f10b2d444419f51d59d171f1a48582d878714","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/80/801cd94b91360bdb765994754a3f10b2d444419f51d59d171f1a48582d878714.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:782e3ef5bbb0faf01a685eb529732c0d77bfa3843ab0c5c3cb1c854a588ec117","bundle_entry_key":"brown-measure-counter","bundle_id":"population.probability-candidate-obstructions-and-spatial-lemmas-005","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"codex-probability-1000-20h-20260906/bundle_005.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.free:candidate-strong-convergence-does-not-force-brown-measure","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# P0189: candidate counterexample to Brown-measure continuity under strong convergence

Status: complete candidate construction, checked by the author; no independent review and no novelty claim. This addresses the literal general conjecture in van Handel, *The strong convergence phenomenon*, arXiv2507.00346v2 (11 February2026), Section6.9, pp.69-70. It does not address the narrower conjectures for independent Ginibre matrices or free limiting families.

Primary source for the question: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.00346 . Primary source for the established limiting Brown measure: Fang, Jiang, Lin and Xu, *On generalized universal irrational rotation algebras and the operator u+v*, https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.4771 , Theorem12.2. Its introduction also states simplicity and uniqueness of trace of the irrational rotation algebra. These literature theorems are dependencies, not results proved here.

## Finite matrices

Fix an irrational theta in(0,1). Choose reduced rational approximants p_j/q_j tending to theta, with q_j tending to infinity. Let omega_j=exp(2*pi*i*p_j/q_j). On the standard basis indexed by k modulo q_j define

\[
 U_j e_k=\omega_j^k e_k,\qquad
 S_j e_k=e_{k-1},\qquad
 V_j=e^{\pi i/q_j}S_j.
\]

Then U_j and V_j are unitary and satisfy

\[
 V_jU_j=\omega_jU_jV_j,\qquad U_j^{q_j}=I,\qquad V_j^{q_j}=-I.
\]

Put A_j=U_j+V_j. Its characteristic polynomial is exactly z^{q_j}. Indeed, in the determinant of zI-U_j-V_j only the all-diagonal permutation and the full cyclic permutation contribute (for q_j>=2). The former contributes

\[
 \prod_{k=0}^{q_j-1}(z-\omega_j^k)=z^{q_j}-1,
\]

because omega_j is primitive. The latter contributes minus the product of the cyclic weights, namely -exp(pi*i)=+1. Thus det(zI-A_j)=z^{q_j}. Cayley-Hamilton gives A_j^{q_j}=0, and every empirical eigenvalue distribution is delta_0.

An equivalent algebraic check is the root-of-unity binomial identity (U_j+V_j)^{q_j}=U_j^{q_j}+V_j^{q_j}=0. The determinant calculation supplies the conclusion without relying on that identity.

## Strong convergence of the pair

Let A_theta be the universal unital irrational rotation C*-algebra generated by unitaries u,v satisfying vu=exp(2*pi*i*theta)uv. This algebra is simple and has a unique faithful tracial state tau, as recalled in the cited primary paper.

Consider the norm quotient

\[
 \mathcal Q=\prod_j M_{q_j}(\mathbb C)\big/\bigoplus_j M_{q_j}(\mathbb C),
\]

where the direct sum consists of sequences whose operator norms tend to zero. The classes of (U_j) and (V_j) are unitaries and satisfy the irrational relation exactly, since omega_j tends to exp(2*pi*i*theta). Universality therefore gives a unital *-homomorphism A_theta to Q. Simplicity makes it injective, hence isometric. Since the quotient norm of a bounded sequence is its limsup norm, for every noncommutative *-polynomial P,

\[
 \limsup_j\|P(U_j,V_j,U_j^*,V_j^*)\|
 =\|P(u,v,u^*,v^*)\|.
\]

The same argument applies to every subsequence. If the norms failed to converge to the displayed value, a subsequence uniformly separated from that value would contradict the same limsup identity. Consequently the pair converges strongly.

The normalized traces also converge to tau. Using the commutation relation, every fixed word is a phase times U_j^a V_j^b. When b is a fixed nonzero integer and j is large, the shift has no diagonal entries, so its trace is zero. If b=0 and a is fixed nonzero, the geometric sum of omega_j^{ak} is zero for all q_j>|a|. The identity word has trace one, and phases converge. These are exactly the canonical irrational-rotation trace values. Thus both norm and tracial versions of strong convergence are satisfied, with a faithful limiting trace.

In particular A_j converges strongly, including all *-polynomials in A_j alone, to a=u+v.

The survey Definition 1.1 also allows fixed finite-dimensional matrix coefficients. For each fixed D, amplify the quotient homomorphism to M_D(A_theta). An injective *-homomorphism is completely isometric, and M_D(Q) identifies with the quotient of the product of M_D(M_qj) by norm-null sequences. Therefore the same limsup identity and subsequence argument apply to every D-by-D matrix-valued *-polynomial. The identification follows entrywise in finite D: a matrix sequence tends to zero in norm exactly when all its entries do, and the quotient norm is the limsup of the block-matrix norms. Thus the precise matrix-coefficient definition is covered.

A separate norm-convergence proof uses the trace computation above for the lower bound and needs no appeal to simplicity. Write P_j for a fixed matrix-valued polynomial and P for its limit. For every positive integer m, with normalized traces on the matrix factors,
\[
 \|P_j\|\ge\big[(\mathrm{tr}_D\otimes\mathrm{tr}_{q_j})((P_j^*P_j)^m)\big]^{1/(2m)}.
\]
Taking the lower limit in j and then m to infinity gives liminf ||P_j|| >= ||P||, because the limiting trace tr_D tensor tau is faithful. Complete contractivity of the universal quotient homomorphism gives limsup ||P_j|| <= ||P||. This independently proves the required full norm convergence. The parent suggested these two explicit extensions during its first bounded review on 6 September 2026; the author checked and incorporated them. The remaining review and novelty status is pending.

## The Brown-measure mismatch

The cited Theorem12.2 states that the Brown measure of u+v, in the tracial von Neumann algebra generated by the irrational rotation pair, is Haar probability measure on the unit circle. It is therefore different from delta_0. The finite empirical measures are all delta_0 and do not converge to the Brown measure of a, despite strong convergence.

The same example also prevents a universal lower spectral-radius conclusion: every A_j has spectral radius zero, whereas the source Theorem11.1 gives spectrum of u+v equal to the closed unit disk and hence spectral radius one.

To make the matrices random rather than deterministic, take Haar unitary Q_j and replace the pair by (Q_j U_j Q_j*,Q_j V_j Q_j*). For every outcome, norms, normalized traces, nilpotency, and eigenvalue distributions are unchanged. This supplies genuinely random families satisfying the same convergence. The two members are dependent; the construction does not claim otherwise. Equivalently, the single random matrix Q_j A_j Q_j* is already a counterexample for a one-variable polynomial.

## Optional realization in every integer dimension

The dimensions q_j suffice for a counterexample along a sequence tending to infinity. If an all-integer-dimension formulation is required, take consecutive continued-fraction denominators, which are coprime. For each sufficiently large N, choose the largest j with q_j*q_{j+1}<=N. The elementary coin theorem gives N=a*q_j+b*q_{j+1} for nonnegative integers a,b. Define the N-dimensional pair as the block direct sum of a copies of the j-th pair and b copies of the(j+1)-st pair. Both block dimensions tend to infinity as N does. Polynomial norms are the maximum of their block norms, traces are convex combinations of block traces, and the sum remains nilpotent. Thus the same counterexample exists with dimension exactly N for every sufficiently large integer N.

## Scope and remaining checks

This is a candidate refutation of the survey's literal implication from arbitrary strong convergence to empirical Brown-measure convergence. It is not a refutation for independent-entry ensembles, free limits, or holomorphic polynomials in independent Ginibre matrices. Yi Han's June2026 paper, arXiv2606.01664, claims the latter case and is compatible with this construction.

Load-bearing obligations are the precise survey scope, the primitive-root determinant sign, isometry of the quotient homomorphism, faithful-trace interpretation, and the cited Brown-measure theorem. All are explicit here. It remains possible that the construction or the general failure of continuity is already known; current-literature novelty is unverified. No validator, numerical eigenvalue computation, or brain ingestion is treated as proof review.
