[Theorem thm:from-r-to-l of arXiv:2411.06195, 'Restrictions of some reinforced processes to subgraphs'] Let the graph $G$ be finite and take $0\le l\le r$. We endow the subdivided graph $G_r$
  with i.i.d.\ edge weights $W_e>0$, $e\in E_r$. Consider the family $W^{(l)}$ of
  corresponding random weights
from Theorem (thm:vrjp-on-G-r-pos-rec of the paper), all realized on the same probability space
with expectation operator ${\mathbb E}$. We abbreviate
$C_\alpha:=2^{-\alpha}\Gamma(\tfrac12-\alpha)/\sqrt{\pi}$
for $0\le\alpha<\frac12$ and ${c_2}:=\gamma+\log 2=1.27036\ldots$, where 
\begin{align}
  
  \gamma=-\int_0^\infty e^{-t}\log t\, dt=0.57721\ldots
\end{align}
denotes the Euler Mascheroni constant. 
For all $\bar e\in E_l$ and $e'\in E_r$, one has
  \begin{align}
    
    {\mathbb E}[(W^{(l)}_{\bar e})^\alpha]
    &\le (2^{-\alpha})^{r-l}{\mathbb E}[W_{e'}^\alpha]
    &\hspace{-1cm}\text{ for } \alpha\in[0,1],\\
    
    {\mathbb E}[(W^{(l)}_{\bar e})^\alpha]
     &\le \frac{1}{C_\alpha}\min_{m\in\{l,\ldots,r\}}\left(C_\alpha 
       (2^{-\alpha})^{r-m}{\mathbb E}[W_{e'}^\alpha]\right)^{2^{m-l}}
     &\hspace{-1cm}\text{ for } \alpha\in[0,\tfrac12),
    \\
      
    {\mathbb E}[\log W^{(l)}_{\bar e}]
    &\le \min_{m\in\{l,\ldots,r\}}
      2^{m-l}\left({\mathbb E}[\log W_{e'}]-(r-m)\log 2+{c_2}\right)-{c_2}.
  \end{align}
  Set $m_0:=r-2-\lfloor\alpha^{-1}\log_2(C_\alpha {\mathbb E}[W_{e'}^\alpha])\rfloor$
  and $m_1:=r-2-\lfloor(\log 2)^{-1}({\mathbb E}[\log W_{e'}]+{c_2})\rfloor$.
  If $m_0\in\{l,\ldots,r\}$, a minimizer in (equation eq:combined-alpha of the paper)
  is given by $m=m_0$. If $m_0<l$ or $m_0>r$, it is given by
  $m=l$ or $m=r$, respectively. The analogous statement holds for $m_1$
  with (equation eq:combined-alpha of the paper) replaced by (equation eq:combined-log of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Decay of the effective weights by restriction

body:
[Definition defextgraph of arXiv:2605.10617, 'Logarithmic scaling of selective sweep curves:\\ from tents to houses'] Let $f\in \mathcal D_I$.
  \begin{enumerate}[a)]
    \item 
      The  {\em extended graph} of $f$ is defined as
      $$
        \mathbb G(f)
         := \bigcup_{t\in I}\big(\{t\} \times [\min(f(t-),f(t)), \max(f(t-),f(t))]\big).
      $$
      Thus, in  words from~[K23], the extended graph  ``contains the graph together with the straight lines connecting the two ends of a jump discontinuity''.
    \item 
      A~{\em parametric representation} of (the extended graph of) $f$ is a mapping $\phi$ which maps $[0,1]$ onto $\mathbb G(f)$ and for which $u \mapsto \phi(u)$ is increasing with respect to the total order $\preceq$ on $\mathbb G(f)$ defined by
      $$
        (t_1,x_1)\preceq (t_2,x_2) :\Longleftrightarrow t_1\le t_2
          \mbox{ and } \left(t_1=t_2 \Rightarrow |x_1 - f(t_1-)| \le |x_2 - f(t_1-)|\right).
      $$
  \end{enumerate}
title: Definition defextgraph of arXiv:2605.10617

[Lem description-of-Pinv of arXiv:2607.05097, 'Asymptotics of Lyapunov Exponents and Phase Transitions for Fluids with Degenerate Forcing'] Let $\mu \in P_{\mathrm{inv}}$ be ergodic. Then there is some $z_0$ such that $\mu(\{z = z_0\}) = 1$. Furthermore, there is some $i$ such that $\mu(\{v \in \operatorname{Span}(\{V_j \mid \Re \lambda_j = \Re \lambda_i\})\}) = 1$, where $V_1,\dots,V_k$ are the generalized eigenspaces of $A(z_0)$ corresponding to the eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k$. Additionally, we have
$$\int \Lambda(z,v)d\mu(z,v) = \Re \lambda_i \,.$$
In particular, if $\mu(\{P_0(z)v = 0\}) = 0$ then
$$\int \Lambda(z,v)d\mu(z,v) = \lambda(A(z_0)) \,.$$
title: Lem description-of-Pinv of arXiv:2607.05097

[Prop mySp-vs-mySp-gl of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] The inclusion of equivariantly cofibrant orthogonal $G$-spectra induces a fully faithful global functor ${\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}\to{\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{gl}$. Moreover, its underlying ${\vphantom{\textup{t}}\smash{\textup{Orb}}}$-functor admits a right adjoint which is levelwise a localization at the equivariant weak equivalences.
    \begin{proof}
        Lemma~(lemma:equiv-spectra-vs-gl-spectra of the paper) already shows that ${\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}\to{\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{gl}$ is fully faithful and admits a pointwise right adjoint which is a localization at the equivariant weak equivalences.
        To complete the proof, it remains to verify the Beck--Chevalley condition for the pointwise right adjoints with respect to \emph{injective} homomorphisms. As the right adjoints are localizations, this amounts to saying that $\alpha^*\colon{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_\text{$G'$-gl}\to{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_\text{$G$-gl}$ sends $G'$-equivariant weak equivalences to $G$-equivariant ones for any injective $\alpha\colon G\to G'$. This is however immediate from Proposition~(prop:i!-left-Quillen-equiv-sp of the paper).
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop mySp-vs-mySp-gl of arXiv:2608.28504

Let V be a finite set, X a random subset, q(A) = P(A subset of X) and p(B) = P(X = B). Then q(A) = sum over B containing A of p(B), and p(B) = sum over A containing B of (-1)^|A minus B| q(A). [Defn of arXiv:2608.29914, 'Fixed points in abstract provability structures'] For each one-variable meet APS term $\triangle v$, we define $\mu(\triangle)\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$ recursively as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\mu(v)=\infty$, 
    \item $\mu(\Box\triangle)=\mu(\triangle)+1$, 
    \item $\mu(\boxtimes\triangle)=0$, 
    \item $\mu(\triangle_0\land\triangle_1) = \min\{\mu(\triangle_0), \mu(\triangle_1)\}$.
\end{enumerate}
Here, $\infty+1=\infty$.
title: Unnumbered defn of arXiv:2608.29914, 'Fixed points in abstract provability structures'

[Proposition prop:vertical of arXiv:2608.24830, 'Motion helps the contact process: survival below\\ the percolation threshold on Poisson Br'] There is $c=c(d)>0$ such that the following holds. Let $\eta>0$, $\epsilon\in(0,1)$,
$0<\Delta\le\Lambda$ and $W>0$, and let $\ell$ satisfy
\begin{equation}

  \Delta\ge c_0\ell^2(\epsilon/3)^{-4/\kappa}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\eta\ell^d\ge1 .
\end{equation}
Let $\mathsf G\ge\max\{c_1\Delta^{1/2}(\epsilon/3)^{-1/d},\,12r\}$, and put $K'=W+2\mathsf G$ and
$K=K'+2\mathsf G$. Let
$B\subseteq Q_W\times[0,t_0]$ and $B'\subseteq Q_W\times[t_0+\Delta,\Lambda]$, and let $A,A'$ be
increasing events determined by $B$ and $B'$ in the sense of (lem:Hprops of the paper). Then
\begin{equation}

  \mathbb{P}_\eta(A\cap A')\le\mathbb{P}_\eta(A)\Big[\mathbb{P}_{\eta(1+\epsilon)}(A')
  +\Gamma\,e^{-c\eta\epsilon^2\Delta^{d/2}}\Big]
  +\Big(\tfrac K\ell\Big)^de^{-c\eta\epsilon^2\ell^d}
  +C_d\,\eta\,(K+\Lambda^{1/2})^de^{-\mathsf G^2/(8d\Lambda)} ,
\end{equation}
where $\Gamma=C_d\,\epsilon^{-d}\big(K\Delta^{-1/2}\big)^{d(d+1)}$ is the factor
(equation eq:Gamma of the paper) of (thm:mixingupper of the paper) at mixing parameter $\epsilon/3$.

body:
[Pro Pro1 of arXiv:2606.22183, 'Expected loss of quasi-arithmetic means of exchangeable random variables'] The following assertions hold.
\begin{itemize}
 \item[(i)] If $n\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\{1\}$ and $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n$ are exchangeable random variables, then the $(n-1)$-dimensional random vectors
 \[
   (\xi_2,\xi_3,\ldots,\xi_n), \quad (\xi_1,\xi_3,\ldots,\xi_n),\quad \ldots\quad (\xi_1,\xi_2,\ldots,\xi_{n-1})
 \]
 have the same distributions.
 
\item[(ii)]
If $h:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a Borel measurable function and $(\xi_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence of exchangeable random variables, then $(h(\xi_n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is also exchangeable.

\item[(iii)]
If $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n\in\mathbb{R}$, and $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n$ are exchangeable random variables,
 then, for each permutation $\sigma$ of $(1,\ldots,n)$, we have $\sum_{i=1}^n \lambda_{\sigma(i)} \xi_i$ has the same distribution as $\sum_{i=1}^n \lambda_i \xi_i$.
\end{itemize}

[Corollary 8 of arXiv:2609.01402, 'Parabolic Lie algebroid connections on parabolic principal bundles over curves'] Let $X$ be a compact connected Riemann surface and $G$ a connected complex reductive affine algebraic group.
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite group of biholomorphisms of $X$ and $E_{G}$ a $\Gamma$--equivariant holomorphic 
principal $G$--bundle on $X$ such that $E_G$ is not semistable. Take any $\Gamma$--equivariant holomorphic Lie 
algebroid $(V,\, \phi)$ on $X$ that satisfies the condition that the anchor map
$\phi$ not surjective. Then the Harder--Narasimhan reduction $E_{P}\,\subset\, 
E_{G}$ of $E_G$ admits a $\Gamma$--equivariant holomorphic $(V,\, \phi)$--connection.

[Definition def-weak-strong-uniqueness-intro of arXiv:2411.04500, '\LARGE Probabilistic Approaches to The Energy Equality in Forced Surface Quasi-Geostrophic'] We say that
	$\mathcal{C}_0 \subset \mathbb{X}_{\alpha,\beta}$ is a weak-strong uniqueness class of (equation PDE-SQG of the paper) if for every control $g \in L^2([0,T];L^2(\mathbb{T}^2))$, the following holds:   for arbitrary two weak solutions (see Definition (def-weak-solution-skeleton-equation of the paper) later on)  $\theta_1, \theta_2 $  of the skeleton equation (equation PDE-SQG of the paper) with the same initial data $\theta_1(0)=\theta_2(0)$ and the same control $ g $, we have $\theta_1=\theta_2$ in $ \mathbb{X}_{\alpha,\beta}$ as long as $\theta_1\in\mathcal{C}_0$ and  $\theta_2$ satisfies the $ H^{\alpha-2\beta}$-energy inequality: for every $ t\in[0,T], $
	$$
	\frac{1}{2}\|\theta_2(t)\|_{H^{\alpha-2\beta}(\mathbb{T}^2)}^2+\int_0^t\|\theta_2(s)\|_{H^{2\alpha-2\beta}(\mathbb{T}^2)}^2 \,\mathrm{d}s \leqslant \frac{1}{2}\left\|\theta_2(0)\right\|_{H^{\alpha-2\beta}(\mathbb{T}^2)}^2+\int_0^t\langle\Lambda^{2\alpha-2\beta} \theta_2, g\rangle \,\mathrm{d}s.
	$$
	Furthermore, the $\mathcal{I}$-closure of $\mathcal{C}_0$ is defined by
	\begin{equation*}
			\overline{\mathcal{C}_0}^{\mathcal{I}}:=\Big\{\theta \in \mathbb{X}_{\alpha,\beta}: \text{there exists a sequence }\{ \theta^{(n)} \} \subset \mathcal{C}_0, \, \text{such that } \theta^{(n)} \rightarrow \theta \text{ in } \mathbb{X}_{\alpha,\beta}, \, \mathcal{I}\big(\theta^{(n)}\big) \rightarrow \mathcal{I}(\theta)\Big\}.
	\end{equation*}

	\left|\mathbb E[S_{m,i}(t)\mid\xi_0]-c_{m,i}\right|\le C(m,i)e^{-t},

	\begin{equation}
	|a_m(t,F)-b_m(F)|\le C(m,F)e^{-t}.
	\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:2nd-order-score of arXiv:2607.04514, 'Boundary-layer asymptotics for Gaussian-smoothed singular measures'] Let \(A>0\) and assume (ass:standing of the paper) with \(r\geqslant r_0\) (the value of \(r_0\) is
  specified below for each expansion). Then there exists \(\sigma_0 > 0\) such that, for every
  \((y,\sigma)\in\mathcal Y_{A,\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}},\sigma_0}\), \(x=\pi(y)\), \(a = a(y,\sigma)\), it
  holds that
  \begin{align*}
    \boldsymbol{s}_\sigma(y) &= \sigma^{-1}\big(\mathsf S_0(a,x,\sigma) + \sigma \mathsf S_1(a,x,\sigma)
    + \sigma^2\mathscr R_{1,\boldsymbol{s}_\sigma}(a,x,\sigma)\big), \qquad r_0=3 \\
    \mathbf{H}_\sigma(y) &= \sigma^{-2} \big( \mathsf H_0(a,x,\sigma) + \sigma\mathsf H_1(a,x, \sigma)
    + \sigma^2\mathscr R_{1,\mathbf{H}_\sigma}(a,x,\sigma)\big), \qquad r_0=4 \\
    \dot{\boldsymbol{s}}_\sigma(y) &= \sigma^{-2} \big(\dot{\mathsf S}_0 (a,x,\sigma)
    + \sigma \dot{\mathsf S}_1(a,x,\sigma) + \sigma^2\mathscr R_{1,\dot{\boldsymbol{s}}_\sigma}(a,x,\sigma)\big),
    \qquad r_0=4.
  \end{align*}
  Here, the coefficients \(\mathsf S_0\), \(\mathsf S_1\), \(\mathsf H_0\), \(\mathsf H_1\),
  \(\dot{\mathsf S}_0\) and \(\dot{\mathsf S}_1\) are explicitly given in
  (thm:first-order-score of the paper) or by the formulas below and have all mixed derivatives up to order
  \(r-r_0+1\) in the variables \(a\), \(x\), and \(\sigma\), uniformly bounded for
  \(x\in\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}\), \(\|a\| \leqslant A\), and \(0<\sigma\leqslant\sigma_0\).
  \begin{align*}
    \mathsf S_1 (a,x,\sigma)
    &= \mathbf J_{\theta}^\top (a,x,\sigma) \nabla_{\theta}\mathsf L_0 (a,x)
    + \mathbf J_\nu^\top(a,x,\sigma) \nabla_a\mathsf L_1(a,x), \\
    \mathsf H_1 (a,x,\sigma)
    &= \mathbf J_{\theta}^\top \mathrm{D}_{\theta a}^2\mathsf L_0\,\mathbf J_\nu
    + \mathbf J_\nu^\top \mathrm{D}_{a\theta}^2\mathsf L_0\, \mathbf J_{\theta}
    + \mathbf Q_\nu[\nabla_a\mathsf L_0]
    + \mathbf J_\nu^\top \mathrm{D}_a^2\mathsf L_1\,\mathbf J_\nu, \\
    \dot{\mathsf S}_1 (a,x,\sigma) &= \partial_\sigma{\mathsf
    S}_0(a,x,\sigma) - (\mathrm{D}_a\mathsf S_1(a,x,\sigma))[a].
  \end{align*}
  The functions \(\mathscr R_{1,\boldsymbol{s}_\sigma}\), \(\mathscr R_{1,\mathbf{H}_\sigma}\) and \(\mathscr R_{1,\dot{\boldsymbol{s}}_\sigma}\) have
  all mixed derivatives up to order \(r-r_0\) in the variables \(a\), \(x\), and \(\sigma\),

body: [Defn alternativeslippery of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $A\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a closed set. A point $\bm{x}\in A$ is \textbf{upwards (resp.~downwards) slippery} in the $k\geq 1$ first coordinates if there is a sequence of points $\bm{x}^j \in A$, $j \geq 0$, converging to $\bm{x}$, such that each $\bm{x}^j$ is an upper (resp.~lower) extremal point in the first $k$ coordinates, the first $k$ coordinates are strictly increasing (resp.~decreasing) with $j$, and the remaining coordinates are nonincreasing (resp.~nondecreasing) with $j$.

Proof (unaudited), elementary Cover-Wendel application; no novelty claimed. For the balanced-sign, zero-threshold ReLU tree committee with fixed even K, a prescribed label-only partition of patterns among sign-compatible hidden units yields a valid strict classifier with probability q(P,N/K)^K, where q(P,n)=2^{1-P} sum_{r=0}^{min(n-1,P-1)} binom(P-1,r). Thus every load a<2/K is constructively feasible with probability tending to one as N tends to infinity at fixed K. At P=2n this procedure succeeds with probability 2^{-K}; above P/n=2 it fails asymptotically. This is a classical Cover-Wendel consequence, not a novelty claim or a nonzero wide-limit lower bound.
K>=2 even; N=Kn; spherical hidden weights of norm sqrt(n)
Independent standard Gaussian inputs across all patterns and disjoint blocks
Fixed balanced readout signs, zero output threshold, ReLU hidden activation, strict correct output signs with no prescribed positive margin
The partition is chosen using labels only and independently of input values; each pattern goes to one unit of the matching readout sign

[Proposition 4 of arXiv:2608.19396, '\bf Penalisation of Two-Dimensional Brownian Motion'] Let $F$ be an integrable random variable defined on the probability space $(\Omega, 
\mathcal{F}_{\infty}, \mathbf{W}^{(2)})$. There exists a continuous martingale $(M_t(F))_{t \geq 0}$, nonnegative if $F \geq 0$, such that for every $t \geq 0$, and every bounded, $\mathcal{F}_t$-measurable random variable $Y_t$, 
$$\mathbf{W}^{(2)} (F Y_t) = W^{(2)} (M_t^{(2)} (F) Y_t).$$
Moreover, $W^{(2)}$-almost surely, 
$$M_t^{(2)} (F) = \mathbf{W}^{(2)} (G)$$
where for all $\omega \in \Omega$ such that $\omega_0 = 0$, 
$$G ((\omega_u)_{u \geq 0}) 
= F((\omega'_u)_{u \geq 0})$$
where $\omega'_u = X_u$ for $0 \leq u \leq t$, and 
$\omega'_u = X_t + \omega_{u-t}$ for $u \geq t$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:32825b066599e46d6df9c644e277f81e15599a55ca6f97b9e617738468c49f38","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/32/32825b066599e46d6df9c644e277f81e15599a55ca6f97b9e617738468c49f38.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:782e3ef5bbb0faf01a685eb529732c0d77bfa3843ab0c5c3cb1c854a588ec117","bundle_entry_key":"multiplicative-counter","bundle_id":"population.probability-candidate-obstructions-and-spatial-lemmas-005","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"codex-probability-1000-20h-20260906/bundle_005.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.free:candidate-compact-initial-law-no-eventual-log-unimodality","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# P0193: a compactly supported initial law with persistent failure of log-unimodality

Status: complete author-checked candidate counterexample, 2026-09-06. No independent review and no novelty certification. This is a proposed negative answer to Hasebe, Ueda and Wang, *Log-unimodality for free positive multiplicative Brownian motion*, arXiv:2009.13848v1 (29 September 2020), Problem 4.7, PDF page 11. The published reference is Colloquium Mathematicum 169 (2022), 209-226; the archived version used here is the arXiv version. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.13848.

## Claim and normalization

Let \(\nu=(\delta_{1/10}+\delta_{10})/2\). In the source normalization
\[\Sigma_{\sigma_t}(z)=\exp\!\left(\frac t2\frac{z+1}{z-1}\right),\]
the law \(\sigma_t\boxtimes\nu\) is **not log-unimodal for every \(t\ge5\pi\)**. Its initial law has support in the compact interval \([1/10,10]\), so this disproves eventual log-unimodality for arbitrary compactly supported positive initial laws, if the argument and source match survive review.

Log-unimodality means unimodality of the image measure under the logarithm; ordinary unimodality on the positive line is a different claim. The initial law is multiplicatively symmetric but is not log-unimodal. Thus the source theorem for symmetric log-unimodal initial laws does not apply.

## The exact source criterion

Lemma 4.1(3), PDF page 8, says that \(\sigma_t\boxtimes\nu\) is log-unimodal if and only if, for every \(R\in(0,\pi)\), the equation
\[\frac{\sin R}{R}\int_0^\infty\frac{r\xi}{1+r^2\xi^2-2r\xi\cos R}\,d\nu(\xi)=\frac1t\tag{1}\]
has at most two solutions \(r>0\). We use its contrapositive by finding four distinct solutions for one value of \(R\), for each specified \(t\).

Put \(a=\log10\), \(u=\log r\), and
\[K_R(s)=\frac{1}{2(\cosh s-\cos R)},\qquad F_R(u)=\frac{K_R(u-a)+K_R(u+a)}2.\]
The integral in (1) equals \(F_R(u)\), because dividing its integrand's numerator and denominator by \(r\xi\) gives
\[\frac{r\xi}{1+r^2\xi^2-2r\xi\cos R}=\frac1{r\xi+(r\xi)^{-1}-2\cos R}=K_R(\log r+\log\xi).\]
Hence (1) is equivalent to
\[F_R(u)=\frac{R}{t\sin R}.\tag{2}\]
For fixed \(R\in(0,\pi)\), the function \(F_R\) is continuous, positive and even, and tends to zero at both infinities.

## Selecting the level and time

The function \(g(R)=R/\sin R\) is strictly increasing from 1 to infinity on \((0,\pi)\). Indeed
\[g'(R)=\frac{\sin R-R\cos R}{\sin^2R}>0,\]
because the numerator vanishes at zero and has derivative \(R\sin R>0\). Also \(g(\pi/2)=\pi/2\).

For each \(t\ge5\pi\), there is therefore a unique \(R_t\in[\pi/2,\pi)\) with
\[g(R_t)=\frac t{10}.\]
For this choice the right side of (2) is exactly \(1/10\), and \(\cos R_t\le0\).

## Four strict crossings

Since \(\cosh(\log10)=101/20\),
\[F_{R_t}(0)=K_{R_t}(a)=\frac1{2(101/20-\cos R_t)}\le\frac{10}{101}<\frac1{10}.\tag{3}\]
At \(u=a\), the contribution from the centered kernel alone gives
\[F_{R_t}(a)=\frac{K_{R_t}(0)+K_{R_t}(2a)}2\ge\frac1{4(1-\cos R_t)}\ge\frac18>\frac1{10}.\tag{4}\]
The same inequality holds at \(-a\) by evenness. Together with the limits zero at both infinities, (3)-(4) and the intermediate value theorem give a solution of \(F_{R_t}(u)=1/10\) in each of the four disjoint intervals
\[(-\infty,-a),\quad(-a,0),\quad(0,a),\quad(a,\infty).\]
Exponentiation is injective, so these give four distinct positive solutions of (1). Lemma 4.1 proves the claim.

## Separate algebra check in the original variable

The same signs can be checked without hyperbolic functions. At \(r=1\), both atom integrands equal
\[\frac{10}{101-20\cos R}\le\frac{10}{101}<\frac1{10}.\]
At \(r=10\), the atom \(\xi=1/10\) contributes, including its mass one half,
\[\frac1{2(2-2\cos R)}=\frac1{4(1-\cos R)}\ge\frac18.\]
At \(r=1/10\), the atom \(\xi=10\) gives the same lower bound. The integral tends to zero as \(r\downarrow0\) and as \(r\uparrow\infty\). Thus there are crossings in \((0,1/10),(1/10,1),(1,10),(10,\infty)\). These strict rational inequalities include the boundary time \(5\pi\), for which \(R_t=\pi/2\).

## Adversarial checks and limits

The crucial direction is the equivalence in Lemma 4.1, rather than a merely sufficient unimodality condition. Its full statement and proof must remain pinned to the source. The four crossings concern a positive density level, not just multiple extrema in an auxiliary transform. The time is selected separately for each \(t\), as the criterion permits. The upper bound on the central value is uniform for \(R\ge\pi/2\); the lower bound at the two flanks is uniform for all \(R\in(0,\pi)\). No numerical root finder or plot is used as proof. The argument only needs failure for arbitrarily large times; it proves failure for every time in the displayed half-line. It makes no assertion about smaller times or optimality of \(5\pi\).

The large-time mechanism can also be understood from \(K_R(s)\to[4\cosh^2(s/2)]^{-1}\) as \(R\uparrow\pi\): its width does not diverge. A separated two-point mixture of this limiting kernel remains bimodal. This observation motivated the construction; the finite-time rational inequalities above are the proof.

[Bigthm thm:Main Theorem1 of arXiv:2602.07920, 'On the position matrix of single-shelf shuffle and card guessing'] Fix $n\geq 2$ and let $M$ be the position matrix as defined above. Then, 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item  $\operatorname{ker}(M)=\operatorname{span}\{\eta^{(j)}: 1\leq j\leq  \lfloor n/2\rfloor\}$ where $\eta^{(j)}:=e_j-e_{n-j+1}$, where $e_k$ is the standard $k$-th basis vector $e_k(j)=\delta_k(j)$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$. 
    \item For every even integer $0\leq i\leq n-1$, $2^{-i}$ is an eigenvalue of $M$ with multiplicity $1$.
    \item For every even integer $0\leq i\leq n-1$, the vector $\zeta^{(i)}$ is an eigenvector of $M$ with eigenvalue $2^{-i}$, where
    \[
    \zeta^{(i)}(k)= \sum_{t=0}^{i}w_t^{(i)}(k-1)^{\underline{t}}\;,\qquad 1\leq k\leq n
    \]
    and 
    \[w_t^{(i)} =2^{i-t}B_{i-t}\binom{i}{t}(n-t-1)^{\underline{i-t}} = 2^{i-t}B_{i-t}\binom{i}{t}\frac{(n-t-1)!}{(n-i-1)!}\;.\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 39 ({\cite[Theorem~B) of arXiv:2604.08127, 'Asymptotics of Brownian occupation measures \\ with unusually large intersections'] {Weinstein1982/83}}]

    For any $d$ and $q > 1$ such that $d(q-1) < 2q$, there exists a constant $\kappa_{d, q}$ such that
    \[  
    \| \psi \|_{2q} \le \kappa_{d, q} \| \nabla \psi \|_2^{\frac{d(q-1)}{2q}} \| \psi \|_2^{1 - \frac{d(q-1)}{2q}} \quad \text{for all } \psi \in H^1(\mathbb{R}^d).
    \]

[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2511.09280, 'Random Walk conditioned to stay above a non-flat floor: curvature effects'] Let \(\beta\in (0,1/6)\). There are \(c,n_0,\lambda_0, r_0\geq 0\) such that for any \(n\geq n_0\), any \(\lambda_0\leq \lambda\leq n^{\beta}\), and any \(r_0 \sqrt{\lambda}n^{2/3}\leq k \leq n-r_0 \sqrt{\lambda} n^{2/3}\),
    \begin{equation*}
        P\bigl( W_{k}\geq \lambda n^{1/3}\bigr)
        \geq
        e^{-c\lambda^{3/2}}.
    \end{equation*}
    In particular, \(E(W_k) \geq Cn^{1/3}\) for some \(C>0\) uniform over \(n,k\) as above.
title: Lemma 11 of arXiv:2511.09280

[Theorem T:BddMnt of arXiv:2412.03521, 'On ergodic properties of stochastic PDEs'] Let $u$ be the solution to~(equation E:SHE of the paper) starting from a nonnegative rough
  initial data $\mu$, namely, $\mu$ is is a nonnegative Borel measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$
  such that~(equation A:icon of the paper) holds. Suppose that the diffusion coefficient
  $b(x,u)=b(u)$ satisfies the following degenerate condition:
   \begin{equation}
        b(0) = 0\;, \quad \text{and} \quad
        |b(u_2)-b(u_1)|\le L_b |u_2-u_1|.
      \end{equation}
  Moreover, suppose that $4 L_b^2 \Upsilon (0) < 1$, namely,
  condition~(equation E:Upsilon_0 of the paper) holds and $L_b<(2\Upsilon(0))^{-1/2}$. Then
  \begin{align}
    \mathbb{E}\left[u(t,x)^2\right] \le \frac{J_0^2(t,x)}{L_b^2\left[1-4L_b^2\Upsilon(0)\right]}, \quad \text{for all $t\ge 0$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$},
  \end{align}
  where we recall that $J_0 (t,x)$ is defined by~(equation E:def-J0 of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let (X, B, mu) be a Lebesgue probability space and let P be a measurable partition of X (in Rokhlin's sense, so that the quotient is again a Lebesgue space). Then there is a family of conditional probability measures (mu_P) indexed by the elements P of the partition, uniquely determined mu-almost everywhere, such that mu_P is supported on P for almost every P, the map P -> mu_P(A) is measurable for every A in B, and mu(A) = integral of mu_P(A) with respect to the quotient measure. In particular conditional expectations are given by integration against the conditional measures.
The Lebesgue (standard) space hypothesis is essential: regular conditional probabilities can fail to exist on general measure spaces, and the partition must be MEASURABLE in Rokhlin's sense - the partition of the circle into orbits of an irrational rotation is not, and has no disintegration.

body:
[Corollary 71 of arXiv:2609.02850, 'Canonical-row Chern flow on Bott--Samelson towers:\\ realizable-volume models for Schubert'] Let $B$ be the support of one of the ordinary Grothendieck, Lascoux, or
Lascoux-atom polynomials above.  Let $D$ be its maximal total degree and put
\[
 \widehat B_D=\{(\alpha,D-|\alpha|):\alpha\in B\}.
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $\widehat B_D$ is $M$-convex and $B$ is $M^\natural$-convex;
\item $B=\operatorname{conv}(B)\cap\ZZ^n$, and
$\operatorname{conv}(B)$ is an integral generalized polymatroid;
\item each homogeneous layer is the full lattice-point set of the
corresponding integral constant-sum section of $\operatorname{conv}(B)$;
\item if $\alpha\in B$ is not of maximal total degree, then
$\alpha+e_i\in B$ for some $i$;
\item if $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\ZZ^n$, with
$\alpha,\gamma\in B$ and $\alpha\le\beta\le\gamma$ coordinatewise, then
$\beta\in B$.
\end{enumerate}
For ordinary Grothendieck polynomials, parts~\textup{(ii)},
\textup{(iv)}, and~\textup{(v)} prove Conjectures~1.1--1.4 of
M\'esz\'aros--Setiabrata--St.~Dizier \cite{MSSD25}.

body:
[Theorem thm:conv_BM_limit of arXiv:2411.03609, 'Asymptotically optimal Wasserstein couplings for the small-time stable domain of attractio'] Let $\bm{\Sigma}$ be a symmetric non-negative definite matrix on $\mathbb{R}^{d \times d}$ and define $\bm{X}^t=((\bm{\Sigma}\bm{B}_{st}+\bm{S}_{st})/\sqrt{t})_{s\in[0,1]}$ for $t\in(0,1]$ where $(\bm{B}_t)_{t \in [0,1]}$ is a standard Brownian motion on $\mathbb{R}^d$ independent of the pure-jump L\'evy process $\bm{S}$ with Blumenthal--Getoor index~$\beta$ (defined in~(equation eq:BG of the paper)).\\
{\nf(a)} Suppose $\beta\in[0,2)$ and fix any $\beta_* \in (\beta,2]$ when $\bm{S}$ is of infinite variation and $\beta_*=1$ otherwise. Then for any $q>0$ with $\mathds{E}[|\bm{X}_1|^q]<\infty$, we have
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{W}_q\big(\bm{X}^t,\bm{\Sigma}\bm{B}\big)
=\mathcal{O}\big(t^{(q\wedge 1)
    (\min\{1/q,1/\beta_*\}-1/2)}\big), 
    \qquad \text{ as }t \downarrow 0.
\end{align*}
{\normalfont(b)} Pick any $\bm{u}_*\in\mathbb{R}^d_{\bm{0}}$ and define $C_*\coloneqq |\bm{u}_*|^{-1}|\psi_{\bm{S}}(\bm{u}_*)|>0$. Then for all $q \geqslant 1$, we have 
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X}^t_1,\bm{\Sigma}\bm{B}_1)
    \geqslant\frac{C_*}{\sqrt{2}} \sqrt{t}+ \mathcal{O}(t^{3/2}),
\quad\text{as }t \downarrow 0.
\end{align*}
{\normalfont(c)}  Let $\lambda$ be the largest eigenvalue of $\bm{\Sigma}^2$. Suppose there exist $\delta\in[1,2)$ and vectors $(\bm{u}_r)_{r\in(0,\infty)}$ with $|\bm{u}_r|=r$ satisfying $c\coloneqq\inf_{r>1}r^{-\delta}|\psi_{\bm{S}}(\bm{u}_r)|>0$. Then for any $C_*\in(0,ce^{-\lambda/2})$ we have
$\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X}^t_1,\bm{\Sigma}\bm{B}_1) \geqslant(C_*/\sqrt{2})t^{1-\delta/2}$ for all sufficiently small $t>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:conv_BM_limit of arXiv:2411.03609

Let g be the cutoff planar Gaussian increment field, m=6, h=2pi/m, 0<A<1/m, and U,V independent uniforms on [0,h), independent of g. Put f_A(t)=t+A sin(mt), q_A(x)=f_A(g(x)+V)-f_A(V), theta_A=U+q_A. The map f_A is smooth strictly increasing, |q_A-g|<=2A, and q_A has stationary increments. With v=Var[g(x)-g(y)], Var[q_A(x)-q_A(y)]=v+A^2(1-exp(-m^2v/2)). Yet C_m(x-y)=E exp[i m(theta_A(x)-theta_A(y))] tends to J1(mA)^2>0. Its m-fold phase field is stationary with zero one-point mean. Hence even a smooth bounded monotone perturbation with logarithmic variance correct to O(1) can fail algebraic decay of periodic order. This is not a Riesz Gibbs model or a P0321 solution.

Let $f_\hbar : \mathfrak{X} \to \R$ be a family of functions, with compact support, such that 
$1+\Q_\hbar (e^{\lambda f_\hbar}-1)\Q_\hbar \ge \delta > 0$ for $\lambda\in[0,1]$ and as $\hbar\to0$, 
\[
\Sigma(f_\hbar;\Q_\hbar) \to \sigma^2 , \qquad \sup_{\lambda\in[0,1]} \| [e^{\lambda f}, \Q] \| \to 0. 
\]
Then $\Upsilon(f_\hbar;\Q_\hbar) = \Sigma/2 +\underset{\hbar\to0}{o(1)} $ and, in distribution $(\mathcal{G}$ denotes the standard Gaussian distribution on $\R)$ as $\hbar\to0$, 
\[
\X_\hbar(g_\hbar)- \E \X_\hbar(g_\hbar)  \to  \sigma\mathcal{G}.

[Proposition prop:counterexample of arXiv:2507.01236, 'Disintegration theorem for multifunctions, \\ with applications to empirical Wasserstein d'] For fixed irrational $q \in (0, 1)$, consider the metric Polish probability space 
    \[
    \mathfrak{X} := [-1, - (1 - q)] \cup [0, 1 - q],
    \]
    equipped with its Euclidean metric $d$ and uniform probability $\mu$. Then $(\mathfrak{X},d,\mu)$ is not $(n,\epsilon,r)$-disintegrable for any $n \in\mathbb{N}$, $r < 1 - q$, and $\epsilon < 1$. In particular, $(\mathfrak{X},d,\mu)$ is not asympotically distintegrable for any rate.

[Lemma 15 of arXiv:2608.17562, '2608.17562'] Let $(X_{i})_{i \geq 1}$ be a sequence of regularly varying \iid random variables with index $-\alpha < 0$ and common
 distribution function $F$.
 Assume that $\widebar{F}(x) \sim x^{-\alpha}$ as $x$ goes to infinity for some $\alpha > 0$,
 suppose that there exists $\eta >0$ such that $F$ is absolutely continuous on $[\eta, +\infty)$
   with density $f$, and
   let $\beta \in (0,\alpha)$.
   \begin{enumerate}[i)]
   \item
     If there exists
     $\eta ,
     c_F,
     C''>0$ and $\gamma > \beta + 1$ such that
\begin{equation}
  
  \widebar{F}(x) \ge \frac{c_F}{x^{\alpha}},\quad x \ge \eta, 
\end{equation} 
 and 
\begin{align}
  
\bigg\vert \frac{f(x)}{F(x)} - \frac{\alpha}{x^{\alpha + 1}}\bigg\vert \leq \frac{C''}{x^{\gamma}}, \quad x > 0, 
\end{align}
then, we have 
\begin{align}
\nonumber 
\int_\eta^\infty  r^{\beta}F(r)^{n}\bigg\vert\frac{f(r)}{F(r)} - \frac{\alpha}{r^{\alpha + 1}}\bigg\vert \dif r

\le
\frac{C''}{\alpha}
c_{F}^{-({\gamma - \beta - 1})/{\alpha}}
  \Gamma\Big(\frac{\gamma - \beta - 1}{\alpha}\Big)\frac{1}{n^{({\gamma - \beta - 1})/{\alpha}}},
\end{align}
where $\Gamma$ denotes the Gamma function.
\item 
  
  If there exists $\eta , 
  c_F,C_f, \gamma > 0$ such that
\[
\widebar{F}(x) \leq \frac{C_{F}}{x^{\alpha}},\quad x \ge \eta, 
\] 
and
\begin{align}
\vert x^{\alpha + 1}f(x) - \alpha \vert \leq \frac{C_f}{x^{\gamma}},\quad x \geq \eta,  
\end{align}
 then we have 
\begin{align*}
  \int_\eta^\infty r^{\beta}F(r)^{n} & \bigg\vert \frac{f(r)}{F(r)} - \frac{\alpha}{r^{\alpha + 1}}\bigg\vert \dif r

\\
& \leq \frac{C_f}{\alpha}c_F^{
  -1 + {\beta - \gamma }/{\alpha}}\Gamma\Big(1 +\frac{\gamma - \beta}{\alpha}\Big)\frac{1}{n^{1 + ({\gamma - \beta})/{\alpha}}} + C_{F}c_F^{-2 + {\beta}/{\alpha}}\Gamma\Big(2 - \frac{\beta}{\alpha}\Big)\frac{1}{n^{2 - {\beta}/{\alpha}}}. 
\end{align*}
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Lemma 28 (Expected logarithmic Vandermonde of the deformed GUE) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{lem:12}
Let \(G_n\) and \(\widetilde G_n\) be independent \(n\times n\)
GUE matrices, normalized so that
\[
\mathbb E\operatorname{Tr}(G_n^2)=n^2.
\]
Let
\[
D_n=\operatorname{diag}
\bigl(\operatorname{spec}(\widetilde G_n)\bigr),
\qquad
Z_n=wG_n+uD_n,
\]
where \(w\in\mathbb R\) and \(u\geq 0\) are fixed, and
\[
a=\sqrt{w^2+u^2}>0.
\]
If
\[
V_n(\lambda)
=
\prod_{1\leq i<j\leq n}|\lambda_i-\lambda_j|,
\]
then
\[
\mathbb E\log V_n(\operatorname{spec}Z_n)
=
\frac{n^2}{4}\log n
+\frac{n^2}{2}\log a
-\frac{n^2}{8}
+O(n\log n).
\]

The implicit constant may depend on \(w\) and \(u\), but not on \(n\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Expected logarithmic Vandermonde of the deformed GUE

[Theorem thm:ascent of arXiv:2608.24195, '\textbf{A Heterogeneous Mixture of Experts Framework for Interpretable Machine Learning}'] Suppose that:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item the design matrix satisfies $\mathrm{rank}(\boldsymbol{X})=p+1$;
  \item the gating auxiliary function
        \[
          Q_{\mathrm{gate}}(\boldsymbol{\Theta})
          = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \sum_{j=1}^{e}
              \tau_{ij}^{(t)}
              \log g_j(\boldsymbol{x}_i;\boldsymbol{\Theta})
        \]
        is twice continuously differentiable.
\end{enumerate}
Define $\boldsymbol{R}^{(t)} = \boldsymbol{T}^{(t)} - \boldsymbol{G}^{(t)}$ and let
\[
  \widehat{\boldsymbol{B}}^{(t)}
  = (\boldsymbol{X}^\top\boldsymbol{X})^{-1} \boldsymbol{X}^\top \boldsymbol{R}^{(t)}.
\]
Further define
\[
  A_t
  = \bigl\langle
      \nabla_{\boldsymbol{\Theta}} Q_{\mathrm{gate}}(\boldsymbol{\Theta}^{(t)}),\,
      \widehat{\boldsymbol{B}}^{(t)}
    \bigr\rangle
\]
and
\[
  C_t
  = \bigl\langle
      \widehat{\boldsymbol{B}}^{(t)},\,
      \nabla^2_{\boldsymbol{\Theta}} Q_{\mathrm{gate}}(\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Theta}}^{(t)})\,
      \widehat{\boldsymbol{B}}^{(t)}
    \bigr\rangle,
\]
where $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Theta}}^{(t)}
= \boldsymbol{\Theta}^{(t)} + \eta_t\gamma_t\widehat{\boldsymbol{B}}^{(t)}$ for some
$\eta_t\in(0,1)$.

Then:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item $A_t \geq 0$, with strict inequality whenever
        $\boldsymbol{R}^{(t)} \notin \mathrm{Null}(\boldsymbol{P}_{\boldsymbol X})$, where
        $\boldsymbol P_{\boldsymbol X}
         = \boldsymbol X(\boldsymbol X^\top\boldsymbol X)^{-1}\boldsymbol X^\top$;
  \item the update
        $\boldsymbol{\Theta}^{(t+1)}
         = \boldsymbol{\Theta}^{(t)} + \gamma_t\widehat{\boldsymbol B}^{(t)}$
        satisfies
        $Q_{\mathrm{gate}}(\boldsymbol{\Theta}^{(t+1)})
         > Q_{\mathrm{gate}}(\boldsymbol{\Theta}^{(t)})$
        whenever $0 < \gamma_t < 2A_t / |C_t|$.
\end{enumerate}

Method: Influential coordinates of bounded low-degree polynomials exact calculation or structural obstruction Result: For d=1, write f=a0+sum_i a_i*x_i. Evaluating at coordinate signs that align with a_i and at their opposites gives |a0|+sum_i|a_i|<=1. Hence Var(f)=sum_i a_i^2<=max_i|a_i|, so max_i Inf_i(f)=max_i a_i^2>=Var(f)^2. Check: The two extreme cube values are a0 plus/minus sum|a_i|. L2 influence for an affine polynomial is exactly a_i^2. The proof is dimension-free and uses the full range constraint. Obstruction: In higher degree, cancellation among monomials prevents this direct l1-coefficient bound. The argument gives no polynomial-in-d control of the largest influence.

body:
Let H^2 be the Hardy space of the unit circle T, realised as the closed subspace of L^2(T) spanned by the exponentials z^n with n >= 0, and let P: L^2(T) -> H^2 be the orthogonal projection. For a continuous symbol phi in C(T) define the Toeplitz operator T_phi on H^2 by T_phi f = P(phi f); the bound ||T_phi|| <= ||phi||_infinity is immediate from ||P|| = 1, and in fact ||T_phi|| = ||phi||_infinity. Then T_phi is Fredholm if and only if phi has no zero on T, and in that case ind T_phi = - wind(phi), the negative of the winding number of the closed curve phi about the origin. In particular T_phi is invertible if and only if phi is nonvanishing with winding number 0, and a Fredholm Toeplitz operator with continuous symbol is never invertible when its winding number is nonzero, even though it may be injective or surjective.
phi is continuous on the unit circle (for merely bounded measurable symbols the criterion is different)
T_phi acts on the Hardy space H^2 of the circle
the winding number is that of the curve phi about 0, defined because phi is nonvanishing

If phi never vanishes, then 1/phi is continuous and T_{1/phi} T_phi - I and T_phi T_{1/phi} - I are compact, so T_phi is Fredholm by Atkinson's theorem. For the index, note ||T_phi - T_psi|| <= ||phi - psi||_infinity, so phi -> T_phi is norm continuous; the winding number classifies the connected components of the nonvanishing continuous functions on T up to homotopy, and phi with winding number n is homotopic within nonvanishing continuous functions to z^n. Finally T_z is the unilateral shift, with index -1, and T_{z^n} = (T_z)^n has index -n by the composition formula (and for n < 0 it is the adjoint power, of index |n|). body:
[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] For $n\in\mathbb N$, let
\[
\cA_nu=d(J_n*u-u)+q_n(x)u'+a_n(x)u,
\qquad
\cA u=d(J*u-u)+q(x)u'+a(x)u.
\]
Assume that the kernels satisfy common support, normalization and nondegeneracy hypotheses and that $q_n,q\ge q_0>0$.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{(i) Semicontinuity under local convergence.}
Suppose that $J_n\to J$ in $C_c^1(\R)$ with a common compact support, and that $q_n\to q$, $a_n\to a$ locally uniformly in $\R$, with common local bounds. Then $\Lp(\cA)\ge \limsup_{n\to\infty}\Lp(\cA_n)$.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{(ii) Quantitative global stability.}
Let $\cA_1,\cA_2$ satisfy common global structural bounds, including a common bound for the supports and $C^1$ norms of their kernels, the bounds for $q_i,a_i$, and the positive lower bound for $q_i$. There exists $C>0$, depending only on these structural data, such that
\[
\big|\Lp(\cA_1)-\Lp(\cA_2)\big|
\le C\Big(
\|J_1-J_2\|_{L^1(\R)}
+\|q_1-q_2\|_{L^\infty(\R)}
+\|a_1-a_2\|_{L^\infty(\R)}
\Big).
\]
Consequently, under uniform convergence of the coefficients and $C_c^1$ convergence of the kernels with common structural bounds, $\Lp(\cA_n)\to\Lp(\cA)$. If $\phi_n>0$ is a principal eigenfunction normalized by $\phi_n(0)=1$, then every subsequence contains a further subsequence converging in $C^1_{\rm loc}(\R)$ to a positive eigenfunction associated with $\Lp(\cA)$. If $\Lp(\cA)$ is simple in the positive cone, the whole sequence converges to the normalized principal eigenfunction. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 8 of arXiv:2609.02416

[Theorem thm:mixinglower of arXiv:2608.24830, 'Motion helps the contact process: survival below\\ the percolation threshold on Poisson Br'] There are $c_0,c_1,C>0$ depending only on $d$ such that the following holds. Fix $K>\ell>0$
large enough and $\epsilon\in(0,1)$, and tessellate $Q_K$ into subcubes of side $\ell$. Let
$(x_j)_{j\in J}\subset Q_K$ be a configuration with at least $\varrho\ell^d$ points in each
subcube, where $\lfloor\varrho\ell^d\rfloor>0$. Let $\Delta\ge c_0\ell^2\epsilon^{-4/\kappa}$,
let $Y_j$ be the position at time $\Delta$ of a Brownian motion started at $x_j$, these being
independent, and let $K-K'\ge c_1\Delta^{1/2}\epsilon^{-1/d}$. Then $(Y_j)_{j\in J}$ can be
coupled with a Poisson process $\psi$ of intensity $\varrho(1-\epsilon)$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, independent
of the initial configuration, so that
\[
  \psi\cap Q_{K'}\subseteq\{Y_j\}_{j\in J}\quad\text{with probability at least}\quad
  1-\Gamma\exp\{-C\varrho\epsilon^2\Delta^{d/2}\} ,
\]
with $\Gamma$ as in (equation eq:Gamma of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2607.06428, 'Impact of spinning on the early-warning signs in non-Markovian stochastic systems'] Let $(W^H_t)_{t\geq 0}$ be a scalar fractional Brownian motion with Hurst index in $H(0,1)$. Then:
\begin{description}
    \item[{\bf(Long-range dependence)}] If $H>1/2$ then 
    \[ \sum\limits_{n=1}^\infty \E [W^H_1(W^{H}_{n+1}-W^H_n)]=\infty. \]
    \item[{\bf(Short-range dependence)}] If $H<1/2$ then
    \[ \sum\limits_{n=1}^\infty \E [W^H_1(W^{H}_{n+1}-W^H_n)]<\infty. \]
 \item [(Self-similarity)] Let $a>0$. Then 
 \[ (a^H W^H_t)_{t\geq 0} \stackrel{\text{law}}{=}(W^{H}_{at})_{t\geq 0}. \]
 \item [(Time-inversion)] It holds
 \[ (t^{2H}W^H_{1/t})_{t>0}\stackrel{\text{law}}{=}(W^H_t)_{t> 0}.  \]
\item [(Stationarity of the increments)] For all $h>0$ we have 
\[ (W^{H}_{t+h} -W^H_t )_{t\geq 0} \stackrel{\text{law}}{=} W^H_h. \]
\item [(Regularity of the increments)] The scalar fractional Brownian motion has a version which is $\alpha$-H\"older continuous with $\alpha<H$. 
\end{description} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Method: Transform asymptotics, exact special case, coupling reduction or identifiability check Result: For a simultaneously started isolated job, total server effort is d*X*min_i S_i. Unit-rate iid exponential slowdowns give mean effort E X for every d, while identical deterministic slowdowns give d*E X. The corresponding completion times are E X/d and E X. Thus the same replica count can buy latency without extra mean work in one model, or multiply mean work without reducing latency in another. A degree optimizer must account for both the joint slowdown law and load. Check: The minimum of d unit-rate exponentials has rate d, so multiplying its mean by d cancels exactly. For deterministic slowdowns every copy runs the whole job, giving the second formula pathwise. Obstruction: This does not determine the optimum at positive load. Queue-state-dependent staggering can change both effort and latency, and an optimization theorem needs a controlled response function.

Fix d>=2 and unit u, with X uniform on the sphere of radius sqrt(d), target y=X.u, and exponential predictor f=integral a exp(b+p.X) dmu, p=w/sqrt(d). Use original Euclidean gradient flow in a,b,w. For every L>=1 initialize a=b=0 and let p have law (1-L^-2)delta_0+L^-2 Unif(L S^(d-1)). This law is rotation invariant, has initial normalized weight second moment 1 and loss 1/2, and satisfies the invariant b=a^2/2. For F=integral a^2 exp(2b+||p||^2) dmu, the actual local flow has F(0)=F prime(0)=0 and F double-prime(0)=2 exp(L^2) M_d prime(L)^2/(d L^2)>=2 exp(L^2)/d, where M_d(s)=E exp(s X_1). Hence no uniform finite C depending only on d, the stated loss and second moment bounds can ensure F(t)<=C t^2 even on law-dependent neighborhoods of zero. Each initial law has compact support and its own local smooth existence interval; no common interval is asserted. This is not an obstruction for fixed support radius or uniformly exponentially integrable initial weights, and it does not disprove a first-order Gronwall bound or give fixed-time learning rates. [Theorem 29 (Neck detection for surgically modified flows) of arXiv:2608.25971, 'Positive \texorpdfstring{$\tau$}{tau}-bi-Ricci curvature and Mean curvature flow with surg'] Fix $\eps>0$, $k\in\mathbb N$, $L\geq10$, and $\Theta>0$, and choose
the standard replacement with $m_0\geq k+2$.  There exist
  \begin{equation*}
  \eta_{\mathrm{surg}}
  =
  \eta_{\mathrm{surg}}(n,\tau,\alpha,\eps,k,L,\Theta)>0
  \end{equation*}
  and
  \begin{equation*}
  H_{\mathrm{surg}}
  =
  H_{\mathrm{surg}}(n,\tau,\alpha,\eps,k,L,\Theta)<\infty
  \end{equation*}
  with the following property.

  Let $(p,t)$ lie in a surgically modified flow satisfying
  Theorem~\ref{thm:estimates-through-surgery}, assume
  $t\geq\tau_nR^2$, and put $r=(n-1)/H(p,t)$.  
  Suppose that
  \begin{equation*}
  H(p,t)\geq H_{\mathrm{surg}}R^{-1},
  \qquad
  \lambda_1(p,t)\leq\eta_{\mathrm{surg}}H(p,t),
  \end{equation*}
  and that $\mathcal P\bigl(p,t,2(L+2)r,\Theta r^2\bigr)$  
  is surgery-free.  Then $p$ is the center of an $(\eps,k,L)$-neck of
  radius $r$.  If $\Theta\geq L^2$, the rescaled flow is $\eps$-close in
  parabolic $C^k$ norm on the corresponding backward cylinder to a round
  shrinking cylinder whose radius at time zero is one.

body:
[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2609.03962, '$L^p$ isomorphisms for the fractional Laplacian on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and their application'] Let $n\ge2$, $s\in(0,2)$, and $p\in(1,\infty)$.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item[\textup{(i)}] Suppose $f\in L^p(\R^n)^n$ and $g\in V_{s,p}$.
        Then \eqref{intro_stokes} has a solution
        $(u,P)\in\Lambda^{s,p}(\R^n)^n\times W_0^{1,p}(\R^n)$, and the
        solutions in this class are exactly the pairs $(u+\lambda,P+c)$
        with $(\lambda,c)$ in
        \[
          \mathcal N_{s,p}
          :=\big\{(\lambda,c)\in(\mathcal P_{[s-n/p]})^n\times
          \mathcal P_{[1-n/p]}:\ \mathrm{div}\,\lambda=0\big\}.
        \]
        Moreover every solution satisfies
        \[
          \inf_{(\lambda,c)\in\mathcal N_{s,p}}
          \big(\|u-\lambda\|_{\Lambda^{s,p}}+\|P-c\|_{W_0^{1,p}}\big)
          \le C\big(\|f\|_{L^p}+\|g\|_{L^p}+\|\flap g\|_{W_0^{-1,p}}\big).
        \]
  \item[\textup{(ii)}] Suppose $f\in\Lambda^{-1,p}(\R^n)^n$ and
        $g\in\Lambda^{s-2,p}(\R^n)$. Then
        \eqref{intro_stokes}---its two equations holding in
        $\Lambda^{-1,p}(\R^n)^n$ and $\Lambda^{s-2,p}(\R^n)$ respectively,
        with the operators extended along the scale as in
        Section~\ref{sec:appstokes}---has a solution
        $(u,P)\in V_{s,p}^n\times L^p(\R^n)$ if and only if
        \[
          f\perp\mathcal P_{[1-n/p']}\quad\text{and}\quad
          g\perp\mathcal P_{[2-s-n/p']}.
        \]
        In that case the pressure $P$ is unique and the solutions are
        exactly the pairs $(u+\lambda,P)$ with
        $\lambda\in(\mathcal P_{[s-1-n/p]})^n$; thus the solution is
        unique whenever $s-1<n/p$, in particular for all $0<s\le1$, and
        unique up to an additive constant vector when $s-1\ge n/p$.
        Moreover every solution satisfies
        \[
          \|P\|_{L^p}
          +\inf_{\lambda\in(\mathcal P_{[s-1-n/p]})^n}
           \|u-\lambda\|_{\Lambda^{s-1,p}}
          \le C\big(\|f\|_{\Lambda^{-1,p}}+\|g\|_{\Lambda^{s-2,p}}\big).
        \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 4 of arXiv:2609.03962

[Definition def:irreducibility of arXiv:2510.00748, '\bf On irreducible central limit theorems'] Fix $d \ge 2$ and consider the sequence of homogeneous sum $\{ Z_n({\bf X}): n \geq 1\} = \{Z_n \} $ defined in (equation eq:defpolchaos of the paper).  We say that $\{Z_n\}$ is \emph{reducible} if for any $n \in \mathbb{N}$ there exist subsets (``boxes'') $B_1,\ldots,B_{m_n} \subset V_n$ (where $B_i = B_i{(n)}$ may depend on $n$), such that $B_i \cap B_j = \emptyset$ for $i\ne j$ (that is, the boxes $B_i$ are disjoint) and
\begin{enumerate}[label={\rm (\roman*)}]
    \item  $m_n \to \infty \,;$
    \item  $\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{d!\|q_n\|^2} \sum_{i=1}^{m_n} \sigma_n^2(B_i) = 1\,;$
    \item  $\lim_{n\to\infty}  \frac{1}{d!\|q_n\|^2} \max_{i=1,\ldots,m_n} \sigma_n^2(B_i) =0 \,.$ 
\end{enumerate}
We say that $\{Z_n\}$ is \emph{irreducible} if it is not possible to find disjoint sets $B_1,\ldots,B_{m_n} \subset V_n$ such that (redCLTcond1 of the paper), (redCLTcond2 of the paper) and (redCLTcond3 of the paper) hold. If $\{Z_n\}$ is irreducible and verifies (equation eq:CLT of the paper), we say $\{Z_n\}$ {\em verifies an irreducible CLT}.
title: Reducibility/Irreducibility

[Proposition 4 (Existence of the limiting invariant measure) of arXiv:2606.31596, 'The Invariant Measure of Multiscale Markov Chains via Fast Arborescence Factorization'] Let $(V,E,r_N)$ be a strongly connected weighted graph satisfying Assumption \ref{FRL}.
Let $\pi_N$ be the unique invariant measure.
Then $\pi=\lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} \pi_N$ exists and is a probability measure, moreover
\begin{equation} 
	 \pi(x) \,=\, 
	 \lim_{N\to \infty}\frac{r_N\left(\mathcal T^F_x\right)}{r_N\left(\mathcal T^F\right)} \,,\quad x\in V\,.
\end{equation}
This is non-zero when $\mathcal T_x^F\cap\mathcal T^F$ is not empty.
title: Existence of the limiting invariant measure

body: [Thm thm_densityArgmaxRiemannian of arXiv:2608.17463, 'Persistence probabilities of fractional L\'evy fields indexed by hyperbolic space and othe'] Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a homogeneous Riemannian manifold where we choose some point $O\in\mathcal{M}$. Let $(X_\eta)_{\eta\in\mathcal{M}}$ be a real-valued separable stochastic process that has strong stationary increments in the sense of Definition~(def_stationaryIncr of the paper) and that attains its maximum on any compact set a.s.\ at a unique point. Choose any $r'<\inj(O)$ and let $0< r < r'$ be given by Lemma~(lem_ballVolumeBoundsGeneralRiemann of the paper) with $A:=\mathcal{B}_{r'}(O)$. Then for any $0<T\leq r$ the random variable $\tau_{\mkern 1.5mu\overline{\mkern-1.5mu\mathcal{B}\mkern-1.5mu}\mkern 1.5mu_T(O)}$ has a density on $\mathcal{B}_T(O)$ with respect to the Riemannian measure on $\mathcal{M}$.

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2604.12317, 'Weak solution for distribution dependent SDEs driven by L\'{e}vy noise'] Assume \( \alpha \in(1,2],~\gamma \in(1, \alpha),~ p>\frac{d}{\gamma-1} \) and \( q>\frac{\alpha}{\alpha-\gamma} \). For any \( b \in L_{\text{loc}}^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}_{+} ; L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{d}))+ L_{\text{loc}}^{q}(\mathbb{R}_{+} ; L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{d})) \) and \( x_{0} \in \mathbb{R}^{d} \), there exists a weak solution to SDE \eqref{EQ:SDE:101}. That is, there exists a probability space \( (\tilde{\Omega}, \tilde{\mathcal{F}}, \tilde{\P}) \) and a left-continuous right-limited process \( \tilde{X} \) and \( \tilde{L} \) on it, where \( \tilde{L} \) is a \levy~ process with generate triple $(\sigma,\nu,0)$ and  adapted to the completion of the filtration $(\tilde{\mathcal{F}}_{t})_{t\geq 0}$,  \( \tilde{\mathcal{F}}_{t}:=\sigma^{\tilde{\P}}\{\tilde{X}_{s}, \tilde{L}_{s}, s \leq t\} \), such that
\[
\tilde{X}_{t}=x_{0}+\int_{0}^{t} b(s, \tilde{X}_{s}) \mathrm{d} s+\tilde{L}_{t}, \quad \forall t \geq 0.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 5 of arXiv:2604.12317

covariance \eqref{Equation: Inner Product Covariance}. Viewing $\xi$ as

as
\[\xi_\eps(x)=(\xi*p_{\eps/2})(x)=\xi\big(p_{\eps/2}(x-\cdot)\big),\qquad x\in\mbb R^2,\]
where $*$ denotes the convolution.

body: quotient_classes(forms, residual): $i\sim j$ iff for some sign $\sigma$, $\operatorname{qrank}(\text{residual}\cup\{f_i-\sigma f_j\})=\operatorname{qrank}(\text{residual})$. residual_certificate(forms, target): if $|\text{forms}|\le r$ return the trivial certificate; otherwise enumerate all canonical signed-difference directions $f_i-\sigma f_j$ and, for $d=1,\dots,\text{target}$, test every $d$-subset of independent directions, returning the first whose quotient has at most $r=\operatorname{qrank}(\text{forms})$ classes. Notes: Exhaustive over signed-difference residuals of dimension $\le$ target, so a NEGATIVE result (None) is a proof that $d_{\rm geo}>$ target within the signed-difference class -- this is what makes the checker a certificate producer in both directions.

[Definition eq:boundary-residual of arXiv:2608.19050, 'Online Permutation Embedding: \\ Optimal Stopping and Scaling Laws'] For \(q>0\) set
    \begin{equation}
    \mathsf B_q(u)
    :=
    \sqrt q\,u-q\log\pa{1+\frac{u}{\sqrt q}}-1,
    \qquad u\ge0,
    \end{equation}
    and for \(p,q>0\) set
    \begin{align}
    \mathsf P_{p,q}(u)
    &:=
    2\sqrt{pq}\sinh u-(p+q)u
     +(p-q)
     \log\frac{\sqrt p\,e^u+\sqrt q}{\sqrt p+\sqrt q\,e^u},
    \\
    \mathsf I_{p,q}(u)
    &:=
    \frac{p+q+2\sqrt{pq}\cosh u}{2\sqrt{pq}\sinh u}
    \pa{\mathsf P_{p,q}(u)-1},
    \qquad u>0 .
    
    \end{align}

[Lemma lem:regunstablecurrents of arXiv:2602.08591, 'The Yang--Mills measure on compact surfaces as a \\ universal scaling limit of lattice gau'] Let $M$ be a smooth compact manifold and $Y\subset M$ a smooth hypersurface. Assume both $M$ and $Y$ are oriented, then the current of integration $[Y]$ on the submanifold $Y$ belongs to the H\"older--Besov space $\mathcal{C}^{-1-\varepsilon}(M)$ and the Sobolev space $H^{-\frac{1}{2}-\varepsilon}(M)$ , $\forall \varepsilon>0$. 
In particular, the unstable currents $U_a, a\in \text{Crit}(f)_1$ have H\"older regularity
$-1-\varepsilon$ for all $\varepsilon>0$.

body:
[Lem 92 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] We have $\sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha,0) \subseteq \sM^{\BOGP,\sym}(\alpha,0)$.

\begin{proof}
We repeat the most relevant part of Definition~\ref{d:SDE.classification.sym}:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}[h]{r|cccccccc}
\MSRheader\\
\hline
\BOGPdefn{sy}\\
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
    By Lemma~\ref{l:control.problems.Lip.to.Lip.sym}, it suffices to show $\sym(\sM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0)) \subseteq \sM^{\BOGP,\sym}(\alpha,0)$, where $\sM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0)$ is defined in \eqref{e:sM.Lip.0.chaos}.
    Consider any $\mu \in \cM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)$ (recall \eqref{e:cM.Lip.0.chaos}), where $L$ is sufficiently large depending on $\alpha,\epsilon$.
    There exists a sequence of $L$-Lipschitz $((\cA_{N_j})^\circ)_{j\ge 1}$ such that
    \[
    \WERR((\cA_{N_j})^\circ,\mu)
    =
        \max\bigg\{
            \bbW_2\Big(\mu((\cA_{N_j})^\circ), \mu\Big),
            \bbW_2\Big(\mu^{\Ising}((\cA_{N_j})^\circ), \cP(\{\pm 1\})\Big)
        \bigg\} \le \epsilon\,,
    \]
    and the correlation functions $\chi_{(\cA_{N_j})^\circ}$ satisfy $\lim_{j\to\infty} \chi_{(\cA_{N_j})^\circ}(0) = 0$ and
    \beq
        
        \chi_{\cA_{N_j}^\circ}(1-\epsilon) \le \epsilon\,.
    \eeq
    That is, we have the same information about the algorithms $((\cA_{N_j})^\circ)_{j\ge 1}$ as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{l:Lip.in.BOGP} (instantiated with $q_0 = 0$), and in addition the estimate \eqref{e:Lip.in.BOGP.sym.chaos}.
    For $\cA_{N_j}$ the perturbation of $(\cA_{N_j})^\circ$ given by Proposition~\ref{p:wlogable},  the estimate \eqref{e:Lip.in.BOGP.sym.chaos} implies
    \[
        \chi_{\cA_{N_j}}(1-\epsilon)
        = \bigg(1-\frac{1}{L^2}\bigg) \chi_{\cA_{N_j}^\circ}(1-\epsilon)
        + \frac{1-\epsilon}{L^2} 
        \le \bigg(1-\frac{1}{L^2}\bigg) \epsilon + \frac{1-\epsilon}{L^2} 
        \le 2\epsilon\,,
    \]
where the last inequality holds for $L$ sufficiently large depending on $\alpha,\epsilon$. By passing to a subsequence of the $j$'s, we may assume that $\chi_{\cA_{N_j}}$ converges both pointwise and in $L^1$ to a limiting function $\chi$, which must then satisfy 
    \[
        \chi(1-2\epsilon) \le \chi(1-\epsilon) \le 2\epsilon\,.
    \]
Therefore $p \equiv \chi^{-1}$ satisfies $p(2\epsilon) \ge 1-2\epsilon$, as required by condition~\ref{it:3.6} (with $2\epsilon$ in place of $\epsilon$).
Arguing identically to the proof of Lemma~\ref{l:Lip.in.BOGP} shows that for some $\hat\epsilon(\epsilon) \ge 2\epsilon$ tending to $0$ as $\epsilon \rightarrow 0$, we have 
    \[
        \cM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)
        \subseteq \cB_{\hat\epsilon}\Big(
            \cM^{\BOGP,\chaos}(\alpha,0;\tilde C(L),\hat\epsilon)
        \Big)\,.
    \]
    Taking a union in $L$ and intersection in $\epsilon$, and applying $\sym$ to both sides, shows
    \begin{align*}
       & \sym(\sM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0))
        \subseteq \sym\bigg(
        \adjustlimits
            \bigcap_{\epsilon > 0} \bigcup_{L>0} \cB_{\epsilon}\Big(
                \cM^{\BOGP,\chaos}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)
            \Big)
        \bigg)\\
       &\qquad \subseteq 
        \adjustlimits
        \bigcap_{\epsilon > 0} \bigcup_{L>0}
        \cB_{\epsilon}\Big(
            \sym(\cM^{\BOGP,\chaos}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon))
        \Big)\\
        &\qquad\stackrel{\eqref{e:BOGP.sym.relation}}{=} \adjustlimits
        \bigcap_{\epsilon > 0} \bigcup_{L>0}
        \cB_{\epsilon}\Big(
        \cM^{\BOGP,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)
        \Big)
        \stackrel{\eqref{e:measure.classes.sym.cM}}{=} \sM^{\BOGP,\sym}(\alpha,0)\,.
    \end{align*}
This concludes the proof.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let f be holomorphic on a punctured disk {z : 0 < |z - a| < r} (an isolated singularity at a) and let f(z) = Σ_{n in Z} c_n (z - a)^n be its Laurent expansion there. The residue of f at a is Res(f,a) = c_{-1}, equivalently Res(f,a) = (1/2πi) ∫_{|z-a|=ρ} f(z) dz for any 0 < ρ < r, the circle positively oriented (the value is independent of ρ). Computation rules: if a is a pole of order at most m, Res(f,a) = lim_{z→a} (1/(m-1)!) d^{m-1}/dz^{m-1} [(z - a)^m f(z)]; in particular for a simple pole Res(f,a) = lim_{z→a} (z-a) f(z), and if f = g/h with g, h holomorphic near a, h(a) = 0 and h'(a) ≠ 0, then Res(f,a) = g(a)/h'(a). The residue at infinity of a function holomorphic on |z| > R is Res(f,∞) = -(1/2πi)∫_{|z|=ρ} f(z) dz for ρ > R; for a rational function the sum of all residues in C together with the residue at infinity is 0. A removable singularity has residue 0, but residue 0 does not imply removable (example: 1/(z-a)^2).

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:723539c0125e0923b393cbcaeb16eea58030f466c9ec59ec30240b4c8d2b95cc","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/72/723539c0125e0923b393cbcaeb16eea58030f466c9ec59ec30240b4c8d2b95cc.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:77195be7bddee76d800b272b0d976777508944a28c6935e1df2658ebfccc0f00","bundle_entry_key":"w733_t363_positive_two_sectors_two_clocks_v1","bundle_id":"population.w733-t363-positive-two-sector-two-clocks-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"neural-network implicit bias","draft":"w733/bundle_009.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.implicit_bias:w733_t363_positive_two_sectors_two_clocks_v1","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Positive activation families with two occupied live sectors

Claim w733-T363-025 v1. Target 2; kind narrowed; proof (unaudited).
No novelty claimed. This is a sufficient family, not a complete basin classification.

## Statement and dependencies

Let x1=(1,1/4), x2=(-1,1/4), both labels +1. Train both layers of the bias-free network f(x)=sum_j v_j ReLU(w_j.x) by gradient flow of summed exponential or logistic loss, with ReLU'(0)=0. Initially every neuron is strictly dead on both examples (D, output arbitrary), or has v_j>0 and lies strictly in A (x1 only), B (x2 only), or C (both active). Assume at least two of A, B, C are occupied.

A global absolutely continuous flow exists. Every such flow reaches normalized parameter margin sqrt(17)/16 and has a convergent normalized parameter direction. No uniqueness at grazing contacts is asserted. There is no initial balance, tilt, prediction-gap, or scale condition.

We use claims 015 and 017 as prior unaudited results: A/B positive neurons never leave their sectors; D remains fixed; each C has at most one strict sector exit; boundary contact sets are null; global existence holds; once both A and B exist, claim017 gives the stated direction and global margin. The elementary existence and contact arguments in claim017 section1 do not require both seeds. The extension proved here is finite creation of B from nonempty A and C, with any number of C neurons. Reflection proves the B/C case. The A/B case is already claim017.

## 1. A surviving shared neuron must exist if B never forms

Suppose initially A and C are occupied, B is absent, and no neuron ever enters strict B. Write w_j=(u_j,y_j), z_ij=w_j.x_i, a_i=-ell'(f_i)>0, and a=norm(x_i)=sqrt(17)/4. Positive live outputs are nondecreasing. For C, ydot_j=v_j(a1+a2)/4>0 almost everywhere before a strict exit. Thus a C cannot hit both boundaries together. Every strict exit under the supposition is C to A, and is irreversible. There are finitely many such exits.

They cannot remove all C. Otherwise take the last finite exit time, including all neurons exiting simultaneously. At this time all x2 predictions vanish, so f2=0, whereas the permanent A seed ensures f1>0. For either loss this gives a1<a2. For every neuron in the last exit group the incoming C equation at z2=0 is

    zdot_2 = v[(17/16)a2-(15/16)a1] > 0.

By continuity of the parameters and losses, this derivative stays strictly positive on incoming C portions of a sufficiently small left neighborhood. Boundary portions are null, and a neuron in this group has not yet strictly exited. Its nonnegative z2 therefore cannot approach zero from above at that time. This contradicts the purported last exit. Consequently at least one C survives forever. Choose a finite base time b after all strict exits, outside the null contact sets; surviving C obey their C equations almost everywhere forever after b. The A sector remains nonempty.

## 2. Eventual output dominance without an initial balance assumption

Set I_i(t)=integral_b^t a_i(s)ds and T=I1+I2. Let N=sum_j(v_j^2+norm(w_j)^2). The bound Ndot<=2a(a1+a2)N implies that bounded T would bound N and both predictions. Their loss derivatives would then have a positive lower bound on the infinite physical-time trajectory, contradicting bounded T. Thus T tends to infinity.

For each surviving C neuron, v_j(t)>=v_j(b)>0 and

    y_j(t)>=y_j(b)+v_j(b)T(t)/4 -> infinity.

The homogeneous balance invariant delta_j=v_j^2-u_j^2-y_j^2 is constant, as follows by differentiating it in every mask almost everywhere. Hence v_j^2>=y_j^2+delta_j, and eventually v_j>=3y_j/4. Finitely many surviving neurons allow a common finite time L after which all these inequalities hold forever. Reset both clocks to zero at L.

## 3. Two weighted inequalities, valid at every C tilt

For a surviving C neuron the cone gives |u|<=y/4 and 0<=z_i<=y/2. Therefore, for t>=L,

    z_i <= 2v/3,
    q_i=z_i/a <= 8v/(3sqrt(17)) < v,
    s_i=v+q_i satisfies v<=s_i<2v.

The strict algebraic certificate for the middle inequality is 64<153. Put c=x1.x2=-15/16. The exact C equations imply

    sdot_1 = a*a1*s1 + a2*(z2+(c/a)*v),
    sdot_2 = a*a2*s2 + a1*(z1+(c/a)*v).

Define b0=15/(8sqrt(17))-1/3>0, certified by 45^2>64*17. Since z_i<=2v/3 and v>=s_i/2, these yield

    sdot_1 <= (a*a1-b0*a2)*s1,
    sdot_2 <= (a*a2-b0*a1)*s2.

Also n=v^2+u^2+y^2<=26v^2/9<=26s_i^2/9. Integrating each inequality and summing over survivors gives finite constants C1,C2>0 such that

    N_C <= C1 exp(2a I1-2b0 I2),
    N_C <= C2 exp(2a I2-2b0 I1).

These are two bounds on the same surviving-C norm, not an independence assertion.

## 4. Both clocks diverge, then shared mass becomes impossible

If I2 were bounded, T tending to infinity would force I1 to infinity; the second bound would imply N_C tending to zero. This contradicts the fixed positive lower bound on every surviving output. If I1 were bounded, the first bound gives the symmetric contradiction. Thus both clocks diverge.

Let H_A be the prediction on x1 from permanent A neurons. The exact one-point hyperbolic solution gives

    H_A >= H_A(L) exp(2a I1), with H_A(L)>0.

Indeed H_A=alpha exp(2a I1)-beta exp(-2a I1), alpha>beta>=0, which bounds it below by (alpha-beta)exp(2a I1). The first C norm bound now gives

    N_C/H_A <= C exp(-2b0 I2) -> 0.

All contributions are nonnegative; f1>=H_A and f2 consists only of surviving C contributions. The C cone estimate from claim016 gives f2<=N_C/sqrt(17); even the weaker elementary f2<=a N_C/2 suffices. Hence E=f1-f2 tends to positive infinity.

For exponential loss a1/a2=exp(-E). For logistic loss f2>=0 gives a1/a2<=2exp(-E). Thus a1/a2 tends to zero. For any epsilon>0, integrating the eventual inequality a1<=epsilon*a2 and using I2 tending to infinity proves I1/I2 tending to zero. Return to the first weighted bound:

    s1(t) <= s1(L) exp(a I1-b0 I2) -> 0.

This contradicts s1>=v>=v(L)>0. The supposition that B never forms is false. A finite strict B sector therefore forms, while the original A persists. Claim017 applies from that finite time with all remaining positive C neurons and dead neurons. It supplies the direction limit and global margin sqrt(17)/16. This completes the extension, conditional on the cited unaudited dependency017.

## 5. Exact Gaussian masses and disjoint inventory change

For independent centered Gaussian hidden coordinates and outputs, each with variance sigma^2>0, put p=atan(1/4)/pi and q=1/4-p/2. The category probabilities A+, B+, C+, D (either output sign) are q,q,p/2,p. The newly completed whole A/C or B/C family has mass

    L_m=2[(1/4+p)^m-(1/4+p/2)^m-(3p/2)^m+p^m].

This is inclusion-exclusion for one required one-point category and C, with D optional, then reflection. It includes claim023's exactly-one-C family J_m=m*p*[(1/4+p/2)^(m-1)-p^(m-1)]. Thus the new disjoint probability increment is L_m-J_m, not L_m itself.

Combining with claim017's disjoint A/B family H_m gives the sufficient global-family mass

    K_m=((1+p)/2)^m-2(1/4+p/2)^m-(3p/2)^m+2p^m.

These expressions hold at sigma=1e-6 and every other positive scale; they are not total basin probabilities. They already contain all claim020 subcone events, so no claim020 probability may be added to K_m.

Separating the two D output signs, the entire L family has 2*binom(m+1,3) permutation orbits. At widths2..6 these are [2,8,20,40,70], totaling140. The disjoint increment over claim023 (at least two C) is [0,2,8,20,40], totaling70. Conditional on acceptance of the analytic claims, the proposed global inventory grows from196 to266 and unknown decreases from2643 to2573;20 source-bad and135 nonfitting orbits are unchanged. No negative-output live orbit or pure-C orbit is classified here. Exact coefficient and orbit checks are recorded separately; no floating-point experiment or independent review is asserted by this proof.

## Review focus

The least trusted step is the simultaneous-last-exit exclusion in section1 under arbitrary absolutely continuous continuations. Section3 is the new weighted two-clock argument; it uses both inequalities to establish divergence before suppressing C mass. [Lemma 11 (Subadditivity and orientation reversal) of arXiv:2609.03916, 'Halfspace Theorems for Anisotropic Minimal Surfaces and Perimeter Minimizers'] Let $\mu$ and $\eta$ be vector-valued Radon measures.  Then, as Radon
measures,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal F_\Phi(\mu+\eta;\cdot)
 \le\mathcal F_\Phi(\mu;\cdot)+\mathcal F_\Phi(\eta;\cdot).
\end{equation}
Consequently, for any locally integral $n$-currents $T$ and $S$,
\begin{equation}
 \mu_{T+S}^\Phi\le\mu_T^\Phi+\mu_S^\Phi.
\end{equation}
Moreover, for $\Phi^-$ defined in
\eqref{old-eq:reversed-integrand-definition},
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal F_\Phi(-\mu;\cdot)=\mathcal F_{\Phi^-}(\mu;\cdot),
 \qquad
 \mu_{-T}^\Phi=\mu_T^{\Phi^-},
 \qquad
 \Mphi(-T_E;A)=P_{\Phi^-}(E;A)
\end{equation}
for every Borel set $A$.
No evenness of $\Phi$ is required.

Every standard initialization 0<|x0|<eta R has a finite first time N
with |x_N|>eta R. While |x_0|,...,|x_t|<=eta R, signs alternate and
 |x_(t+1)|>=q |x_t|.
Consequently N is at most the smallest positive integer with
q^N |x0|>eta R. Equality |x0|=eta R is also harmless; a step leaves it.
This holds for BOTH usual separate bias corrections and uncorrected Adam.

For b=.9 and p=1, every dormant eigenvalue lambda2>38 obeys the premise.
In claim008's diagonal family the active coordinate evolves independently.
Any nonzero perturbation of its dormant x2, with moments still initialized
to zero, eventually exceeds eta R, however small that perturbation is.

an explicit finite escape scale R<1/38-1/lambda2. This does NOT say that
the perturbed trajectory has a particular asymptotic curvature or cannot
later return to a small neighborhood.

 M'=bM+(1-b)X, V'=dV+(1-d)X^2,

alpha_t=0,Vhat'=V' in the uncorrected case.

Assume past |X_s|<=R, s<=t. The corrected Vhat' is a convex combination
of X_0^2,...,X_t^2 (standard v0=0). Hence sqrt(Vhat')<=R. For the raw

 M X<=0,   |M|<=c |X|,   X!=0.                              (1)

because 1-b-bc=c. Set E=(1-alpha_t)D<=D<=R+rho<c/2.

[Definition 40 of arXiv:2605.02002, 'Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI'] (Uniform spatial mixing) We say the RFIM measure $\mu_{\widetilde{G}}$ on $G$ satisfies $\operatorname{USM}(C)$ for some constants $C>0$ if for any edge $(u,v)\in E$ and all $r\geq 1$, we have 
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}_h[
\sup_{\theta\in[0,\theta_*]}\sup_{\Lambda\subset V,\tau_0\in\Omega(\mu_\Lambda)}&\sup_{\tau_1,\tau_2\in\Omega(\partial B((u,v),r))}\\&d_{TV}({(1-\theta)\otimes\mu^{\tau_0,\tau_1}}(\sigma_{uv}\in\cdot),{(1-\theta)\otimes\mu^{\tau_0,\tau_2}}(\sigma_{uv}\in\cdot)
]\leq e^{-Cr},
\end{aligned}$$where we use $\sigma_{uv}$ to denote the configuration $(\sigma_u,\sigma_v)$. Here $d_{TV}$ is the total variation distance and the outer expectation is taken with respect to the random field $h$. The subset $
\partial B((u,v),r)$ is the boundary of the $r$-neighborhood of the edge $(u,v)$ defined in \eqref{neighborhood}, and thus $\tau_1,\tau_2$ ranges over any two possible boundary configurations of the $r$-neighborhood $B((u,v),r)$. We use the notation ${(1-\theta)\otimes \mu^{\tau_0,\tau_i}}$ to stand for the measure $(1-\theta)\otimes \mu^{\tau_0}$ further pinned by $\tau_i$ on $\partial B((u,v),r)$, and we assume that $\tau_1,\tau_2$ are consistent with $\tau_0$ whenever they have overlapping supports.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:af20ba1d93c91c59f91fc73963b765154efe901c9edb835424dd8a4c25f00702","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/af/af20ba1d93c91c59f91fc73963b765154efe901c9edb835424dd8a4c25f00702.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:d5427a86385ff05607dd6ee1e6f91c71d4b1ce8a40776ab41bf8c4918f3bcda4","bundle_entry_key":"rank-one-gd","bundle_id":"population.t419-lora-rank-one-all-scale-finite-accuracy-and-boundedness-20261020","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"LoRA and unbalanced linear-network gradient dynamics","draft":"w705/bundle_005.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.lowrank:lora-rank-one-all-scale-gaussian-gd-finite-accuracy-euler","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T419-C015 v1: rank-one population GD at all Gaussian scales, finite requested accuracy

Kind: narrowed. Target: 1. Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claimed.
This covers arbitrary input/output dimensions and every s>0 at rank one. The chosen constant GD step depends on eps and can be extremely small. It is not a linear-convergence theorem for one step size simultaneously for all accuracies.

Prior work: Kunin, Raventos, Domine, Chen, Klindt, Saxe and Ganguli, Get rich quick: exact solutions reveal how unbalanced initializations promote rapid feature learning, arXiv:2406.06158, Appendix A.2, especially A.2.4 equations (30)-(33), printed p.19, and A.2.5 equation (34), p.20, already give the single-neuron unbalanced gradient-flow solutions and basin boundary under whitened data. With zero output weight, their saddle boundary reduces to w0^T beta_star=0. Gradient-flow convergence from the present initialization is therefore settled, not a new result. The quantitative estimate below uses an equivalent spectral expression for that known flow and an elementary, deliberately conservative finite-horizon Euler-error argument to obtain a specified ordinary GD hitting time. Du-Hu-Lee arXiv:1806.00900, Theorem 3.2 instead initializes both rank-one factors with a small Gaussian; it is not the zero/random all-scale theorem here. Literature novelty of the finite-step corollary is unresolved.

## Statement

Let Delta=u v^T, where u in R^m and v in R^p are unit vectors and m,p>=1. Consider simultaneous GD on f(b,a)=||b a^T-Delta||F^2/2, with b0=0 and a0~N(0,s^2 I_p), any s>0. Fix 0<rho<1 and 0<eps<1. Define the following deterministic real constants:

 D=2p s^2/rho, nu_bar=1+D/2,
 U_bar=2+32 nu_bar/(s^2 rho^2),
 V_bar=1+4 sqrt(p)/rho^(3/2),
 T=(1+D) log[16 nu_bar(V_bar+U_bar)/eps],
 R=sqrt(D+4)+2, L=6R^2+1,
 M=(R^2/2+1)R.

Choose any constant step

 0<eta<=min{1,1/M,[eps/(4RM)] exp[-L(T+1)]},

and take N=ceil(T/eta). With probability at least 1-rho over a0,

 ||b_N a_N^T-Delta||F<=eps.

The guarantee includes p>1, a proper input-side rank-one bottleneck, at every initialization scale. The signal condition number is 1. For a rank-one target of singular value lambda>0, use normalized scale s/sqrt(lambda), normalized step eta lambda, and normalized requested error eps/lambda in this statement. It is only a hitting-time guarantee for the prescribed eps, with no efficiency or independently checked proof claim.

## One initial event; no independence multiplication

Write x0=v^T a0 and z0=a0-x0 v. With probability at least 1-rho,

 d=||a0||^2<=D, |x0|>=s rho/2.

Indeed E||a0||^2=ps^2 and Markov bounds the first failure probability by rho/2. The standard normal density is at most 1/sqrt(2pi), so P(|x0|<s rho/2)<=sqrt(2/pi)rho/2<rho/2. Use a union bound; the two events need not be independent. Fix this event. In particular d>0 and x0 is nonzero.

## Known flow in a spectral representation

Both GD and gradient flow keep b in span(u), so write b=beta u and a=x v+z with z orthogonal to v. The normalized gradient flow is

 beta'=x-beta||a||^2,
 x'=beta-beta^2 x,
 z'=-beta^2 z,
 beta(0)=0, x(0)=x0, z(0)=z0.

As in the cited primary source, ||a||^2-beta^2=d is conserved. In Z=(beta,x,z) coordinates define the symmetric block operator

 H_d=[[ -d/2, 1 ],[ 1, d/2 ]] on (beta,x),
 H_d=(d/2)I on the z coordinates.

Then the exact flow is equivalently

 Z'=H_d Z-(||Z||^2/2)Z,
 Z(t)=w(t)/sqrt(1+integral_0^t ||w(tau)||^2 d tau),
 w(t)=exp(t H_d)Z0.

The displayed expression follows by differentiating its positive scalar denominator. It starts at Z0 and solves the same ODE, so uniqueness identifies it with the source's known single-neuron flow; it is not an additional claimed discovery. Its denominator never vanishes. Alternatively, boundedness below gives global existence directly.

Let nu=sqrt(1+d^2/4), g=nu-d/2=1/(nu+d/2). The two eigenvalues of the 2-by-2 block are nu and -nu, with orthonormal eigenvectors e_plus,e_minus. Choose e_plus with positive beta and x entries. Decompose

 w(t)=a_plus e^(nu t)e_plus+a_minus e^(-nu t)e_minus+e^(d t/2)z0.

Because Z0=(0,x0,z0), the spectral projections give

 a_plus^2=x0^2(1+d/(2nu))/2>=x0^2/2,
 a_minus^2=x0^2(1-d/(2nu))/2<=a_plus^2.

In particular a_plus is nonzero. The limiting factors are

 Z_star=sign(a_plus)sqrt(2nu)e_plus,

and their product is the target: the positive eigenvector obeys x/beta=nu+d/2=1/g, while its scaled squared norm is 2nu=g+1/g, hence beta_star^2=g and beta_star x_star=1. Its z component is zero.

## Explicit exponential flow error bound

Let h(t)^2=1+integral_0^t ||w(tau)||^2 d tau and

 Q(t)=h(t)^2/[a_plus^2 e^(2nu t)/(2nu)].

Orthogonality of the three spectral components gives the exact formula

 h(t)^2=1+a_plus^2(e^(2nu t)-1)/(2nu)
          +a_minus^2(1-e^(-2nu t))/(2nu)
          +||z0||^2(e^(d t)-1)/d.

Subtract the leading exponential term. Since 2nu>=2g, ||z0||^2<=d, and a_plus^2>=x0^2/2, it follows that

 |Q(t)-1|<=U e^(-2gt), U=2+8nu/x0^2.

To see every term, the initial constant and the two constant/decaying eigenmode corrections contribute at most (2nu/a_plus^2+1+a_minus^2/a_plus^2)e^(-2nu t), bounded by (4nu/x0^2+2)e^(-2gt). The z integral contributes at most [2nu||z0||^2/(d a_plus^2)]e^(-(2nu-d)t), bounded by (4nu/x0^2)e^(-2gt).

Also, after division of w(t) by a_plus e^(nu t), the nonleading vector has norm at most

 V e^(-gt), V=1+sqrt(2)||z0||/|x0|.

When U e^(-2gt)<=1/2, Q>=1/2, Q^(-1/2)<=sqrt(2) and |Q^(-1/2)-1|<=sqrt(2)|Q-1|. Consequently

 ||Z(t)-Z_star||<=2sqrt(nu)(V+U)e^(-gt).

For completeness, flow loss decreases from f0=1/2, so ||beta a||<=2. The invariant gives beta^2(beta^2+d)<=4, whence beta^2<=2 and ||Z(t)||^2=2beta^2+d<=4+d<=6nu. Also ||Z_star||^2=2nu. The product map is Lipschitz with bound at most ||Z(t)||+||Z_star||<=4sqrt(nu) along the segment between these points, so

 ||beta(t)a(t)-v||<=8nu(V+U)e^(-gt).

On the chosen event, nu<=nu_bar, U<=U_bar, V<=V_bar, and g>=1/(1+D). The definition of T therefore ensures for every t>=T both the required Q condition and

 ||beta(t)a(t)-v||<=eps/2.

For the Q condition explicitly, e^(-gT)<=eps/[16nu_bar(V_bar+U_bar)], so U e^(-2gT)<=U_bar/[256nu_bar^2(V_bar+U_bar)^2]<1/2. This avoids any implicit large-time qualification.

## Rigorous finite-horizon GD transfer

This is an analytical Euler-error bound; no floating-point computation is used or asserted as a certificate. Let F=-grad f for the reduced pair Z=(beta,a), with f=||beta a-v||^2/2. Set H=T+1. The exact flow has ||Z(t)||<=sqrt(D+4)=R-2 for every t>=0. On the whole pair-norm ball of radius R,

 ||F(Z)||<=(R^2/2+1)R=M,
 ||DF(Z)||op<=6R^2+1=L.

The first bound follows from ||beta a-v||<=R^2/2+1. For the second, expand the Hessian quadratic form

 ||d_beta a+beta d_a||^2+2<beta a-v,d_beta d_a>;

its absolute value is at most (3R^2/2+1)(d_beta^2+||d_a||^2), which is smaller than L times that squared norm. The larger L is deliberately conservative.

For one exact-flow step, integration of F and its Lipschitz bound gives the local defect

 ||Z(t+eta)-Z(t)-eta F(Z(t))||<=eta^2 L M/2.

Let E_k=||Z_k^GD-Z(k eta)||. Provided the current GD point is in the radius-R ball, the segment to the flow point is also in it and

 E_(k+1)<=(1+eta L)E_k+eta^2 L M/2.

With E_0=0 this yields

 E_k<=(eta M/2)[(1+eta L)^k-1]
     <=(eta M/2)e^(L H)<=eps/(8R)

whenever k eta<=H. This also closes the ball condition inductively: the exact flow is within R-2 and eps/(8R)<1, so every proposed GD point stays within R-1. No boundedness of the computed GD sequence is assumed without proof.

Since eta<=1, N eta lies in [T,T+1]=[T,H]. The product map (beta,a)->beta a has derivative norm at most R on the radius-R ball, so

 ||beta_N a_N-beta(N eta)a(N eta)||<=R E_N<=eps/8.

Combining the flow error eps/2 and this transfer error gives a GD residual at most 5eps/8<eps. Reintroducing the unit output vector u preserves Frobenius residual norms and proves the statement.

## Limits

The step is constant during this finite run, chosen from deterministic parameters s,p,rho,eps rather than the sampled initializer. It may scale exponentially poorly with T and is not offered as a practical algorithmic rate. Choosing a different eta for a smaller eps is permitted in this theorem; claiming convergence at one fixed eta for all eps would require another argument. The high-probability event is essential and C013 still permits a rare escape event outside it. No expectation statement follows.

The entire rank-one flow component is known from the cited primary paper. The Euler argument is a standard method applied explicitly here, not an assertion of specialist-level novelty. The proper input-side bottleneck at ranks greater than one and arbitrary scales, efficient step/rate dependence, and Target 2 excess risk remain open in this work.
