[Theorem 256 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Assume $\boldsymbol{\Theta}$ is realized by a bipartite gluing graph $\mathsf{G}$, with bipartition $\epsilon : [m] \rightarrow \{\pm 1\}$. Then the vector $\boldsymbol{v} = \epsilon_1\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_1}$ has $\mathfrak{G}$-orbit $\{\epsilon_i\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_i}\,\,|\,\,i\in [m]\}$, this orbit is good (\textit{cf.} Definition~\ref{def:goodor}) and has minimal size $m = \textnormal{rank}(\boldsymbol{\Theta}) + 1$. For any $i \in [m]$ and $h \in [H]$ we have
\[
T^{(h)}(\epsilon_i \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_i}) = \left\{\begin{array}{ccc}  \epsilon_i \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_i} && \textnormal{if}\,\,h \notin \mathcal{H}_i, \\[0.6ex] \epsilon_{i'_h}\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_{i'_h}} && \textnormal{if}\,\,h \in \mathcal{H}_i. \end{array}\right.
\]
The genus of the spectral curve $\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ is $\mathsf{g}_{\boldsymbol{v}} = \textnormal{corank}(\boldsymbol{\Theta})$ and the group $\hat{\mathfrak{G}}$ is the Weyl group of type $A_{m - 1}$ (\textit{i.e.} the symmetric group in $m$ elements).

The bidifferential $\mathcal{B}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}}}$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:Bcont} is defined on $\Sigma^{[2],\circ}_{\boldsymbol{v}} = \Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}} \times \Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ and can simply be denoted $\mathcal{B}_{\boldsymbol{v}}$. Its matrix of biresidues is \textbf{\foreignlanguage{russian}{B}} = $\textnormal{\textbf{Id}} - \boldsymbol{1}$, and the bidifferential itself is equal to
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{B}_{\boldsymbol{v}} = \mathcal{B}^{\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}},\mathcal{L}} - \frac{\dd z_1\dd z_2}{(z_1 - z_2)^2},
\end{equation}
where $(z_1,z_2) = Z_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}}}$, the Lagrangian $\mathcal{L} \subset H_1(\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}},\amsmathbb{Z})$ is spanned by cycles around the components of the gluing locus (\textit{cf.} Definition~\ref{def:spcurv1}), and $\mathcal{B}^{\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}},\mathcal{L}}$ is the fundamental bidifferential of Section~\ref{sec:fund02}.

From the analytic continuation of first-kind functions in Proposition~\ref{Lem:Holo1form}, we get a linear isomorphism
\[
\begin{array}{ccc} \textnormal{Ker}(\boldsymbol{\Theta}) & \longrightarrow & H^1(\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}},\amsmathbb{C}) \\
\boldsymbol{v}' & \longmapsto & \mathfrak{u}_{\boldsymbol{v};\boldsymbol{v}'} \end{array}
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 256 of arXiv:2601.16377

[Definition D:Noise of arXiv:2412.03521, 'On ergodic properties of stochastic PDEs'] In equation~(equation E:NS-vort of the paper), the finite dimensional noise $QW_t$ is defined
  as follows: we start from a $\mathbb{R}^m$-valued Wiener process $W$ defined
  on a probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$. Recall that $f_k$
  is given in~(equation D:f_k of the paper) and denote by $\{e_n; n=1,\ldots,m\}$ the standard
  basis of $\mathbb{R}^m$.  Define $Q:\mathbb{R}^m\to{H}$ by $Qe_n = q_n
  f_{k_n}$, where the $q_n$ are some strictly positive numbers, and the wave
  numbers $k_n$ are given by the set $\mathcal{Z}_0$. Then for $t \ge 0$ and $x
  \in \mathbb{T}^2$ we have
  \begin{align}
    QW_t(x)=\sum_{n=1}^m q_nW^n_tf_{k_n}(x).
  \end{align}
  Notice that $QW_t$ is an element of $H=L^2_0(\mathbb{T}^2)$.
title: Definition D:Noise of arXiv:2412.03521

body:
[Definition H-reduced graph of arXiv:2506.06559, 'Bi-infinite incipient cluster in high dimensions'] Let $G$ be a multigraph, we say that an edge $\{x,y\}$ is \emph{H-reducible} if $x$ and $y$ both have an edge degree at least 3 in $G$ and $x$, $y$ are only connected by one edge. 

We define a multigraph $\tilde{G}$, called \emph{H-reduction of $G$ by $\{x,y\}$}, in the following manner:
\begin{itemize}
\item if $x$ and $y$ have degree 3, then $V(\tilde{G})=V(G)\setminus \{x,y\}$ and $E(\tilde{G})=E(G) \setminus (\{\{x,z\}; x\sim_G z\} \cup \{\{y,z\}; y\sim_G z\}) \cup \{e_{x\setminus y}, e_{y \setminus x}\}$ with $e_{x\setminus y}=\{z_1, z_2\}$ where $z_1,z_2$ are the neighbours of $x$ which are not $y$ (and a symmetrical definition of $e_{y\setminus x}$)
\item if $x$ has degree 3, $y$ has degree at least 4, then then $V(\tilde{G})=V(G)\setminus \{x\}$ and $E(\tilde{G})=E(G) \setminus (\{\{x,z\}; z\sim_G z\} ) \cup \{e_{x\setminus y}\}$.
\item if $x$ and $y$ both have degree at least 4, then  $V(\tilde{G})=V(G)$ and $E(\tilde{G})=E(G)\setminus \{x,y\}$.
\end{itemize}
title: H-reduced graph

Put sigma_0=1/(80 sqrt(d)) and E_good={||Z_0||_F<=4, sigma_min(E^T Z_0)>=sigma_0}. This right-orthogonally invariant event has probability at least 2/5, using the settled Gaussian singular-value estimate of C07. For 0<rho<=1/100 and S=10 log(100/(sigma_0 rho)), on E_good the flow is global, ||Z(s)||_F<=4 and min_{O in O(2)}||Z(S)-E Lambda^(1/2)O||_F<rho/2. Conditional on E_good and either determinant branch, the angle of the orthogonal polar factor of Lambda^(-1/2)E^T Z(S) is uniform. This is not an entry guarantee or failure probability for exact DDPM GD: finite-step comparison, free centroid and subsequent unrestricted angular tracking remain open.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:92b7f4c445312ae0f1543ef32880eb76688589f6d22f03c71cf972636381a685","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/92/92b7f4c445312ae0f1543ef32880eb76688589f6d22f03c71cf972636381a685.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:ba6f0e3af1f9cf70660d7ca1b6bbc70a1aa812bf95b8a3cbaf03087d57123297","bundle_entry_key":"t309-c16","bundle_id":"population.t309-anisotropic-covariance-gaussian-entry-draft","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian mixture learning and covariance gradient flows","draft":"w721/bundle_009.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.learning:anisotropic-covariance-factor-flow-gaussian-random-entry-uniform-phase","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Own work draft; T309-w721-C16 v1; proof (unaudited); Target 2 route 12 entry substep.

# Quantitative Gaussian entry for the anisotropic covariance-factor surrogate

This supplies the covariance-surrogate random-entry estimate missing from C12. It uses C07's Gaussian singular-value event as settled input, without re-proving its probability. It does not compare unrestricted exact DDPM GD with this surrogate, release the centroid, or prove a full-GD failure probability. No target resolution or novelty finding is asserted.

## Statement

Let d>=2, E^T E=I_2, Lambda=diag(1,9), D=E Lambda E^T. Let Z(s) solve

    Z_dot=(D-ZZ^T)Z,

from a d-by-2 matrix Z_0 with iid N(0,1/d) entries. Put sigma_0=1/(80 sqrt(d)). Define the event

    E_good={||Z_0||_F<=4, sigma_min(E^T Z_0)>=sigma_0}.

It has probability at least 2/5. For every 0<rho<=1/100, set

    L=100/(sigma_0 rho), S=10 log L.

On E_good the flow exists globally, ||Z(s)||_F<=4, and

    min_{O in O(2)} ||Z(S)-E Lambda^(1/2) O||_F <rho/2.    (1)

Conditional on E_good and either determinant branch, the angle of the orthogonal polar factor of Lambda^(-1/2)E^T Z(S) is uniform. The time S=O(log d+log(1/rho)); all constants here are independent of d. This is an exact deterministic-flow and Gaussian-initialization statement, not a training experiment or a claim that the DDPM trajectory equals this flow.

## 1. Global bounded flow

Set Q=ZZ^T, R=tr Q=||Z||_F^2. Then

    R_dot=2 tr(DQ)-2||Q||_F^2
         <=2||Q||_F(sqrt(82)-||Q||_F).

The rank of Q is at most two, hence ||Q||_F>=R/sqrt(2). At R>=16 this is larger than sqrt(82), since 16^2/2=128>82. Thus the derivative points inward at the norm-4 boundary and beyond it. On ||Z_0||<=4 the solution cannot exit this ball. The polynomial ODE is locally Lipschitz and bounded solutions extend globally. This bound does not use an incorrect isotropic replacement for the largest eigenvalue 9.

## 2. Exact covariance formula

Write A=E^T Z_0, B=(I-EE^T)Z_0. On E_good, A is invertible, ||A||_F,||B||_F<=4 and sigma_min(A)>=sigma_0. Define

    W(s)=E exp(Lambda s) A+B,
    H(s)=I+A^T diag(e^(2s)-1,(e^(18s)-1)/9) A+2s B^T B.

Then H=I+2 integral_0^s W(u)^T W(u) du is positive definite and

    Q(s)=W(s) H(s)^(-1) W(s)^T.                        (2)

Differentiating gives Q_dot=DQ+QD-2Q^2 and Q(0)=Z_0 Z_0^T. The actual covariance has this same Riccati equation, so uniqueness gives (2). No identity Z=W H^(-1/2) for the actual factor trajectory is assumed.

Let Q_pp=E^T Q E. Inverting its planar factor in (2) gives

    Q_pp^(-1)=Lambda^(-1)+T(s),
    T(s)=exp(-Lambda s) A^(-T)
       [I+2s B^T B-A^T Lambda^(-1) A]
          A^(-1) exp(-Lambda s).

Consequently

    ||T(s)||_op<=e^(-2s) sigma_0^(-2)(17+32s).         (3)

All inverses are legitimate: A is invertible on E_good and H is positive definite for every nonnegative time.

## 3. Planar and perpendicular entry errors

At S, (3) and sigma_0^(-2)=L^2 rho^2/10000 give

    ||T(S)||<=rho^2(17+320 log L)/(10000 L^18)
              <=337 rho^2/(10000 L^17)<rho^2/25,       (4)

using L>=1 and log L<=L. Our actual parameters give S>=1. In particular ||T||<1/18. Matrix inversion then yields

    ||Q_pp-Lambda||_op
       <=81||T||/(1-9||T||)<=162||T||.                (5)

Let C=Lambda^(-1/2)E^T Z(S), and O its orthogonal polar factor. Its singular values are positive. The inequality |sqrt(x)-1|<=|x-1| for x>=0 gives

    ||C-O||_F<=||CC^T-I||_F
                  <=||Q_pp-Lambda||_F.

Multiplying by Lambda^(1/2), and using (5), bounds the planar factor error by

    ||E^T Z(S)-Lambda^(1/2)O||_F
          <=486 sqrt(2)||T||<700||T||<=28rho^2.         (6)

For the perpendicular part, (e^(18s)-1)/9 >= e^(2s)-1 for s>=0; this follows by comparing the corresponding integrals of 2e^(18u) and 2e^(2u). Therefore

    H(s)>=(e^(2s)-1) A^T A.

For s>=1 this gives

    ||(I-EE^T)Z(s)||_F^2
       =tr(B H(s)^(-1) B^T)
       <=32 sigma_0^(-2)e^(-2s).

At S the last expression is at most 32rho^2/(10000 L^18)<rho^2/100. Combining with (6) and rho<=1/100 bounds the total factor error by

    28rho^2+rho/10 <=(19/50)rho<rho/2.

This proves (1). Orthogonality of planar and perpendicular errors could give a slightly tighter bound, but is not needed.

## 4. Probability and the correct phase symmetry

C07's settled Gaussian good event has probability at least 2/5 and implies both ||Z_0||<=4 and sigma_min(E^T Z_0)>=sigma_0. It is therefore a subset of E_good, proving the stated probability. We do not condition on C07's particular column-based construction of that event, since that construction need not be invariant under right rotations.

E_good itself IS invariant under Z_0 -> Z_0 O for every O in O(2), because Frobenius norm and singular values are unchanged. The Gaussian law has the same right invariance. The ODE is right equivariant: (ZO)(ZO)^T=ZZ^T, and uniqueness implies Z(s;Z_0 O)=Z(s;Z_0)O. Thus C at time S right-rotates in the same manner. Its left polar decomposition C=S_C O_C is unique because C is invertible; right rotation preserves S_C and rotates O_C. Rotations preserve either determinant branch and act transitively on its circle. The conditional angular law on each nonnull branch is therefore uniform. Reflection interchanges the two branches, and both have positive probability on this invariant event.

This is right-factor symmetry of the covariance surrogate. It is not a physical-plane rotational symmetry of the anisotropic teacher, and it is not a symmetry of the component-identifying DDPM correction. Keeping those distinct is necessary for the eventual probability-transfer argument.

## Remaining transfer

This result supplies a norm-bounded logarithmic-time surrogate entry estimate and the invariant event needed for its uniform phase. To connect it to C15 one must still compare actual finite-step DDPM GD over this entry interval, release centering and planarity, and control their accumulated angular effects. The free-centroid and extra-direction estimates for the equilateral case do not automatically establish those anisotropic statements. No product of independent success probabilities, full-GD basin mass, or annealing obstruction is claimed here.

Let $\Sigma$ be a spacelike hypersurface with timelike unit normal $e_0$ in a spacetime $(\bar{M}, \bar{g})$. For any normal variation with variation vector field $V = \phi e_0$ compactly supported on $\Sigma$, the second variation of the volume functional $\operatorname{Vol}(\Sigma_t)$ at $t=0$ is given by $\left. \frac{d^2}{dt^2} \operatorname{Vol}(\Sigma_t) \right|_{t=0} = - \int_\Sigma \left( |\nabla \phi|^2 - (|h|^2 + \operatorname{Ric}(e_0, e_0)) \phi^2 \right) d\mu_g$. In particular, when $\operatorname{Ric}(e_0, e_0) \ge 0$, any maximal hypersurface ($H=0$) strictly maximizes volume among nearby compact perturbations.
\Sigma is a spacelike hypersurface in Lorentzian spacetime
\phi is a smooth compactly supported function
Ric(e_0, e_0) >= 0 (dominant energy condition)

[Theorem 16 (The PF continuity equation is not well posed) of arXiv:2607.25685, 'Mimicking diffusion processes with differential equations'] Let $v$ be given by \eqref{eq:cev} and $T>0$. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(i)}] $v\notin L^1_\loc\big([0,T]\times\R\big)$. The weak
formulation of Definition~\ref{def:class} is not meaningful for general
$u\in L^\infty((0,T);L^1\cap L^\infty)$, and assumptions \textup{(R1)}, \textup{(R3)} of
Theorem~\ref{thm:DL} fail.
\item[\textup{(ii)}] For every $x_0$ with $|x_0|\ge1$ there is \emph{no} absolutely
continuous $Z:[0,T]\to\R$ with $Z(0)=x_0$ and $Z(t)=x_0+\int_0^tv(Z(s),s)\,\dd s$.
Consequently no regular Lagrangian flow exists: condition \textup{(i)} of
Definition~\ref{def:rlf} fails on the set $\{|x|>1\}$.
\item[\textup{(iii)}] For every $x\in(-1,1)$ there is exactly one such solution, namely
\eqref{eq:cequantile}, and\\ $Z(t,\cdot):(-1,1)\to\R$ is a smooth increasing bijection.
\item[\textup{(iv)}] The Cauchy problem fails to be solvable
for any initial condition $u_0\in L^1\cap L^\infty$  with
$u_0=0$ a.e.\ on $[-1,1]$: there is no
narrowly continuous family of probability measures $(\mu_t)_{t\in[0,T]}$ with
$\mu_0=u_0\Leb$ solving \eqref{eq:cont} and satisfying the integrability
hypothesis of Theorem~\ref{thm:super}.  
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The PF continuity equation is not well posed

\|a(v_2,\mu^{(2)})-a(v_1,\mu^{(1)})\|+\Big(\int_{\mbR^d}\|b(v_2,\mu^{(2)},z)-b(v_1,\mu^{(1)},z)\|^2\differential{z}\Big)^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq L \dist_m((v_1, \mu^{(1)}), (v_2, \mu^{(2)})) .
$$
Moreover, suppose that $b$ is continuous with respect to variables $v$ and $\mu$. Then, the stochastic differential equation \eqref{eq:Eq_interaction} has a solution, which is unique, and for every $t>0$, the measure $\mu_t$ is a random element in $\cM_m.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 12 ($\AS$) of arXiv:2511.07350, 'Decoupling of clusters in independent sets in a percolated hypercube'] Define the random independent set $\hat{I}$ in $\Qp$ via the following procedure.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item Let $\cH$ be $\cE$ or $\cO$, with probabilities proportional to $e^{\Psi^\cE}$ and $e^{\Psi^\cO}$ respectively.
		\item Let $\tilde{S}$ denote a subset of $\cH$ which includes each $v \in \cH$ independently with probability
		$\fr{2^{-\N(v)}}{1 + 2^{-\N(v)}}$.
		\item If $\tilde{S}$ contains any triple of vertices which is \emph{2-linked},
        terminate the algorithm with a result of failure.
		Otherwise, remove all dimers from $\tilde{S}$ and let $S_1$ denote the resulting set of well-separated singletons (which share no neighbors).
		\item Let $S_2$ denote a collection of dimers constructed by including each $\{u,v\} \in \Dim^\cH$ independently with probability
		$\fr{2^{-\N(\{u,v\})}}{1 + 2^{-\N(\{u,v\})}}$.
		\item If any neighbor of a dimer in $S_2$ also neighbors a vertex in $S_1$, {or if any pair of dimers in $S_2$ overlap or share a neighbor,}
        terminate the algorithm with a result of failure.
		Otherwise, let $\hat{S} = S_1 \cup S_2$.
		\item Let $\hat{I}$ denote the independent set with $\hat{I} \cap \cH = \hat{S}$ and with every vertex in $\Q \setminus \cH$
		which does not neighbor $\hat{S}$ included independently with probability $\fr{1}{2}$ each.
	\end{enumerate}

[Definition def-thin-disk of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] Let $W\in(0, \frac{\gamma^2}{2})$. 
	    Sample $(\mathcal{W}, T) \sim \mathcal{M}^\mathrm{wed}(W) \times (1-\frac{2}{\gamma^2}W)^{-2}\textup{Leb}_{\mathbb{R}_+}$, and write $\mathcal{W} = \{(u, \mathcal{D}_u)\}$. The \emph{weight $W$ quantum disk} is the concatenation of the quantum disks $\{\mathcal{D}_u \: : \: u \leq T\}$ according to the ordering induced by $u$. Its left (resp.\ right) boundary length is the sum of the left (resp.\ right) boundary lengths of its constituent $\mathcal{D}_u$.
	    We define the infinite measure ${\mathcal{M}}^\mathrm{disk}_{0,2}(W)$ to be the law of the weight $W$ quantum disk.
	    For $x\in [0,T]$, the \emph{quantum cut point measure} assigns  mass
	    $x$ to the collection of cut points between the quantum disks $\{\mathcal{D}_u:u\leq x\}$.

[Lemma 24 (the pressure of an $H^s$ distributional solution) of arXiv:2609.01093, 'Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold'] Let $s>\frac n2$ and let $(v,B)$ be a distributional solution of
\eqref{eq:mhd} on $[0,T]\times\Rn$ with data $(v_0,\Binf)$, in the sense of
Section~\ref{sec:introduction}, such that
$v,b=B-\Binf\in C([0,T],H^s)$. Define
\[
 p_{\mathrm R}:=\Riesz_i\Riesz_j
 \big(v^iv^j-\Binf^ib^j-b^i\Binf^j-b^ib^j\big).
\]
Then $p_{\mathrm R}\in C([0,T],H^s)$,
$\nabla p_{\mathrm R}\in C([0,T],H^{s-1})$, and
\[
 \partial_tv+\Div_x(v\otimes v-B\otimes B)+\nabla p_{\mathrm R}=0
 \quad\text{in }\mathcal D'((0,T)\times\Rn).
\]

[Prop 13 (\cite{duerinckx2020mean},\,Corollary 3.5) of arXiv:2609.00598, 'Supercritical mean--field limit for magnetized Hamiltonian dynamics'] Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item[{\rm(i)}]$\rho \in L^{\infty}(\mathbb{T}^{2});$ 
   \item[{\rm(ii)}]
   $X_{N}=(x_{1},\cdots\!,x_{N})\in \Delta_{N}^{c}$ and $\rho_{N}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\delta_{x_{i}}$. 
\end{itemize}
Then there exist a constant $C>0$ such that
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{V}_{N}(\rho,\rho_{N}) \geq -C\big(1+\left\Vert \rho \right\Vert_{\infty}\big)
\frac{1+\log N}{N}. 
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 36 (Negligible resets give the ordinary Gumbel law) of arXiv:2605.14511, 'Clumsy and Careless:\\ Stationary-Entry Flux in Non-monotone Coupon Collectors'] Assume equal standard probabilities and
\[
        \rho_n n\log n\to0.
\]
Let $T_n$ be the reset-button completion time.  Then, for every $y\in\Rbb$,
\[
        \Pbb\left(T_n\le n\log n+ny\right)
        \longrightarrow
        \exp(-e^{-y}).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
        \frac{T_n-n\log n}{n}\Rightarrow G,
\]
where $G$ is the standard coupon-collector Gumbel variable with distribution function
\[
        \Pbb(G\le y)=\exp(-e^{-y}).
\]

body:
[Thm sharp of arXiv:2411.14236, 'Size of chaos for Gibbs measures\\of mean field interacting diffusions'] Suppose that the following three conditions hold true.
\begin{itemize}
\item
(Log-Sobolev inequalities)
There exists $\rho > 0$ such that the non-linear and linear
log-Sobolev inequalities hold:
\[
\forall m \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X),
\qquad
2\rho H(m|m_*)
\leqslant
\begin{cases}
I(m|\Pi[m]),~\text{and} \\
I(m|m_*).
\end{cases}
\]
\item
(Transport inequalities)
There exists $\gamma \geqslant 0$ such that
for both $\mu = m^{N,k|[k-1]}_{*,\bm{x}^{[k-1]}}$ and $\mu = m_*$,
the probability measure $\mu$ satisfies the transport inequality
\[
\forall \nu \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X),\qquad
\lvert \langle \nabla_1 W(x^k, \cdot),
\nu - \mu \rangle\rvert^2
\leqslant \gamma
H(\nu | \mu )
\]
uniformly in $k \in [N]$, $\bm{x}^{[k]} \in \mathcal X^{k}$.
\item
(Square integrability)
There exists $M \geqslant 0$ such that
\begin{align*}
\int_{\mathcal X^2} \lvert \nabla_1 W(x,y)
- \langle \nabla_1 W(x,\cdot), m_*\rangle\rvert^2
m^{N,2}_*(\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} x\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} y) &\leqslant M, \\
\int_{\mathcal X} \lvert \nabla_1 W(x,x)
- \langle \nabla_1 W(x,\cdot), m_*\rangle\rvert^2
m^{N,1}_*(\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} x) &\leqslant M.
\end{align*}
\end{itemize}
Then for all $k \in [N]$,
\[
\int_{\mathcal X^{k-1}} H(m^{N,k|[k-1]}_{*,\bm{x}^{[k-1]}} | m_*)
m^{N,k-1}_*(\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\bm{x}^{[k-1]})
\leqslant
\frac{36\bigl(1+\frac\gamma\rho\bigr)^3M}{\rho N^2}
\biggl( k + \frac{3\gamma}{\rho}\biggr),
\]
and consequently,
\[
H(m^{N,k}_* | m_*^{\otimes k}) \leqslant
\frac{18\bigl(1+\frac\gamma\rho\bigr)^3M}{\rho N^2}
\biggl( k^2+ \Bigl(1+\frac{6\gamma}{\rho}\Bigr)k\biggr).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm sharp of arXiv:2411.14236

[Theorem 13 of arXiv:2606.15178, 'The distribution of the de Moivre experiment'] Let $ X\sim \mathcal{B}^{(s)}(n,p) $ be a bi$^{s}$nomial random variable with parameters $ n $ and $ p $, with $p\neq q$, and set
	$$ \mu_s=E(X)=np\frac{(s+1)p^{s}-1}{(p-q)},\qquad \sigma^2_s=V(X)=npq\frac{ 1-(s+1)^2(pq)^s}{(p-q)^2}. $$
	Then the standardized variable $ Z=\frac{X-\mu_s}{\sigma_s} $ converges in distribution, as $n\rightarrow\infty$, to the standard normal distribution $N(0,1)$; in other words, $X$ has, for large $n$, an approximate normal distribution with mean $\mu_s$ and variance $\sigma_s^2$.
title: Theorem 13 of arXiv:2606.15178

Let (X_k)_{k = 0..n} be a martingale with respect to a filtration, with bounded differences |X_k - X_{k-1}| <= c_k almost surely for constants c_k. Then for every t > 0, P(X_n - X_0 >= t) <= exp(-t^2 / (2 sum_{k=1}^n c_k^2)) and P(X_n - X_0 <= -t) <= exp(-t^2 / (2 sum c_k^2)); hence P(|X_n - X_0| >= t) <= 2 exp(-t^2 / (2 sum c_k^2)). The upper-tail bound holds for supermartingales and the lower-tail bound for submartingales.

body: A discrete-time Markov chain on a countable state space S with transition matrix P is irreducible if for every pair of states x, y in S there exists n >= 0 with P^n(x,y) > 0 (y is reachable from x). The period of a state x is the greatest common divisor of {n >= 1 : P^n(x,x) > 0}; an irreducible chain has a single common period shared by all states, and the chain is aperiodic if this common period equals 1, equivalently if for some x and all sufficiently large n, P^n(x,x) > 0. [standard, e.g. Levin and Peres, Markov Chains and Mixing Times]
title: Irreducible and Aperiodic Discrete-Time Markov Chain

[Lemma lem_NN20 of arXiv:2607.11469, 'Breuer-Major-Donsker invariance principle'] Let $(Y_n)_{n\geq 1}$ be a sequence of random elements 
in $\mathbf{D}([0,1])$. 
Suppose that there is some $p > 2$ and $C \in(0, \infty)$
such that 

\noindent
\begin{align}
\| Y_n(t) - Y_n(s) \|_{p} \leq C \Big(  \frac{  \lfloor nt \rfloor - \lfloor ns \rfloor}{n} \Big)^{\frac12}
\end{align}
for any $0 \leq s \leq t \leq 1$
and for any $n\geq 1$.
Then,  $\{Y_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ is tight
in $\mathbf{D}([0,1])$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Tightness criterion

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let \(q\in Y^{\rm rv}\), and suppose that a Zariski-open neighbourhood
\(U_{\rm prod}\ni q\) admits a biregular product trivialization
\[
 \pi^{-1}(U_{\rm prod})\cong U_{\rm prod}\times F
\]
over \(U_{\rm prod}\).  Then there is a principal Zariski-open product
neighbourhood \(U\ni q\), \(U\subset U_{\rm prod}\), such that for every
\(V\Subset U\) there are constants \(0<c_V\le C_V<\infty\), independent
of \(t<T\), for which
\begin{equation}
 c_V\eta\le S_t\le C_V\eta
 \qquad\text{on }\pi^{-1}(V).
\end{equation}
Moreover, uniformly in \(f\in F\),
\begin{equation}
 \omega(t)|_{V\times\{f\}}
 \le C_V\pi^*\eta|_{V\times\{f\}},
 \qquad 0\le t<T.
\end{equation}
Consequently, if \(K\Subset Y^{\rm rv}\) has the
Zariski-open-product property, then
\[
 c_K\eta\le S_t\le C_K\eta
 \qquad\text{on }\pi^{-1}(K)
\]
for constants independent of \(t<T\).

body:
[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] Let \(a>1\) and \(r_a(\xi)=e^{-2\xi}-e^{-2a\xi}\), \(\xi>0\). Then
\(0<r_a(\xi)<1\) for every \(\xi>0\), and
\[
        \rho_a:=\sup_{\xi>0}r_a(\xi)
        =
        (a-1)a^{-a/(a-1)}<1.
\]
Moreover, \(r_a\in L^1(0,\infty)\),
\begin{equation}

        \int_0^\infty r_a(\xi)\,\mathrm d\xi
        =
        \frac12\left(1-\frac1a\right),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}

        \int_0^\infty r_a(\xi)(1-r_a(\xi))\,\mathrm d\xi
        =
        \frac{(a-1)(a+3)}{4a(a+1)}.
\end{equation}
Finally, \(r_a(\xi)=2(a-1)\xi+O(\xi^2)\) as \(\xi\downarrow0\), and \(r_a\)
decays exponentially as \(\xi\to\infty\).

body: Counterexample (campaign status: exact-certificate): Let r = 2^{2t}, H a Walsh-Hadamard matrix, A_r = {+-H_{*j} : 1<=j<=r} (signed columns). The fibre is fully closed; its full dual is the projectivized {(1/r)Hv : v in {+-1}^r}/{+-1}. A bent sign vector has full Walsh support, so one admissible witness meets every edge of a perfect matching: the weighted batching can be a SINGLE batch with a legal one-row basis exchange. Yet every coordinate-basis selector certificate satisfies dcb(A_r) = r - floor(log2(2r)): a rank-(r-d) image of the cube has at least 2^{r-d} points while selector feasibility permits at most 2r signed basis images, so 2^{r-d} <= 2r; the matching construction attains the bound. Notes: Does NOT refute linear rigidity: ell(A_r) = r - log2(2r), so dcb ~ ell. It refutes that selected-row atom charges alone pay the remainder - unused global defect must also be allocated. Its lone batch has kappa ~ r/log r (p.38). Exponents reconstructed from flattened 'r = 22t', '2r-d' [EXTRACTION: r=2^{2t}, 2^{r-d}; bent vectors need even Walsh dimension, consistent].

Setting: online SGD for a soft committee machine with K students w_1..w_K in R^N and M = K orthonormal teachers v_1..v_K, activation g(x) = erf(x/sqrt 2), output sum_i g(w_i . x), Gaussian inputs, no noise, step eta/N. As N -> infinity the overlaps Q_ij = w_i . w_j and R_in = w_i . v_n follow a deterministic ODE in time t = steps/N (the Saad-Solla equations, including the eta^2 term). Take K = M = 2 and restrict to the symmetric slice Q_11 = Q_22 = q, Q_12 = c, all R_in = r, which the ODE preserves. For every eta in [2499/5000, 2501/5000], the solution from (q, c, r) = (1, 0, 0) exists for all t >= 0 and converges exponentially to an equilibrium x*(eta). That equilibrium is the unique zero of the slice drift in a certified box where it is physical (q - c > 0, q + c - 4 r^2 > 0) and Hurwitz in the slice. Its antisymmetric block has exactly the plateau's unstable direction (lambda > 0). Hence the spherical start reaches the symmetric saddle along its stable manifold.
K = M = 2

body: Localized regime of the bounded-density conjecture for quadratic forms (Proposition 4). Let X_1..X_n be independent with densities <=1 and Q(x)=x^T A x with A symmetric. (a) If some 2x2 PRINCIPAL submatrix B of A (two original coordinates i, j) is definite, then ||p_Q||_inf <= pi/sqrt(det B). Proof: condition on the other n-2 ORIGINAL coordinates (independent, so Fubini is genuine); given them Q is a quadratic-plus-linear form in (X_i, X_j); complete the square (B invertible), which shifts (X_i, X_j) and keeps their joint density <=1; for definite B each set {s <= y^T B y <= s+h} is an elliptic annulus of area at most pi h/sqrt(det B), so the conditional density is at most pi/sqrt(det B); average. (b) Hence if A has a 3x3 PRINCIPAL submatrix A_[S] all of whose eigenvalues have modulus >= c>0, and A_[S] is definite or diagonal, then ||p_Q||_inf <= pi/c: for definite A_[S], Cauchy interlacing puts both eigenvalues of every 2x2 principal block of A_[S] at modulus >= c with one sign, so det >= c^2; for diagonal A_[S], two of the three diagonal entries share a sign and form a definite diagonal block with det >= c^2. This contains the separable case. (c) For other well-conditioned blocks the bound K/c is not proved. A block may have no definite 2x2 principal block at all, e.g. [[0,1,1],[1,0,1],[1,1,0]] (eigenvalues 2, -1, -1), and the rank-3 coarea bound ||p_S||_inf <= K||rho||_inf^{2/3} is false for general bounded densities on R^3: a density rho <= B placed on a thin shell around {S = s} gives p_S of order B s^{1/2}/sqrt(l1 l2 l3) for a definite form, unbounded in s. So the localized regime is settled for forms with a definite 2x2 principal block of determinant >= c^2, in particular when a well-conditioned 3x3 principal block is definite or diagonal; the other localized forms stay open, together with the DELOCALIZED forms (every 3x3 principal block near-singular), which is the CLT regime.

[Corollary corollary_repl_lemma_ave of arXiv:2411.17653, 'Exclusion processes with non-reversible boundary: hydrodynamics and large deviations'] For any function $H \in C^{1,2}( {\Omega_T})$and for every $\delta > 0$, it holds that
\begin{equation} 
\lim_{\epsilon\to 0}\lim_{N\to+\infty}\mathbb{P}_{\nu_N} \left( \sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} \Big | \int_0^t \eta_{sN^2}(\epsilon_N)\nabla^+_N H_s(0) - \pi^N_s \ast \iota_\epsilon(\epsilon_N)\partial_u H_s(0) ds\Big| > \delta \right) =0,
\end{equation} and
\begin{equation} 
\lim_{\epsilon\to 0}\lim_{N\to+\infty}\mathbb{P}_{\nu_N} \left( \sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} \Big | \int_0^t \eta_{sN^2}(\tau_N)\nabla^+_N H_s(\tau_N) - \pi^N_s \ast \iota_\epsilon(\tau_N)\partial_u H_s(1) ds\Big| > \delta \right) =0.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 18 (A sufficient condition for proxy-faithfulness) of arXiv:2608.25188, 'Transforms for LLM Quantization:\\ The Great Inversion and Format Co-Design'] Let transforms $A,B$ act on the same operand under a common grouping and produce group-RMS profiles with $\sum_g\sigma_g^2=S_A\ge S_B$ and per-group crest factors $M_g=\mathrm{CF}_g\,\sigma_g$ all lying in a band
$\mathrm{CF}_g\in[\underline c,\bar c]$ (necessarily $1\le\underline c\le\bar c\le\sqrt G$
for a group of size $G$). If that band is tight relative to the proxy gap,
$\bar c^2/\underline c^2 < S_A/S_B$, then the $L^2$ proxy $\sum_g\sigma_g^2$ and the
AbsMax step-size surrogate $\sum_g M_g^2$ rank $A$ and $B$ the \emph{same} way. When
the crest-factor profiles differ enough to break this condition, which a
concentrating transform induces, the ranking can \emph{invert}. Note that the aggregate $\sum_g\sigma_g^2$ is the operand's Frobenius energy divided by $G$, hence unchanged by any orthogonal map: between two rotations $S_A=S_B$ and the sufficient condition is unavailable, so this proposition bites only where the transforms change that energy. What a concentrating rotation still changes is the crest-factor band, and that is the route by which the two surrogates come apart.

[Lemma lem_2a of arXiv:2607.11469, 'Breuer-Major-Donsker invariance principle'] Let $\mathbf G$ have an absolutely continuous spectral measure with density
$\mathfrak m\in L^1(\mathbb T)$. For $q\ge2$, the $q$-decimated sequence
has spectral density
\begin{align}
\mathfrak m_q(\theta)
=
\frac1q\sum_{\ell=0}^{q-1}
\mathfrak m\left(\left[\frac{\theta+2\pi\ell}{q}\right]_{\mathbb T}\right)
\end{align}
for a.e. $\theta\in\mathbb T$.
If, in addition, $\rho_G\in\ell^1(\mathbb Z)$, then the equality holds
pointwise for the continuous versions.
title: Lemma lem_2a of arXiv:2607.11469

motion, as well as i.i.d. family

independent of the family of Brownian motions.

Let V = V(F) and p in V. If v in ker(J_F(p)) is tangent to an analytic curve gamma(t) = p + t*v + (t^2 / 2)*w + O(t^3) in V, then the quadratic form Q_F(p)(v) must lie in the image of J_F(p): specifically, J_F(p)*w + Q_F(p)(v) = 0. Therefore, the quadratic obstruction q_p(v) must vanish: q_p(v) = 0 in k^m / im(J_F(p)).
F: k^n -> k^m polynomial
p in V(F)
gamma is an analytic curve in V with gamma(0)=p, gamma'(0)=v, gamma''(0)=w

[Thm 12 of arXiv:2608.12804, 'Scaling Limits for Ising Models on Inhomogeneous Random Graphs and Applications'] Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a compact subset of the metric space $(AC[0,1],d_{AC})$. Then, the conditional law of
$\mathbb G_N$ given $A_N$, viewed as a
$\mathcal P(C(\mathcal C))$-valued random probability measure, converges
weakly in probability to the law of $\mathbb G$. In particular, the
unconditional laws of $\mathbb G_N$ converge weakly
to the law of $\mathbb G$ as probability measures on $C(\mathcal C)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Thm mainhaar of arXiv:2412.00593, 'A new approach to strong convergence II.\\The classical ensembles'] Let $\boldsymbol{U}^N=(U_1^N,\ldots,U_r^N)$ be i.i.d.\ Haar-distributed
random matrices in $\mathrm{U}(N)/\mathrm{O}(N)/\mathrm{Sp}(N)$,
and let $\boldsymbol{u}=(u_1,\ldots,u_r)$ be free Haar unitaries.
Let $\varepsilon\in [\frac{1}{c\sqrt{N}},1]$ and $q_0\in\mathbb{N}$. 
For every noncommutative polynomial $P\in\mathrm{M}_D(\mathbb{C})\otimes 
\mathbb{C}\langle\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{u}^*\rangle$ of degree $q_0$ 
with matrix coefficients of dimension $D\le e^{cN\varepsilon^2/
\log^2(N\varepsilon^2)}$, we have
$$
	\mathbf{P}\big[
	\|P(
	\boldsymbol{U}^N,
	\boldsymbol{U}^{N*})\|\ge (1+\varepsilon)
	\|P(\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{u}^*)\|
	\big] \le
	\frac{N}{c\varepsilon}
	\,e^{-cN\varepsilon^2/\log^2(N\varepsilon^2)}.
$$
Here $c$ is a constant that depends only on $q_0$ and $r$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm mainhaar of arXiv:2412.00593

body: [Lemma lem:nointerventionof2s of arXiv:2509.16541, 'Two-stage Bootstrap Percolation'] When $q \leq p^2$, the bootstrap percolation of $2$s internal to the region within  $\ell^\infty$-distance $M$ of $B_0$ produces no connected component of $2$s with diameter larger than $\frac{1}{p}\log(1/p)$ with high probability.

Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be measures on the same measurable space $(X, \Sigma)$, with $
u$ possibly signed or complex. $
u$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\mu$, written $
u \ll \mu$, if $
u(A) = 0$ for every $A \in \Sigma$ with $\mu(A) = 0$ (for signed $
u$, equivalently $|
u|(A) = 0$, where $|
u|$ is the total variation). If $
u$ is FINITE (or finite signed/complex), this is equivalent to the $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ condition: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $\delta > 0$ with $|
u(A)| < \varepsilon$ whenever $\mu(A) < \delta$; for infinite $
u$ the $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ condition is strictly stronger (e.g. $
u(A) = \int_A |x|^{-1}dx$ on $(0,1)$ has $
u \ll$ Lebesgue but fails $\varepsilon$-$\delta$). Any measure of the form $
u(A) = \int_A f\,d\mu$ with $f \geq 0$ measurable (or $f \in L^1(\mu)$ for signed $
u$) satisfies $
u \ll \mu$; the Radon-Nikodym theorem is the converse under $\sigma$-finiteness. $\mu$ and $
u$ are mutually singular, $\mu \perp 
u$, if there is $A \in \Sigma$ with $\mu(A) = 0$ and $
u(X\setminus A) = 0$. Lebesgue decomposition: for $\sigma$-finite $\mu, 
u$ there is a unique splitting $
u = 
u_{ac} + 
u_s$ with $
u_{ac} \ll \mu$ and $
u_s \perp \mu$. Related but different: a FUNCTION $F: [a,b]	o\mathbb{R}$ is absolutely continuous iff its Lebesgue-Stieltjes measure is absolutely continuous w.r.t. Lebesgue measure iff $F(x) = F(a) + \int_a^x F'$ with $F' \in L^1$; the Cantor function is continuous, increasing, but not absolutely continuous (its measure is singular). Sharp edge: $
u \ll \mu$ is not symmetric, and $
u \ll \mu$ with $\mu \ll 
u$ (equivalence) does not make the density bounded or bounded below.
mu and nu are measures on a common measurable space (X, Sigma); nu may be signed or complex
the epsilon-delta characterisation requires nu finite

body:
[Dfn 232 (truncated Lipschitz algorithm) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Consider an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm $\cA_N$ with input $(\bG, \bg^\aux)$. Denote its output $\bx\equiv\cA_N(\bG,\bg^\aux)$. For $a\in [M]$, define the random variable
	\[\fm_a\equiv
		\fm_a(\bG,\bg^\aux;\cA_N)
		\equiv
		\frac{(\bg^a,\bx)}{N^{1/2}}\,,
	\]
where we recall that $\bg^a$ is the $a$-th row of $\bG$.
	For $K > 0$, define
	\[
		S_K(\cA_N) = \bigg\{
			a \in [M] : 
			\Big|\E\fm_a(\bG,\bg^\aux;\cA_N)\Big|
			\ge K
		\bigg\}\,.
	\]
Let $\hbG \in \R^{M\times N}$ be a matrix of i.i.d. gaussians independent of $(\bG, \bg^\aux)$.
	Then define the \textbf{truncated algorithm} $\cA_{N[K]}$ as the function
	\[\cA_{N[K]}\Big(\bG, 
	\bg^{\aux+}
	\equiv(\bg^\aux, \hbG)\Big)
	\equiv
	\cA_N\Big(\tbG(\bG,\hbG;S_K(\cA_N)), \bg^\aux\Big)\,,
	\]
where $\tbG$ is the row-splicing operation from Definition~\ref{d:row.splice}. In words, if $|\E\fm_a| \ge K$, then $\cA_{N[K]}$ ignores the $a$-th row $\bg^a$ of $\bG$ and replaces this input with the independent gaussian vector $\hat\bg$. 	Clearly $\cA_{N[K]}$ is also an $L$-Lipschitz function, with output
	\[\tilde{\bx} \equiv 
		\cA_{N[K]}(\bG, (\bg^\aux, \hbG)) \stackrel{\textit{d}}{=}
		\bx
		= \cA_N(\bG, \bg^\aux)\,.
	\]
It follows that $\cA_{N[K]}$ is also an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm in the sense of Definition~\ref{d:Lip}.
title: truncated Lipschitz algorithm

body: [Conj connectedness of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] For any $(M,\Phi)$ as in \zcref{assum:1} with $M$ atoroidal, the spaces $\mathcal{Z}(\Phi)$ and $\mathcal{Z}_\aleph(\Phi)$ are connected.\footnote{One could conjecture the stronger statement that $\mathcal{Z}(\Phi)$ and $\mathcal{Z}_\aleph(\Phi)$ are contractible. This should be thought of as an analogue of the fact that whenever $\Phi$ is a pseudo-Anosov flow, the set of homology classes of $\Phi$-horizontal surfaces is a cone over a convex subset of a face of the Thurston norm ball.} (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)

[Lemma 38 (Traces on spacelike hypersurfaces) of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] Let $\mathbb Q\in L^1_{\rm loc}$ be torus invariant and suppose that
\bel{eq:weak-current-production}
\nabla_\alpha\mathbb Q^\alpha=-\lambda+r\,dV_g,
\qquad
\lambda\in\Meas^+_{\rm loc},
\qquad
r\in L^1_{\rm loc}.
\ee
Then the almost-everywhere function in~\eqref{eq:weak-normal-flux} admits a right-continuous representative of locally bounded variation. For every pair of continuity levels $s_0<s_1$, one has
\bel{eq:weak-Gauss-Green}
\mathfrak H_{\mathbb Q}(s_1)
+\lambda(\mathcal D_{s_0,s_1})
=\mathfrak H_{\mathbb Q}(s_0)
+\int_{\mathcal D_{s_0,s_1}}r\,dV_g.
\ee
In particular, if $r=0$, the normal flux~$\mathfrak H_{\mathbb Q}$ is non-increasing toward the future. The same identity holds between two torus-invariant spacelike Lipschitz hypersurfaces, with the normal fluxes defined by one-sided approximation; these traces do not depend on the Lipschitz time function used between the hypersurfaces.

Own-work draft, C010 version 2, proof (unaudited); no novelty or independent-audit claim. Fix input dimension d>=1 and finite total mean-field time T>=0, with equal hidden widths m>=36. Let h_i=sigma(w_i dot x), z_j=m^(-1)sum_i B_ji h_i, and f=m^(-1)sum_j a_j sigma(z_j). Assume sigma is globally C2 with absolute values of sigma and its first two derivatives at most one; data satisfy ||X||<=1 and |Y|<=1; loss is population half-squared error. Initialize two independent runs with every coordinate of w_i, every a_j and every B_ji mutually independent standard normal variables. Train all parameters simultaneously using fresh-iid SGD samples or finite minibatch averages, with multiplier m on w,a and m^2 on B, common deterministic nonnegative steps eta_k summing to at most T; the runs may see independent data. Write S2=sum eta_k^2. Explicit constants kappa_T and C_{d,T} from proof section 1 give beta_T=exp(-kappa_T T)>0 and an initialization-selected compatible permutation tuple with expected population loss-chord barrier bounded by C_{d,T}[(sqrt(log m)m^(-1/(d+2))+sqrt(S2))^(beta_T/2)+m^(-1/2)]. Hence eta_max<=m^(-2/(d+2)) gives O_{d,T}(m^(-beta_T/(2(d+2)))(log m)^(beta_T/4)). On an initialization event of failure probability at most 18/m, empirical exponential tails of alpha_j=1+|a_j(0)|+|a'_j(0)| and initial row/weighted-column averages control all trained lower adjoints. Truncating alpha at K yields C_T[K^2 D+384 exp(-K^2/128)] in the boundary-L1/middle-cut norm D; optimizing K gives the concave capped Osgood modulus. The proof uses accumulated Hilbert martingale noise rather than a maximum-based Hilbert gradient Lipschitz constant. All Gaussian arrays are unbounded; no trained-layer independence or teacher model is assumed. This is not a ReLU, fixed independent-data step, low-risk convergence, growing-depth, growing-time or dimension-free theorem, and it does not close the unrestricted permutation conjecture.
All globally bounded C2, bounded data, fully independent iid standard Gaussian initialization and simultaneous mean-field SGD hypotheses in the statement
Fixed d,T; initialization-selected matching; fresh data and common deterministic step schedule; shrinking steps for the vanishing-rate corollary
title: Gaussian depth-three SGD permutation connectivity via Osgood cut stability (unaudited owner draft)

Method: Polynomial mixing with plus Ising boundary conditions explicit structural calculation Result: The direct disagreement coupling proves the high-temperature part. Write N=n^2 and c=4*tanh(beta). A single disagreement vanishes if its site is updated, while at most four neighboring updates create disagreement with probability at most tanh(beta). Thus the expected Hamming distance contracts by1-(1-c)/N when c<1. Iteration and the coupling inequality give tmix(1/4)<=N*log(4*N)/(1-c), up to integer rounding. Check: Changing one neighboring spin changes the heat-bath plus probability by at most tanh(beta), since the conditional probability is(1+tanh(h))/2. A path coupling along single-spin differences extends the bound to arbitrary initial pairs. Boundary sites have at most four variable neighbors, so the estimate remains valid with fixed plus boundary. Obstruction: For4*tanh(beta)>=1 the coefficient ceases to contract. This is a failure of the local metric argument, not a lower bound showing slow mixing; the low-temperature interface regime remains unresolved here.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0194-polynomial-mixing-with-plus-ising-boundary-conditions

[Lemma 19 (A signed-measure criterion) of arXiv:2605.11451, '2605.11451'] Let $\mu$ be a nonzero finite signed measure on $[0,1]$ whose density has sign pattern $+,-,+$: it is positive on $(0,a)$, negative on $(a,b)$, and positive on $(b,1)$, allowing $a=0$ or $b=1$ by the corresponding one-sided interpretation. Assume
\[
 \int_0^1\dd\mu=0,
 \qquad
 \int_0^1 x\,\dd\mu(x)\le0.
\]
Then
\[
 \int_0^1\phi(x)\,\dd\mu(x)>0
\]
for every strictly decreasing strictly convex $C^1$ function $\phi$ on $[0,1]$.

Assume sigma:R->R has the following univariate approximation property (Assumption 1): there is a constant c_sigma>=1 such that every L-Lipschitz h:R->R constant outside [-R,R] can, for every delta>0, be uniformly approximated on R to error delta by a+sum_{j=1}^w alpha_j sigma(beta_j z-gamma_j), with w<=c_sigma R L/delta. Thus each fixed k admits polynomial dependence on both d and epsilon^(-1); this does not extend uniformly to all Lipschitz radial profiles or bound the network parameters.

[Lemma lem:geodesics_from_b of arXiv:2605.26048, 'Classification of the eternal solutions and multiple coalescing shocks in the KPZ fixed po'] [bhat-bus-soren]
Let $b:\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ be an eternal solution for the directed landscape. For $(x,t) \in \mathbb{R}^2$, define $g_{(x,t)}^{b,L/R}$ as in Definition (def:b-geodesics of the paper).
Then, the following hold
\begin{enumerate} [label=(\roman*), font=\normalfont]
\item  $g_{(x,t)}^{b,L}:(-\infty,t] \to \mathbb{R}$ \rm{(}resp. $g_{(x,t)}^{b,R}:(-\infty,t] \to \mathbb{R}$\rm{)} is a semi-infinite geodesic that is the leftmost (resp. rightmost) directed landscape geodesic between any two of its points. In particular, $g_{(x,t)}^{b,L}$ and $g_{(x,t)}^{b,R}$ are continuous functions $(-\infty,t] \to \mathbb{R}$.
\item  Let $s < r < t$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}$, and let $
w = g_{(x,t)}^{b,L}(r)$.
Then,
\[
g_{(x,t)}^{b,L}(s) = g_{(w,r)}^{b,L}(s),
\]
 In particular, recalling Definition (def:color of the paper), we have $\xi_{x,t}^b = \xi_{w,r}^b$. The analogous statement holds when replacing $L$ with $R$.
\item 
More generally, let $t = s_0 > s_1 > \cdots$ be any decreasing sequence with $\lim_{n \to \infty} s_n = -\infty$. Set $g(t) = x$, and for each $i \ge 1$, let $g(s_i)$ be \textit{any} maximizer of $z \mapsto b(z,s_{i}) + \mathcal{L}(z,s_i; g(s_{i - 1}),s_{i - 1})$ over $z \in \mathbb{R}$. Then, pick \textit{any} point-to-point geodesic of $\mathcal{L}$ from $(g(s_{i}),s_{i})$ to $(g(s_{i-1}),s_{i-1})$, and for $s_{i} < s < s_{i-1}$, let $g(s)$ be the location of this geodesic at time $s$. Then, $g:(-\infty,t] \to \mathbb{R}$ is a semi-infinite geodesic. 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:geodesics_from_b of arXiv:2605.26048

body:
Tarry (1900) showed by exhaustion that no Latin square of order 6 has an orthogonal mate, so Euler's thirty-six officers problem has no solution; a pair of orthogonal Latin squares exists for every order n except n = 2 and n = 6 (Bose, Shrikhande, Parker 1960, refuting Euler's conjecture for all n congruent to 2 mod 4 beyond 6). A Latin square has an orthogonal mate if and only if it can be decomposed into n disjoint transversals. For the cyclic Latin square of order n (the Cayley table of the integers mod n): when n is odd the diagonals give n disjoint transversals, so it has an orthogonal mate; when n is even it has no transversal at all, because a transversal would be a complete mapping of Z_n and the sum of all elements of Z_n, n/2, is not zero (a parity obstruction), so in particular it has no orthogonal mate. The even-order cyclic result is a statement about the cyclic square only; other Latin squares of the same even order (n = 4, 8, 10, ...) can have transversals and mates.
the transversal obstruction is for the cyclic square (Cayley table of Z_n) with n even; it does not transfer to arbitrary Latin squares of even order
Tarry's result is specific to order 6; orthogonal mates exist for every order other than 2 and 6
a transversal is a set of n cells, one per row, column and symbol
title: Tarry's theorem for order 6 (thirty-six officers) and transversals of cyclic Latin squares

[Cor lq-to-lr of arXiv:2601.19145, 'Stochastic Persistence in Infinite Dimensions'] Fix $T > 0,p > 1$, $q \in (2,\infty]$ and suppose that $u_t,y_t^+,y_t^- \in L^p(\Omega;C([0,T];C(\overline D)_+))$ and there is $0 < \eta^* \leq 1/2$ such that, for all $r \in [2,q)$, $Z_t \in L^p(\Omega \times [0,T]; \gamma(\mathcal{U},\mathcal{B}_{\eta^*-1/2,r}))$. With $y_t = y^+_t - y_t^-$, suppose
    $$u_t = S(t)u_0 + (S * y)_t + (S \diamond Z)_t \,.$$
    Then for all $0 < \eta \leq \eta^*  $ there is $r \in [2,q)$ such that
    $$
    \mathbb{E}\Big[\int_0^T \|u_t\|_{L^q}^pdt\Big] \lesssim \|u_0\|_{L^r}^p + \mathbb{E}\Big[\int_0^T \|y^+_t\|_{\eta-1,r}^pdt\Big] + \mathbb{E}\Big[\int_0^T \|Z_t\|_{\gamma(\mathcal{U},\mathcal{B}_{\eta-1/2,r})}^p dt\Big] \,.
    $$
    
    Specifically, we may choose 
    \begin{equation}
    \frac{1}{r} = \Big(\frac{\eta\wedge \frac{1}{p}}{N} + \frac{1}{q}\Big) \wedge \frac{1}{2} \,.
    \end{equation}
    Furthermore, the $\lesssim$ only depends on $p,q,\eta,r$ (and $T$, but the constant is uniform over all $T$ in any bounded subset of $(0,\infty)$).

body:
[Prop 14 of arXiv:2607.13849, 'Rearranged Stochastic Heat Equation with an Entropy Gradient Structure'] Let 
$h \in T/{\mathbb N}^*$
and 
$\varphi \in \mathcal{C}^1(\mathbb{S}) \cap {\mathcal U}^2(\mathbb{S})$.
Then, 
for all $0\leq s\leq t\leq T$,
	\begin{align}
		0\leq \langle \varphi, \mathscr{J}_{t}(X^{(h)}) -\mathscr{J}_{s}(X^{(h)})\rangle =\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=N_s+1}^{N_t} \int_0^h\int_{\mathbb{S}} \varphi'(\mathbf{x})\frac{1}{D_{\mathbf{x}}F_{\mu_{j},r}^{-1}(\mathbf{x})}\mathrm{d}\mathbf{x}\mathrm{d}r,
	\end{align}
    where, for all $r>0$,
\begin{align}
\mathbb{S}\ni \mathbf{x}\mapsto F_{\mu_j,r}^{-1}(\mathbf{x}) =(F_{\mu_j\star\Gamma_r})^{-1}(\mathbf{x}):= \tilde{F}_{\mu_{j},r}^{-1}(2{x}){\mathbbm 1}_{{(0,1/2)}}(x) + \tilde{F}_{\mu_{j},r}^{-1}(-2{x}) {\mathbbm 1}_{{(-1/2,0)}}({x}),
\end{align}
with $x$ denoting the representative of 
${\mathbf x}$ in $(-1/2,1/2]$, and 
with $\mu_{j}$ denoting the law of $X_{t_j^{-}}^{(h)}$, that is,  $\mu_{j}:= \mathrm{Leb}_{\mathbb{S}}\circ (X_{t_j^{-}}^{(h)})^{-1}$, for $j\in \{1,\ldots, N\}$,
and 
$\tilde{F}_{\mu_{j},t}(z):= (\tilde{F}_{\mu_{j}}\star\Gamma_t)(z)= (\tilde{F}_{\mu_{j}\star\Gamma_t})(z) $, for $z \in {\mathbb R}$. 

{Here, we impose 
$F_{\mu_j,r}^{-1}({\mathbf x})$ to be equal to 
$0$ when $x=0$ and $x=1/2$, but, due to the Gaussian convolution, $\mu_j \star \Gamma_r$ has the whole ${\mathbb R}$ as support. In particular, 
$\tilde{F}^{-1}_{\mu_j,r}(0)$
is equal to $-\infty$
and 
$\tilde{F}^{-1}_{\mu_j,r}(1)$
to $+ \infty$. 
Our choice of letting 
$F_{\mu_j,r}^{-1}({\mathbf x})$ be equal to $0$ when 
$x=0$ or $1/2$ is for simplicity. This does not have an impact on the proof.}

[Prop 29 of arXiv:2607.28238, 'Well-posedness and large deviations for the obstacle problem of first-order stochastic con'] Assume \textbf{Hypotheses (H1)} and \textbf{(H2)$'$} hold.
Let $\{h^\varepsilon\}_{\varepsilon>0}\subset S_M$ and $h\in S_M$ satisfy
\[
h^\varepsilon\rightharpoonup h
\qquad

Then, for any $\alpha>0$, the kinetic solutions $u_\alpha^{h^\varepsilon}$ and $u_\alpha^h$ of \eqref{eq:skeleton-obstacle-problem-viscous} with controls $h^{\varepsilon}$ and $h$, and with
initial data $u^0$ satisfy that, as $\varepsilon\rightarrow 0$,
\[
u_\alpha^{h^\varepsilon}\rightarrow u_\alpha^h\qquad\text{strongly in }L^2(Q_T).
\]

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a family of sequences of complex Wishart matrices, 
$$Z^i_N=Y^i_N(Y^i_N)^*\in M_N(L^\infty(X))\quad,\quad i\in I$$
with each $Y^i_N$ being a $N\times M$ matrix, with entries following the normal law $G_1$, and with all these entries being pairwise independent, the rescaled sequences of matrices
$$\frac{Z^i_N}{N}\in M_N(L^\infty(X))\quad,\quad i\in I$$
become with $M=tN\to\infty$ Marchenko-Pastur, each following the law $\pi_t$, and free.

body:
[Lemma L_SB of arXiv:2510.26724, 'Sharp Fuss-Catalan thresholds in graph bootstrap percolation'] Suppose that $H$ is a strictly balanced graph
and that $K$ is a proper subgraph 
of the graph $H\setminus e$,  
obtained from $H$ by 
removing some $e \in E(H)$. 
Let $x$ denote the number of vertices in 
$K$ that are not in $e$. 
Then we have that $0\leqslant x\leqslant v(H)-2$
and 
\[
e(K) \leqslant \lambda(H)x, 
\]  
with equality if and only if 
either 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $x=0$ and so $e(K)=0$; or else
\item $x=v(H)-2$ and $e(K)=e(H)-2$.
\end{enumerate}
In all other cases, in fact, 
\[
e(K) \leqslant \lambda(H) x-\xi(H),
\] 
where $\xi(H)>0$ is as in 
Definition (D_xi of the paper).

body:
[Corollary eq:approx-moment-bound of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[corollary]{cor:approx-matching}
Retain the setup of (thm:bulk-universality of the paper), except that exact matching in (equation eq:array-assumptions of the paper) is not assumed, and set
\[
 \delta_{I,r,N}=\abs{\mathbb E J_{I,N}^r-\mathbb E G^r},
 \qquad 1\le r\le m.
\]
Here
\[
 q_N=L^{p-1}N^{-(p-2)/2}(\log N)^{(p-1)/2},
\]
as in (equation eq:qN-main of the paper).  Then, for all sufficiently large \(N\),
\begin{equation}
 \left|\log\frac{\mathbb E\mathcal Z_{N,L}^J(V,\varepsilon,f)}
 {\mathbb E\mathcal Z_{N,L}^G(V,\varepsilon,f)}\right|
 \le C\sum_{I\in[N]^p}
 \left(q_N^{m+1}+\sum_{r=1}^m\delta_{I,r,N}q_N^r\right).
\end{equation}
For an identically distributed triangular array, with errors \(\delta_{N,r}\), the right-hand side is
\[
 CN^p\left(q_N^{m+1}+\sum_{r=1}^m\delta_{N,r}q_N^r\right).
\]
Thus a right-hand side of \(o(1)\) implies the ratio conclusion, and \(o(N)\) implies pressure convergence. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Sequential approximate moment matching

For a fixed total of n vertices, moving a vertex from a larger part to a part smaller by at least two increases the number of cross-edges, so the maximizing part sizes differ by at most one. [Lem 16 of arXiv:2608.05185, '\large\bf ON THE HEAT FLOW CONJECTURE FOR RANDOM MATRICES'] Let \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_N\) be the eigenvalues of
\(\mathbf{X}_{N,c}\), counted with algebraic multiplicity.  For every
bounded Borel measurable real-valued \(f\) and every \(\theta\in\R\), put
\[
 \mathsf{X}_f=\sum_{j=1}^{N}f(\lambda_j).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \log\E\!\left[
 \mathrm{e}^{\theta(\mathsf{X}_f-\E\mathsf{X}_f)}
 \right]
 \leq
 \frac{N\theta^2}{2}\left\|f\right\|_\infty^2
 \mathrm{e}^{\left|\theta\right|\left\|f\right\|_\infty}.
\end{equation}
Consequently, for every coupling of
\((\mathbf{X}_{N,c})_{N\geq1}\) having the prescribed marginals,
\begin{equation}
 L_{\mathbf{X}_{N,c}}
 \overset{\mathrm{w}}{\longrightarrow}\mu_c
 \qquad\text{almost surely}.
\end{equation}

	\[

			\left(
			\left\|\frac{\Gamma\Gamma^*}{M}\right\|_{\op}^{1/2}
			-1
			\right)_+
			\right]
		\le
		3\sqrt{\frac{d}{M}} .
	\]

body:
[Theorem divergence RW of arXiv:2411.14350, 'Randomized Geodesic Flow on Hyperbolic Groups'] [Woe93]

A random walk $(X_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ on a non-elementary hyperbolic group $G$ with transition probabilities given by $p(x,y)= \mu(x^{-1}y)$, where $\mu$ is a measure whose support is a finite generating set of $G$, converges to a random point $X_{\infty}\in \partial G$ almost surely. The hitting distribution on $\partial G$ is denoted by 
\begin{equation}
\nu_g(\cdot)= \mathbb P_g[X_\infty \in \cdot].
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma lem:maximal-selected-slice of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Put $j_i=\sqrt2a_i$, $\widehat A_i=\operatorname{ad}_{j_i}$, and let
$\mathcal A_i$ denote the zero Fourier projection for conjugation of
$\operatorname{Sym}_0(H)$ by the coordinate circle of plane $i$.  Let
$P_{i,m}$ be the Fourier projections for the same circle acting by
conjugation on $S_2(W)$.  For bounded status scalars $\alpha,\beta$, set
\[
 \mathcal F_{B,i}(Y)=\frac1{\sqrt N}\left(
 \alpha\{[\widehat A_i,X_B],Y\}a_i
 +\beta\{X_B,[\widehat A_i,Y]\}a_i\right)
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12q}$}
\]
and, for
\[
 \mathsf M_i^{\rm C}=|a_i\rangle\langle a_i|-N^{-1}I_W,
 \qquad
 \mathsf M_i^{\rm W}=\mathsf M_i^{\rm C}-X_{B_i},
\]
define the correctly ordered generalized defect
\[
 \mathcal D_{i}^{\bullet}(B,Z)
 =(n-2)\left[
 \mathcal F_{B,i}(P_{\mathcal R}\mathsf M_i^\bullet Z)
 -\mathsf M_i^\bullet\mathcal F_{B,i}(P_{\mathcal R}Z)
 \right].
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12q_1}$}
\]
Then:

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item for every own-circle-invariant $C_i$, the
zero-coefficient/zero-active-mode block vanishes,
\[
 \mathcal D_i^\bullet(C_i,P_{i,0}Z)=0;
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12q_2}$}
\]
\item for every $m\ne0$, every own-circle-invariant family
$C_i\in\operatorname{Sym}_0(H)$, and arbitrary ancillary contractions
$S_{i,-m}$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \left\|\frac1N\sum_i
   \bigl(\mathcal D_i^\bullet(C_i)P_{i,m}\bigr)
       \otimes S_{i,-m}\right\|_{\rm op}
 \le \frac CN
       \left(\frac1N\sum_i\|C_i\|_F^2\right)^{1/2};}
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12q_3}$}
\]
In particular $C_i=\mathcal A_iB$ gives the right side
$CN^{-1}\|B\|_F$.  The assertion is stable under passive Hilbert amplification, status,
reflection, adjunction, and full transpose; and
\item in the residual packetless cell
$(g,t_\partial,f_R;u,o,v)=(1,1,2;0,0,1)$, use its unique
$\mathsf V$ supernode.  In its coefficient-zero sector the complete
selected-time tensor is one prescribed bounded gate.  Writing
$\mathcal H_{\rm act}$ for the root-facing active curvature-letter
carrier and $E_{\rm in},E_{\rm out}$ for all other rails declared by the
native chronological matricization, that gate is the typed map
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 G_\Xi(B):\mathcal H_{\rm act}\otimes E_{\rm in}
       \longrightarrow W\otimes E_{\rm out},\\
 G_\Xi(B)=\frac1N\sum_i\sum_{m\ne0}
 \bigl(\mathcal D_i^\bullet(\mathcal A_iB)P_{i,m}\bigr)
 \otimes S_{i,-m},\\
 \|G_\Xi(B)\|_{\rm op}\le \frac CN\|B\|_F.
 \end{gathered}
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12q_4}$}
\]
This is the exact selected-time gate for the low-debit cell
\[
 (g,t_\partial,f_R;u,o,v)=(1,1,2;0,0,1).
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12q_5}$}
\]
The chronological sum and its endpoint energy are not part of this local
statement; they are proved separately in
(lem:packetless-root-time,lem:packetless-endpoint-energy of the paper).
\end{enumerate}

[Proposition 44 of arXiv:2607.08536, 'Soft edge limit of the Laguerre beta-ensemble at the lower edge'] Let $B(t)$ be standard Brownian Motion, and let $U\sim\textup{Unif }[0,1]$ be independent. Let $\mathcal{F}_t,t\ge 0$ be the filtration of $B$ enlarged with $U$. Suppose $\xi\sim\log\mathrm{beta}'(p,q)$ with $p+q\ge 10(p-q)^2+10$, then there exists a finite stopping time $\sigma$ with respect the filtration $\mathcal{F}_t, t\ge 0$ such that 
    \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
        \item $B(\sigma)+(p-q)\sigma\ed \xi $,
        \item $\pr(\sigma \ge \frac{1}{p+q})=1$ and $\pr(\sigma\neq \frac{1}{p+q})\le \frac{1}{p+q}$,
        \item There exist absolute constants $c_1,c_2>0$ such that $\pr(\sigma>\frac{u}{p+q})\le c_1e^{-c_2u^{1/3}}$.       
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:dual_strip of arXiv:2606.12143, 'Continuous stochastic flows driven by white noise and their duals'] Let both $(\sigma,b)$ and $(\sigma^*,b^*)$ satisfy Assumption~(assu:H of the paper) and conditions~(item:1a of the paper), (item:1b of the paper), (item:2c of the paper), and~(item:2d of the paper) on ${\mathbb R}$. Assume that for all $x\in I$ and $s,t\in{\mathbb R}$,
\begin{align}
\sigma^*(x,t,s)=-\sigma(x,t,s),\qquad
b^*(x,t)=-b(x,t)+\tfrac12\partial_x\bar\sigma(x,t).
\end{align}
Assume that the flows $(\mathcal S,\mathcal S^{\mathrm b})$ defined above exist and satisfy the absorption condition.
Then, almost surely, $\mathcal S^{\mathrm b}=\mathcal S^*$ in the sense of~(equation eq:def_dual_+ of the paper). In particular, $\{(\mathcal S^*_{-r,-x}(a),\,x\ge r)\}_{(a,r)\in I \times {\mathbb R}}$ forms a stochastic flow on $I\times{\mathbb R}$ with boundary conditions $\eta^*$, and $(\mathcal S^*)^*=\mathcal S$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:dual_strip of arXiv:2606.12143

body: In statistics, sufficiency is a property of a statistic computed on a sample dataset in relation to a parametric model of the dataset. A sufficient statistic for a model parameter contains all of the information that the dataset provides about that parameter. It is closely related to the concepts of an ancillary statistic which contains no information about the model parameters, and of a complete statistic which only contains information about the parameters and no ancillary information.

body:
[Definition of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] A \textbf{ramp function} is a function $f\colon [-\infty,+\infty)\to \bR$ which satisfies the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
    \item $f\circ \log\colon [0,+\infty)\to\bR$ is of class $C^2$,
    \item $f'(\lambda)>0$ and $f''(\lambda)>0$ for $\lambda\in\bR$,
    \item $\lim_{x\to 0^+}\frac{f''(\log x)}{x}=\frac{d}{dx}\Big|_{x=0}f\circ\log>0$,
    \item $\lim_{\lambda\to+\infty}f'(\lambda)=+\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'

[Lemma HLP of arXiv:2609.02541, 'A note on the norm of the embedding of $\text{PW}^2$ into $\text{PW}^q$'] Assume that $f,g: [0, \infty) \xrightarrow{} \mathbb{R}^{+}$ are non-increasing functions with 
    \begin{equation}
    
    \int_0^t f(x) dx \leq \int_0^t g(x)dx
    \end{equation}
    for all $0<t< \infty$.
    Then 
    $$\int_0^{\infty} \Phi(f(x))dx \leq \int_0^{\infty} \Phi(g(x))dx$$
    holds for every increasing convex function $\Phi: \mathbb{R}^{+} \xrightarrow{} \mathbb{R}^{+}$ such that $\Phi(0) = 0$.
title: Hardy--Littlewood--Pólya majorization principle

[Conjecture 9 of arXiv:2604.20617, 'Structured random perturbations of \\ tridiagonal twisted Toeplitz matrices'] Consider the symbol on $[0,1] \times \T$
\[ a(x,z) = \sum_{j=-q}^p a_j(x) z^j, \]
where for all $j$ $a_j(x)$ are continuous complex-valued functions on $[0,1]$. Let $\mu_n$ be the sequence of eigenvalue-counting measures
\[ \mu_n = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{\lambda \in \text{sp}(R_n(a))} \delta_{\lambda}. \]
Then $\mu_x$ converges weakly to the measure
\[ \mu = \int_0^1 \nu_x~dx. \] (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)

\end{enumerate}

[Lemma lem:berry-esseen of arXiv:2608.06159, 'Majority Dynamics on Resampled Sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi Graphs:\\[0.5ex] Gaussian Winner '] Let $\rX_{1}, \rX_{2}, \ldots, \rX_{n}$ be independent random variables with zero means, variances $\sigma_{1}^{2}, \sigma_{2}^{2}, \ldots, \sigma_{n}^{2}$, respectively, and finite absolute third moments $\E[|\rX_{j}|^{3}] = \rho_{j} < \infty$. Define the normalized random variable \(\rS_{n}:=\sum_{j=1}^{n}\rX_{j}/\sqrt{\sum_{j=1}^{n}\sigma_{j}^{2}}\). Let $F_{n}(x)$ and $\Phi(x)$ denote the cumulative distribution functions of $\rS_{n}$ and the standard normal distribution, respectively. There exists a universal constant $\gC_{\mathrm{BE}}$ such that, for any \(n\),
    \[\sup_{x\in \R} |F_{n}(x) - \Phi(x)| \leq \gC_{\mathrm{BE}} \sum_{j=1}^{n} \rho_{j} ( \sum_{j=1}^{n} \sigma_{j}^{2})^{-3/2},
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 10 (Product-shell bookkeeping) of arXiv:2609.01570, 'A Proof of Fraenkel's Conjecture'] For distinct \(a,b\in A\), write
\[
 d_{ab}=\normQ{ab^{-1}},\qquad P_{ab}=bd_{ab}.
\]
Then
\[
 P_{ab}\in\{a,Q-a,Q+a,2Q-a,2Q+a,\ldots\},
 \qquad \frac1{d_{ab}}=\frac b{P_{ab}}.
\]
For every \(a\in A\), every subset \(B\subseteq A\setminus\{a\}\),
and all real numbers \(L\ge0\) and \(T>0\), if
\[
 \sum_{b\in B}b\le L
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 P_{ab}\ge T\quad(b\in B),
\]
then
\[
 \sum_{b\in B}\frac1{d_{ab}}\le\frac LT.
\]
Also, \(P_{ab}=a\) implies \(b\mid a\).

In the special case \(s=1\), call \(b\) good when
\(b\mid Q-1\) or \(b\mid Q+1\).  If such a good \(b\) satisfies
\(P_{ab}\in\{Q-a,Q+a\}\), then \(b\mid a-1\) or \(b\mid a+1\).
If moreover \(a>1\) and \(b>a\), this forces \(b=a+1\).

[Definition def:Codimension of arXiv:2609.01464, 'Removability of non-isolated singularities for Einstein metrics and RCD spaces'] Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space of Hausdorff dimension $n$, and $\Sigma\subset X$ be a subset. Let $0\leqslant k\leqslant n$. We say that $\Sigma$ {\rm has 
    (Assouad)
    codimension greater than $k$} if either $k=n$ and $\Sigma=\emptyset$; or $k<n$ and there is $0\leqslant c<n-k$, $\mathcal{K} > 0$, and $\rho_0>0$ such that the following holds. For every $x\in X$, every $0<r\leqslant \rho_0$, and every $0<s\leqslant 1$ we have that $\Sigma\cap B_r(x)$ can be covered by $\leqslant \mathcal{K} s^{-c}$ balls of radius $sr$. We stress that if $k=n$, we have $\Sigma=\emptyset$.

[Definition of arXiv:2609.03959, 'The combinatorial Hopf algebra of signed graphs'] Given a connected signed graph $\Sigma = (V,E, \sigma)$ and $S\subseteq V$, define $I_\Sigma(S)$ to be the set of edges $e\in E$ satisfying one of the following conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\sigma(e)=+$ and the endpoints of $e$ are in $S$
\item $\sigma(e) = +$ and the endpoints of $e$ are in $V\backslash S$ 
\item $\sigma(e) = -$ and $e$ has one endpoint in $S$ and the other one in $V\backslash S$.
\end{itemize}
Then define $$\zeta_x(\Sigma) := \sum_{A \subseteq V} x^{rk(I_\Sigma(A))}. $$

[Lemma fixed-rec-var of arXiv:2608.19050, 'Online Permutation Embedding: \\ Optimal Stopping and Scaling Laws'] Let \(\mathcal{T}\) be a non-empty finite rooted binary tree, and let \(L\) and
\(R\) denote its left and right subtrees. Let \(\tau := \tau_1\) denote the stopping time for the root of $\mathcal{T}$ under the canonical algorithm. Then for almost every $x\in(0,1)$,
\[
    \EE[T^*_\mathcal{T} \mid X_\tau=x]
    =
    \EE[\tau\mid X_\tau=x]
    + \frac{\beta(L)}{x}
    + \frac{\beta(R)}{1-x},
\]
and
\[
    \pVar{T^*_\mathcal{T}\mid X_\tau=x} =
    \pVar{\tau\mid X_\tau=x} 
    + \frac{v(L)}{x^2}
    + \frac{v(R)}{(1-x)^2}
    + \frac{1-x}{x^2}\,\beta(L)
    + \frac{x}{(1-x)^2}\,\beta(R).
\]

[Lemma 3 (weak pullback calculus) of arXiv:2609.01093, 'Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold'] Let $X$ be an orientation-preserving global bi-Lipschitz map as above.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $E_i$ is skew-adjoint on $L^2(\mu)$. In particular
  \[
   \int_{\Real_y^n}(E_if)\phi d\mu=-\int_{\Real_y^n}f(E_i\phi)d\mu
  \]
  whenever $f,\phi,E_if,E_i\phi\in L^2(\mu)$.
\item[(ii)] Let $F=F^i\eframe_i$ be a vector field along $X$ whose Cartesian components belong to $L^1_{\rm loc}(\Real^n_y;\Rn)$. If
  $q,c^{ij}\in L^1_{\rm loc}(\mu)$, then
  \[
   \Div_{\gmetric}F=q,
   \qquad
   (\curl_{\gmetric}F)^{ij}=c^{ij}
  \]
  in the conjugated distributional sense if and only if
  \[
   \partial_a(J\Kmat_i^aF^i)=Jq,
   \qquad
   \partial_a\!\left(J\Kmat_i^aF^j-J\Kmat_j^aF^i\right)=Jc^{ij}
   \quad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\Real^n_y).
  \]
  Equivalently, for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Real^n_y)$,
  \begin{equation}
   \int q\varphi d\mu=-\int F^i\Kmat_i^a\partial_a\varphi d\mu,\qquad
   \int c^{ij}\varphi d\mu=-\int\bigl(F^j\Kmat_i^a-F^i\Kmat_j^a\bigr)
          \partial_a\varphi d\mu.
  \end{equation}
  With the convention in \eqref{eq:metric-tensor-divergence}, the same
  calculation gives, whenever
  $H:=\Div_{\gmetric}T\in L^1_{\rm loc}(\mu)$,
  \begin{equation}
   JH^j
   =\partial_a(J\Kmat_i^aT^{ji})
   \quad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\Real_y^n)
  \end{equation}
  for every locally integrable tensor $T$.
\item[(iii)] If $\mathcal C_X^{-1}F\in W^{1,p}_{\rm loc}$ for some
  $1\le p\le\infty$, then 
  \begin{equation}
      \partial_aF^i=A_a^jE_jF^i,
  \end{equation}
  and the conjugated divergence and curl in
  (ii) agree almost everywhere with the pointwise formulas $\Kmat^a_i\partial_aF^i$ and
  $\Kmat^a_i\partial_aF^j-\Kmat^a_j\partial_aF^i$.
\item[(iv)] The conjugated derivatives commute on their common
distributional domain:
  \[
   E_iE_j=E_jE_i.
  \]
\end{enumerate}

Let X be a real random variable with E[X^2] < infinity and G a sub-sigma-field. Among all G-measurable real A with E[A^2] < infinity, m = E[X | G] minimizes E[(X - A)^2], and A attains the minimum if and only if A = m almost surely; uniqueness holds only up to almost-sure equality. body:
[Lemma 20 (Rank reduction for an affine latent parameterization) of arXiv:2608.31157, 'Sharp Approximation Rates for Neural Networks with Affine Latent Parameterizations'] Let $\Phi$ be an architecture and let
$\calA\in\aff(M,P_\Phi)$ be given by
\[
 \calA(\bmxi)=\bmA\bmxi+\bma.
\]
Put $r_{\calA}:=\rank(\bmA)$.  If $r_{\calA}\ge1$, there is a
full-column-rank matrix
$\bmR\in\R^{P_\Phi\times r_{\calA}}$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \calA(\R^M)
 =\left\{\bmR\bmmu+\bma:
          \bmmu\in\R^{r_{\calA}}\right\}.
\end{equation}
Define the complete parameter vector in effective coordinates by
\[
 \bmtheta(\bmmu):=\bmR\bmmu+\bma.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \calF_{\Phi,\calA}
 =\left\{\Phi_{\bmtheta(\bmmu)}:
          \bmmu\in\R^{r_{\calA}}\right\}.
\]
If $r_{\calA}=0$, the family contains exactly one realized function.

[Theorem 13 of arXiv:2608.19179, 'A random walk on $p$-groups with a symmetric perfect pairing'] In the case of the matrix \[ \begin{mat}{ccc|c}
   & & & *\\
   & M& &\vdots\\
   & & & *\\ \hline
   * & \hdots & * & *
   \end{mat},\]
   the joint distribution of $g$ and $q$ satisfies the following properties:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(A)] $g$ is a uniformly random element of $ker(M)$.
\item[(B)] The joint distribution of $g$ and $q$ is invariant by the operation
\[
q \rightarrow q+a
\]
for any $a \in \Z_p$,
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Under the partition convention of Randomstrasse101 Definition 14.2, the shape with one edge uv, U={u} and V={v}, gives a symmetric n by n Rademacher matrix A with zero diagonal. Its expected operator norm is Theta(sqrt(n)), so this shape has exponents f=1/2 and g=0. Deterministically ||A||>=sqrt(n-1) by its Frobenius norm. For each unit real x, P(|x^T A x|>=r)<=2exp(-r^2/4); a 1/4 sphere net of size at most 9^n and integration give the O(sqrt(n)) expectation bound. This does not resolve the existence conjecture for every fixed shape.

[Defi eq: 2.1.3 local conv of arXiv:2605.03151, 'Giants through Higher-Order paths in Random Simplicial Complexes'] We say that a sequence of $d$-dimensional finite random simplicial complexes $(X_n)_{n \geq 1}$ \textit{converges locally weakly in probability} to a $(d-1)$-rooted random simplicial complex $(X, o)$ with (possibly random) law $\mu$, when, for every $r \geq 0$ and $H_* \in \mathcal{S}_{d-1}$,
\[  \tag{2.1.3}
\frac{1}{s_{d-1} \left( X_n \right)} \sum_{\sigma \in S_{d-1}(X_n)} \1 \left\{ B_{X_n}(\sigma; r) \cong H_* \right\} \overset{\mathbb{P}}{\to} \mu \left( B_X(o; r) \cong H_* \right).
\]

body:
[Applemma 13 (Theorem~3.27 in~\cite{K97}) of arXiv:2607.17396, '2607.17396'] Let $(\mathcal{X}, d_\mathcal{X})$ and $(\mathcal{Y}, d_\mathcal{Y})$ be metric spaces, and let
$\left\{\xi_{n}, n\geq 1\right\}$ and $\xi$ be random elements with values in $\mathcal{X}$
such that
$
\xi_n \xrightarrow{\mathcal{D}} \xi$ as $n\to\infty$.
Let $f:\mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ and $f_{n}: \mathcal{X}\to \mathcal{Y}$, $n \geq 1$, be measurable mappings,
and let $C\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{X})$ be such that
$
\mathbf{P}(\xi\in C)=1.
$
Assume that
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty} d_\mathcal{Y}\bigl(f_{n}(s_{n}), f(s) \bigr)=0
$$
whenever
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty} d_\mathcal{X}(s_{n},s)=0, \qquad s\in C,\quad s_{n} \in \mathcal{X},\ n \geq 1.
$$
Then
$$
f_{n}(\xi_{n})\xrightarrow{\mathcal{D}} f(\xi), \ \  n \to \infty.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem~3.27 in~\cite{K97}

body:
[Lemma L:Xalpha-bd of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Take any $\alpha_0 \in (0, 1)$, $\delta_0 > 0$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $j_0, x \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ with $x, j_0 \le n/10$. Take parameter $\alpha \ge \alpha_0$, and set (for $j\in\llbracket1-n, n+x-1 \rrbracket$)
$\bar X(j) = \bar X[j, 1; x, n]_\textsf{L}$.
Then there exists $c > 0$ depending only on $\alpha_0, \delta_0$ such that for all $\epsilon \in (0, n^{-1/3})$ we have
$$
\mathbb{P}\left(\max_{j\in\llbracket0,n+x-1 \rrbracket} \bar X(j) - \frac{\delta_0(j-j_0)^2}{n} \ge \Delta_\alpha(n) + \epsilon n\right) \le 2\exp\left(-c \epsilon^{3/2}n \left(1 \wedge \frac{\epsilon^{1/2}}{(1/2 - \alpha)\vee 0}\right) \right).
$$

body:
[Lem 11 of arXiv:2604.13134, '\bf From Gaussian to Gumbel: extreme eigenvalues of complex Ginibre products with exact ra'] Recall   
 \[a_n = \sqrt{\log(\alpha_n + 1)} - \frac{\log(\sqrt{2\pi}\log(\alpha_n + e^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}}))}{\sqrt{\log(\alpha_n + e)}} \quad \text{and}\quad b_n=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\log(\alpha_n + e)}}.\]Set
	$$u_n(j, x) = \frac{j-1}{\sqrt{\alpha_n}} + a_n + b_n x.$$
	For  $|x|\leq2\log\log \alpha_n$ and as $n\to\infty,$  the following estimates hold uniformly: 
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item If $1\leq j\leq j_n,$ then
		$$ M^{(n)}_{j, j}(x)=\frac{1+O((\log \alpha_n)^{-1})}{\sqrt{2\pi}u_n(j,x)}\exp(-\frac{u^{2}_n(j, x)}{2}).
		$$
		\item If $j_n< j\leq  t_n,$ then
		$$
			M^{(n)}_{j, j}(x)\leq \frac{1}{u_n(j,x)}e^{-\frac{3u^{2}_n(j, x)}{8}}+n^{-4/5} .
		$$
	\end{enumerate}
title: Lem 11 of arXiv:2604.13134

Every thick subcategory of the category of $p$-local finite spectra $\operatorname{Sp}_{(p)}^c$ is of the form $\mathcal{C}_{p, n} = \{X \in \operatorname{Sp}_{(p)}^c \mid K(p, m)_*(X) = 0 \text{ for all } m < n\}$ for some $0 \le n \le \infty$. p is a prime number

For any set of dimension d, a power exponent s>d gives zero Hausdorff measure, while s<d gives infinite measure; at s=d either zero, finite positive, or infinite behavior can occur. Multiplying r^d by a slowly varying factor can change the critical measure while leaving the dimension unchanged. Check: The two off-critical conclusions are the defining threshold property of Hausdorff dimension. At the critical exponent, a smooth interval has finite positive H^1, while a countable union of disjoint intervals with divergent total length has infinite H^1; critical zero examples exist among dimension-one Cantor sets. Obstruction: One needs fine local occupation estimates, not just dimension or existence of Minkowski content. The predicted logarithmic correction has not been proved here.

[Definition of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] Let \((\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})\) be a complete probability space supporting a family of \(d\)-dimensional
	Wiener processes \((W(\cdot,\xi))_{\xi \in [0,1]}\) and a family of initial random variables
	\((X_0(\xi))_{\xi \in [0,1]}\) taking values in \(\mathbb{R}^d\). A family of stochastic processes
	\(X=(X(\cdot,\xi))_{\xi \in [0,1]}\) is called a \emph{strong solution} to (equation eq:fibered-McKean-Vlasov-SDE of the paper) if
	the following conditions hold: 
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
		\item For almost every \(\xi \in [0,1]\), \(\mu^{\xi}=\mathrm{Law}(X(\cdot,\xi))\).  
		\item For almost every \(\xi \in [0,1]\), the process \(X(\cdot,\xi)\) has continuous paths, is adapted to the filtration generated by the Wiener process \(W(\cdot,\xi)\) and the initial condition \(X_0(\xi)\), and satisfies the following integral equation \(\mathbb{P}\)-a.s.:
		\[
			X(t,\xi) = X_0(\xi) + \int_{0}^{t} b_{\xi}(s,X(\cdot,\xi),\mu) \,ds + \int_{0}^{t} \sigma_{\xi}(s,X(\cdot,\xi),\mu) \,dW(s,\xi), \quad t \in [0,T].
		\]  
	\end{enumerate}
	We say that \emph{strong uniqueness} holds if any two strong solutions \(X\) and \(X'\), defined on the same probability space, driven by the same family of Wiener processes, and starting from the same initial conditions, satisfy \(X(\cdot,\xi)=X'(\cdot,\xi)\) \(\mathbb{P}\)-a.s.\ for almost every \(\xi \in [0,1]\).

	We say that \emph{uniqueness in law} holds if for any two strong solutions \(X\) and \(X'\), possibly defined on different probability spaces and driven by different Wiener processes but sharing the same fibered law for their initial conditions, one has that \(\mathrm{Law}(X(\cdot,\xi))=\mathrm{Law}(X'(\cdot,\xi))\) for almost every \(\xi \in [0,1]\).

[Lem 15 of arXiv:2604.26396, '\LARGE Limiting spectral distributions of large consistent rank correlation matrices'] \citep[Lemma~2.12]{bai2010spectral}
Let $\{X_k\}_{k=1}^n$ be a complex martingale difference sequence with respect to the filtration $\{\rF_k\}_{k=0}^n$. Then, for $p>1$,
$$
\E\Bigl[\Bigl|\sum_{k=1}^n X_k\Bigr|^p\Bigr]
\leq
K_p\E\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{k=1}^n |X_k|^2\Bigr)^{p/2}\Bigr],
$$
where $K_p>0$ is a constant. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem {\cite[Theorem~1.1.4 and Remark~1.1.5 of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ I:\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple C'] {LevelLineGFFI}}]
Suppose that $h$ is a GFF on $\BH$ with piecewise constant boundary conditions that change only finitely many times. For all $u \in \BR$ and $x \in \partial \BH$, we let $\gamma_u^x$ be the level line of $h$ with height $u$ starting from $x$ and ending at $\infty$ (when it exists). Fix $x_2 \leq x_1$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $u_2 < u_1$, then $\gamma_{u_2}^{x_2}$ a.s.\ stays to the left of $\gamma_{u_1}^{x_1}$ (possibly touching it).
\item If $u_2 = u_1$, then $\gamma_{u_2}^{x_2}$ may intersect $\gamma_{u_1}^{x_1}$ and, upon intersecting, the two curves merge and never separate.
\item If $u_1 - u_2 \geq 2 \lambda$, then $\gamma_{u_1}^{x_1}$ and $\gamma_{u_2}^{x_2}$ do not intersect each other a.s.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Load-bearing hypotheses: A is densely defined, dissipative, AND Ran(λ_0 − A) = X (or at least dense) for some λ_0 > 0. What fails without the range condition: a dissipative operator can be closed and densely defined and still generate nothing. Counterexample: X = L²(0, 1), A f = f' with D(A) = {f ∈ H¹(0,1) : f(0) = f(1) = 0}. Then A is densely defined and closed, and Re⟨f', f⟩ = (|f(1)|² − |f(0)|²)/2 = 0, so A is dissipative (indeed both A and −A are). But solving λf − f' = g with f(0) = 0 gives f(x) = −∫_0^x e^{λ(x−s)}g(s) ds, and the second boundary condition f(1) = 0 forces the constraint ∫_0^1 e^{−λs} g(s) ds = 0: Ran(λ − A) is a closed subspace of codimension 1, not dense, for every λ > 0. Hence A is not a generator, although dropping one boundary condition (D = {f ∈ H¹ : f(1) = 0}) gives exactly the generator of the left shift semigroup. The range condition is what encodes 'the right number of boundary conditions'. What fails without density: X = C[0,1] with the sup norm, A f = f' on D(A) = {f ∈ C¹[0,1] : f(1) = 0}. Solving λ f − f' = g with f(1) = 0 gives f(x) = ∫_x^1 e^{λ(x−s)}g(s)ds, so ‖f‖ ≤ ‖g‖/λ: A is dissipative and Ran(λ − A) = X for every λ > 0. Yet the closure of D(A) is {f ∈ C[0,1] : f(1) = 0}, a proper closed subspace, so A generates no C_0-semigroup on C[0,1] (generators are densely defined); it generates one on the smaller space. Density is automatic only when X is reflexive, which C[0,1] is not. Related trap: for the norm inequality version, dissipativity means ‖(λ − A)x‖ ≥ λ‖x‖ for all λ > 0 - checking it for a single λ, or checking Re⟨Ax, x⟩ ≤ 0 only on a core without knowing the operator is closed or closable there, proves nothing about the closure being a generator unless the range condition is verified on that same core.
X is a Banach space
A is dissipative
the range condition Ran(λ_0 − A) = X (or dense) is the hypothesis at issue
title: Pitfall: Lumer-Phillips Needs the Range Condition (and Density) - Dissipativity Alone Is Not Enough

        &= \mathbb{E}[X_1\,|\,\mathcal{F}_1']\cdot\mathbb{E}[X_2\,|\,\mathcal{F}_2'].

body:
[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2606.16164, 'A Low-Regularity Semigroup Sewing Lemma via Quotient Structures'] Let $\tau\in[0,T]$, $\beta\in\mathbb R$, and $\gamma\in(0,1]$. Then there exists a linear map
\[
\mathcal I_\tau^{\mathrm d}: \mathcal A^{\gamma}(\Delta_\tau^2;B_\beta) \to C([0,\tau];B_\beta),
\]
obtained from a dyadic recursion on $\mathcal D^\tau$ and continuous extension to $[0,\tau]$, such that, for every $A\in \mathcal A^{\gamma}(\Delta_\tau^2;B_\beta)$, $\mathcal I_\tau^{\mathrm d}(A)_0=0$. If we define the dyadic remainder $\mathcal R_\tau^{\mathrm d}(A):=A-\delta\mathcal I_\tau^{\mathrm d}(A)$, then
$
\delta \mathcal R_\tau^{\mathrm d}(A)=\delta A.
$
Moreover, if $\gamma\in(0,1)$, then
\begin{equation}

\mathcal R_\tau^{\mathrm d}(A)\in C^{\gamma}(\Delta_\tau^2;B_\beta)\ \text{\, and \, }\ \|\mathcal R_\tau^{\mathrm d}(A)\|_{\gamma,\beta;\tau}\le C_\gamma\|\delta A\|_{\gamma,\beta;\tau};
\end{equation}
if $\gamma=1$, then
\begin{equation}

\mathcal R_\tau^{\mathrm d}(A)\in C_{\log}^{1}(\Delta_\tau^2;B_\beta)\ \text{\, and \, }\ \|\mathcal R_\tau^{\mathrm d}(A)\|_{1,\log;\tau,\beta}\le C_{T}\|\delta A\|_{1,\beta;\tau}.
\end{equation}
while, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, $\|\mathcal R_\tau^{\mathrm d}(A)\|_{1-\varepsilon,\beta;\tau}\le C_{\varepsilon,T}\|\delta A\|_{1,\beta;\tau}$. Here the constants can be chosen independently of $\tau\in[0,T]$.
