[Definition 240 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] If $\boldsymbol{v} \in \amsmathbb{R}^H$ is non-zero, we set $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}} = (\boldsymbol{v} \otimes \boldsymbol{v},0)\in (\amsmathbb{R}^{H} \otimes \amsmathbb{R}^{H}) \oplus \amsmathbb{R}$ and construct the complex surface
\[
\Sigma^{[2]}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}}} = \left( \bigsqcup_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{w}} \in \mathfrak{G}^{[2]}.\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}}} (\widehat{\amsmathbb{H}}^{+} \sqcup \widehat{\amsmathbb{H}}^-) \times (\widehat{\amsmathbb{H}}^+ \sqcup \widehat{\amsmathbb{H}}^-) \right)\Big/\sim.
\]
The equivalence relation identifies for each $h \in [H]$, $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,\epsilon_1',\epsilon_2' \in \{\pm 1\}$ and $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{w}} \in \mathfrak{G}^{[2]}.\boldsymbol{v}$:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\prod_{i = 1}^2 (\widehat{\amsmathbb{R}}^{\epsilon_i} \setminus \amsmathbb{B}^{\epsilon_i})$ with $\prod_{i = 1}^{2} (\widehat{\amsmathbb{R}}^{\epsilon_i'} \setminus \amsmathbb{B}^{\epsilon_i'})$ both in the $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{w}}$-th copy;
\item $\overline{\amsmathbb{B}}_{h}^{+} \times \widehat{\amsmathbb{H}}^{\epsilon}$ in the $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{w}}$-th copy with $\overline{\amsmathbb{B}}_{h}^- \times \widehat{\amsmathbb{H}}^{\epsilon}$ in the $T_1^{(h)}(\widetilde{\boldsymbol{w}})$-th copy;
\item $\widehat{\amsmathbb{H}}^{\epsilon} \times \overline{\amsmathbb{B}}_h^+$ in the $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{w}}$-th copy with $\widehat{\amsmathbb{H}}^{\epsilon} \times \overline{\amsmathbb{B}}_h^-$ in the $T_2^{(h)}(\widetilde{\boldsymbol{w}})$-th copy.
\end{itemize}

Let us denote for $\textnormal{supp}_i(\widetilde{\boldsymbol{w}}) = \big\{h \in [H] \quad \big|\quad T_i^{(h)}(\widetilde{\boldsymbol{w}}) \neq \widetilde{\boldsymbol{w}}\big\}$ for $i = 1,2$. The image in $\Sigma^{[2]}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}}}$ of the $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{w}}$-th copy of
\[
\bigcup_{ \epsilon,\epsilon' \in \{\pm 1\}} \bigg(\widehat{\amsmathbb{H}}^{\epsilon} \setminus \bigcup_{g \in \textnormal{supp}_1(\widetilde{\boldsymbol{w}})} \overline{\amsmathbb{B}}_g^{\epsilon}\bigg) \times \bigg(\widehat{\amsmathbb{H}}^{\epsilon'} \setminus \bigcup_{g \in \textnormal{supp}_2(\widetilde{\boldsymbol{w}})} \overline{\amsmathbb{B}}_g^{\epsilon'}\bigg)
\]
is denoted $\Sigma^{[2]}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}},\widetilde{\boldsymbol{w}}}$ and called the $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{w}}$-th sheet. The $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}}$-th sheet is called the principal sheet.

[Definition 2 of arXiv:2608.30859, 'Conservation Laws with Discontinuous Flux:\\ A First Application to Traffic Flow'] A BV function is a \emph{weak solution} to \eqref{eq:original} with initial data as in (H1)-(H2) if:
\begin{itemize}
    \item The map $t \to u(t, \cdot)$ is continuous from $[0, T]$ to $L^1_{loc}(\mathbb R)$,  satisfies the initial conditions, and $0\leq u(t,x) \leq u_{\max}$.
    \item There exists a Lebesgue measurable function $\theta (t, x):[0, T] \times \mathbb R \to [0, 1]$ such that
    \[u_x(t, \cdot) = \chi_{\theta=1}[u_x(t, \cdot)]_+ - \chi_{\theta=0}[u_x(t, \cdot)]_- \quad \text{for a.e.} \; t \in [0, T]. \]
    \item For every compactly supported test function $\varphi (t, x) \in C_c((0, T) \times \mathbb R)$:
    \[\int_0^T \int_{\mathbb R} u \varphi_t + (\theta f(u) + (1-\theta) g(u)) \varphi_x \, dx \, dt=0.\]
\end{itemize}
title: Definition 2 of arXiv:2608.30859

body: [Lem 21 of arXiv:2607.21759, 'Marchenko--Pastur law for tensor powers of exchangeable unconditional vectors'] For $r \leq d \leq n$, the following inequality holds when $d - r \leq n - d$: \[\binom{n - d}{d - r} \leq \biggl(\frac{d}{n}\biggr)^r \binom{n}{d}.\]

[Lemma 41 of arXiv:2604.08127, 'Asymptotics of Brownian occupation measures \\ with unusually large intersections'] Suppose $d \ge 1$, $q > 1$, and $0 < \gamma$ such that $d(q-1) < 2q$ and $\gamma \le \frac{2q}{d(q-1)}$. Then the variational problem
    \[
    \rho_{d, q, \gamma} = \sup \{ \| \xi \|_q^{\gamma} - \mathcal{I}(\xi) : \xi \in \widetilde{\mathcal{X}}_{\le 1}(\mathbb{R}^d) \} = \left(\frac{2q - \gamma d(q-1)}{2q} \right) \left( \frac{\gamma d(q-1)}{q} \right)^{\frac{\gamma d(q-1)}{2q - \gamma d(q-1)}} \kappa_{d, q}^{\frac{4\gamma q}{2q - \gamma d(q-1)}}
    \]
    has a unique solution, which is an element of $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$.

[Theorem 1 (Relaxation to condensation) of arXiv:2609.01436, '2609.01436'] Assume \cref{ass:CL}, and let $(F_t)_{t\geq0}$ be a conservative isotropic measure solution with particle number $N>0$ and energy $E>0$. Let $F_{\rm be}$ be the Bose--Einstein equilibrium with the same particle number and energy. Suppose that \({\overline T}/{\overline T_c}<1, \)
or equivalently, $N_c=F_{\rm be}(\{0\})>0$, and that \(\|F_t-F_{\rm be}\|_1^\circ\to 0\) as \(t\to\infty\). Then there exists a finite time $T\geq0$ such that \begin{equation} N_c(T)=F_T(\{0\})>0. \end{equation} Furthermore, the condensate persists for all later times: \begin{equation} N_c(t) \geq e^{-\sqrt{NE}(t-T)}N_c(T)>0, \qquad t\geq T. \end{equation} As $t\to\infty$, \(N_c(t)\to N_c \) and \(\|F_t-F_{\rm be}\|_1\to 0. \) (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma LEM:Dr1 of arXiv:2412.09790, 'Critical threshold for weakly interacting log-correlated focusing Gibbs measures'] Given $N \in \mathbb{N}$, 
let $Y_N = \pi_N Y(1)$, 
where $Y$ is as in (equation P2 of the paper).
Then,  there exist small $\varepsilon > 0$ and  a constant $c_0=c_0(\varepsilon)>0$ 
	such that for any $\delta>0$, we have
\begin{align*}
		\bigg|\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}:\! Y_N^3\!:\Theta dx\bigg|
		&\le
		C(\delta)\|:\! Y_N^3\!:\|_{W^{-\varepsilon,\infty}}^2
		+\delta\|\Theta\|_{H^{\frac d2}}^2,\\
		\bigg|\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}:\! Y_N^2\!:\Theta^2 dx\bigg|
		&\le
		C(\delta)\|:\! Y_N^2\!:\|_{W^{-\varepsilon,\infty}}^4
		+\delta\Big(\|\Theta\|_{H^{\frac d2}}^2
		+\|\Theta\|_{L^4}^4\Big),\\
		\bigg|\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}Y_N\Theta^3 dx\bigg|
		&\le
		C(\delta)\|Y_N\|_{W^{-\varepsilon,\infty}}^{c_0}
		+\delta
		\Big(\|\Theta\|^2_{H^{\frac d2}}
		+\|\Theta\|_{L^4}^4\Big),
	\end{align*}
	
	
	
	\noindent
	uniformly in $N\in\mathbb{N}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma LEM:Dr1 of arXiv:2412.09790

[Satz thm:HOSph of arXiv:2507.08692, 'Some notes on higher order concentration of measure'] Let $n \ge 3$, and let $f$ be a function which is $\mathcal{C}^d$ in some neighbourhood of ${\mathbb S}_p^{n-1}$ and with $\mu_{p,n}$-mean zero.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item Assuming that $\lVert f^{(k)} \rVert_{\mathrm{op}(q),q} \le (3^{1/q} \cdot 4 q^{1/p} n^{-1/p})^{d-k}$ for all $k=1,\ldots,d-1$ and $\lVert f^{(d)} \rVert_{\mathrm{op}(q),\infty} \le 1$, it holds that
		\[
		\int \exp\Big\{c_pn |f|^{p/d} \Big\} d\mu_{p,n} \le 2,
		\]
		where a possible choice of the constant $c_{p,d}$ is given by
		\[
		c_p = \frac{(q^p-1)^p(p-1)^p}{2 \cdot 3^{p-1}\log^{p-1}(2)q^{p^2+2}e}.
		\]
		\item For any $t\ge 0$, it holds that
		\begin{align*}
			&\mu_{p,n}(|f| \ge t)\le\\
			&2 \exp\Big\{- \frac{C_pn}{d^p} \min\Big(\min_{k=1, \ldots,d-1} \Big(\frac{t}{\lVert f^{(k)} \rVert_{\mathrm{op}(q),q}}\Big)^{p/k}, \Big(\frac{t}{\lVert f^{(d)} \rVert_{\mathrm{op}(q),\infty}}\Big)^{p/d}\Big)\Big\},
		\end{align*}
		where a possible choice of the constant $C_{p,d}$ is given by
		\[
		C_p = \frac{(p-1)^p}{4 \cdot 3^{p-1}q^2\log^{p-2}(2) e^p}.
		\]
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Identify which estimate needs d > 6 and whether it is an artefact. Result: The source's proof of the Alexander-Orbach behaviour for the oriented IIC uses a zigzag-path count converging like sum_m m^{(4-d)/2}, which needs d > 6, while the oriented IIC's mean-field structure (Hofstad-den Hollander-Slade) holds for d > 4. The zigzag count controls the resistance between the origin and level n via the number of paths that go up, come back down and go up again; in d = 5, 6 these counts diverge, meaning the crude flow bound fails, but the true resistance may still be of order n (mean-field, tree-like) because the divergent terms are overcounting: paths in the oriented IIC cannot return to earlier times, so a zigzag in the bound corresponds to two disjoint upward paths connected through the IIC's backbone, whose number is controlled by the two-point function squared, giving a convergent sum for d > 4 if the backbone is used correctly. So I expect the Alexander-Orbach value d_s = 4/3 to hold for the oriented IIC in d = 5, 6 as well, and the obstruction to be technical (the resistance lower bound of Kumagai-Misumi type needs a better flow construction using the backbone). This is a prediction with a proposed route (flow along the oriented backbone with branching at the pivotal levels), not a proof. Key identity: Oriented paths cannot return to earlier times, so the zigzag overcount should be replaceable by a backbone-branching flow with convergence for d > 4. Obstruction: The improved flow construction is not carried out.

body:
Let N,d be positive integers, B_x,B_w>0, B_y>=0, lambda>=0 and 0<=alpha<=beta with alpha+lambda>0. Suppose 0<epsilon<B_x B_w/2. Put kappa=(beta+lambda)/(alpha+lambda), R=max{B_x B_w,B_y,1}, and L=ceil(2 kappa log(B_x B_w/(2 epsilon)))+1. There exists one fixed L-layer attention-only transformer, depending on these bounds and not on the dataset, with token dimension D=2d+3 and at most three heads per layer, with the following property. For every training dataset (x_i,y_i) for 1<=i<=N and query x_(N+1) such that ||x_i||_2<=B_x for all 1<=i<=N+1, |y_i|<=B_y, alpha I <= X^T X/N <= beta I, and ||w_ridge||_2<=B_w/2, where X has rows x_i^T and w_ridge minimizes (1/(2N)) sum_i (<w,x_i>-y_i)^2+(lambda/2)||w||_2^2, its output prediction differs from <w_ridge,x_(N+1)> by at most epsilon. Its second-to-last-layer tokens all contain an estimate of w_ridge with Euclidean error at most epsilon/B_x. The architecture uses normalized ReLU attention: on S tokens h_i, each layer sends h_i to h_i+(1/S) sum_m sum_j ReLU(<Q_m h_i,K_m h_j>) V_m h_j, with no MLP. Initially h_i=[x_i;y'_i;0_d;1;t_i], where y'_i=y_i and t_i=1 for training tokens, and y'_(N+1)=t_(N+1)=0. The prediction is coordinate d+1 of the last query token; the weight estimate is coordinates d+2 through 2d+1 of each penultimate token. The parameter norm max_layer(max_m{||Q_m||op,||K_m||op}+sum_m ||V_m||op) is at most 4R+8/(beta+lambda). Source: arXiv:2306.04637, Theorem 4, equations (3)–(6), PDF pages 5–7; proof Appendix D.1, PDF pages 41–42. This is the paper's normalized-ReLU-attention architecture.

Gradient descent starts at zero with step 1/(beta+lambda). Strongly convex gradient descent gives ||w_t-w_ridge||_2 <= exp(-t/(2 kappa)) ||w_ridge||_2. For T=L-1 the assumed solution bound gives ||w_T-w_ridge||_2<=epsilon/B_x. The paper implements these T steps exactly in attention layers: the derivative s-t of the square loss equals 2 ReLU((s-t)/2)-2 ReLU(-(s-t)/2), so two heads encode the residual-gradient terms, and a third head encodes the ridge penalty. value of \(p\). Then the expected mean-field centered Lyapunov functional satisfies
\begin{equation}
    \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm d t}\overline{\mathcal L}_p(t)
    \leqslant
    -\lambda_{p}\,\overline{\mathcal L}_p(t).
\end{equation}

Moreover, for the quadratic case \(p=2\), there exists a local martingale
\(\overline M_{2,t}^J\) such that the averaged pathwise functional
\(\overline L_2^J(t)\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
    \mathrm d \overline L_2^J(t)

    -\lambda_{2}\,\overline L_2^J(t)\,\mathrm d t

        \right|^2
    \right)\mathrm d t
    +
    \mathrm d \overline M_{2,t}^J,
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
    K_{\mathrm{tr}}
    :=
    \frac{\sigma^2\tau(S)}{m^2}.
\end{equation}

For two independent collections of n independent uniform unit-square points sharing n labels, the maximum same-label induced subposet agreement C_n satisfies liminf E C_n/n^(1/3)>=exp(-2). Partition each square into m-by-m cells, m=floor(n^(1/3)). Keep a label when its two points occupy the same cell, and retain it only if no other kept label shares that row or column. The retained labels have identical comparisons in both posets. For a fixed label the match probability is1/m^2; conditional on its cell, another label is a conflicting match with probability(2m-1)/m^4. Therefore the expected retained number is n/m^2*[1-(2m-1)/m^4]^(n-1), asymptotic to exp(-2)*n^(1/3).

Second check. Two retained labels have distinct row and column indices, so each of their coordinate orderings is determined by cell indices in both independent samples. Independence over labels gives the exact no-conflict probability. The bound is liminf E C_n/n^(1/3)>=exp(-2).

Limits. The isolated-cell matching discards many usable labels and supplies no matching upper constant. Optimizing a local grid construction does not establish existence of the global optimal limit.

[Definition 6 of arXiv:2606.31287, '\bf Heat kernel lower bound estimates for symmetric pure jump processes via averaged jump '] \rm 
 Let $(\sX,d,m,\sE, \sF)$ be an MMD space.
\begin{enumerate}  
\item[\rm (i)] We say that the Dirichlet form $(\sE, \sF)$ is conservative if its associated Hunt process is conservative. 

\item[\rm (ii)] We say that the transition density upper bound estimate ${\rm UHK}(\phi)$ holds for the Dirichlet form $(\sE, \sF)$ if the Hunt process $X$ associated with $(\sE, \sF)$  has a jointly continuous density function
 $p(t, x, y)$ on $(0, \infty )\times \sX \times \sX$ with respect to the measure $m$ and there is a positive constant $c_{\ref{e:2.6}} >0 $ so that 
\begin{equation}
 p(t, x, y) \leq c_{\ref{e:2.6}}\left( \frac{1}{V(x, \phi^{-1}(t))} \wedge
\frac{t}{V(x, d(x,y))\phi (d(x, y))} \right)
\end{equation}
for any $t > 0$ and $x, y \in \sX$.  
Here $\phi^{-1}$ denotes the inverse function of $\phi$.
 
\item[\rm (iii)] We say that the near diagonal lower bound estimate ${\rm NLHK}(\phi)$
 holds for the Dirichlet form $(\sE, \sF)$ if the Hunt process $X$ associated with $(\sE, \sF)$  has a jointly continuous density function $p(t, x, y)$ on $(0, \infty)\times \sX \times \sX$ with respect to the measure $m$ and there exist constants $\e_{\ref{e:1.9}} \in (0,1)$ and $c_{\ref{e:1.9}} > 0$ such that  
\be 
p(t, x ,y )\ge \frac{c_{\ref{e:1.9}}}{V(x , \phi^{-1}(t))} \quad \hbox{for any } x ,y \in \sX
\hbox{ with }  d(x, y) < \e_{\ref{e:1.9}}\phi^{-1}(t)  .
\ee

 \item[\rm (iv)]  We say that the transition density lower bound estimate for the Dirichlet transition density, ${\rm NDL}(\phi)$ for short, holds for the Dirichlet form $(\sE, \sF)$ if the Hunt process $X$ associated with $(\sE, \sF)$   has a jointly continuous density function $p(t, x, y)$ on $(0, \infty)\times \sX \times \sX$ with respect to the measure $m$ and there exist  $\e_{\ref{e:2.15}} \in (0, 1)$ and $c_{\ref{e:2.15}} > 0$ so that for every $x_0 \in \sX$, $r > 0$, $t\in (0, \phi (\e_{\ref{e:2.15}}r))$ and 
 $B = B(x_0, r)$, 
 \begin{equation}
 p^B(t, x, y) \geq   \frac{c_{\ref{e:2.15}}}{V(x_0, \phi^{-1}(t))}  \quad \hbox{for } x, y \in B(x_0, \e_{\ref{e:2.15}} \phi^{-1}(t)).
 \end{equation}
 Here $p^B(t, x, y)$ is the transition density function of the part process $X^B$ of $X$ killed upon leaving the ball $B$. 
\end{enumerate}

[Lem 184 (quenched second moment bounds for 
$\bar{D}^{\Ising}$ and 
$\bar{D}^{\frozen,\Ising}$) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] In addition to Lemma~\ref{l:barD.Ising.second} we have the quenched second moment bound
	\[\max\bigg\{
	\bE\Big[\Delta\bar{D}^{\Ising}(q_d)^2\Big]
	: 0\le d\le\dmax-1
	\bigg\}
	\le \frac{\SMAX_N(\Ising)^2\BUCKETS\delta}{N}\]
where $\SMAX_N(\Ising)$ is a random variable satisfying the bound
	\[\P\Big(\SMAX^N(\Ising) \ge \log N\Big)
	\le \exp
	\bigg(
	-\frac{(\log N)^2}{L^{O(1)}}
	\bigg)
	\,.\]
The same bound holds with $\bar{D}^{\frozen,\Ising}$ in place of
$\bar{D}^{\Ising}$.

\begin{proof}
Recall that we can rewrite \eqref{e:drift.error.Ising} as
	\[
	\frac{\Delta \bar{D}^{\Ising}(q_d)}{(\delta_d)^{1/2}}
	=\frac{1}{|B|^{1/2}}
	\bigg(\sum_{i\in B}
	\frac{\be_i}{|B|^{1/2}},
	\by\bigg)
	\equiv \frac{(\be_B,\by(q_{d+1}))}{|B|^{1/2}}\,,
	\]
where we abbreviate $B\equiv B^\Ising$.
If we define the random variable
	\[
	\SMAX_N(\Ising)
	\equiv\max
	\bigg\{
	\Big|( \be_B,\by(q_{d+1}))\Big|
	: 
	0\le d\le \dmax-1, B\in \mathcal{B}^\Ising(q_d)
	\bigg\}\,,
	\]
then we have the quenched second moment bound
	\[
	\bE[\Delta \bar{D}^{\Ising}(q_d)^2]
	= \frac{\delta_d}{N}
	\sum_{B\in \mathcal{B}^\Ising(q_d)}
	(\be_B,\by(q_{d+1}))^2
	\le  \frac{\SMAX_N(\Ising)^2\BUCKETS\delta}{N}\,.
	\]
The bound on $\SMAX_N(\Ising)$ follows by a similar argument as the bound for $\SMAX_N(\RomII)$ from Lemma~\ref{l:barD.II.second.quenched}, with the simplification that $\|\be_B\|=1$ is trivially bounded. 
This proves the claim for $\bar{D}^{\Ising}$, and the claim for
$\bar{D}^{\frozen,\Ising}$ follows by using \eqref{e:barD.vs.plus}.
\end{proof}

[Definition 3 of arXiv:2609.02017, 'Optimal girth-dependent bounds for the Bethe approximation of the permanent'] For $\bs{q}=(q_1,\ldots,q_d)\in\Delta_d$, let
\[
  H(\bs{q}):=-\sum_{i=1}^d q_i\log q_i
\]
denote the usual Shannon entropy, and define the complementary entropy functional
\[
  H_{\mr c}(\bs{q}):=-\sum_{i=1}^d(1-q_i)\log(1-q_i).
\]
We call the difference
\[
  S(\bs{q}):=H(\bs{q})-H_{\mr c}(\bs{q})
\]
the local Bethe entropy functional.
If $\mu$ is a
probability distribution on a finite set, we write $H(\mu)$ for the
entropy of its probability vector; for a finite random variable $U$, we write $\mc{L}(U)$ for its law and set $H(U):=H(\mc{L}(U))$.

Thus, we are left with computing $E(f)$ and $E(g)$, and regarding the 3 possible approaches here, from the proof of Theorem 2.10, the situation with them is as follows:

\medskip

(1) \underline{Symmetry proof}. Normally, the idea here would be to exploit the symmetry between heads and tails, with the goal of reaching to the following formula:
$$(1-p)E(f)=pE(g)$$

[Ppn 127 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Take independent random variables $\sss\sim\tphi$ and $\xxx\sim\sphi$.
Let $\vY^\frozen$ be a subsequential limit of the $\vY^{\frozen,N}$ processes, and let $\hvY^\frozen(t)\equiv \vY^\frozen(t-\sss)+\xxx$. Take the coordinate sum
	\beq
	\iY^\frozen\equiv
	\sum_{\sigma\in\{\RomI,
		\RomII,\RomIII\}}
	\iY^{\frozen,\sigma}\,.\eeq
Let $\iX^\frozen$ and $\iX^{\frozen,\Ising}$ be the unique solutions of the SDEs \eqref{e:iX.sde} such that  $\iX^\frozen(q_*)$ is equidistributed as $\iY^\frozen(q_*)$, and 
$\iX^{\frozen,\Ising}(q_*)$ is equidistributed as $\iY^{\frozen,\Ising}(q_*)$. Then the (one-dimensional) processes 
$\iX^\frozen$ and $\iY^\frozen$
satisfy the same Fokker--Planck equations on the time interval $[q_*,1]$.
As a consequence, for each fixed $t$ the marginal law of $\iX^\frozen(t)$ agrees with the marginal law of $\iY^\frozen(t)$.
The same statements hold for $\iX^{\frozen,\Ising}$ and $\iY^{\frozen,\Ising}$.

\begin{proof}
This follows from Lemma~\ref{l:projected.fokker.planck},  using the regularity estimates from Corollary~\ref{c:reg.in.limit}. 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 45 of arXiv:2608.29585, '2608.29585'] For every $d\ge1$ and all $i,j$,
\begin{equation}
 x_i-x_j=(z_i-z_j)\bigl(1-(z_iz_j)^{-1}\bigr).
\end{equation}
Consequently, in the residue field of $\widehat\cO_d$,
\begin{equation}
 \bar x_i=\bar x_j
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \bar z_i=\bar z_j
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 \bar z_i=\bar z_j^{-1}.
\end{equation}
Thus the full inverse image of an $x$-residue class consists of either
one inversion-stable $z$-disk or two $z$-disks exchanged by inversion; a
finite node cluster may meet one or both disks.

[Thm 68 of arXiv:2509.01797, 'Relation between Wick powers and excursion clusters of the 2D GFF'] Let $n\geq 1$.
Then the field $\psi_{n,A}$ is the limit, as $\gamma\to 0^{+}$,
of the following continuous function supported of $D\setminus A$:
\begin{equation}

\ind_{D\setminus A}
\He_{n}(\gamma V_{A}^{1/2})V_{A}^{n/2} \exp\Big(-\dfrac{\gamma^{2}}{2} V_{A}\Big),
\end{equation}
where $\He_{n}$ is the $n$-th probabilistic Hermite polynomial \eqref{Eq Herm 3},
and $V_{A}$ is the function given by \eqref{Eq V A CR}.
The convergence holds both in
$L^{2}(d\PP,\sigma(\Phi),H^{-\eta}(\C))$ 
and almost surely in $H^{-\eta}(\C)$ (for the Sobolev norm) for every $\eta>0$.

$$\mathbb{P}_{p_c+\varepsilon,p_c}^{\Xi}(o\longleftrightarrow \infty)>0,\quad \mu_\xi \mbox{-almost every}\,\,\Xi.$$

[Tm FW_FS of arXiv:2411.05441, 'Sticky diffusions on star graphs : characterization and It\^o formula'] The unbounded linear operator $L$, defined by (equation generator2 of the paper) with domain given by (equation eq:domain of the paper), is the generator of a strongly continuous semigroup on $C_0(\Gamma)$, associated to a conservative Markov process $X$ on $\Gamma$ having continuous paths. Moreover, writing $X(t)= (i(t), x(t))$, where $x(t)$ is the diffusive part on $[0,\infty)$ generated by $L_i$ and $i(t)$ selects the edges and denoting by $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ the natural filtration associated to $X$, we have the following:
\begin{enumerate}[label={\textnormal{(\roman*)}}]
 \item  Let $t \geq 0$, and $\tau := \inf \{ s > t : x(s) = 0 \}$. Then $x$ coincides with a one dimensional diffusion on $[0,\infty)$, with generator $L_{i(t)}$, on $[t,\tau)$.
 
 \item  If $\eta = 0$, then we have
 \[
  \int_0^t \mathbf{1}_{\{x(s) = 0 \}}\, ds = 0 \quad \textnormal{for all } t \geq 0,
 \]
 and there exists a one-dimensional Brownian motion $W$ and a continuous increasing process $\ell_X$, both adapted to $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \geq 0}$, such that 
 \begin{equation}
  dx(t) = \sigma_{i(t)}(x(t)) dW(t) + b_{i(t)}(x(t)) dt + d\ell_X(t),
 \end{equation}
 and the process $\ell_X$ increases only when $x(t) = 0$. Furthermore, we have
 \[
   \left ( \sum_{i=1}^N \frac{2 \rho_i}{\sigma_i^2(0)} \right) \ell_X(t) = \lim_{\delta \to 0} \frac{1}{\delta} \int_0^t \mathbf 1_{\{x(s) \leq \delta \}} \, ds
 \]
 in expectation\footnote{\textit{i.e.}, in $L^1$.}.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Tm FW_FS of arXiv:2411.05441

body: [Definition 3.2 of arXiv:2607.29403, 'Strong invariants and Tverberg numbers in convexity spaces'] Let F ⊆2X be a set system. Its comatching number is the largest m for which there are distinct points p1, . . . , pm ∈X and sets C1, . . . , Cm ∈F such that pi ∈Cj ⇐⇒ i ̸= j. Equivalently, the incidence graph of (X, F) contains the bipartite complement of a matching of size m as an induced subgraph. Observation 3.3. If G generates C, then G and C have the same comatching number.

and the divergence is $+\infty$ if $\sigma_q^2\le 0$. Moreover $R_q$ is additive across independent product factors. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a metric space $X$, let us call $K\subset X$ compact when any open cover $K\subset\cup_iU_i$ has a finite subcover. Then, the following happen:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Compact implies closed and bounded.

\item The converse of this fact is not true.

\item Closed inside compact is compact.

\item If $K_1\supset K_2\supset K_3\supset\ldots$ are non-empty compacts, then $\cap_iK_i\neq\emptyset$.

\item If $K$ is compact, any sequence $\{x_n\}\subset K$ has a limit point in $K$.
\end{enumerate}
Also, coming as good news, in the case $X=\mathbb R^N$, compact means closed and bounded.

[Definition def:conditional-egu of arXiv:2512.21026, 'Minimax Duality in Game-Theoretic Probability\thanks{Work in progress: mistakes are likely'] Let $(\mathcal{Y},\hat\mathcal{Z},T)$ be a sequential gamble space.
  Let $t \in \{1,\ldots,T-1\}$ and $s\in\mathcal{Y}^t$.
  Define $\hat\mathcal{Z}|_s \subseteq (\mathcal{Y}^{<T-t} \to \overline{\mathbb{R}})$ by $\hat\mathcal{Z}|_s = \{\hat Z(s \oplus \, \cdot \,) : \hat Z \in \hat\mathcal{Z}\}$.
  For any $X:\mathcal{Y}^T\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}$, we define $\overline{\textsf{\textbf{E}}}[X\mid s] := \overline{\textsf{\textbf{E}}}[X(s \oplus \, \cdot \,)]$ with respect to the sequential gamble space $(\mathcal{Y},\hat\mathcal{Z}|_s,T-t)$.
title: Conditional game-theoretic upper expectation

[Lemma of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] \Authornote{Jeff}{alt version}{blue}
	For any deviation vector $\eta_\tau$ associated with a non-trivial shape $\tau$ such that
$\eta_\tau \neq \eta_0$, we have
\[
    \mathbb{E}\!\left[\eta_\tau^\top M^{-1}\eta_\tau\right]
    =   
    \frac{1}{1-\gamma}\,
    \mathbb{E}\!\left[\|\eta_\tau\|_2^2\right] + O(1) \,.
\]
Equivalently, \[ 
\mathrm{Var}(\mathsf{correct}(\tau)) =   \frac{1}{1-\gamma} \cdot \mathrm{Var}(\eta_\tau) +O(1) \,.
\]
\Authornote{Jeff}{notice an error bound of $O(d)$ is interesting here as $\eta_0$ would have deviation $m/d$ by itself, so we are making polynomial improvement}{blue}

[Theorem {\cite[Theorems~1.1.4 and 1.1.5 of arXiv:2609.04140, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ III:\\ uniqueness'] {LevelLineGFFI}}]
	Let $h$ be a GFF on $\BH$ with piecewise constant boundary conditions that change only finitely many times. For all $u \in \BR$ and $x \in \partial \BH$, we denote by $\gamma_u^x$ the level line of $h$ with height $u$ starting from $x$ and ending at $\infty$. Fix $x_2 \leq x_1$ and $u_1, u_2 \in \BR$.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item If $u_2 < u_1$, then $\gamma_{u_2}^{x_2}$ a.s.\ stays to the left of $\gamma_{u_1}^{x_1}$.
		\item If $u_2 = u_1$, then $\gamma_{u_2}^{x_2}$ may intersect $\gamma_{u_1}^{x_1}$ and, upon intersecting, the two curves merge and never separate.
		\item If $u_1 - u_2 \geq 2 \lambda$, then $\gamma_{u_1}^{x_1}$ and $\gamma_{u_2}^{x_2}$ do not intersect each other a.s.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem Boundary-corrected Harnack inequality of arXiv:2608.12376, 'A Heat Kernel Expectation Approach to Boundary-Corrected Li--Yau Estimates for the Dirichl'] Let $w$ be a positive solution of the Dirichlet heat equation

\[
w_t=\Delta w
\]

on the Euclidean half-space

\[
\mathbb R^n_+
=
\{x_n>0\},
\]

and assume that

\[
\Delta\log w(x,t)
\geq
-\frac n{2t}
-\frac1{x_n^2}.
\]

Then for every smooth curve

\[
\gamma(t)=(x(t),t),
\qquad
t\in[t_1,t_2],
\]

with

\[
x(t)\in\mathbb R^n_+,
\]

we have

\[
\begin{aligned}
\log
\frac{w(x(t_2),t_2)}
     {w(x(t_1),t_1)}
\geq&
-\frac14
\int_{t_1}^{t_2}
|x'(t)|^2\,dt
\\
&-\frac n2
\log\frac{t_2}{t_1}
\\
&-
\int_{t_1}^{t_2}
\frac1{x_n(t)^2}\,dt .
\end{aligned}
\]

$$A=UDU^*$$
with $U\in U_N$, and with $D\in M_N(\mathbb C)$ diagonal. The converse holds too.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Counterexample to the usual pathwise lifetime monotonicity coupling Result: Consider a deterministic contact schedule with A initially infected: A-C at time .1, A-B at 1, C-B at 9, B-D at 10, and no other contacts. Baseline infectious lifetimes are L_A=.5, L_C=12, L_B=2. Then B is infected at 9 and infects D at 10. Multiply every lifetime by 3: A now infects B at 1; B is removed at 7, cannot be reinfected at 9, and D is never infected. Check: Check both timelines: C remains infectious at 9 in each case; A has already died at 1 only in the baseline. The example refutes infection-set inclusion under scaled lifetimes on a fixed contact schedule. Obstruction: This is not a counterexample to survival monotonicity or to the Brownian epidemic conjecture. It blocks a direct attractiveness proof; a Brownian contact-support realization was not proved.

Let (X, mu) and (Y, nu) be sigma-finite measure spaces, 1 <= p <= infinity, and f : X x Y -> [0, infinity] product-measurable. Then the L^p(mu) norm of the y-average dominates in the direction: || integral_Y f(., y) dnu(y) ||_{L^p(dmu)} <= integral_Y || f(., y) ||_{L^p(dmu)} dnu(y). For signed or complex f the same holds provided the right-hand side is finite, and then the inner integral converges absolutely for mu-a.e. x. The inequality is the continuous form of the triangle inequality for the L^p norm and reduces to it when nu is counting measure on two points. The reverse inequality is false for p > 1 and TRUE for 0 < p <= 1 with the roles of the two sides exchanged. Special case worth naming: taking nu counting measure on the integers gives || sum_n f_n ||_p <= sum_n || f_n ||_p. [standard; e.g. Stein, Singular Integrals and Differentiability Properties of Functions, Appendix A.1]

[Definition 7 of arXiv:2603.26936, 'Sharp Riemannian heat kernel estimates on the cut locus and the Parabolic Anderson model'] Let $\alpha>0$ and consider the following Hilbert space of space-time functions, 
\begin{align}
\mathcal{H}_{\alpha,\rho}=L^2(\mathbb{R}_+,\, \mathcal{H}^{\alpha,\rho}).  
\end{align}
On a complete probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$ we define a centered Gaussian family $\{W_{\alpha,\rho}(\phi); \phi\in L^2(\R_+)\cap\mathcal{H}_{\alpha,\rho}(M)\}$, whose covariance is given by 
\[
\mathbf E\left[ W_{\alpha,\rho}(\varphi) W_{\alpha,\rho}(\psi)\right]
=\int_{\R_+}\ \left\langle \varphi (t,\cdot) , \psi (t,\cdot)\right\rangle_{\alpha,\rho}  dt \, ,
\]
for $\varphi$, $\psi$ in $\mathcal{H}_{\alpha,\rho}$ in the space variable. This family is called
colored noise on $M$ that is white in time.
title: Definition 7 of arXiv:2603.26936

[Theorem 36 of arXiv:2608.07239, 'Unified framework for asymptotically uniform iterative construction of generalised random '] Let $T$ be an FIS of $G$ and let $V':=V\setminus\overline{N}(T)$, $\alpha':=\alpha-|T|$, and $P':=(\tfrac{\ell}{2}\alpha')^{-1}$. Let $U\subset V'\setminus(F\cup R^*(T))$ with $U_{\max}:=\max\{|\overline{N}(v)\cap U|:v\in V'\}$, and define $M':=\max\{M,U_{\max},\tfrac{\alpha}{\alpha'}R_{\max}^{(a)}\}$. Finally, define
		\begin{align}
			\mathscr{Q}(T,U)&:=\exp\Bigg(\tfrac12P'\sum_{v\in V'}\left(P|R^*(v)|-P'|R^*(v)\cap V'|\right)\Bigg.
			\\&\quad+P|F|-P'|F\cap V'|+P\b(V)-P'\b(V')
			\\&\quad\Bigg.+\tfrac12P|R^*(T)|-P'|R^*(T)\cap V'|-\b(T)-P'|U|\Bigg)\prod_{t=\alpha'+1}^{\alpha}\frac{t}{n_t}.
		\end{align}
		Assume that $\alpha'\to\infty$, with $\ell$ fixed and $M'=O((\alpha')^{\sfrac12}/(\log\alpha')^2)$. Then the IMFIS process samples an FMIS that contains the \emph{target set} $T$ and is disjoint from the \emph{exclusion set} $U$ with probability $$\mathbb{P}(|\boldsymbol{S}_{\infty}|=\alpha\wedge T\subset\boldsymbol{S}_{\infty}\wedge U\cap\boldsymbol{S}_{\infty}=\emptyset)=(1+O(\mathscr{E}(\alpha',M')))\mathscr{Q}(T,U).$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma eq:mixture-remainder-X of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[lemma]{lem:product-mixture-path}
Let \(\mu_i\) and \(\gamma_i\), \(1\le i\le M\), be probability laws whose
moments agree through order \(m\), and put
\[
 \mu_{i,t}=(1-t)\mu_i+t\gamma_i,
 \qquad \lambda_t=\bigotimes_{i=1}^M\mu_{i,t},
 \qquad A(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^M}F(z)\,\lambda_t(\,\mathrm d z),
\]
where \(F:\mathbb R^M\to(0,\infty)\) is \(C^{m+1}\).  Let
\(Z\sim\lambda_t\), \(X_i\sim\mu_i\), and \(Y_i\sim\gamma_i\) be
independent.  Assume \(0<A(t)<\infty\) on \([0,1]\), that the
expressions below are absolutely integrable, and that differentiation
under the finite product measure is justified.  Set
\(\Delta_i^X=X_i-Z_i\) and \(\Delta_i^Y=Y_i-Z_i\).  If, uniformly in
\(t\in[0,1]\),
\begin{align}
 &\sum_{i=1}^M\mathbb E\left[
  \left\lvert\Delta_i^X\right\rvert^{m+1}
  \int_0^1(1-s)^m
  \abs{\partial_i^{m+1}F(Z+s\Delta_i^Xe_i)}\,\mathrm d s\right]
 \le R A(t),\\
 &\sum_{i=1}^M\mathbb E\left[
  \left\lvert\Delta_i^Y\right\rvert^{m+1}
  \int_0^1(1-s)^m
  \abs{\partial_i^{m+1}F(Z+s\Delta_i^Ye_i)}\,\mathrm d s\right]
 \le R A(t),
\end{align}
then
\begin{equation}
 \left\lvert\log A(1)-\log A(0)\right\rvert\le \frac{2R}{m!}.
\end{equation}

[Definition def:SaS-measure of arXiv:2606.02003, 'Higher-Order Multifractional Stable Motion:\\ Definition and Fundamental Properties'] Let $(E,\mathcal{E})$ be a measurable space with $\sigma$-finite measure $m$.
Set $\mathcal{E}_0 := \{A \in \mathcal{E} : m(A) < \infty\}$.
A mapping $M_\alpha : \mathcal{E}_0 \to L^0(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$
is a \emph{S$\alpha$S random measure with control measure $m$} if:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item For every $A \in \mathcal{E}_0$:
  $M_\alpha(A) \sim \mathrm{S}\alpha\mathrm{S}(m(A)^{1/\alpha})$, i.e.,
  \begin{equation}
  
  \mathbb{E}\bigl[e^{i\theta M_\alpha(A)}\bigr]
  = e^{-|\theta|^\alpha m(A)},
  \quad \theta \in \mathbb{R}.
  \end{equation}
\item For pairwise disjoint $A_1, A_2, \ldots \in \mathcal{E}_0$,
  the variables $M_\alpha(A_1), M_\alpha(A_2), \ldots$ are independent.
\item For pairwise disjoint $\{A_j\} \subset \mathcal{E}_0$ with
  $\bigcup_j A_j \in \mathcal{E}_0$:
  $M_\alpha\!\left(\bigcup_j A_j\right) = \sum_j M_\alpha(A_j)$
  almost surely.
\end{enumerate}
title: S$\alpha$S random measure

[Corollary 31 of arXiv:2606.09904, 'Non-explosion principles for branched rough differential equations with unbounded coeffici'] Let \(N \in \mathbb{N}\), \(\gamma \in (\frac{1}{N + 1}, \frac{1}{N}]\) and 
  \(\mathbf{X} : [0, T] \to G_N(\CH)\) be such that \(\<\mathbf{X}, \sigma\> = 0\) for all 
  \(\sigma \in \CT_{\left\lfloor\frac{N}{2}\right\rfloor} \setminus \{\mathbf{1}\}\). 
  Then, \(\mathbf{X}\) is a \(\gamma\)-H\"older branched rough path if and only if 
  for any \(\tau \in \CT_N \setminus \CT_{\left\lfloor\frac{N}{2}\right\rfloor}\), there 
  exists \(f^\tau \in C^{\gamma|\tau|}([0, T], (\mathbb{R}^d)^{\otimes |\tau|})\) such that
  \[\mathbf{X}_t = \mathbf{1} + \sum_{\tau \in \CT_N \setminus \CT_{\left\lfloor\frac{N}{2}\right\rfloor}} f^\tau(t) \tau.\]
  Moreover, we have that 
  \[\mathbf{X}_{st} \equiv \mathbf{X}_s^{-1} \curvearrowright \mathbf{X}_t 
    = \mathbf{1} + \sum_{\tau \in \CT_N \setminus \CT_{\left\lfloor\frac{N}{2}\right\rfloor}} (\delta f^\tau)_{st} \tau.\]

	\[\p\big(T^t(q(o),q(x)\big) \neq T(x)) < \|x\|^{4d} e^{-\mathfrak{c}_1 t}.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 19 (Wasserstein-1 distance) of arXiv:2605.24445, 'Matrix concentration inequalities for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains'] Let $(\Omega, d)$ be a Polish metric space and let $\mu,\nu$ be two probability measures on $\Omega$ with finite first moment.
The \emph{Wasserstein-1 distance} between $\mu$ and $\nu$ is
\[
    W_1(\mu,\nu)
    \;:=\;
    \inf_{\pi \in \Pi(\mu,\nu)}
    \int_{\Omega\times \Omega} d(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}\pi(x,y),
\]
where $\Pi(\mu,\nu)$ is the set of all couplings of $\mu$ and $\nu$,
i.e., all probability measures $\pi$ on $\Omega\times\Omega$
with marginals $\mu$ and $\nu$.
title: Wasserstein-1 distance

[Corollary 12 of arXiv:2608.19744, 'Conditioned Brownian motion and local equivalence of path ensembles'] Consider the birth-death process with immigration introduced above and let
    $A_T=\int_0^T \de s \, X_s$.
For $0<\theta<a/(c-b)$, define $r_\theta=\sqrt{\frac{c\theta}{a+b\theta}}$ and $\beta_\theta
      =br_\theta+\frac{c}{r_\theta}-b-c$.
Moreover, let
\[
    v_\theta
      =\frac{2ac r_\theta^3}{(c-br_\theta^2)^3},
    \qquad
    I_{\mathrm{BDI}}(\theta)
      =\left(
          \sqrt{a+b\theta}-\sqrt{c\theta}
       \right)^2.
\]
Then, for every fixed $n\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}$ and $z\in\mathbb R$,
\[
    \bbP_n(A_T\leq\theta T+z)
    \sim
    \frac{
      \psi_{\beta_\theta}(n)
      \langle\psi_{\beta_\theta},\mathbf 1\rangle_{\ell^2(\pi)}
    }{
      \beta_\theta\sqrt{2\pi v_\theta T}
    }
    \exp\!\left(
       -I_{\mathrm{BDI}}(\theta)T+\beta_\theta z
    \right).
\]
On every fixed time interval, the conditioned process converges in total
variation to the birth-death process with rates
\[
    q^{(\theta)}(n,n+1)=r_\theta(a+bn),
    \qquad
    q^{(\theta)}(n,n-1)=\frac{c}{r_\theta}n.
\]
Its invariant law is negative binomial with shape parameter $a/b$ and
mean $\theta$.

body: [Lem points_are_shielded_away of arXiv:2604.14122, 'The scaling limit of random walk and\\ the intrinsic metric on planar critical percolation'] The following holds for $R \in \mathbf N$ large enough. Fix $0<p'<1$. Suppose again that $M,a$ are chosen so that $\mathbf{P}(F_1\cap F_2\cap F_3)\geq 1-p'/2$. For $0<b<a$, let $F_5(b)$ be the event that for every $i\leq m$, there exists $\hat{v}_i\in \operatorname{int}\phi$ such that $\hat{v}_i$ is another open touch-point of the closed clusters of the segments $\phi_{i-1}$ and $\phi_i$. Moreover, we ask that $\hat{v}_i$ is at distance at least $br$ away from $v_i$. For $0<c<b$, let $F_6(c)$ be the event that there exist closed paths from $\phi_{i-1}$ and $\phi_{i}$ to $\hat{v}_i$ that are contained fully outside of the box $B(v_i,c^{1/3}r)$. Also, let $F_7(c)$ be the event that for all $i$, once $\phi_{i-1}$ or $\phi_i$ leave the box $B(v_i,c^{1/3}r)$, they don't enter $B(v_i,cr)$ again. There exists $b_0=b_0(p',M,a)>0$ such that for every $b<b_0$ there exists $c_0=c_0(p',M,a,b)>0$ such that for every $c<c_0$ we have that $\mathbf{P}(F_1\cap F_2\cap F_3 \cap F_5 \cap F_6 \cap F_7) \geq 1-p'$ for all radii $r$ such that $crn\geq R$.

[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2608.04644, 'Khinchin's and Chung's Laws of the Iterated Logarithm at Time Zero for the Linear Stochast'] \cite[Theorem 2.4]{T1994}
Let $\{X(t)\}_{t\in S}$ be a mean-zero continuous Gaussian process.
Denote $\sigma^2 := \sup_{t\in S} \|X(t)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2$. Suppose that  there exist constants $M > \sigma$, $p > 0$, and $0 < \varepsilon_0 \leqslant \sigma$ such that
\[
N(S, d_X, \varepsilon) \leq (M/\varepsilon)^p \quad \text{for all } \varepsilon < \varepsilon_0.
\]
Then, for any $u > \sigma^2[(1 + \sqrt{p})/\varepsilon_0]$, the following holds:
\[
\mathbb{P}\left\{ \sup_{t\in S} X(t) \geq u \right\} \leq \left(\frac{KMu}{\sqrt{p}\,\sigma^2} \right)^p \Phi\left(\frac{u}{\sigma} \right),
\]
where $\Phi(x) = (2\pi)^{-1/2} \int_x^\infty e^{-y^2/2}\,dy$ and $K$ is a universal constant. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 11 of arXiv:2608.04644

body: Let $M$ predictors $f_1, \dots, f_M$ of a target $y$ have errors $e_m = f_m - y$ with error covariance $\Sigma_E$ (the $M \times M$ covariance of the vector $(e_1, \dots, e_M)$ over the population of inputs). An affine stack $\sum_m w_m f_m + b$ with $\sum_m w_m = 1$ has error $\sum_m w_m e_m + b$, so after the intercept removes the mean error its risk is $w^T \Sigma_E w$, and the optimal weights are the minimum-variance portfolio $w^* = \Sigma_E^{-1}\mathbf{1} / (\mathbf{1}^T \Sigma_E^{-1}\mathbf{1})$; without the sum constraint the least-squares stack is the ordinary regression of $y$ on $(f_1, \dots, f_M, 1)$. Consequently every random-matrix result about the noisy-covariance portfolio problem transfers to ensemble weighting with $q = M / n_{\mathrm{cal}}$, $n_{\mathrm{cal}}$ the number of calibration cases the weights are fitted on: the plug-in (least-squares) stack's out-of-sample risk is inflated by the factor $1/(1 - q)$ relative to the optimum, its in-sample risk understates the optimum by $1 - q$, and any cleaning of the covariance must be applied to $\Sigma_E$. The covariance of the predictions themselves, $\operatorname{Cov}(f_1, \dots, f_M)$, is NOT the object to clean: writing $f_m = y + e_m$ it equals $\operatorname{Var}(y)\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^T + (\text{cross terms}) + \Sigma_E$, a rank-one spike of the size of the signal variance over the error covariance. The stacking weight's departure from equal weights, $w - \mathbf{1}/M$, is orthogonal to $\mathbf{1}$, so it lives entirely in the small-eigenvalue subspace of the prediction covariance; a bulk-versus-spike cleaner applied to that matrix (Marchenko-Pastur truncation, shrinkage toward $\operatorname{tr}/p \cdot I$, a rotationally invariant estimator floored relative to the top eigenvalue) keeps the signal spike and destroys exactly the directions stacking needs. At $q = 0.025$ (23 members, 932 calibration rows) the whole prize from cleaning $\Sigma_E$ is bounded by about $2.5$ percent; the prize grows like $q/(1-q)$ as the calibration set shrinks.

[Thm main of arXiv:2601.19145, 'Stochastic Persistence in Infinite Dimensions'] Under our (as1 of the paper)--(as-compact of the paper), the following statements hold: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item For all $x \in \mathcal{M}_+$, almost surely all limit points $\mu$ of $\mu_t^x$ as $t \to \infty$ satisfy $\mu \in P_{inv}(\mathcal{M}_+)$.
        \item $X_t$ is stochastically persistent, meaning for all $\epsilon > 0$ there exists a compact set $\mathcal{K}_\epsilon \subset \mathcal{M}_+$ such that for all $x \in \mathcal{M}_+$ $$\mathbb{P}(\liminf_{t \to \infty} \mu_t^x(\mathcal{K}_\epsilon) \geq 1 - \epsilon) = 1 \,.$$
        \item $P_{inv}(\mathcal{M}_+)$ is nonempty.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm main of arXiv:2601.19145

body:
Use the convention $\hat\varphi(\zeta)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\varphi(x)e^{-ix\cdot\zeta}dx$ for $\zeta\in\mathbb C^d$, and let $R\ge0$, $B_R=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:|x|\le R\}$. (a) Test functions: $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ with $\operatorname{supp}\varphi\subset B_R$ if and only if $\hat\varphi$ extends to an entire function on $\mathbb C^d$ satisfying, for every $N\in\mathbb N$, a bound $|\hat\varphi(\zeta)|\le C_N(1+|\zeta|)^{-N}e^{R|\operatorname{Im}\zeta|}$. (b) Distributions: if $u\in\mathcal E'(\mathbb R^d)$ has $\operatorname{supp}u\subset B_R$ and order at most $N$, then $\hat u(\zeta)=\langle u,e^{-ix\cdot\zeta}\rangle$ is entire on $\mathbb C^d$ and $|\hat u(\zeta)|\le C(1+|\zeta|)^{N}e^{R|\operatorname{Im}\zeta|}$. Conversely, if an entire $U$ on $\mathbb C^d$ satisfies $|U(\zeta)|\le C(1+|\zeta|)^{N}e^{R|\operatorname{Im}\zeta|}$ for some constants $C,N$, then $U=\hat u$ for a unique $u\in\mathcal E'(\mathbb R^d)$ with $\operatorname{supp}u\subset B_R$. The support-and-growth correspondence is an exact equivalence; the order is not preserved in both directions - the forward implication gives the exponent $N$ from the order $N$, while the converse only returns a distribution of order at most $N+d+1$. Consequence: the exponential factor records the size of the (convex hull of the) support, the polynomial factor records smoothness versus singularity order. Corollary: a nonzero compactly supported distribution never has compactly supported Fourier transform, since a nonzero entire function cannot vanish on a nonempty open subset of $\mathbb C^d$.
convention with kernel e^{-i x . zeta} (with e^{-2 pi i x . zeta} the exponent becomes 2 pi R |Im zeta|)
support contained in the closed ball of radius R (for a general compact convex K replace R|Im zeta| by the supporting function of K evaluated at Im zeta)
(b): u is a distribution with compact support and finite order; the polynomial exponent equals the order only in the forward direction

[Theorem thm_cond_as_conv of arXiv:2606.16609, 'On stability of outliers from the circular law'] Let $G$ be a complex Ginibre matrix conditioned on $\{ \lambda_1 = z \}$ with $|z| > 1$. Then, the diagonal overlap associated to $\lambda_1$ converges almost surely to a constant, namely:
$$
\mathscr{O}_{11} \xrightarrow[N \rightarrow \infty]{a.s.} \frac{|z|^2}{|z|^2-1}.
$$
title: Almost-sure convergence of diagonal overlaps

[Theorem 9 (Conditional epigraph structure) of arXiv:2606.17517, 'Killed resolvents and measure-valued stopping gains for reflected optimal stopping with ma'] Assume that $V$ is continuous. Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{ass:vertical-H}
and \ref{ass:nonempty-sections} hold. Define
$   b(x_1):=\inf\mathcal D(x_1)$ for $x_1\ge0$.
Then $b$ is well defined with values in $[0,\infty)$, and
$   \mathcal D
   =
   \{(x_1,x_2)\in\R^2_+:x_2\ge b(x_1)\}$.
   
If, in addition, Assumption~\ref{ass:horizontal-H} holds, then $b$ is
monotone. More precisely, $H$ nonincreasing in $x_1$ implies $b$ nonincreasing,
whereas $H$ nondecreasing in $x_1$ implies $b$ nondecreasing.

body:
[Conj 89 of arXiv:2509.01797, 'Relation between Wick powers and excursion clusters of the 2D GFF'] Let $n\geq 1$.
For $\varepsilon>0$, consider the family of random variables
\begin{displaymath}
(A, (Z_{j,\varepsilon},[\Gamma_{Z_{j,\varepsilon}}])_{1\leq j\leq n}).
\end{displaymath}
As $\varepsilon\to 0$, this family converges in law towards
\begin{displaymath}
(A,(Z_{j},[\Gamma_{j}])_{1\leq j\leq n}),
\end{displaymath}
with the following properties.
\begin{itemize}
\item $A$ is the same FPS as previously.
\item $(Z_{j})_{1\leq j\leq n}$ are random points on $A$,
sampled, conditionally on $A$, in an i.i.d. way according to the probability measure
\begin{displaymath}
\dfrac{\nu_{A}}{\nu_{A}(A)},
\end{displaymath}
where $\nu_{A}$ is the FPS measure \eqref{Eq nu a Mink non norm}.
\item The family of equivalence classes of loops
$([\Gamma_{j}])_{1\leq j\leq n}$
is \textbf{independent} from
$(A,(Z_{j})_{1\leq j\leq n})$,
with an i.i.d. distribution according to the measure
$\hat{\mu}^{\rm loop}_{\text{SLE}_{4}}$.
\end{itemize} (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Conjecture 89 of arXiv:2509.01797

body:
[Thm gl-sp-pres of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Both ${\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_\textup{gl}$ and ${\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{gl}$ are globally presentable.
    \begin{proof}
        In light of Corollary~(cor:LSp-vs-Sp-param of the paper), it will suffice to prove the first statement. 

        By Proposition~(prop:L-gl-Bousfield of the paper), each individual category ${\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_\text{$G$-gl}$ is presentable, so it remains to show global cocompleteness. For this, let us write $R\colon{\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_\textup{gl}\to{\mathpalette\ulhelper{{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{lvl}$ for the right adjoint from the previous lemma. If $X\in\PSh(\textup{Glo})$ is any presheaf, then $R(X)\colon{\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_\textup{gl}(X)\to{\mathpalette\ulhelper{{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{lvl}(X)$ is a fully faithful right adjoint (as a limit of such functors), so its left adjoint is a Bousfield localization. Moreover, if $f\colon X\to Y$ is any map in $\PSh(\textup{Glo})$, then $f_!\colon{\mathpalette\ulhelper{{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{lvl}(X)\to{\mathpalette\ulhelper{{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{lvl}(Y)$ descends through the localization functor as $f^*$ preserves the essential image of the fully faithful right adjoint $R$ (the latter being part of a global functor); in particular, $f^*\colon{\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{gl}(Y)\to{\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{gl}(Y)$ has a left adjoint, and it only remains to verify the Beck--Chevalley condition for pullbacks in $\PSh(\textup{Glo})$. As localizations are in particular essentially surjective, this may be done after precomposing with ${\mathpalette\ulhelper{{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{lvl}\to{\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_\textup{gl}$. Using once more that Beck--Chevalley maps compose, this then follows at once from ${\mathpalette\ulhelper{{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{lvl}$ being globally cocomplete (Proposition~(prop:Splev-cc of the paper)) and the localization being a left adjoint.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm gl-sp-pres of arXiv:2608.28504

DRAFT independent obstruction, review pending. Let T_i be iid positive integers with P(T_i=m)=1/[m(m+1)], m>=1. Set S_k=sum_{i=1}^k T_i and Y_t=max{k:S_k<=t}. Then T_i is finite almost surely, P(T_i>=m)=1/m and E[T_i]=infinity. Strong laws for the truncations min(T_i,M), followed by M increasing to infinity, give S_k/k -> infinity. Thus Y_t -> infinity but Y_t/t -> 0 almost surely despite unit regeneration displacements. This holding process is outside uniformly elliptic nearest-neighbor iid RWRE and does not refute C0041; it refutes only an inference from finite-a.s. regeneration times and bounded displacements to positive speed.

No claim to satisfy the C0041 model

body:
[Lemma lower_bound_weighted_inner_product of arXiv:2608.23765, '\texorpdfstring{Tight Majorizations and Convergence Rates\\ of Nuclear Norm Minimization I'] \mbox{}\\
Let $\varepsilon > 0$
and let $\mathbf{X} \in \R^{d_1 \times d_2}$ 
with SVD given by $ \mathbf{X} = \mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}} \diag (\boldsymbol{\sigma}) \mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X}}^\top$, where
$\diag (\boldsymbol{\sigma}) \in \R^{d_1 \times d_2}$ is the rectangular diagonal matrix with the extended vector of nonincreasing singular values $\boldsymbol{\sigma} \in \R^{D}$ of $\mathbf{X}$ on the diagonal.
Consider the weight operator
$ W_{\mathbf{X}, \varepsilon} : \R^{d_1 \times d_2} \to \R^{d_1 \times d_2} $
of (def:optimalweightoperator of the paper) with harmonic-mean core matrix (eq:harmonic:mean of the paper). Define the matrices
$\mathbf{L}_{\mathbf{U}} = \mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}} \diag (\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_{d_1}) \mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}}^\top $
and
$ \mathbf{L}_{\mathbf{V}} = \mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X}} \diag (\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_{d_2}) \mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X}}^\top $,
where $ \lambda_i := \max \left( \sigma_i, \varepsilon \right)$
for $1 \le i \le \max \left( d_1, d_2 \right)$ with the convention of $\sigma_i = 0$ for $i > d$.

Let now $\mathbf{Z} \in \R^{d_1 \times d_2}$
be arbitrary with SVD given by $ \mathbf{Z} = \sum_{k=1}^d \sigma_k (\mathbf{Z}) \mathbf{u}_k \mathbf{v}_k^\top $, where $\sigma_k (\mathbf{Z})$
denotes the $k$-th singular value of $\mathbf{Z}$. Then,
it holds that 
\begin{equation*}
    \innerproduct{ \W{\mathbf{X}}{\varepsilon} (\mathbf{Z}), \mathbf{Z} }
    \ge
    \sum_{k=1}^d
    \frac{ \sigma_k^2 (\mathbf{Z})}{ 
        \innerproduct{ \mathbf{L}_{\mathbf{U}}, \mathbf{u}_k \mathbf{u}_k^\top }/2 
        +
        \innerproduct{ \mathbf{L}_{\mathbf{V}}, \mathbf{v}_k \mathbf{v}_k^\top  }/2
    }.
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lower Bound for Weighted Inner Product of Harmonic Mean

Method: Exact identities, finite controls and structural obstruction Result: With fixed color counts N_i, the exact sum rule is sum_x Cov(eta_i(0),eta_j(x))=Cov(eta_i(0),N_j)=0. At zero separation the same-color covariance is rho_i*(1-rho_i), and the different-color covariance is -rho_i*rho_j. In the symmetric uniform-arrangement baseline, exchangeability gives off-site values -rho_i*(1-rho_i)/(N-1) for the same color and +rho_i*rho_j/(N-1) for different colors. Check: The off-site formulas follow both from sampling without replacement and from the sum rule plus exchangeability. They sum exactly to cancel the zero-site covariance. A decay claim uniform in the ring size must account for this order1/N correction. Obstruction: For biased multi-color dynamics the stationary correlations depend on the ordering structure and cannot be derived from the conservation identities alone. These identities give signed integral constraints, not the requested asymptotic decay kernel. No analysis of the relevant stationary horizon or matrix-product correlations is completed.

[Lemma 14 (Graphical Cauchy--Schwarz) of arXiv:2608.12492, 'Weak Limits of Wiener Chaos: Primitive--Fock Classification and Hilbert--Stein Extraction'] Consider a finite loop-free tensor network whose vertices carry Hilbert tensors
$(z_v)_{v\in V}$ and whose edges contract pairs of Hilbert legs.  If all
legs are contracted, its scalar value satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \left|\operatorname{Contr}_G((z_v)_{v\in V})\right|
 \le\prod_{v\in V}\norm{z_v}.
 
\end{equation}
If exactly $r\ge1$ edges join two distinguished vertices carrying $x$
and $y$, one may first perform all these $r$ contractions and obtains the sharper
bound
\begin{equation}
 \left|\operatorname{Contr}_G((z_v)_{v\in V})\right|
 \le\norm{x\otimes_ry}
 \prod_{v\ne x,y}\norm{z_v}.
 
\end{equation}
No edge is allowed to join two legs of the same vertex.  The same
inequalities hold for a network with open output legs, with the
absolute value replaced by the Hilbert norm of the output tensor.

[Proposition 22 of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Assume the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:positive-barrier-row-universality}. For each$i\in[n]$, define
		\[
			\bar\ell_i
			:=\E_i\ell_i(W_i)
			=\E_i\ell_i(G_i),
		\]
		where the equality follows from covariance matching $\Cov(W_i)=\Cov(G_i)$.  Then
		$\bar\ell_i$ is nonnegative, and
		\[
			\max_{Z_i\in\{W_i,G_i\}}
			\E_i|\ell_i(Z_i)-\bar\ell_i|^2
			\le
			C\beta^{-2}\dim(\mathsf V)(\tau/\lambda_{\Sigma}+1)^2.
		\]
		Covariance matching gives $	\E_i r_i(W_i)^2
			=\E_i r_i(G_i)^2,$ and hence
		\[
			\E_i\frac{r_i(W_i)^2}{2(n+\bar\ell_i)}
			=
			\E_i\frac{r_i(G_i)^2}{2(n+\bar\ell_i)}.
		\]

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Test whether the constant 1 in front of t is forced by the Gaussian comparison and whether the Bernoulli case can beat it. Result: For the Gaussian matrix Edelman's exact law gives P(sqrt n s_n <= t) = 1 - e^{-t^2/2 - t} ~ t as t -> 0, so the constant 1 is exactly the Gaussian density at zero of sqrt n s_n; the conjecture says Bernoulli matrices are no worse than Gaussian up to the exponentially small singular mass. A sufficient condition would be a local limit theorem for sqrt n s_n at zero uniform in n, which is a universality statement at the hard edge (the smallest singular value) and is known (Tao-Vu 2010 hard-edge universality) only in the form P(sqrt n s_n <= t) = (1 - e^{-t^2/2-t}) + O(n^{-c}) for t in a fixed range, which gives the conjecture for t >= n^{-c'} but not for t between c^n and n^{-c'}. The gap regime is exactly the small-ball regime where the Rudelson-Vershynin constant C appears. No improvement obtained. Key identity: Gaussian case: P(sqrt n s_n <= t) = 1 - exp(-t^2/2 - t), so the conjectured constant is the Gaussian value. Obstruction: Hard-edge universality covers t >= n^{-c}; the conjecture needs the constant 1 down to exponentially small t.

[Theorem 15 of arXiv:2608.07365, 'A pathwise Ito formula \\for weakly differentiable functions'] Let $(\Omega,B,P_x)$ be the canonical Wiener space as in Section \ref{sec:Bessel} and   $\pi=(\pi_n)_{n\geq1}$ be a sequence of partitions of $[0,T]$ satisfying Assumptions~\ref{ass:partitioncond} and \ref{ass:partitioncond2}. Let
$$
F \in W^{2+,p}(\mathbb{R}^d)\cap W^{2,1}(\mathbb{R}^d),
\qquad 1<p<\infty.
$$
Then there exists a polar set $E\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ such that, for every starting point
$x_0\notin E$, 
$$
\mathbb{P}_{x_0}\left(\ F\in W^2_{B,\pi}\  \right)=1.
$$
Equivalently, for $x_0\notin E$, there exists a sequence $(F_m)_{m\geq1}\subset C_b^2(\mathbb{R}^d)\cap W^{2,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ such that
$$
F_m(B(t))\mathop{\to}^{m\to\infty} F(B(t)),\qquad t\in[0,T],
$$
and
$$
\mathbb{P}_{x_0}\left(\  \|\nabla^2F_m-\nabla^2F\|_{W^0_{B,\pi}}\mathop{\to}^{m\to\infty} 0\right)=1.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 23 of arXiv:2604.07478, 'Mixing Times and Cutoff for the Rook's Walk'] Let $n,d$ be any parameters for the Rook's Walk. Then for $\epsilon\in(0,1)$,
   \[t_\text{mix}(\epsilon) \leq \frac{d(n-1)}{2n} \log d + c_u(\epsilon) \frac{d(n-1)}{n}\]
   where $c_u(\epsilon)$ is a constant dependent only on $\epsilon$.
   \begin{proof}
      Let $u=4\epsilon^2+1$. Then,
      \[u^{1/d} =e^{\log(u^{1/d})}=e^{\frac{1}{d}\log(u)}\]
      Now, $e^x$ is concave up so the first order Taylor approximation is a lower bound; That is, $e^x \geq 1+x$. Therefore,
      \[e^{\frac{1}{d}\log (u)} \geq 1+ \frac{1}{d}\log( u)\]
      or equivalently,
      \[u^{1/d} -1 \geq \frac{\log u}{d}\]
      Now, recall our upper bound from Theorem \ref{main1} and substitute,
      \begin{align*}
          t_\text{mix}(\epsilon) &\leq -\frac{d(n-1)}{2n}\log\left((4\epsilon^2+1)^{1/d}-1 \right)\\
          &= \frac{d(n-1)}{2n}\log\left(\frac{1}{(4\epsilon^2+1)^{1/d}-1 }\right)\\
          &\leq \frac{d(n-1)}{2n}\log\left(\frac{d}{\log (4\epsilon^2 +1)}\right)\\
          &= \frac{d(n-1)}{2n}\left(\log(d) -\log\log(4\epsilon^2+1)\right)\\
          &= \frac{d(n-1)}{2n}\log(d) +c_u(\epsilon) \frac{d(n-1)}{n}
      \end{align*}
      as required.
      
   \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 23 of arXiv:2604.07478

[Corollary eq:diagonal-free-spike of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[corollary]{cor:diagonal-free-spike}
Consider the diagonal-free ordered model
\[
 h_{N,\mathrm{df}}^J(x)=N^{-1/2}
 \sum_{\substack{I\in[N]^p:\ i_1,\ldots,i_p\ \mathrm{distinct}}}J_Ix_I,
 \qquad x\in\mathbb S^{N-1}(1),
\]
with i.i.d. centered \(K\)-sub-Gaussian entries having common law
\(\mu\).  There is \(M=M(p,K)\) such that, for all sufficiently large
\(a\) and every \(\eta>0\),
\begin{align}
 &\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Crt}_{N,\max}^{J,\mathrm{df}}
 \left([ap^{-p/2}-M,(a+\eta)p^{-p/2}+M]\right)\notag\\
 &\hspace{45mm}\ge-\overline I_\mu(a,\eta).
\end{align}
Here \(\operatorname{Crt}_{N,\max}^{J,\mathrm{df}}\) denotes the local-maximum count for \(h_{N,\mathrm{df}}^J\).  Thus the localized one-spike lower-bound mechanism does not rely on repeated tensor indices; this corollary does not compare its exponent with Gaussian diagonal-free complexity.

[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2608.29713, '\textbf{A Cartan geometry from a correspondence space in Riemannian geometry}'] Let $N$ be a smooth manifold of dimension $2n-1$. Cartan geometries of type
$(G,H)$ on $N$, up to isomorphism, are in natural bijection with Cartan datums on $N$. More precisely:
\begin{enumerate}
\item from a Cartan geometry $(p:\mathcal P\to N,\omega)$ of type
$(G,H)$ one obtains the underlying structure
$(\bar g,U,\alpha,\mathcal E,\mathcal B,\Psi)$ of
Proposition~\ref{thm:euc-onminusone-structure-new}, together with the linear connection
$\nabla^{\gamma}$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:canonical-linear-connection-induced};
\item conversely, from a Cartan datum
$\mathcal S:=(\bar g,U,\alpha,\mathcal E,\mathcal B,\Psi,\nabla)$ one constructs canonically a
Cartan geometry $(p_{\mathcal S}:\mathcal P_{\mathcal S}\to N,\omega_{\mathcal S})$ of type
$(G,H)$;
\item these two constructions are mutually inverse, up to canonical isomorphism of $H$-principal fiber bundles.
\end{enumerate}

[Theo 15 of arXiv:2608.30578, 'Compactly Supported Solutions near a Nehari Critical Value'] Assume that $0<\alpha<1$, $m\in L^\infty(\Omega)$, $m\leq0$ a.e. in
$\Omega$, and that
\[
\Omega^0:=\operatorname{int}\{x\in\Omega:m(x)=0\}
\]
is a nonempty connected $C^{1,1}$ domain compactly contained in$\Omega$. Assume also that
	$m<0$ a.e. in $\Omega\setminus\overline{\Omega^0}$.
Then the following assertions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item[i)]
For every
$\lambda\in(\lambda_{1,\Omega},\lambda_{1,\Omega^0})$, problem
\eqref{Eq1} possesses a non-negative weak solution $u_\lambda^-$ such that
\[
E_\lambda(u_\lambda^-)>0,
\qquad
E_\lambda''(u_\lambda^-)<0,
\]
and
\[
E_\lambda(u_\lambda^-)\rightarrow0
\qquad\text{as }\lambda\uparrow\lambda_{1,\Omega^0}.
\]

\item[ii)]
If $\lambda\geq\lambda_{1,\Omega^0}$, then problem \eqref{Eq1} has no
positive weak solution.

\item[iii)]
As $\lambda\uparrow\lambda_{1,\Omega^0}$,
\[
\|u_\lambda^-\|\rightarrow0.
\]
Moreover, after normalizing $\|\varphi_{1,\Omega^0}\|=1$,
\[
\frac{u_\lambda^-}{\|u_\lambda^-\|}
\rightarrow
\widetilde{\varphi}_{1,\Omega^0}
\qquad\text{strongly in }H_0^1(\Omega),
\]
where $\widetilde{\varphi}_{1,\Omega^0}$ denotes the zero extension of
$\varphi_{1,\Omega^0}$ to $\Omega$.

[Definition 1 (The large deviation principle) of arXiv:2605.18198, 'Large deviations of crowding in finite $\beta$-ensembles'] Let $a_n$ be a monotonic increasing sequence with $\lim_{n\to \infty} a_n=\infty.$
A sequence of probability measures $\{\mu_n\}$ on $(\mathcal X,\mathcal B)$ is said to satisfy a \textit{large deviation principle} (LDP) with speed $a_n$ and  rate $I$ if the following hold
\begin{enumerate}
	\item for any open $\mathcal O\subseteq \mathcal X$,
	\[
	\liminf_{n \to \infty}a_n^{-1}\log \mu_n(\mathcal O)\ge - \inf_{x\in \mathcal O}I(x),
	\]
	
	\item for any closed $\mathcal F\subseteq \mathcal X$,
	\[
	\liminf_{n \to \infty}a_n^{-1}\log \mu_n(\mathcal F)\le - \inf_{x\in \mathcal F}I(x).
	\]
\end{enumerate}
title: The large deviation principle

[Theorem thm-detprocess of arXiv:2411.14876, 'Limit theorems for stochastic exponentials of matrix-valued L\'evy processes \\'] Let $L=(L_t)_{t\geq 0}$ be a Lévy process in $\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ with characteristic triplet $(\Sigma_L, \gamma_L, \nu_L)$ and fulfilling (equation eq-nonsingular of the paper) and let $D=(D_t)_{t\geq 0}$ be the determinant process of its stochastic exponential defined in (equation eq-detprocess of the paper). 
	Then $D$ is a left (and right) Lévy process taking values in $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$. In particular, $D_t=\mathcal{E}(\check{L})_t$ for the real-valued (additive) Lévy process $\check{L}=(\check{L}_t)_{t\geq 0}$ given by
	$$\check{L}_t= \operatorname{tr}(L_t) + \frac12 \sum_{\substack{m,n=1\\m\neq n}}^d (\sigma_{(m,m),(n,n)} - \sigma_{(m,n),(n,m)})\cdot  t  + \sum_{0<s\leq t} (\det(\Id + \Delta L_s)-1- \operatorname{tr}(\Delta L_s)), \quad t\geq 0,$$
where $\sigma_{(m,j),(n,\ell)}$ denotes the covariance between the Gaussian components of $L^{(m,j)}$ and $L^{(n,\ell)}$.

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2609.01346, '2609.01346'] Suppose a solution of \eqref{eq:profile-system} approaches, as $s\to s_0$,
\[
 (x,r,\theta)\longrightarrow(x_0,r_0,\theta_0),
 \qquad r_0>0,
 \qquad \theta_0\in\{\pi/2,-\pi/2\},
\]
and assume
\begin{equation}
 x_0\sin\theta_0\neq0.
\end{equation}
Then the solution has a unique local continuation through $s_0$ in the class of
nondegenerate crossings.  If $u=(\theta-\theta_0)^k$, then $u$ is strictly
monotone near $s_0$, and
\begin{equation}
 \theta(s)-\theta_0
 \sim
 \left(\frac{k r_0^{k-1}x_0\sin\theta_0}{A}\right)^{1/k}
 (s-s_0)^{1/k},
\end{equation}
where the real $k$-th root is understood.  In particular,
\begin{align}
 x(s)-x_0&=O(|s-s_0|^{(k+1)/k}),\\
 r(s)-r_0&=O(|s-s_0|),\\
 \left|\frac{d\theta}{ds}(s)\right|&\sim
 \frac1k\left|\frac{k r_0^{k-1}x_0\sin\theta_0}{A}\right|^{1/k}
 |s-s_0|^{-(k-1)/k}.
\end{align}
Writing $\gamma=(x,r)$, there are constants $C>0$ and $\eta>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \left|
 \frac{d\gamma}{ds}(s)-\frac{d\gamma}{ds}(t)
 \right|
 \leq C|s-t|^{1/k}
 \qquad
 \text{whenever }|s-s_0|<\eta\text{ and }|t-s_0|<\eta.
\end{equation}
Consequently the profile curve is $C^{1,1/k}$ near the crossing, and the
exponent $1/k$ is optimal.  It is also locally $W^{2,p}$ for every
$1\leq p<k/(k-1)$, but it is not $W^{2,k/(k-1)}$ at the crossing.
title: Lemma 5 of arXiv:2609.01346

body: [Cor 3 of arXiv:2608.26698, 'Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion '] The mapping class group $\mathrm{MCG}(S^2 \times S^3)$ is isomorphic to $(\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}) \rtimes \mathbb{Z}/2$, where the action of the nontrivial element of $\mathbb{Z}/2$ on $\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}$ is given by sending an element to its inverse. In other words, $\mathrm{MCG}(S^2 \times S^3)$ has the following presentation: \[\left\langle a, b, v | ab = ba, v^2 = 1, vav = a^{-1}, vbv = b^{-1} \right\rangle,\] where $a$ and $b$ can be represented by the Dehn twists $\mathbf{t}_{S_1, \alpha}$ and $\mathbf{t}_{S_1 \# S_1, \alpha}$ respectively, and $v$ can be represented by $R$. It follows that $\mathrm{MCG}(S^2 \times S^3)$ is residually finite and virtually torsion-free, and has trivial center. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor 3 of arXiv:2608.26698

body:
[Lemma 25 (Eigenvalue rigidity) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{lem:rigidity}
Let \(A\) be a matrix such that \(A/\sqrt n\) has the distribution of GUE.
Let
\[
\lambda_1 \leq \lambda_2 \leq \cdots \leq \lambda_n
\]
denote its eigenvalues, and let \(\gamma_i\) be the corresponding classical
location for the semicircle law, defined by
\[
\int_{-\infty}^{\gamma_i}
\frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{(4-x^2)_+}\,dx
=
\frac{i}{n}.
\]
Then for every \(1\leq i\leq n\),
\[
\mathbb P\left(
n^{-1/3}\min(i,n-i+1)^{1/3}
\left|\lambda_i-\sqrt n\,\gamma_i\right|
\geq T
\right)
\ll
n^{O(1)}\exp(-cT^c)
\]
for all \(T>0\), where \(c>0\) is an absolute constant.

In particular, with overwhelming probability,
\[
\lambda_i
=
\sqrt n\,\gamma_i
+
O\!\left(
n^{1/3}\min(i,n-i+1)^{-1/3}\log^{O(1)} n
\right),
\]
and the same estimate holds with \(\lambda_i\) replaced by
\(\mathbb E\lambda_i\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Eigenvalue rigidity

body:
[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2608.19832, 'Sharp Convex Concentration for Symmetric Random Tensors with Subgaussian Coordinates'] Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\R$ with
$\int e^{x^2/K^2}\,d\mu\le2$. Let $\nu\ll\mu$, and assume
\[
 h=D(\nu\Vert\mu)<\infty.
\]
There is a coupling $(U,V)$ of $\mu$ and $\nu$ such that
\begin{align}
 \E\left[\E(\abs{U-V}\mid U)^2\right]
 &\le C K^2h\log\left(e+\frac1h\right),
 \\
 \E\left[\E(\abs{U-V}\mid V)^2\right]
 &\le C K^2h\log\left(e+\frac1h\right),
 \\
 \E\abs{U-V}^2
 &\le C K^2(\sqrt h+h).
 
\end{align}
The right sides are interpreted as zero when $h=0$.

[Lem 30 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recall from Lemma~\ref{l:freeprob.V.convex} that $z_{\min}$ is the unique minimizer of $V$ on the interval $[z_0,\infty)$.
    We have $z_{\min} = z_0$ if and only if
    \beq
        
        \alpha \le \mu_1 \textup{ and } \hv_1 < 0\,.
    \eeq
    If \eqref{e:zmin-equal-z0} does not hold, $z_{\min}$ is the unique solution to the equation $V'(z) = 0$ for $z\in(z_0,\infty)$.

\begin{proof}
Recall that if $\hv_1 > 0$, then $V(z)\uparrow\infty$ as $z\downarrow z_0$, so in this case clearly $z_{\min} > z_0$.
If instead $\hv_1 < 0$, then $z_0 = \hw_1$, so we have $z_{\min}=z_0$ if and only if the derivative $V'$ stays nonnegative as $z\downarrow \hw_1$. To this end, recall that as $z\downarrow \hw_1$ we have $m(z)\uparrow\infty$, so
    \[\sum_{j=1}^r \lambda_j \bigg(
        \frac{\hv_j m(z)}{\alpha - \hv_j m(z)}\bigg)^2
        \longrightarrow \sum_{j=1}^r \lambda_j = 1\,.\]
We also have $m_2(z)/m(z)^2 \to 1/\mu_1$, and substituting into
\eqref{e:fp-V-pr} gives
    \[
        V'(z)
        \longrightarrow 1 - \frac{\alpha}{\mu_1}
    \]
   as $z\downarrow\hw_1$. This is nonnegative if and only if $\alpha \le \mu_1$, which yields the condition \eqref{e:zmin-equal-z0}. Otherwise, we must have $z_{\min} > z_0$; in this case, since $V$ is strictly convex and twice differentiable, the value $z_{\min}$ must be the unique solution to the equation $V'(z) = 0$ for $z\in(z_0,\infty)$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[campaign result 2026-09-14, author_checked_exact_integer_arithmetic_no_independent_read] This refutes the literal p=d condition in M. Neri and P. Pinto's Remark 3.7 in Quantitative limit theorems for generalized Polya urns with applications to random tree models, arXiv:2607.07309. Let R be a real d-by-d replacement matrix with each row sum equal to lambda, let I_d be the identity matrix, and define symm(A)=(A+A^T)/2. Set C_d=J_d=I_d. The real symmetric matrix G=symm(C_d J_d(R^T-lambda I_d) C_d^T)=symm(R^T-lambda I_d) has largest eigenvalue at least zero. Thus the strict inequality lambda_max(G)<0 cannot hold on the full d-dimensional space for any balanced replacement matrix. This statement concerns the full-space matrix in the remark; it does not assert failure of every possible restriction to mean-zero vectors. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
All row sums of R equal lambda; d>=1.

Ansatz 20, stated inside Open Problem 8 of Aldous and Janson (arXiv:2303.02529), claims for nonnegative f with f(j) = O(j^k) that (i) if sum_i a(i) f(i) converges then sum_{i <= n} a(n,i) f(i) tends to it, and (ii) if it diverges then sum_{i <= n} a(n,i) f(i) is asymptotic to sum_{i <= n} a(i) f(i); here a(n,j) is the probability that the tagged harmonic descent chain started at n visits j and a(j) = 6 H_{j-1} / (pi^2 (j-1)) is its fixed-j limit. Our result (id P0341, 2026-09-08): BOTH parts are FALSE, on the single observation that a(n,n) = 1 exactly - the chain starts at n, so it visits n surely. For (i), take f(j) = 1{j = 2^r}: f is bounded (hence of polynomial growth) and a(2^r) = O(r 2^-r), so S = sum a(i) f(i) converges; but at n = 2^K the truncated sum contains the top term a(2^K, 2^K) = 1, forcing liminf >= 1 + S against the predicted S. For (ii), take g(j) = j 1{j = 2^r} (so g(j) <= j): since a(j) j ~ (6/pi^2) log j the truncated limiting sum at n = 2^K is of order K^2 while the actual sum is at least its root term 2^K, so the ratio diverges. The refutation is scoped to the displayed Ansatz, not to Open Problem 8 as a whole - explicit bounds on |a(n,m) - a(m)| remain open. Verification as the source words it: each piece re-derived (the asymptotics of a(j) and a(j) j, the summability of a(2^r), the polynomial-growth hypothesis for both test functions, and a(n,n) = 1 from the definition); no rate of convergence and no numerical evaluation is needed anywhere. Prior art not cleared.

body:
[Theorem thm:erm-fragile of arXiv:2608.20480, 'When Clean Data Hurts: Learning with Monotone \\ Corruptions Beyond Binary Classification'] There is a countable, closed class $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{frag}}$ of finite coordinatewise range, with $d_{\mathrm{DS}}(\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{frag}})=1$, that is ordinarily PAC learnable by a proper ERM.  Nevertheless, for every fixed $\alpha>0$ and every possibly randomized ERM rule $A$, an oblivious adversary using at most $\alpha n$ additions can force
\[
    \liminf_{n\to\infty}
    \sup_{D,h^\star,\mathsf{Adv}}
    \mathbb{E} L_D(A(T),h^\star)
    \geq
    c_\alpha>0,
\]
where the supremum ranges over oblivious adversaries of budget at most $\alpha n$, and $c_\alpha$ may be taken of order $e^{-1/\alpha}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Oblivious additions destroy ERM

[Lemma 4 (Order statistics) of arXiv:2506.09333, 'On the Dimension-Free Concentration of Simple Tensors via Matrix Deviation'] Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent random variables satisfying $\norm{X_i}_\psitwo \le 1$ for all $i$. Let $t>0$, $q \ge 2$ and 
    $k \coloneqq t/\ln_+(en/t)$.
    Then,\footnote{By convention, we set $1/0=\infty$ in defining $k$, and the sum over an empty set is zero.} with probability at least $1-2e^{-t}$, we have
    \begin{equation} 
        \sum_{i \le 3k} (X_i^*)^2 \lesssim t
        \quad \text{and} \quad 
        \sum_{i > k} (X_i^*)^q \lesssim_q n.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Order statistics

[Theorem 10 (Uniform concentration of LOO) of arXiv:2608.30261, 'Estimating Population-Risk Curves Along Nonconvex Gradient Flows from the Training Sample'] Assume \eqref{eq:loss-range-length}, finite $\beta_{n-1}$ in
\eqref{eq:uniform-stability}, the size-$(n-1)$ modulus

$r>0$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$, let $s_n(r,\delta),c_n^-\in[0,\infty)$ be the
finite deterministic concentration radius and bounded-difference coefficient
defined in \cref{eq:sn-definition,eq:bounded-difference-c}.  Then, with probability
at least $1-\delta$,
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{u\in\mathcal U}
 |\Score_{n,\mathcal U}^{\LOO}(u)-\Risk_{S,\mathcal U}^-(u)|
 \leq s_n(r,\delta),
\end{equation}
where
\begin{align}
 s_n(r,\delta)
 &=2\omega_{n-1}(r)
 +c_n^-\sqrt{\frac n2
 \log\frac{2\mathcal N(\mathcal U,\rho,r)}{\delta}},\\
 c_n^-&=\frac{B_{n-1}^{\rm rng}}n+\frac{2(n-1)}n\beta_{n-1}.
 
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2608.16752, 'Absorption Probabilities for Random Convex Hulls: Distribution-Freeness via the Wall-Cross'] For integers $n,d\geq 1$ we have
$$
\sum_{\ell=1}^{n}
\stirling{n}{\ell}\,
2^{\,n-\ell}
\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}
\binom{\ell-1}{j}
=
\sum_{q\geq 0}
\stirlingb{n}{d-1-2q},
$$
where the numbers $\stirlingb{n}{k}$ with $n\in \{1,2,\ldots\}$, $k\in \mathbb Z$,  are defined by the generating function
$$
\sum_{k\in \mathbb Z} \stirlingb{n}{k} t^k
=
(t+1)(t+3)\cdots(t+2n-1).
$$

body: [Definition 34 of arXiv:2608.27630, 'Oriented planar maps and \\ annular mating of trees'] Let $\cD=(\bH, \phi,  0, \infty)$ be an embedding of a quantum disk from $\mathcal{M}_2^{\mathrm{disk}}(\frac{\gamma^2}{2};a,b)$ as in Definition~\ref{def-quantum-disk} and~\eqref{eq:QD-dis}, and let $\eta'$ be a  space-filling  $\SLE_{\kappa'}(0;\kappa'/2-4)$ from 0 to $\infty$ independent from $\phi$ and  parameterized by LQG area with respect to $\phi$. body:
[Lemma circular_law of arXiv:2606.16609, 'On stability of outliers from the circular law'] Let $\{ \lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_N \}$ the spectrum of a complex Ginibre matrix conditioned on $\{ \lambda_1 = z \}$ with fixed $z \in \mathbb{C}$; almost surely, the empirical spectral distribution
$$
\frac{1}{N-1} \sum_{k=2}^N \delta_{\lambda_k}
$$
converges weakly to the circular law. That is to say that, for any continuous bounded function~$\phi$, we have
$$
\frac{1}{N-1} \sum_{k=2}^N \phi(\lambda_k) 
\xrightarrow[]{N \rightarrow \infty} 
\frac{1}{\pi} \int_{\mathbb{D}} \phi(z) \mathrm{d} z.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Conditional Circular Law \cite{Thomas2026}

[Definition 5 of arXiv:2604.19220, 'Split merge dynamics for expanding intervals and point processes on the real line.'] For $ r,s > 0, $ a random variable has a distribution $\beta_{r, s}(0,1)$ if its density 
with respect to the Lebesgue measure  $ dx $ on $ [0,1]$ is 
$$ \beta_{r, s}(0,1)(x)=  \frac{x^{r-1} (1-x)^{s-1}}{\int_0^1 x^{r-1} (1-x)^{s-1} dx}{\mathbf 1}_{x \in [0,1]}.$$ For $ a <  b $ we denote $ Y \overset{d}{=} \beta_{r, s}(a,b) $
if $ \frac{Y - a }{b- a } $ has $\beta_{p, q}(0,1)$ distribution. We often drop 
$ (0,1) $    in $\beta_{p, q}(0,1).$ The density of $ \beta_{r, s}(a,b) $ is $ (b-a) \beta_{r, s}(0,1)(\frac{x-a}{y-b}).$  By convention we set $ \beta_{r, s}(a,a)= \delta_a (dx). $

    \[\WERR(\cA_N,\tilde{\cA}_N)
    \equiv
        \max\bigg\{
        \bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_N),
        \mu(\tilde \cA_N)
        	\Big)^2,
        \bbW_2\Big(
        	\mu^{\Ising}(\cA_N),
        \mu^{\Ising}(\tilde \cA_N)
        \Big)^2
        \bigg\}
        \le C_1 \delta + C_2e^{-c_0N}\,.
    \]

[Lem 76 (Kolmogorov continuity lemma for distributions) of arXiv:2510.22155, 'Random walks in space-time random media in all spatial dimensions: the full subcritical fl'] Let $(t,\phi) \mapsto V(t,\phi)$ be a map from $[0,T]\times \mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ into $L^2(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ which is linear and continuous in $\phi$. Fix a non-negative integer $r$. Assume there exists some $\kappa>0, q>d/\kappa$ and $\alpha<-r$ and $C=C(\kappa,\alpha,q,{T})>0$ such that 
		\begin{align*}\mE[|V(t,S^\lambda_{x}\phi)|^q]^{1/q}&\leq C\lambda^{\alpha },\\  \mE[|V(t,S^\lambda_{x}\phi)-V(s,S^\lambda_{x}\phi)|^q]^{1/q}&\leq C\lambda^{\alpha -\kappa} |t-s|^{\kappa },
		\end{align*}uniformly over all smooth functions $\phi$ on $\mathbb R$ supported on the unit ball of $\mathbb R$ with {$\|\phi\|_{C^r}\leq 1$}, and uniformly over $\lambda\in(0,1]$ and $0\leq s,t\leq T$. Then for any $\tau>1$ and any $\beta<\alpha-\kappa$ there exists a random variable $\big(\mathscr V(t)\big)_{t\in[0,T]}$ taking values in $C([0,T],C^{\beta,\tau}(\mathbb R^d))$ such that $(\mathscr V(t),\phi)=V(t,\phi)$ almost surely for all $\phi$ and $t$. Furthermore, one has that $$\mE[\|\mathscr V\|^q_{C([0,T],C^{\beta,\tau}(\mathbb R^d))}]\leq C',$$ where $C'$ depends on the choice of $\alpha,\beta,q,\kappa,$ and the constant $C$ appearing in the moment bound above but not on $V,\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Kolmogorov continuity lemma for distributions

[Definition 24 of arXiv:2605.26664, 'Mixing times for Glauber dynamics of lozenge tilings of the hexagon'] Removing the six locations at which $\mathfrak{A}_{q;a,b,c}$ is tangent to $\partial \mathfrak{X}_{a,b,c}$ disconnects $\mathfrak{X}_{a,b,c} \setminus \overline{\mathfrak{L}}_{q;a,b,c}$ into six frozen regions $\mathfrak F^i_{q;a,b,c},i\in\{ N, NE, SE, S, SW, NW \}$ (see \Cref{fig:liquid}).
  We let $p^i_{q;a,b,c},i\in \{ NW, NE,E,  SE, SW, W \}$ denote the six tangency points; see Fig \ref{fig:liquid}, and 
   we let  $p^{SW}_{q;a,b,c}=(x^{SW}_{q;a,b,c},0)$ and $p^W_{q;a,b,c}= (0,y^W_{q;a,b,c})$.

[Lemma lem:feature-conjugacy of arXiv:2607.00149, '\bf Uniform-in-time Propagation-of-Chaos for\\ Stein Variational Gradient Descent'] Let $\widetilde b_j$ be the columns of $\widetilde B$, and let $b_j^H$ be the columns of $B_H$.  Define
\[
        \widetilde f_j(y)
        :=\operatorname{div}_y\widetilde b_j(y)-\widetilde b_j(y)\cdot\nabla\widetilde V(y),
\]
and
\[
        f_j^H(x)
        :=\operatorname{div}_x b_j^H(x)-b_j^H(x)\cdot\nabla V_H(x).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
        f_j^H(H(y))=\widetilde f_j(y),
        \qquad j=1,\ldots,m.
\end{equation}
Consequently, if $\rho_H=H_{\#}\widetilde\rho$, then
\begin{equation}
        \rho_H F_H=\widetilde\rho\,\widetilde F.
\end{equation}

[Proposition 15 of arXiv:2605.12475, 'Central limit theorem for the homozygosity of the hierarchical Pitman-Yor process'] For all $1 \leq k \leq L$, the following multivariate CLT holds 
\bal
(X_{1,k}(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta), X_m(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta), T_1(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta), T_m(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta), Y_m(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta)) \xrightarrow{D} N(\bm{0}, \bm{\Sigma})
\eal
as $\theta_0, \theta \to \infty$ such that $\frac{\theta_0}{\theta} \to c$, where the covariance matrix is given by
\bal
\bm{\Sigma} = \begin{pmatrix}
1 - \beta & B_k(\alpha, \beta, c, m, L) & 0 & 0 & 0 \\

0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \sigma_{Y,L}^2
