[Theorem thm:convbls of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Consider a bounded simply-connected domain $D$ and sequence $(\widetilde D_m)_{m\geq 1}$ of approximating metric graphs via the lattice $\frac{1}{m}\mathbb{Z}^2$. 

In these domains consider the Brownian loop soup 
$\mathcal{L}_D$ at the critical intensity 
($\alpha=1/2$ or central charge $c=1$) and the metric graph loop soup $\widetilde \mathcal{L}_{\widetilde D_m}$ also at the critical intensity. 
Let $\widetilde \Xi^a_{\widetilde D_m}$ denote the PPP of Brownian boundary to boundary excursions of intensity $a \geq 0$ on the metric graph $\widetilde D_m$, 
and $\Xi^a_{D}$ the corresponding PPP of Brownian boundary to boundary excursions in the continuum.

Finally, let $(\widetilde C_k^m)_{k \geq 1}$ be the clusters of 
$\widetilde \Xi^a_{\widetilde D_m} 
\cup \widetilde \mathcal{L}_{\widetilde D_m}$, 
and $(C_k)_{k \geq 1}$ the clusters of 
$\Xi^a_{D} \cup \mathcal{L}_D$,  listed say by the order of decreasing diameter. 
Denote by $\widetilde \gamma, \gamma$ closed paths on the metric graph and in the continuum respectively.

Then for any $z_1,\dots, z_n \in D$ distinct points, and any $\varepsilon_1, \dots, \varepsilon_n \geq 0$, we have that the probabilities
$$\tilde p_{a,m} := \mathbb{P}\left(\nexists \widetilde C_i^{m}\text{ with }\widetilde \gamma \in \widetilde C_i^{ m}\text{ such that} \sum_{j=1}^{n}
\indx_{\widetilde \gamma}(z_j)
\text{ odd}
 \: \& \: \widetilde C_i^{m} \cap \bigcup_{j=1}^n\mathbb{D}(z_j, \varepsilon_j) = \emptyset\right)$$ 
converge, as $m \to \infty$ to 
$$p_a := \mathbb{P}\left(\nexists C_i\text{ with }\gamma \in C_i\text{ such that} \sum_{j=1}^{n}
\indx_{\gamma}(z_j)
\text{ odd}
 \: \& \: C_i \cap \bigcup_{j=1}^n\mathbb{D}(z_j, \varepsilon_j) = \emptyset\right).$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:convbls of arXiv:2604.15146

Own work, proof (unaudited), W719-T295-C010 v1; conditional route calculation, no novelty claim. The exact omitted-row GD perturbation satisfies Delta_next=(I-eta Q_minus)Delta-(eta/m)((a_i^T x)^2-g_i^2)(a_i^T x)a_i, with explicit symmetric polynomial secant matrix Q_minus. Assuming row norm/projection bounds, same-rate perturbation contraction rho=1-eta mu, and an error envelope R0 rho^t, the norm-only forcing bootstrap yields normalized envelope coefficient at most D0+(eta B/rho)(d/m)(log d)t. Its scalar inequality admits equality; at t=ceil(1/eta), eta=c/log d, linear m leaves a log d deficit. This is a proof-strategy obstruction, not an actual GD lower bound. Let ell=log d and assume ||a_i||<=A sqrt(d), |g_i|<=G sqrt(ell), ||h_t||<=r, |a_i^T h_t|<=K sqrt(ell)||h_t||, ||I-eta Q_minus||<=rho, and ||h_t||<=R0 rho^t. Here B=A K(2G^2+3GKr+K^2r^2) and D0=sqrt(d/ell)||Delta_0||/R0. Then sqrt(d/ell)||Delta_t||/(R0 rho^t)<=D0+(eta B/rho)(d/m)ell*t. No relative-error bound follows without comparing R0 rho^t to actual ||h_t||. At m of order d log d this particular coefficient is bounded after t of order 1/eta, but all trajectory assumptions still need proof. No actual divergence or oversampling necessity is established.
quartic noiseless phase retrieval loss normalized by 1/(4m); omitted-row loss keeps denominator m
forcing calculation assumes max row norm<=A sqrt(d), max signal projection<=G sqrt(log d), error radius<=r, relative incoherence constant K
geometric-series calculation additionally assumes norm contraction of the actual secant matrices and a same-rate error upper envelope; neither is established here

[Thm 12 (Convergence of root statistics and their expectations) of arXiv:2608.06576, 'The Resultant Distribution Method: Universality for $p$-adic Random Matrices and Polynomia'] Fix an integer $m\geq 1$. Let $K_1,\ldots,K_m$ be finite extensions
of $\Q_p$, and let
$$
U\subseteq\mc{O}_{K_1}^{\new}
\times\cdots\times\mc{O}_{K_m}^{\new}
$$
be clopen. Let $P_1^S,P_2^S,\ldots$ be random elements of $\mathscr{P}^S$
satisfying the assumptions of
\Cref{thm: resultant distribution convergence introduction}, and let
$P_\infty^S\in\mathscr{P}^S$ be the limiting random polynomial provided
by that theorem. Suppose that
$$
\mathbf{P}\left(P_\infty^S\text{ has a repeated root}\right)=0.
$$
Then $Z_U(P_n^S)\overset{d}{\longrightarrow}
Z_U(P_\infty^S)$. If, in addition, the degree tightness assumption is strengthened to moment tightness, i.e.,
$$
\lim_{D\to\infty}\sup_{n\geq 1}
\mathbf{E}\left[(\deg P_n^S)^m
\mathbf{1}_{\{\deg P_n^S>D\}}
\right]=0,
$$
then
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbf{E}\left[
Z_U(P_n^S)\right]=\mathbf{E}\left[
Z_U(P_\infty^S)\right].
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Convergence of root statistics and their expectations

[Lemma lem:singfiltfunc of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] Let 
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
    V \arrow[r,"f"]\arrow[d,swap,"T"] & V'\arrow[d,"T'"] \\
    W \arrow[r,swap,"g"] & W' 
\end{tikzcd}
\]
be a commutative diagram of normed vector spaces over $K$, where $f$ and $g$ are non-expansive. 
Then $\operatorname{gr}f$ and $\operatorname{gr}g$ are filtration preserving in the sense that
\[
(\operatorname{gr}f)(\cF^-(T)_{\leq\beta})\subseteq \cF^-(T')_{\leq\beta},\qquad (\operatorname{gr}g)(\cF^+(T)_{\geq\beta})\subseteq \cF^+(T')_{\geq\beta}.
\]

[Defn 1 (Markov Kernels) of arXiv:2510.22155, 'Random walks in space-time random media in all spatial dimensions: the full subcritical fl'] Fix $d\ge 1$. Let $I$ be any locally compact additive subgroup of $\mathbb R^d$, for example $I=\mathbb R^d$ or $I=A \mathbb Z^d$ where $A$ is some nonsingular $d\times d$ matrix. Let $\mathcal B(I)$ denote the Borel $\sigma$-algebra on $I$. 
A \textit{Markov kernel} on $I$ is a continuous function from $I\to \mathcal P(I)$, where $\mathcal P(I)$ is the space of probability measures on $(I,\mathcal B(I))$ equipped with the topology of weak convergence of probability measures. 

Any Markov kernel $K$ on $I$ shall be written as $K(   x,A)$, which is identified with the continuous function from $I\to \mathcal P(I)$ given by $x\mapsto K(   x,\cdot)$. We denote by $\mathcal M(I)$ the space of all Markov kernels on $I$.

We equip $\mathcal M(I)$ with the weakest topology under which the maps $T_{f,   x}:\mathcal M(I)\to \mathbb R$ given by $$K\stackrel{T_{f,   x}}{\mapsto}  \int_I f(   y)\;K(   x,\mathrm d   y)$$ 
are continuous, where one varies over all $x\in I$ and all bounded continuous functions $f:I\to \mathbb R$. This topology endows $\mathcal M(I)$ with a Borel $\sigma$-algebra which allows us to talk about random variables taking values in the space of Markov kernels. For $   a\in I$ define the translation operator $\tau_a:\mathcal M(I)\to \mathcal M(I)$ by $(  \tau_{   a} K)(   x,A):= K(x+   a,A+   a)$ which is a Borel-measurable map on this space.
title: Markov Kernels

[Lemma 18 of arXiv:2608.14802, 'Dynamical Gibbs-non-Gibbs transitions for finite-alphabet models on trees'] Let $i\in \{2,3\}$ and $R_i>0$ the threshold given in Corollary \ref{cor: differential normalized potts map}. Then, for each $r_i\in (0,R_i)$ there exists $t^{(i)}_2=t^{(i)}_2(r_i)<\infty$ 
and a unique family $\left(l^{(i)}(t)\right)_{t\geq t^{(i)}_2}$ 
such that the following holds. 

The family defines a continuation of $l^{(i)}_+$, i.e. it satisfies $\lim_{t\rightarrow \infty}l^{(i)}(t)=l^{(i)}_+$ and $l^{(i)}(t)\in U_{r_i}$ for all $t\geq t^{(i)}_2$. [Definition 12 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] A limiting point \(\xi=(\mu_t)_{t<T}\) is \emph{based at \(q\)} with
respect to the limiting morphism \(\pi\) if
\(\pi_*\mu_t\rightharpoonup\delta_q\).  Such a \(q\) is unique when it
exists, and we denote it by \(q_\pi(\xi)\).  It is
\emph{Type-I based at \(q\)} if there is \(C_\xi<\infty\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \int_Xd_\eta(\pi(x),q)^2\,d\mu_t(x)\le C_\xi(T-t)
 \qquad\text{for every }0\le t<T.
\end{equation}
If \(q\in Y^{\rm rv}\) and \(\rho_q\) is a localized
squared-distance barrier from \cref{def:squared-distance-barrier},
compactness and the defining comparisons for \(\rho_q\) show that this
is equivalent to
\[
 \int_X\rho_q\circ\pi\,d\mu_t\le C'_\xi(T-t).
\]
For an arbitrary holomorphic map, qualitative basing alone need not
imply this rate.  For the semiample K\"ahler--Ricci flow considered here,
\Cref{lem:automatic-label} proves that every limiting point is based at
a unique point \(q_\pi(\xi)\) and is Type-I based there.  Thus
\eqref{eq:label-moment} is never an additional hypothesis below.  When
\(q_\pi(\xi)\in Y^{\rm rv}\), we simply say that \(\xi\) is based at
the regular value \(q_\pi(\xi)\).
title: Definition 12 of arXiv:2609.02878

[Theorem 23 of arXiv:2608.30549, '\vspace{-1cm}Maximally Spread Out Measures and Implications\\{} for Phase Transitions in A'] Let $(\XX,\norm{\cdot})$ be a quasi-normed space with modulus of concavity $C_2 \ge 1$.
    Assume that $\SC$ satisfies {\ConditionZetaTextAlphaC{(\alpha,C_0)}} for some constants $\alpha, C_0>0$.
    Let $s\ge0$, $t\in \RR$ (with $t>0$ if $s=0$), and let $c_1>0$. 
    Let $(\SC_n)_{n\in\NN}$ be a sequence of finite $2^{-n}$-separated subsets $\SC_n \subset \SC$,
    and let $n_0\in \NN$ such that
    \begin{equation}
        \num\SC_n \ge \exp\bigl( c_1 \cdot 2^{ns}n^{t}\bigr)
        \quad \text{for all $n\ge n_0$.}
        
    \end{equation}
    Then the measure $\mu$ given in \cref{definition_measure_SC_n} satisfies the following:
    There exist $r_0>0$ and $c>0$ such that
    \begin{equation}
        \om{\mu}\bigl(\ball(x,r)\bigr) 
        \le \exp\biggl( - c  
        \cdot \Bigl(\frac{1}{r}\Bigr)^{s} \cdot \Bigl( \log_2 \Bigl(\frac{1}{r}\Bigr)\Bigr)^{t-\alpha s}\biggr)
        
    \end{equation}
    for all $r\in (0,r_0)$ and all $x\in \XX$.
title: Theorem 23 of arXiv:2608.30549

[Definition def:disagree-polymer-len-energy-decor of arXiv:2509.04333, 'The limiting law of the Discrete Gaussian level lines'] Let $(\gamma,\{D_i\},\{h_i\})$ be a labeled disagreement polymer. Its \emph{length} ${\ensuremath{\mathscr N}}(\gamma)$ and \emph{energy} 
		${\ensuremath{\mathscr E}}_\beta(\gamma)$ are defined as
		\[{\ensuremath{\mathscr N}}(\gamma)=\sum_{e\in\gamma}|(\nabla \phi)_e|\quad,\quad 
		{\ensuremath{\mathscr E}}_\beta(\gamma) := \beta\sum_{e \in \gamma} |(\nabla \phi)_e|^2\,.\]
		To describe the law of the disagreement polymer, we will use a family of decoration functions $\Phi$ on subsets ${\ensuremath{\mathsf W}}\subset \mathbb Z^2$---each referred to as a cluster if it is also connected---
        satisfying the following properties.
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item  If ${\ensuremath{\mathsf W}}$ is not connected, then $\Phi({\ensuremath{\mathsf W}}) = 0$.
			
			\item 
			The function $\Phi$ is translation invariant, as well as invariant under a rotation by $\pi/2$ or reflection with respect to one of the axes.
			
			\item There exists a constant $C > 0$ such that for every ${\ensuremath{\mathsf W}}$, we have 
			$
			|\Phi({\ensuremath{\mathsf W}})| \leq \exp(-(\beta - C){\ensuremath{\mathbf d}}({\ensuremath{\mathsf W}}))
			$, 
			where ${\ensuremath{\mathbf d}}({\ensuremath{\mathsf W}})$ is the size of the smallest connected set of bonds in $(\mathbb Z^2)^*$ containing all the boundary bonds of ${\ensuremath{\mathsf W}}$.
		\end{enumerate}
title: Energy, length and decorations of a disagreement polymer

[Lemma reductiontoA2 of arXiv:2507.16188, 'The noisy voter model with general initial conditions'] Let $\{W_i\}_{i=1}^m$ be subsets with $|W_i|\leq 3$ and $\operatorname{dist}_G(W_i,W_j) \geq \frac{1}{2}(\log n)^{1+\beta}$, and let $\Delta$ denote the maximum degree in $G$. Then for every $t\geq 0$,
\[
\sum_{i=1}^m d_{\textsc{tv}}^{\mathsf{x}_0}(W_i,t)^2 \leq 18q\Delta n \left( t^2\mathcal{A}^{(2)}_t(\mathsf{x}_0) + (t+1)e^{-4 \theta t}\right) + O(n^{-9})\,.
\]
title: Lemma reductiontoA2 of arXiv:2507.16188

\[
\overline{F}_{N(k)}(n):=\mathbb{P}(N(k)\ge n)=F_n(k),
\]
and consequently

\begin{eqnarray*}
F_{N(k)}(n)&:=&\mathbb{P}(N(k)\le n)=1-F_{n+1}(k),\\
f_{N(k)}(n)&:=&\mathbb{P}(N(k)=n)=F_n(k)-F_{n+1}(k).
\end{eqnarray*}

body:
[Lemma 14 (\textsf{Zero-temperature convergence of the free energy}) of arXiv:2609.02064, 'Coalescence and fluctuations of O'Connell--Yor polymers\\ via the free-energy correlation '] Fix $n\in\Z_{>0}$, $\al\in\R$, and a compact interval
  $J\subset\R$.  For every $p<\infty$,
  \begin{align}
    \EE\Big[
      \sup_{u\in J}
      |F_u^{\al,\be}-L_u^{\al}|^p
    \Big]
    \longrightarrow0
    \qquad\text{as }\be\to\infty.
  \end{align}
  In particular, for fixed $u,v\in\R$,
  \[
    \EE\bigl[F_u^{\al,\be}F_v^{\al,\be}\bigr]
    \longrightarrow
    \EE\bigl[L_u^{\al}L_v^{\al}\bigr].
  \]

body: [Lemma lem:gff_ergodic of arXiv:2411.13133, 'Connectivity of the adjacency graph of\\ complementary components of the $\SLE$ Fan'] Suppose that $r > 0, r \neq 1$ and $h$ is a GFF on $\mathbf{H}$ with boundary conditions given by $-a$ on $\mathbf{R}_-$ and $b$ on $\mathbf{R}_+$. Let $\theta_r$ be the transformation from the space of distributions on $\mathbf{H}$ to itself given by $(\theta_r(h))(\phi) = h((1/r^2)\phi(\cdot/r))$. Then $\theta_r$ is ergodic and measure-preserving on $(\mathcal {D}'(\mathbf{H}), \mathcal {F}, \mathbf{P})$, where $\mathcal {D}'(\mathbf{H})$ is the space of distributions on $\mathbf{H}$, $\mathcal {F}$ is the $\sigma$-algebra generated by the random variables $(h, \phi)$ for $\phi \in C_0^\infty(\mathbf{H})$ and $\mathbf{P}$ is the law of $h$.

body:
[Theorem Th_degrees of arXiv:2607.14792, 'On the degree distribution of large tentacular Bienaymé--Galton--Watson trees'] Let $d \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 2}$. Assume that $k_n = o(n)$, $k_n\rightarrow \infty$ and $\mu(2)>0$.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item If $k_n=o( n^{\frac{d-1}{d}})$, then \[\mathbb{P}\left(\mathrm{deg_{max}}(T_n^{k_n}) \leq d  \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.\]
        \item Let $c>0$. If $k_n\underset{n \to \infty}{\sim} cn^{\frac{d-1}{d}}$, 
        \[\phi_{d+1}\left(T_n^{k_n}\right) \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{(d)} \mathrm{Poi}\left( c^d\frac{\mu(d+1)\mu(1)^{d-1}}{\mu(2)^d} \right). \]
        \item If $k_n^d/n^{d-1} \rightarrow + \infty$ as $n\rightarrow +\infty$, then for every $p \geq 1$ 
\[ \frac{n^{d-1}}{k_n^d}\phi_{d+1}\left(T_{n}^{k_n}\right) \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{L^p} \frac{\mu(1)^{d-1}\mu(d+1)}{\mu(2)^d}.\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition prop:CPRE-BDS of arXiv:2507.00329, 'Oriented bond-site percolation in random environment and contact processes with periodic r'] Let $\varDelta>0$ be a random variable, with $\mathbb{E}[\varDelta^{1+\varepsilon}]<\infty$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, and fix $\delta>0$ and $p\in(0,1)$. Let $(\varDelta_x)_{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}}$ be an i.i.d.\ family of random variables distributed according to $\mathcal{L}(\varDelta)$, the law of $\varDelta$. Consider the generalised contact process on $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}$ with $\mathbb{X}\sim\mathrm{PPP}(1)$ and recovery times  $(\mathbb{Y}_x)_{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}}$ given by independent copies of the following Cox point processes:
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item With probability $p$ (independent of everything else), let $\mathbb{Y}_x\sim\mathrm{PPP}(\delta)$.  
        \item Otherwise, let $\mathbb{Y}_x\sim\mathrm{PPP}(\varDelta_x)$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then, there exists some $\delta_c:=\delta_c(p,\mathcal L(\varDelta))>0$ such that, for every $\delta<\delta_c$, the generalised contact process has a positive probability of survival. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Contact process in (spatial) random environment

[Theorem teoBismutLip of arXiv:2605.07832, 'A Bismut -Elworthy formula for BSDEs with degenerate noise'] Assume that Hypotheses (hyp:base of the paper), (ip-psiphi-li of the paper) and (hyp:operatorG of the paper) and condition (equation link_gat_der_mall_der of the paper) hold true.
Then for every $0\leq s< t\leq T$ and $x,h\in H$ 

we get the following Bismut formula
\begin{align}
\widetilde{\mathbb E}\left[ \langle \nabla_x\,Y^{s,x}_t,h\rangle \right]
= & 
\widetilde{\mathbb E}\int_t^T\psi\left(r,X_r^{s,x},Y_r^{s,x},Z_r^{s,x}\right)
\int_s^r\langle \widetilde u_{h,s,x,r}(\sigma),d\widetilde W_\sigma\rangle_{U}\,dr \notag \\
&+\widetilde{\mathbb E}\displaystyle\int_t^T Z_r\widetilde G(r)^{-1}\bar B(r,X_r^{s,x})\int_s^r\langle\widetilde u_{h,s,x,r}(\sigma),d\widetilde W_\sigma\rangle_U dr \notag \\
& 
+\widetilde{\mathbb E}\left[  \phi(X_T^{s,x})\int_s^T\langle \widetilde u_{h,s,x,T}(\sigma),d\widetilde W_\sigma\rangle_{U}\right],
\end{align}
where $\widetilde \mathbb E $ is the expectation with respect to the probability measure $\widetilde \mathbb P$ such that $\dfrac{d\widetilde \mathbb P}{d \mathbb P}:=\bm{\Psi}$, where $\bm\Psi$ is defined in (equation girsanov-density of the paper).
\newline Moreover, if $h=Ja$, $a\in U$, then equality (equation Bismut-lip of the paper) holds true also for $t=s$ and there exists a positive constant $C$, which depends on $A,\bar B,\widetilde G,J,K_\phi,K_\psi,L_\psi$ and $T$, such that
\begin{align}

|\langle \nabla_xY_s^{s,x},Ja\rangle_U|
\leq \frac{C(1+|x|^m)|a|_U}{(T-s)^\frac12}, \qquad s\in[0,T), \ a\in U.
\end{align}

body:
[Theorem thm:module-stability of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Fix a declared global circuit state $\tau$.  Let $\mathcal T$ be any finite
composition of correlated same-$C$ distance-hereditary pair combs,
signed-$K_5$ pair combs, safe word decorations, and normalized boundary
operations.  Let $m$ be the total $C$-degree of
$\mathcal T\mathfrak q_C$, counting the incoming token as its two
underlying coefficient occurrences.  If no new smoothing carrier is
adjoined, the raw tangle has a finite circuit-anchored presentation
$\zeta_{\mathcal T,\tau}\in\mathscr P_\tau$ satisfying
\[
  \|\zeta_{\mathcal T,\tau}\|_{\mathscr P_\tau}
  \le C_0^mK^{m-2}h^2,
\tag{2.4.6}
\]
where $C_0$ is numerical and independent of $n$, $m$, and $E$.  In
particular, arbitrarily many interleaved combs still pay $h^2$ only once.
Every declared port and context occurs once, token degree remains one,
and the circuit-base normalization is deferred to (eq:2.3.17 of the paper).  No ordinary
open-component norm is asserted for a $K_5$ branch.

title: Proposition 8 of arXiv:2605.09372

body: In mathematics, an orthogonal polynomial sequence is a family of polynomials such that any two different polynomials in the sequence are orthogonal to each other under some inner product.

Let $\xi\in L^2(\mathcal{F}_T)$ be such that $\E[L(T,\xi)]\leq 0\leq \E[R(T,\xi)]$. Then, the doubly mean reflected BSDE \eqref{MRBSDE} admits a unique solution $(Y,Z,K)\in \mathcal{S}^2\times\mathcal{M}^2\times BV[0,T]$. body:
[Definition def:valid of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix $\lambda \in (0,1)$ and a send sequence $\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$. Fix an initialising state~$\Psi_0$. Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be a transition rule on
a set of high-level states which includes~$\Psi_0$. Let $\Psi^{*}$ be the $\Psi_0$-closure of $\mathrm{hls}$. The transition rule~$\mathrm{hls}$ is 
\emph{\newsym{Psi-valid}{validity condition for hls - Definition~(def:valid of the paper)} {\Psi^*\mbox{-valid}}}  if 
for every $\psi \in \Psi^*$ and every integer $t > \tau^\psi$, the following holds.
\begin{itemize}
\item  { Let $\overline{X}(\psi,t) \sim \mathsf{Po}(F_{[j^\psi]}^\psi(t))$.}
Let $\Psi'$ be the random high-level state 
$\Psi' = \mathrm{hls}(\psi, { \overline{X}(\psi,t)}, t)$.
For every high-level state $\psi'$ 
such that $\mathbb{P}(\Psi' = \psi')>0$, 
let $A(\psi,\psi',t) = \mathrm{dist}({ \overline{X}(\psi,t)} \mid \Psi'=\psi')$.  
Then for all $\psi'$, $A(\psi,\psi',t) \gtrsim \mathsf{Po}(F_{ [j^\psi]}^{\psi'}(t))$. 
\end{itemize}

Fix a $\Psi^*$-valid transition rule 
$\mathrm{hls}$. 
Recall the function~$\phi_{\cdot,\cdot}$ from Definition~(def:phi of the paper).
For any high-level states
$\psi,\psi' \in \Psi^*$ 
and $t> \tau^{\psi}$,  we define 
\newsym{phi-2}{stochastic domination 
map determined by hls $\psi$ and $\psi'$ - see Definition~(def:valid of the paper)}
{\phi_{\psi,\psi',t}} as follows.
If $A(\psi,\psi',t) \gtrsim 
\mathsf{Po}(F_{ [j^\psi]}^{\psi'}(t))$ then
$\phi_{\psi,\psi',t} = \phi_{A(\psi,\psi',t),
\mathsf{Po}(F_{ [j^\psi]}^{\psi'}(t)) }$.
Otherwise $\phi_{\psi,\psi',t}$ is the identity.
title: Definition def:valid of arXiv:2602.21315

body:
[Defn def:main-func of arXiv:2412.03415, 'Critical first passage percolation on random graphs'] For any pair of vertices $u\neq v \in [n]$, let $\mathscr{P}_n(u,v)$ denote the collection of all (self-avoiding) paths from $i,j$. For any path $\boldsymbol{\pi} \in \mathscr{P}_n(u,v)$ let the total passage time using this path be given by $T(\boldsymbol{\pi}) = \sum_{e\in \boldsymbol{\pi}} t_e$ and let $|\boldsymbol{\pi}|$ denote the number of edges in $\boldsymbol{\pi}$.  Let $T_n(u,v) = \min_{\boldsymbol{\pi} \in \mathscr{P}_n(u,v)} T(\boldsymbol{\pi})$ denote the optimal passage time between these two vertices and 
\[\mathscr{P}_{\opt}(u,v) = \left\{\boldsymbol{\pi} \in \mathscr{P}_n(u,v): \boldsymbol{\pi} = \arg \min T(\boldsymbol{\pi}) \right\},\]
denote the collection of optimal paths. Let 
$H_n(u,v) = \min \set{|\boldsymbol{\pi}|: \boldsymbol{\pi} \in \mathscr{P}_{\opt}(u,v) },$
denote the hopcount, namely the minimal number of edges amongst all optimal paths between $u,v$.
title: Main functionals of interest

body:
[Lem app-hilbert-cocycle of arXiv:2608.27939, 'Entropy and domination for quasi-Hitchin representations'] For every nontrivial $\gamma\in\Gamma$, and the H\"{o}lder cocycle $c_H$ as above,  the period  of $\gamma$ with respect to $c_H$ is precisely the 
Hilbert length with respect to the Hitchin representation $\rho_0$:
\begin{equation}
  \ell_{c_H}(\gamma)
  :=c_H(\gamma,\gamma^+)
  =\ell^H_{\rho_0}(\gamma).
\end{equation}
In particular, all nonzero periods of $c_H$ are positive.

body:
[Proposition 20 of arXiv:2609.03831, 'On flows generated by square-integrable vector fields'] Let $\v \in L^2(\R^d)$ be a compactly supported divergence-free vector field.
	Suppose that the operator $B_0(\rho) := \d_t \rho + \v \cdot \nabla_x \rho$
	with $D(B_0) = C^\infty_c(\R^{d+1})$ is essentially skew-adjoint in $L^2(\R^{d+1})$.
	Then for any open interval $I\subset \R$ the vector field $\v$
	has the renormalization property in the class $L^2(I \times \R^d)$.
title: Proposition 20 of arXiv:2609.03831

[Definition of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] A \textbf{norm} on a vector space $V$ over $K$ is a function $\|\cdot\|\colon V\to[0,\infty)$ such that
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
    \item $\|v\|=0$ iff $v=0$,
    \item $\|av\|=|a|\cdot\|v\|$ for all $a\in K$, $v\in V$,
    \item $\|v+w\|\leq \max(\|v\|,\|w\|)$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'

body: [Definition 11 of arXiv:2609.01574, 'A linear bound for Fujita's freeness conjecture'] Let $Z$ be a normal variety. We use $b$-divisors as in \cite[Section~2]{FH23}. If $\mathbf D$ is a $\mathbb Q$-Weil $b$-divisor over $Z$ and $Z'\to Z$ is a birational model, we denote its trace on $Z'$ by $D_{Z'}$. If $F$ is a prime divisor over $Z$, we set $\mult_F\mathbf D:=\mult_F D_{Z'}$, where $Z'$ is any model on which $F$ appears. If $D_{Z'}$ is $\mathbb Q$-Cartier, we denote by $\overline{D_{Z'}}$ its Cartier closure. Its trace on every birational model $h\colon Z''\to Z'$ is $h^*D_{Z'}$. We say that $\mathbf D$ \emph{descends to $Z'$} if $\mathbf D=\overline{D_{Z'}}$. We denote the canonical $b$-divisor over $Z$ by $\mathbf K_Z$.

[Theorem thm:LMTparallel of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] {LandryMinskyTaylor2025_TransverseSurfacesAndPseudoAnosovFlows_PUB}}]
Let \(\varphi\) be a pseudo-Anosov flow on \(M\), and let \(S_{1}\) and \(S_{2}\) be two isotopic embedded subsurfaces in \(M\) which are almost transverse to \(\varphi\).
Let \(N\) be a \(I\)-bundle cobounded by \(S_{1}\) and \(S_{2}\). (Such \(N\) is unique if \(S_{i}\) is not a fiber of \(M\).)
If \(S_{1}\) and \(S_{2}\) are minimally transverse to blowup \(\varphi^{\sharp}_{1}\) and \(\varphi^{\sharp}_{2}\), respectively, then \(\varphi_{1}^{\sharp}\) and \(\varphi_{2}^{\sharp}\) has same combinatorial type.

Furthermore, if the surfaces are transverse to a single blowup \(\varphi^{\sharp}\), then \(N\) is a product sutured manifold \(S_{1}\times I\) endowed with product flow, and hence \(S_{1}\) and \(S_{2}\) are isotopic along flowlines of \(\varphi^{\sharp}\).

body:
[Theorem 24 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let \(\iota\colon X\to S\) be a smooth representable morphism of fpqc algebraic \(\F_p\)-stacks of relative dimension \(d\).
Assume that  $F^{\dR}_{X/S}$ splits. 
Then there is an isomorphism
\[
F_{X/S,*}\Omega_{X/S}^{\bullet}
\simeq
\bigoplus_{i=0}^d
\Omega_{X^{(1)}/S}^i[-i]
\]
in $\mcalD_{\qcoh}(X^{(1)})$.
This isomorphism is canonically obtained from a given retraction
\[
(\varphi \colon F_{X/S,*}\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}
\longrightarrow
\mcalO_{X^{(1)}},\, \varphi \circ F^{\dR}_{X/S} \simeq \id_{\mcalO_{X^{(1)}}})
\]
in \(\mcalD_{\qcoh}(X^{(1)})\).

In particular, if \(\iota\) is projective, then, for every
\(\iota\)-ample line bundle \(L\) on \(X\), we have
\[
R^i\iota_*
\bigl(\Omega_{X/S}^j\otimes L^{-1}\bigr)=0
\qquad
(i+j<d) \quad \text{and} \quad R^i\iota_*
\bigl(\Omega_{X/S}^j\otimes L\bigr)=0
\qquad
(i+j>d) 
\]
title: Theorem 24 of arXiv:2609.00567

\end{enumerate}

In particular a window omitting one site has variance at most 1/4, so a positive size-uniform lower bound proportional to its volume is impossible as N grows. metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:5bd16760a5ae06001bdb31c94de2c044cc910609eb166a6aab5ad45688c43ae2","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/5b/5bd16760a5ae06001bdb31c94de2c044cc910609eb166a6aab5ad45688c43ae2.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:927afb676ae68f04ff269bf2890ea471aa6c7d98f43063cd34f03e1dbddf9ae5","bundle_entry_key":"fixed","bundle_id":"population.probability-variance-joint-laws-and-voronoi-partials-007","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"codex-probability-01a07a40/bundle_007.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.stochastic:fixed-mass-complement-window-variance-obstruction","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Fixed mass and the ARW window-variance questions

Status: author-checked scope counterexample only. No independent review or novelty claim. The intended mesoscopic hyperuniformity problems remain unsolved.

Source: Levine and Silvestri, *Universality Conjectures for Activated Random Walk*, arXiv:2306.01698v2, Conjecture 27 and Question 28, PDF pages 15-16. Corpus entries P0389 and P0390. The two questions concern different laws, but share the following necessary correction to the observation-window quantifier.

## Deterministic complement identity

Let T be a finite set with N sites, and let I_x be zero-one occupation indicators with exactly k occupied sites almost surely. For every B contained in T,

$$S_B=\sum_{x\in B}I_x=k-S_{T\setminus B},\qquad \operatorname{Var}(S_B)=\operatorname{Var}(S_{T\setminus B}).$$

Both counts are bounded by their respective window sizes. The variance bound for a variable in an interval of length a is a squared divided by four. Thus

$$\operatorname{Var}(S_B)\le\frac14\min\{|B|,N-|B|\}^2.$$

This proof uses only fixed total mass, which holds after every free-chain addition and throughout each fixed-particle-number wake chain.

## Proper boxes already contradict the unrestricted lower bound

Take d=1 and T the cycle with L vertices. Fix any positive subcritical density rho, and put k=floor(rho L). Take the proper interval B consisting of L-1 vertices. If x is the omitted vertex, S_B=k-I_x, so its variance is at most 1/4. It cannot be at least c(L-1) for any positive c independent of L.

Uniform free driving is translation equivariant. For the wake chain, the unique stationary law is translation invariant because the transition kernel commutes with translations. Therefore each single-site mean is rho_L=k/L in both ensembles, and the variance of this proper box is exactly rho_L(1-rho_L). The whole torus gives the even simpler value zero, but the proper interval shows that requiring merely a strict subset does not repair the claim.

At zero density the configuration is empty and has variance zero for every window, giving another boundary exception. The positive fixed-density argument above does not rely on that exception.

## Global cancellation is not mesoscopic hyperuniformity

Under any fixed-mass law,

$$\sum_{y\in T}\operatorname{Cov}(I_x,I_y)=\operatorname{Cov}(I_x,k)=0.$$

Consider, only as a comparison model, a uniformly chosen k-subset of T. For x distinct from y,

$$\mathbb E I_x=\frac{k}{N},\qquad\mathbb E I_xI_y=\frac{k(k-1)}{N(N-1)}.$$

For a window with b sites, expansion of the variance gives

$$\operatorname{Var}(S_B)=b\,\rho_N(1-\rho_N)\frac{N-b}{N-1},\qquad\rho_N=k/N.$$

When b grows but b/N tends to zero and rho_N tends to a number strictly between zero and one, this is asymptotic to b times rho(1-rho). Therefore exact finite-volume covariance cancellation is compatible with volume-order mesoscopic fluctuations. Passing a finite-torus zero sum to an infinite-volume covariance sum requires additional uniform tail control.

## What remains

The natural next version restricts windows away from full volume, or takes the thermodynamic limit before the window limit. Neither restriction is asserted to have been prescribed by the source. Proving the ARW transition and its exponent in such a regime remains the actual mathematical problem. These elementary identities do not show that either actual ARW law is a uniform subset law, negatively associated, or hyperuniform.

## Second check

An exact rational enumeration of all k-subsets for small N independently checks the comparison variance and complement formula. The enumeration is a finite arithmetic control, not evidence that an unbounded ARW conjecture is solved. Its receipt is in ARW_window_exact_controls.json.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:fe56473d9868d2782c2a89777340b484cd00d87a0d02c3b14bb0ec55ac348696","revision_digest":"sha256:cf38744a8a54150d443152ab5f511e998b5f43349a24472578ee6c85abc20d91","source_id":"owner-probability-exposition-20260907:fixed","source_revision":"author-checked-private-20260907-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body: In mathematics, Sperner's lemma is a combinatorial result on colorings of triangulations, analogous to the Brouwer fixed point theorem, which is equivalent to it. It states that every Sperner coloring of a triangulation of an -dimensional simplex contains a cell whose vertices all have different colors.
title: Sperner's lemma

body:
[Definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a group of matrices $G\subset O_N$, the function
$$\chi:G\to\mathbb C\quad,\quad 
\chi(g)=\sum_{i=1}^Ng_{ii}$$
is called main character of $G$. More generally, the function
$$\chi_t:G\to\mathbb C\quad,\quad 
\chi_t(g)=\sum_{i=1}^{[tN]}g_{ii}$$
is called main truncated character of $G$, of parameter $t\in(0,1]$.
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'

For a complex n by n matrix A and epsilon >= 0, the closed epsilon-pseudospectrum is Lambda_epsilon(A) = {z in C : sigma_min(zI - A) <= epsilon}, sigma_min the smallest singular value and ||.|| the spectral norm. Then Lambda_epsilon(A) is the set of eigenvalues of all A + E with ||E|| <= epsilon, and for epsilon > 0 and z not in the spectrum of A, z is in Lambda_epsilon(A) exactly when ||(zI - A)^-1|| >= 1/epsilon. A witness: if (zI - A) v = s u for unit singular vectors with s = sigma_min(zI - A), then E = s u v* has norm s and makes z an eigenvalue of A + E.
A is a complex n by n matrix
epsilon >= 0

[Lemma lem:walkG of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Let $\mathbb{P}^W_{n}$ be the probability measure on lazy random walks $(S_k)_{k \geq 0}$, with independent steps, 
that start from $n$ and at each step go up or down with probability $p/2$, 
and stay at their current position with probability $1-p$. 
Now consider the infinite measure $\nu^W := \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} \mathbb{P}^W_n$. Then $\nu^W(S_m = 0) = 1$ for all $m \geq 0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 16 of arXiv:2609.02017, 'Optimal girth-dependent bounds for the Bethe approximation of the permanent'] For every $e\in E$, define
\begin{align*}
  \mathsf J_e^+
  &:=
  p_e\KL\bigl(
    \mc{L}(X_\star\mid E_e=1)
    \,\big\|\,
    \mc{L}(X_\star)
  \bigr),\\
  \mathsf J_e^-
  &:=
  (1-p_e)\KL\bigl(
    \mc{L}(X_\star\mid E_e=0)
    \,\big\|\,
    \mc{L}(X_\star)
  \bigr).
\end{align*}
We set $\mathsf J_e^+=0$ when $p_e=0$ and
$\mathsf J_e^-=0$ when $p_e=1$; the formulas below are interpreted
using the same convention.
Thus, recalling \eqref{eq:mutual-information}, we have
\[
  I(X_\star;E_e)=\mathsf J_e^++\mathsf J_e^-.
\]
For every $v\in V$, define
\[
  \mathsf J_v^+
  :=\sum_{e\ni v}\mathsf J_e^+,
  \qquad
  \mathsf J_v^-
  :=\sum_{e\ni v}\mathsf J_e^-.
\]
title: Definition 16 of arXiv:2609.02017

[Theorem thm:domregime of arXiv:2606.01866, 'Phase Transition of a Semiflexible Membrane in Two Dimensions'] For $d=2$, let $\{\phi_x\}_{x\in V_N}$ be as in (thm:compregime of the paper). Fix $\delta\in(0,1)$. Then the following holds for $x,y\in V_N^\delta$:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
        \item(DGFF domination regime) If $\lambda<0$, then
            \[\operatorname{Cov}(\phi_x,\phi_y)=\operatorname{Cov}^\nabla_N(\phi_x,\phi_y)+O(N^\lambda).\]
        \item(MM domination regime) If $\lambda>2$, then
        \[\operatorname{Cov}(\phi_x,\phi_y)=N^{-\lambda}\operatorname{Cov}^{\Delta}_N(\phi_x,\phi_y)+O(N^{4-2\lambda}\log N).\]
    \end{enumerate}
    Here, $\operatorname{Cov}^{\Delta}_N(\phi_x,\phi_y)$ denotes the covariance of the two-dimensional MM with zero boundary conditions. It coincides with the Green function $G^{\Delta}_N(x,y)$ of the following boundary value problem: for any fixed $y\in V_N$,
    \begin{equation}
        \begin{aligned}
            \Delta^2 G^{\Delta}_N(x,y)&=\delta_y(x),&&\quad \forall x\in V_N,\\
            G^{\Delta}_N(x,y)&=0,&&\quad \forall x\in\partial_2 V_N.
        \end{aligned}
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Theorem 4 of arXiv:2511.05218, 'On the Color Discrepancy of Spanning Trees in Random and Randomly Perturbed Graphs'] For any $\alpha\in(0,1)$, there exists a constant $\lambda=\lambda(\alpha)$ such that the following statement holds. For any graph $G_{\alpha}$ on $n$ vertices with $\delta(G_{\alpha})\geq\alpha n$, and a probability function $p=p(n)$ with $\frac{1}{n^{2}}\ll p(n)\ll\frac{1}{n}$, with high probability, the randomly perturbed graph $H=G_{\alpha}\cup G(n,p)$ contains a spanning tree $T$ with $\left|\sum_{e\in E(T)}\chi(e)\right|\geq\lambda pn^{2}$ under any coloring $\chi:E(H)\rightarrow\{+1,-1\}$.

[Defi 1 (Indistinguishability) of arXiv:2512.02766, 'Fine-Graining and Continuous Space Scaling Limit of the $H^{2|2}$ Model on the Hierarchica'] Given a finite weighted graph $\mathcal{G}=(V,E,W)$, we say that a subset $U\subset V$ is \emph{indistinguishable from outside} if
\begin{equation*}
    \forall i,j\in U, \forall k\notin U,\quad W_{ki}=W_{kj}.
\end{equation*}
If additionally a boundary condition $\eta\in \mathbb{R}_{+}^{V}$ is given, $U$ is indistinguishable from outside if additionally
$$\forall i,j\in U,\ \eta_{i}=\eta_{j}.$$
In words, for a given vertex $k$ not in $U$, it is connected to all vertices in $U$ with the same weight.
title: Indistinguishability

[Theorem 49 of arXiv:2504.02435, 'Poisson-Voronoi percolation in higher rank'] Let $\lambda,R>0$ and $p\in(0,1)$.
    Then there is a random closed subset $\mathcal{Z}=\mathcal{Z}^{(\lambda)}_{p,R}$~of~$X$ defined as a $G$-equivariant measurable function of $\omega^{(\lambda)}_p$ such that the following hold a.s.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[{\rm(1)}] $\mathcal{Z}$ is normal,
        \item[{\rm(2)}] ${\rm vol}(\partial(\mathcal{Z}))=0$,
        \item[{\rm(3)}] for every cluster $\omega\subseteq \omega^{(\lambda)}_p$ there is a cluster $Z\subseteq \mathcal{Z}$ such that $        \omega^{(\lambda)}_p\cap Z=\omega$, in particular, $Z\cap\omega'=\emptyset$ for every cluster $\omega'\subset\omega_p^{(\lambda)}$ with $\omega'\ne\omega$,
        \item[{\rm(4)}] $\mathcal{B}_{R}(x)\subseteq \mathcal{Z}$ for every $x\in \omega^{(\lambda)}_p$ such that $\mathcal{B}_{6R}(x)$ only intersects one cluster of $\omega^{(\lambda)}_p$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

$D(\varepsilon p^2)$-tuple has less than $C_{\rm red}+4<2^{122}$ elements. If
arbitrary nonzero integer elements are allowed, every $D(p^2)$-tuple has

[Theorem thm:FP of arXiv:2609.00636, 'Forcing monochromatic subdivisions'] Let $d \ge 1$ and $n \ge 1$. If $H$ is a non-empty graph satisfying
\[
  |N_H(X)| \ge (d+1)|X|
\]
for every $X \subseteq V(H)$ with $|X| \le 2n-2$, then $H$ contains
every tree with at most $n$ vertices and maximum degree at most~$d$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Defi 24 (Gaussian Random Variable) of arXiv:2608.01860, 'A Variational Characterization of a Gibbs Measure related to the Aviles-Giga Functional'] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$ be a probability space. We call a random variable $X:\Omega\to \R$ Gaussian if $X_*\mathbb{P}=\mathbb{P}\circ X^{-1}$ is a Gaussian measure on $\R$.\\
 Let $B$ be a Banach space. A $B$-valued random variable $X$ is said to be a centered Gaussian random variable if, for all $\xi\in B'$, $\langle X,\xi\rangle_{B,B'}$ is a Gaussian random variable with mean zero.
title: Gaussian Random Variable

[Proposition 17 of arXiv:2608.17493, 'Integrals of some compound processes'] Let $M$ be a homogeneous Skellam-type process defined above. Then, for $x>0$,
\begin{align}
	P\bigg\{&\int_0^t M(s)\dif s\in \dif x\bigg\} \nonumber\\
	&=  e^{-\lambda t} \sum_{n\ge0} \frac{1}{n!} \sum_{\substack{k_1,\dots,k_I=0\\k_1+\dots+k_I=n}}^n \binom{n}{k_1,\dots, k_I} \prod_{i\in\mathcal{I}} \Bigg( \bigg(\frac{\lambda_i}{i}\bigg)^{k_{(i)}}  \sum_{h_{(i)} = 0}^{k_{(i)}} \binom{k_{(i)}}{h_{(i)}} (-1)^{h_{(i)}} \Bigg)\nonumber \\
	&\ \ \ \times\mathds{1}_{(t\sum_{j\in\mathcal{I}} j h_{(j)} ,\infty)}(x) \frac{\big(x-t\sum_{j\in\mathcal{I}} j h_{(j)}\big)^{n-1}}{(n-1)!}\dif x, 
\end{align}
where $I = |\mathcal{I}|<\infty$ and, for $i\in\mathcal{I}$, $(i)$ denotes the index of $i$ in the increasingly ordered version of $\mathcal{I}$ (thus, for instance $(\min\{\mathcal{I}\}) = 1$ and $(\max\{\mathcal{I}\}) = I$).

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.30178, '2608.30178'] Assume that \(0<q_1,q_2\le1\).  Then the model
\eqref{eq:noimm-system} is source-conservative.  Moreover, for the associated
source-stopped process and every \(t\ge0\), 
\begin{align}
  \E_{x,y}H(X_t,Y_t)
 +\E_{x,y}\int_0^{t\wedge\tau_0}
 \left[D_1^{(q_1)}(X_s)+\frac{a_1}{a_2}D_2^{(q_2)}(Y_s)\right]\dd s
  \le H(x,y).
 
\end{align}
Consequently,
\(\bigl(H(X_t,Y_t)\bigr)_{t\ge0}\) is a nonnegative supermartingale.  If, in
addition, \(b_{10},b_{20}>0\), then, almost surely,
\beqnn
\lim_{t\to\infty}(X_t,Y_t)
=
\begin{cases}
	(X_{\tau_0},Y_{\tau_0}), & \tau_0<\infty,\\
	(0,0), & \tau_0=\infty.
\end{cases}
\eeqnn (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Concept (campaign status: structural reading, standing): in the reconstructed framework the sharp Rademacher singularity conjecture's difficulty is a COUNTING problem at ell = 1. Erdos's Littlewood-Offord bound forces every component defect ell >= 1 with equality exactly for support-2 dependencies (equal or opposite row/column pairs), and quantises the spectrum: no component has ell in (1, 1.4150). The affordability budget log2(N_fibre) < n(ell-1) + 2 log2 n - o(n) has NO exponential room at ell = 1 - saturated exactly by the ~2n^2 coincident pairs, which IS the conjecture's constant 2n^2 2^{-n}. Above the gap the budget is at least 0.415n bits. So all Layer-II machinery (rigidity, congestion, absorption, connectors) operates in a regime with a log-factor to spare, and the sharp constant lives entirely in exact treatment of the ell = 1 slice plus multiplicity control.
title: The ell = 1 slice carries the sharp conjecture's whole difficulty

body:
[Definition d:p-dir-structure of arXiv:2510.13659, 'On the energy image density conjecture of Bouleau and Hirsch'] Let $p \in (1,\infty)$.
		We say that $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,\mathcal{E}_p, \mathcal{F}_p, \Gamma_p)$ is a $p$-Dirichlet structure if it satisfies the following properties:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item			\textbf{Probability space}: $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ is a probability space and $\mathcal{F}_p$ is a subspace of $L^p(X,\mu)$ such that $\mathds{1}_X \in \mathcal{F}_p$.
			\item \textbf{Completeness:} 
			$\mathcal{E}_p$ is a semi-norm on $\mathcal{F}_p$ such that $\mathcal{F}_p$ is a Banach space when equipped with the norm $\norm{f}_{\mathcal{F}_p}=(\norm{f}_{L^p}^p+\mathcal{E}_p(f))^{1/p}$.
			\item \textbf{Homogeneity:} For all $f\in \mathcal{F}_p$ there exists a finite non-negative Borel measure $\Gamma_p \langle f \rangle$ on $X$ such that $\Gamma_p \langle f \rangle(X)= \mathcal{E}_p(f)$   and for all $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$
			\[
			\Gamma_p\langle \lambda f\rangle = |\lambda|^p \Gamma_p\langle f\rangle.
			\]
			\item \textbf{Absolute continuity of energy measure}:  For all $f \in \mathcal{F}_p$, we have $\Gamma_p \langle f \rangle \ll \mu$.
			\item \textbf{Sublinearity:} For every $f,g\in \mathcal{F}_p$ and $A\subset X$, 
			\[
			\Gamma_p\langle f+g\rangle(A)^{\frac{1}{p}}\le \Gamma_p\langle f\rangle(A)^{\frac{1}{p}}+\Gamma_p\langle g\rangle(A)^{\frac{1}{p}}
			\]
			\item \textbf{Chain rule:} For all $f\in \mathcal{F}_p$, $g\in \Lip(\mathbb{R})$ with $g(0)=0$,  we have $g \circ f \in \mathcal{F}_p$ and
			\[
			\Gamma_p\langle g\circ f\rangle  \le \left((\Lip_a[g] \circ f)(x)\right)^p   \,\Gamma_p\langle f\rangle.
			\]
			Note that the measure $\left((\Lip_a[g] \circ f)(x)\right)^p   \,\Gamma_p\langle f\rangle$ is well-defined due to the absolute continuity of energy measure; that is, this measure does not depend on the choice of $f$ from the $\mu$-a.e.~equivalence class.
			\item \textbf{Locality:} For every $f\in \mathcal{F}_p$ and any measurable  set $A\in \mathcal{X}$, if $f|_A=c$ $\mu$-a.e., then $\Gamma_p\langle f\rangle(A)=0$. In particular, $\Gamma_p \langle \mathds{1}_X \rangle$ is the zero measure.
			\item \textbf{Weak lower semicontinuity:} For every $f\in L^p(X)$, and for any sequence of functions $(f_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}\in \mathcal{F}_p$ such that $f_n\to f \in L^p(X)$ with $\sup_{i\in \mathbb{N}} \mathcal{E}_p(f_i)<\infty$, then $f\in \mathcal{F}_p$ and
			\[
			\Gamma_p\langle f \rangle(A)\le \liminf_{i\to \infty} \Gamma_p\langle f_i \rangle(A)
			\]
			for every measurable set $A\subset X$.
		\end{enumerate}
title: Definition d:p-dir-structure of arXiv:2510.13659

Let M be a local martingale with M_0 = 0, let M^*_T = sup_{t <= T} |M_t| for a stopping time T, and let [M] be the quadratic variation. There are constants 0 < c_p <= C_p < infinity depending ONLY on p such that c_p E[ [M]_T^{p/2} ] <= E[ (M^*_T)^p ] <= C_p E[ [M]_T^{p/2} ]. The admissible range of p differs by regularity: for CONTINUOUS local martingales the two-sided bound holds for every 0 < p < infinity; for general cadlag local martingales it holds for every p >= 1, and the case 0 < p < 1 genuinely requires continuity (Davis' theorem covers p = 1 in the general case). In discrete time the same holds with [M]_n = sum_{k <= n} (M_k - M_{k-1})^2 the square function, for 1 <= p < infinity. The constants are UNIVERSAL in the sense of depending on p alone - not on the martingale, the filtration, the time horizon or the dimension - and they blow up as p decreases to 0 and as p increases to infinity; explicit admissible choices grow like p for the upper constant. For p = 2 the inequality is an identity with c_2 = C_2 replaced by the Ito isometry together with Doob's L^2 maximal inequality, which is the cheap case one should reach for first. [Burkholder (1973), Davis (1970), Burkholder-Davis-Gundy (1972); see Revuz and Yor, Continuous Martingales and Brownian Motion, 3rd ed., Theorem IV.4.1]

Let n,d>=1 and T>=2 be integers. For each i in {1,...,n}, let tokens x_it in R^d, query z_i in R^d and label Y_i in {-1,+1} be fixed, and fix a linear prediction head v in R^d. Define token scores gamma_it=Y_i v^T x_it; globally optimal token indices satisfy opt_i in argmax_t gamma_it. Fix selected token indices alpha_i in {1,...,T}. Assume the attention-SVM constraints (x_i,alpha_i-x_it)^T W z_i>=1 for every i and every t!=alpha_i are feasible. Let W_alpha be the unique minimum-Frobenius-norm solution of these constraints, where ||W||_F=(sum_{a,b}W_ab^2)^(1/2). Equivalently it minimizes the squared Frobenius norm, a strictly convex objective. Define support indices T_i={t!=alpha_i:(x_i,alpha_i-x_it)^T W_alpha z_i=1}. The selection alpha is locally optimal exactly when gamma_i,alpha_i>gamma_it for every i and every t in T_i; W_alpha is then called a locally optimal direction. This condition compares the selected token only with support indices. It does not impose comparison with all non-support tokens. This card defines the fixed-head geometry; it makes no gradient-descent convergence assertion.

For a measure space (X, mu) and measurable sets A, B, d_mu(A, B) = mu(A symmetric difference B), possibly infinite. For measurable sets A_i and B_i (i = 1, 2, ...), d_mu(union A_i, union B_i) <= sum_i d_mu(A_i, B_i) and d_mu(intersection A_i, intersection B_i) <= sum_i d_mu(A_i, B_i). The constant 1 is attained, and coordinatewise convergence alone is not enough: on a one-point probability space, the families with A_i^(m) = X exactly for i = m (and empty otherwise) converge in every coordinate to the empty family, yet their union is X for every m.

[Definition of arXiv:2506.06559, 'Bi-infinite incipient cluster in high dimensions'] \ \\
(i) Let $G$ be a finite connected (not necessarily simple) graph, and $S \subset V(G)$, $|S| = 3$. 
We say that $x \in V(G) \setminus S$ is 3-connected to $S$ if there exist 3 edge-disjoint paths between $x$ and 
each element of $S$, respectively. The graph $G$ is said to be 3-connected to $S$ if $x$ is 3-connected to $S$ 
for any $x\in V(G) \setminus S$. \\
(ii) When $G$ is also simple, we call an edge $\{x,y\}$ strongly H-reducible (for the graph $G$ and 
the set $S$), if $x,y\in V(G) \setminus S$, $\{x,y\}$ is H-reducible and the graph $G$ H-reduced by $\{x,y\}$ 
is still 3-connected to $S$.

[Corollary 9 of arXiv:2607.04193, 'Onsager--Machlup Functionals for Generalized Newtonian Equations of Motion with Time-Varyi'] Let $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P})$ be an abstract Wiener space (where $\Omega$ is a separable Banach space and $\mathbb{P}$ is the centered standard Gaussian measure on $\Omega$). 
Let $A \subseteq \Omega$ be a $\mu$-measurable, symmetric, and convex set, and let $f: \Omega \to [0, \infty)$ be a $\mathbb{P}$-measurable, symmetric, and convex function. Then for every $t > 0$, the following estimate holds:
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb{P}\bigl(\{x \in \Omega : f(x) \le t\} \cap A\bigr)
    \ge
    \mathbb{P}\bigl(\{x \in \Omega: f(x) \le t\}\bigr) \mathbb{P}(A).
\end{equation*}
title: Corollary 9 of arXiv:2607.04193

[Definition eq:fourier-f of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[definition]{def:function-classes}
Let \(\mathcal V_m\) be the class of \(V\in C^{m+1}(\mathbb R)\) such that \(\inf V> -\infty\) and
\[
 \max_{1\le r\le m+1}\norm{V^{(r)}}_\infty<\infty.
\]
Let \(\mathcal F_m\) be the Fourier--Wiener class of real-valued functions
\[
 f(x)=c+\int_\mathbb R e^{itx}\widehat f_0(t)\,\mathrm d t,
 \qquad c\in\mathbb R,
\]
where
\begin{equation}
 \int_\mathbb R(1+\left\lvertt\right\rvert^{m+1})\left\lvert\widehat f_0(t)\right\rvert\,\mathrm d t<\infty.
\end{equation}
Here \(\widehat f_0(-t)=\overline{\widehat f_0(t)}\), so \(f\) is real.
Thus compact support and \(C^\infty\) regularity are not imposed; the
displayed integrability is exactly what the trace-derivative proof uses.

[Proposition AS of arXiv:2609.00324, 'Quantitative Stability for Fractional Yamabe minimizers'] Let $(M,[\hat{h}])$ be the conformal infinity of an asymptotically hyperbolic manifold $(X^{n+1},g^+)$, and $p\geq 3$. Let $u_0$ be a non-integrable minimizer of the fractional Yamabe energy and suppose that it satisfies the $\text{AS}_p$ condition. Then, there exists a sequence $(u_k)_{k\in \mathbb{N}} \subset H^\gamma (M)$ with $u_k \to u_0$ in $H^\gamma (M)$ such that 
\begin{align*}
    \lim_{k\to \infty}\frac{I_\gamma [u_k,\hat{h}] -\Lambda_\gamma (M,[\hat{h}])}{\|u_k - u_0\|_{H^\gamma (M)}^{p-\alpha} } = 0 \quad \forall \alpha>0.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2607.13273, 'Asymptotics of transition densities for L\'evy processes with stochastic resetting'] Assume that for every $t>0$ there exists a transition density $p(t,y)$ of the L\'evy process $\boldsymbol{Y}$  and let $\theta\in\mathbb{S}^{d-1},$ $\lambda>0$, and $x\in\Rd$. If there exist Borel functions $f,A,\tilde{A}:\mathbb{R}_+\to\mathbb{R}_+$, and $r_0>0$ such that
	\[
        \lim_{r\to\infty} \frac{p(t,r\theta)}{f(r)}= A(t), \, t>0,
        \quad\text{ and } \quad
        \frac{p(t,r\theta-z)}{f(r)}\leq \tilde{A}(t),\, t>0, r>r_0, z\in \{0,x\}, 
	\]
	\[
        \lim\limits_{t\to\infty} e^{-\lambda t} \tilde A(t)=0
        \quad \text{ and } \quad
        \int\limits_{0}^\infty e^{-\lambda t} \tilde A(t)\, \dx[t]<\infty,
	\]
	then the density $p_\lambda$ of the corresponding process with resetting $\boldsymbol{X}$ satisfies
	\[
		\lim\limits_{\substack{r\to\infty\\t\to\infty}}\frac{p_\lambda(t,x,r\theta)}{f(r)}=\int\limits_0^\infty \lambda e^{-\lambda s}A(s)\, \dx[s].
	\]

  \item

  $\kappa_0$ is defined in \eqref{eq:kappa_0}.
  \end{enumerate}
  \end{enumerate}

[Lemma r small enough of arXiv:2608.25065, 'Detection of first homology via random geometric graphs in the thermodynamic regime'] \label[lemma]{approximate 1-chains}
    Suppose $r_0 > 0$ is
    sufficiently small
    that
    \begin{equation} 
        3/|\log r| \le 1, \qquad
        4 Q \rho r|\log r|
        \le \mathrm{inj}(M)
    \end{equation}
    for all $0<r\le r_0$.
    Then, for all $0 < r \le r_0$,
    on the event $A_{Q,\rho}(n,r)$, 
    the following holds. 
    
    Suppose that 
    $c = \sum_{i=1}^N t_i \ell_i \in C_1(M)$
    and suppose that
    each $\mathrm{diam} (|\ell_i|) \le 2r$
    and 
    $\partial c \in C_0(\mathring{G}^n_M(r))$.

    Then, there exists $c' \in C_1(\mathring{G}^n_M(r))$
    and $\sigma \in C_2(M)$
    such that
    \[
        \partial \sigma = c' - c
    \]
    and for all $x' \in |\sigma|$,
    there exists $x \in |c|$
    such that $d_M(x',x) \le 4Q\rho r|\log r|$.

    In particular,
    $\partial c' = \partial c$
    and $|c'|$
    lies within the $4Q\rho r|\log r|$-neighborhood of $|c|$.

[Definition 3 of arXiv:2605.30616, 'Brownian motion: the hyperbolic number setting'] Let $\left(X,\sigma\left(X\right)\right)$ be a measurable space equipped
with a set $X$ and a $\sigma$-algebra $\sigma\left(X\right)$. Suppose
\[
\mu:\sigma\left(X\right)\rightarrow\mathbb{H}
\]
is a $\mathbb{H}$-valued function satisfying the $\sigma$-additivity:
if $\left\{ X_{k}\right\} _{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a family of mutually
disjoint measurable subsets of $X$ in $\sigma\left(X\right)$, then
\[
\mu\left(\overset{\infty}{\underset{k=1}{\cup}}X_{k}\right)=\overset{\infty}{\underset{k=1}{\sum}}\mu\left(X_{k}\right),\;\;\;{in\;\;\;}\mathbb{H},
\]
where the convergence is in the topology of $\mathbb{H}$. Then this
function $\mu$ is called a $\mathbb{H}$-valued measure.

body:
Little Picard theorem: if f is entire and nonconstant, then the complement of its image, C minus f(C), contains at most one point; i.e. a nonconstant entire function omits at most one complex value. Great Picard theorem: if f is holomorphic on a punctured disk 0 < |z - a| < r and has an essential singularity at a, then for every ε in (0,r) the image of the punctured disk 0 < |z - a| < ε is all of C with at most one point removed, and every value so attained (again with at most one exception) is attained infinitely often. Both exceptional values are genuinely possible and the count is sharp: exp(z) is entire and omits exactly the value 0, and exp(1/z) has an essential singularity at 0 and omits exactly 0 near 0. Meromorphic versions: a nonconstant meromorphic function on C omits at most two values of the Riemann sphere, and near an essential singularity a meromorphic function takes every spherical value with at most two exceptions. If f is entire and transcendental (not a polynomial), then f takes every complex value, with at most one exception, infinitely often.
Little: f entire and nonconstant
Great: f holomorphic on a punctured disk about a with an isolated essential singularity at a

In the second case the same argument applied to 1/f (holomorphic since f omits 0) shows 1/f is bounded near 0, so f has a pole or removable singularity at 0, again a contradiction. [Defn 11 of arXiv:2608.12804, 'Scaling Limits for Ising Models on Inhomogeneous Random Graphs and Applications'] A function $f: [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$ is absolutely continuous if for every $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists a $\delta > 0$ such that for any finite collection of pairwise disjoint subintervals $\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^n$ of $[0,1]$ satisfying
\(
\sum_{i=1}^n (y_i - x_i) < \delta
\),
we have
\(
\sum_{i=1}^n |f(y_i) - f(x_i)| < \varepsilon
\).

body: Let (Omega, F, mu) be a measure space, p a real number with 1 <= p <= infinity, and f, g in L^p(mu). Then f + g is in L^p(mu) and ||f+g||_p <= ||f||_p + ||g||_p, where ||h||_p = (integral over Omega of |h|^p d mu)^{1/p} for p < infinity and ||h||_infinity = ess sup |h|. This triangle inequality is exactly what makes ||.||_p a norm on L^p(mu) for 1 <= p <= infinity. [standard, e.g. Folland, Real Analysis]
title: Minkowski's Inequality for L^p Norms

[Thm 16 of arXiv:2607.21759, 'Marchenko--Pastur law for tensor powers of exchangeable unconditional vectors'] For each $p \in \N$, let $\mathbf x^{(1)}_p,\dotsc,\mathbf x^{(m)}_p$ be $m = m(p)$ i.i.d.\ random vectors in $\R^p$, with $\Sigma_p = \E \mathbf x\mathbf x^\trp$ satisfying $\tr \Sigma_p^2= o(p^2)$, and also \begin{equation} 
    \frac{\mathbf x_p^\trp A_p \mathbf x_p - \tr(\Sigma_pA_p)}{p} \to 0\quad\text{in probability}\end{equation} for any sequence of PSD matrices $A_p \in \R^{p\times p}$ with $\opnm{A_p} \leq 1$. Assume $\ESD(\Sigma_p) \wkconv \rho$ for some deterministic measure $\rho$. Assume in addition for each $p$ and $m = m(p)$, we have a diagonal matrix $T_p = \diag\{R_1,\dotsc,R_{m}\}$, with nonnegative entries and independent of $\bigl\{\mathbf x_p^{(k)}\bigr\}_{k=1}^m$, and $\ESD(T_p) \wkconv \tau$ for some deterministic measure $\tau$ with probability $1$. Then, assuming $p / m \to c$ for some fixed $c > 0$, the weighted sample covariance matrix $\widetilde K_{p} = \frac{1}{m} \sum_{k=1}^m R_k \mathbf{x}_p^{(k)} {\mathbf{x}_p^{(k)}}^\trp$ converges weakly with probability $1$ to some deterministic measure $\mu$, which is uniquely determined by its Stieltjes transform \[
        s_\mu(z) = \int_0^\infty \frac{1}{\lambda \int_0^\infty \frac{x}{1 + c x \tilde s(z)}\,d\tau(x) - z }\,d\rho(\lambda)\quad \text{for }z\in \C^+,
    \] where $\tilde s$ is defined by \[
        \tilde s(z) = \int_0^\infty \frac{\lambda}{\lambda \int_0^\infty \frac{x}{1 + c x \tilde s(z)}\,d\tau(x) - z }\,d\rho(\lambda) \quad \text{for }z\in \C^+.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 16 of arXiv:2607.21759

[Corollary cor: Susc_internal_2 of arXiv:2608.00399, 'The Heavy-tailed Frog Model'] Let $d \geq 2$, $\delta \in (0, 1)$, $\varepsilon > 0$, $\lambda > 0$, $K > 0$, and $\alpha > 0$. Let $Q \in \mathcal{H}_{\alpha, K}$ (see (equation def: H_alpha of the paper)).
    Let $Q_L$ be defined as in equation (equation def: Q_L of the paper).
    Let $\ell^*$, $r^*$, and $m$ be as defined above.
    Then, for every $v \in \mathbb{T}^d_m$ and uniformly for every $A \subseteq B_v$ with $|A|/|B_v| \ge 1 - \delta$, we have
    \begin{align}
        L^d \, \mathbb P_L \left( \frac{|\mathcal{R}^{(2)}_v(A) \cap B_{v + e}|}{|B_{v + e}|} \le 1 - \delta \text{ for some } e \in \{ \pm e_1, \ldots, \pm e_d \} \right) \rightarrow 0, 
    \end{align}
    as $L \to \infty$, where $e_1, \ldots, e_d$ denote the standard basis vectors of $\mathbb Z^d$.

AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. Known-source analytic consequence, proof unaudited: for every compactly supported probability law mu on R, positive semicircular heat mu_t=mu free-plus semicircle_t has finite logarithmic energy E(t)=Sigma(mu_t), and E is C1 for all t>0 with E_prime(t)=Phi(mu_t)/2=(2*pi^2/3) integral p_t^3. Phi is continuous at every positive time. Biane's density-cube Lipschitz estimate, uniform support and weak time continuity give uniform density-cube continuity by Arzela-Ascoli; Voiculescu's one-variable chi*=chi heat-integral definition then pays differentiation. The free Fisher constant is checked by an explicit Cauchy-cubic contour identity. No density or finite initial energy is required of mu. This closes the scalar positive-noise regularity input, but the real matrix observation-law and calibration-transfer steps remain separate. This is a consequence of known results, not a novelty claim.
mu is a compactly supported probability on R; t>0.
Centered semicircular convolution has variance parameter t.
Natural logarithmic energy; free Fisher is squared L2 norm of the scalar conjugate variable.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:c9a38a4454c119864483fe3d56de48bed233e05a501fd18f980119baa59c1242","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/c9/c9a38a4454c119864483fe3d56de48bed233e05a501fd18f980119baa59c1242.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:f7ee46a2e3388a11ce13fc89ccd7a2a712259b34ba37615dbe0afe0e0398d634","bundle_entry_key":"positive-free-heat-entropy-c1-biane-voiculescu-w718","bundle_id":"population.t287-near-square-c1-and-finite-variance-comparison-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian channels and extensive-rank matrix inference","draft":"w718/bundle_008.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.gaussian_channels:positive-free-heat-entropy-c1-biane-voiculescu-w718","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Positive semicircular heat: continuity of Fisher information and C1 entropy

Target 2 analytic input. Proof draft, unaudited. This is an explicit
consequence of known Biane and Voiculescu results, not a novelty claim.
It does not by itself establish the observation law for the real matrix
model or prove the T287 MMSE comparison.

Let mu be a compactly supported probability law on R. Write
mu_t=mu free-plus sigma_t, where sigma_t is the centered semicircle law
of variance t>0, p_t its density, and

    E(t)=Sigma(mu_t)=double integral log|x-y| mu_t(dx)mu_t(dy).

Then E is C1 on (0,infinity), with

    Phi(t)=(4*pi^2/3) integral p_t(x)^3 dx,
    E'(t)=Phi(t)/2.                                  (1)

No density, non-atomicity or finite initial logarithmic energy of mu is
assumed. In particular finite-rank/zero-atom input laws are allowed.

## Primary inputs and normalization

1. Biane, *On the free convolution with a semi-circular distribution*,
   Indiana Univ. Math. J.46 (1997),705-718, DOI10.1512/iumj.1997.46.1467.
   Lemma2, journal p709, defines v_t and gives its positive-level equation.
   Corollaries1-3, journal p711, give the continuous Cauchy boundary,
   a continuous density, and p_t(psi_t(u))=v_t(u)/(pi*t).
   Proposition4, journal p714, gives
   |p_t(x)^2 p_t'(x)|<=1/(4*pi^3*t^2) where p_t>0.
2. Voiculescu, *Free Entropy*, arXiv:math/0103168, chi.4 (one variable),
   and Section3.5 definition and chi*.1. In one variable
   chi(mu)=Sigma(mu)+3/4+(1/2)log(2*pi)=chi*(mu), and

   chi*(mu_t)=(1/2)integral_0^infinity
                  [1/(1+u)-Phi*(mu_(t+u))]du+(1/2)log(2*pi*e).

   Section3.3, J.1 and J.3 identify the scalar conjugate variable and
   the score under a positive semicircular perturbation. The Phi*
   convention is its squared L2 norm, Section3.4. We verify the scalar
   density constant explicitly below rather than borrow a classical
   Fisher-information convention.

All source artifacts and SHA256 values are recorded in SOURCES.jsonl.
The hypotheses quoted here were checked in the original journal PDF
and the author's arXiv survey, not inferred from an unrelated classical
de Bruijn card.

## Uniform spatial regularity and continuity in heat time

The v_t equation gives v_t<=sqrt(t): if v_t>0,
1/t=integral[(u-x)^2+v_t^2]^-1 mu(dx)<=1/v_t^2.
At v_t=0 the bound is immediate. Therefore

    0<=p_t(x)<=1/(pi*sqrt(t)).                       (2)

Set q_t=p_t^3. Proposition4 gives |q_t'|<=3/(4*pi^3*t^2) on the open
positivity set. Since q_t is continuous and zero on its complement,
this is a global Lipschitz bound on R. To see the extension across zeros,
integrate within each positive component; if two points lie in different
components, the values at their adjacent boundary zeros bound the
absolute difference by the same constant times the distance.

Fix 0<a<b<infinity. Realize mu as the law of a bounded selfadjoint X,
free from a variance-one semicircular S. The norms of X+sqrt(t)S for
t in [a,b] are bounded by ||X||+2sqrt(b). Thus all p_t have a common
compact support. Norm continuity of X+sqrt(t)S gives weak continuity
of its laws (first for polynomials, then for continuous functions on
the common compact interval).

For any t_k->t in [a,b], the q_(t_k) are uniformly bounded by (2),
uniformly Lipschitz and have common compact support. Every subsequence
has an Arzela-Ascoli uniformly convergent further subsequence, say to q.
Taking cube roots gives uniform convergence p_(t_k)->q^(1/3). The
weak-continuity statement forces q^(1/3)=p_t, since continuous densities
of the same law agree everywhere. Every possible subsequential uniform
limit is therefore q_t. Hence q_(t_k)->q_t uniformly, and

    t -> integral p_t^3                             (3)

is continuous on [a,b]. This argument does not assume joint parameter
regularity beyond Biane's actual spatial estimates.

## The exact scalar Fisher constant

Fix t>0, abbreviate p=p_t and define
G(z)=integral(z-x)^-1 p(x)dx. By Biane Corollary1 its upper boundary is
continuous, with G(x+i0)=h(x)-i*pi*p(x), h=PV integral p(y)/(x-y)dy.
It is bounded on compact subsets of the closed upper half-plane and
decays as O(1/|x|) off the compact support. In particular the boundary
function lies in L3(R).

For epsilon>0, the contour integral of G(z+i*epsilon)^3 around an upper
half-disk vanishes: it is analytic there and its large arc is O(R^-2).
Thus integral_R G(x+i*epsilon)^3 dx=0. Let epsilon decrease to zero.
Continuous boundary values give a uniform compact bound; outside a
fixed interval |G(x+i*epsilon)|<=2/|x| for 0<epsilon<=1. Dominated
convergence justifies passing the cubic integral to the boundary.
Taking imaginary parts gives

    integral p(x) h(x)^2 dx=(pi^2/3) integral p(x)^3 dx.                (4)

The scalar conjugate variable is 2h(X_t). This is Voiculescu J.1 with
the Hilbert-transform normalization removed; it can also be checked
directly from its defining polynomial identity:

    double integral [f(x)-f(y)]/(x-y) p(x)p(y)dxdy
                           =2 integral f(x)h(x)p(x)dx.

The principal-value passage is valid here: q_t is Lipschitz, so p_t is
Holder1/3, compactly supported, and its symmetric principal-value
integrals converge; the subtracted polynomial numerator is nonsingular.
Polynomial uniqueness in L2 on compact support identifies the score.
Therefore Phi*(mu_t)=4 integral p h^2=(4*pi^2/3)integral p^3, as asserted.
By (3), Phi*(mu_t) is continuous at every positive time.

## From the defining heat integral to the derivative

J.3 writes the score as t^(-1/2) E[S|X+sqrt(t)S]. The conditional
expectation is an L2 contraction and E S^2=1, hence

    0<=Phi*(mu_t)<=1/t.                              (5)

The bounded continuous compact density at positive t gives finite
logarithmic energy; thus the one-variable chi*=chi identity is finite
there. Apply Section3.5 at times 0<t1<t2 and subtract its two defining
improper heat integrals with the same upper cutoff T. The reference
1/(1+u) terms cancel. The result is

    chi(mu_t2)-chi(mu_t1)
      =(1/2)integral_t1^t2 Phi*(mu_v)dv
         -(1/2)lim_(T->infinity) integral_(T+t1)^(T+t2) Phi*(mu_v)dv.

The last term vanishes by (5), bounded by
(1/2)log((T+t2)/(T+t1)). Subtracting the constant between chi and Sigma
therefore gives the integral identity for E. The continuity already
proved gives E'(t)=Phi*(mu_t)/2 at every t>0, proving (1).

## Consequence once the matrix spectral identity is attached

For a compact symmetric input law mu, suppose a square matrix channel
has limiting normalized MI

 i(s)=Sigma(dilation_sqrt(s)(mu) free-plus sigma_1)-Sigma(sigma_1).

Dilation and the heat semigroup give
i(s)=E(1/s)+(1/2)log(s)-Sigma(sigma_1). Consequently i is C1 for s>0 and

    i'(s)=1/(2s)-Phi*(mu_(1/s))/(2s^2).              (6)

This is a conditional matrix consequence. The real Gaussian-reference
spectral identification and transfer assumptions remain to be paid in
separate files. [Thm 12 (Bounding  star discrepancy discrepancy by $L^1$-Wasserstein distance) of arXiv:2605.03528, '\bf Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance and discrepancies {\em versus} Wasserstein distances'] Let $\nu $ be an absolutely  continuous distribution on $\R^d$
with density $g\!\in {\cal L}^{\frac{r}{r-1}}(\R^d, \lambda_d)$ for some $r\!\in (1,+\infty]$ and finite first moment. Then, for every probability distribution  $\mu$ on $\R^d$with  finite first moment,
\begin{equation}
D^\star(\mu,\nu)\le C_{r,d}{\cal W}^{\ell^\infty}_1(\mu,\nu)^{\frac{d}{r+d}} \big \| g\big\|^{\frac{r}{r+d}}_{{\cal L}^{\frac{r}{r-1}}(\lambda_d)}.
\end{equation}
with $C_{r,d} =  \begin{pmatrix}r+d \\ r \end{pmatrix}^{-\frac{1}{r+d}}\bigg( \Big(\frac dr\Big)^{\frac{r}{r+d}} + \Big(\frac rd\Big)^{\frac{d}{r+d}} \bigg)$ for $r\ge 1$.

If $g$ is bounded, one has:
\[
D^\star(\mu,\nu)\le C_{1,d}{\cal W}^{\ell^\infty}_1(\mu,\nu)^{\frac{d}{d+1}} \big\| g\big\|^{\frac{1}{d+1}}_{\infty}.

\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Bounding  star discrepancy discrepancy by $L^1$-Wasserstein distance

For a real continuous local martingale M starting at zero, quadratic variation [M] is characterized by: [M] starts at zero, is adapted, continuous and increasing, and M^2 - [M] is a continuous LOCAL martingale. Uniqueness is up to indistinguishability. For each finite T, squared-increment sums along deterministic partitions of [0,T] with mesh tending to zero converge in probability to [M]_T. If E([M]_T) is finite at every finite T, the compensated square is a true martingale; this condition is equivalent to M being a true martingale with E(M_T^2) finite at every finite T. Brownian motion has [B]_t=t. Merely assuming M is a true continuous martingale does not justify the compensated-square integrability upgrade.
The filtration satisfies the usual conditions.
M is real, continuous, a local martingale, and M_0=0.
title: Quadratic Variation: Local Martingale and Integrability Conditions

DRAFT counterexample to the first-moment inference: For integer n>=2, let N_n=n^2 with probability 1/n and zero otherwise. Then E N_n=n tends to infinity, P(N_n>0)=1/n tends to zero, and E N_n^2/(E N_n)^2=n. For any nonnegative witness N with 0<E N and E N^2<=C(E N)^2, Cauchy-Schwarz instead guarantees P(N>0)>=1/C. [Dfn 220 (achievable measures) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For $(b,\sigma,p) \in \sS \times \sP$, let $\mu(b,\sigma,p)$ denote the law of $X(1)$ given by the stochastic integral
    \beq
        
        X(t)
        = \int_0^t p'(s)^{1/2}
        b_s\,ds
        +
        \int_0^t \Big[ (sp)'(s) \Big]^{1/2} \sigma_s\,dB(s)\,.
    \eeq
The \textbf{sets of achievable measures} 
for the Ising and spherical problems are defined to be 
    \begin{align*}
        \cM^{\Ising}(\alpha) 
        &= \Big\{
            \mu(b,\sigma,p) : p \in \sP, (b,\sigma,w) \in \Adm^{\Ising}(\alpha,p)
        \Big\}, \\
        \cM^{\sph}(\alpha) &= \Big\{
            \mu(b,\sigma,p) : p \in \sP, (b,\sigma) \in \Adm^{\sph}(\alpha,p)
        \Big\}.
    \end{align*}
Define $\cM^{\Ising, \concave}(\alpha)$ and $\cM^{\sph, \concave}(\alpha)$ analogously, but with the additional restriction that $p\in\sP_c$. Let $\ocM^{\Ising}(\alpha)$,
$\ocM^{\sph}(\alpha)$,
$\ocM^{\Ising, \concave}(\alpha)$, $\ocM^{\sph, \concave}(\alpha)$
 be the closures of these sets in the 
    $\bbW_2$ metric.

[Theorem quadratic of arXiv:2412.07936, 'Simple Norm Bounds for Polynomial Random Matrices via Decoupling'] [Quadratic Recursion]

Let $\{x_i\}_{i = 1}^n$ be a sequence of i.i.d random variables with ${\mathbb E} x_i= 0$,  ${\mathbb E} x_i^2= 1$ and $|x_i| \leq L$ for all $1\leq i \leq n$. Let $\{{\bf A}_{i,j}\}_{(i,j) \in {\mathcal T}^2_n}$ be a double sequence of deterministic matrices of the same dimension. Define 
$$
{\bf F}({\bf x}) = \sum_{(i,j) \in {\mathcal T}^2_n} {\bf A}_{i,j} x_{i}x_{j}.
$$
Suppose that ${\bf F}({\bf x})$ is also permutation symmetric, i.e.,\xspace ${\bf A}_{i,j} = {\bf A}_{j,i}$, $\forall (i,j) \in {\mathcal T}^2_n$. Then for $a,b,c\in {\mathbb Z}_{\geq 0}$ and $2 \leq t < \infty$,
$$
{\mathbb E} \norm{{\bf F}({\bf x}) - {\mathbb E} {\bf F}({\bf x})}_{4t} ~ \leq ~ 2 (32t)^{2} \cdot \left( \sum_{\substack{a,b,c: \\a+b+c=2 }} L^c \cdot \norm{ {\bf F}_{a,b,c}}_{4t} \right).
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem quadratic of arXiv:2412.07936

    Let $G$ be a transitive graph of polynomial growth with $d \geq 1$, and suppose that $J: V \times V \to \mathbf{R}_+$ is a transitive kernel with $J(x,y) = O(d_G(x,y)^{-d\alpha})$ with $\alpha>1$.

body: Mordell-Weil theorem: Let A be an abelian variety over a number field K. Then A(K), the group of K-rational points of A, is a finitely generated abelian group, called the Mordell-Weil group; equivalently A(K) is isomorphic to Z^r x T, where r >= 0 is the rank and T is the finite torsion subgroup. The special case in which A = E is an elliptic curve and K = Q is Mordell's theorem, which answers a question apparently posed by Henri Poincare around 1901 and was proved by Louis Mordell in 1922; the general case is due to Andre Weil (1928). It is a foundational theorem of Diophantine geometry and of the arithmetic of abelian varieties.

body: Method for the bounded-density quadratic-form conjecture. ||p_Q||_inf <= (1/2 pi) int |phi_Q|, so a bounded density follows from |phi_Q(t)| <= C min(1, |t|^{-1-kappa}). The decay per large eigen-direction is NOT uniform over amplitudes: for every t and lambda there is a density f <= 1 with Re int f(x) e^{i t lambda x^2} dx >= 1/2 (f the indicator of a unit-measure subset of {cos(t lambda x^2) >= 1/2}), so van der Corput, which needs an amplitude of bounded variation, does not apply to one rough coordinate. What is uniform over all laws is the decay along spread directions: for orthonormal v_1..v_k with sum_j v_ji^2 <= 1/2 for every coordinate i, the Fresnel identity e^{i eta lambda V^2} = (4 pi i eta lambda)^{-1/2} int e^{-i xi^2/(4 eta lambda) + i xi V} d xi and the geometric Brascamp-Lieb inequality (Hoelder with p_i >= 2 and int |psi_i|^p <= 4 pi/sqrt p) give |E e^{i eta (sum_j lambda_j V_j^2 + diagonal + linear)}| <= (4 pi)^{k/2} prod_j |eta lambda_j|^{-1/2} for every diagonal and every linear term, and three spread large directions give a bounded density. The conjecture is hard exactly where a coordinate carries a large part of an eigenvector (a pivot or a hub), where the one-coordinate obstruction returns.

Let T be an arbitrary index set and suppose that for every finite subset {t_1, ..., t_n} of T a probability measure mu_{t_1, ..., t_n} on R^n (or on S^n for a Polish space S with its Borel sigma-algebra) is given. Suppose the family is CONSISTENT: (i) permuting the indices permutes the measure correspondingly, and (ii) the marginal of mu_{t_1, ..., t_n, t_{n+1}} on the first n coordinates is mu_{t_1, ..., t_n}. Then there is a probability measure P on the product space S^T equipped with the PRODUCT sigma-algebra whose finite-dimensional marginals are exactly the given family, and P is unique. TWO LIMITATIONS, both routinely forgotten. FIRST, the topological hypothesis is essential: for general measurable spaces the theorem is FALSE, and there are consistent families with no extension (Andersen and Jessen); what is really needed is that the marginals be inner regular in a suitable sense, which Polish spaces provide. SECOND, the resulting measure lives on the PRODUCT sigma-algebra, every member of which is determined by countably many coordinates. When T is uncountable, sets such as {the path is continuous}, {sup_t X_t <= c}, or {the path is bounded} are therefore NOT measurable for that sigma-algebra, so the theorem does not by itself construct Brownian motion as a continuous process; it constructs a process with the right finite-dimensional laws, and a separate regularity theorem - Kolmogorov's continuity criterion - is needed to produce a modification with continuous paths. [Kolmogorov (1933); see Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th ed., Theorem 2.1.21, and Billingsley, Probability and Measure, Section 36]

the state space Polish (or otherwise inner regular by compacts); the theorem fails for general measurable spaces
the conclusion is on the PRODUCT sigma-algebra only

Consistency makes this well defined, since a given cylinder has many representations differing by adding dummy coordinates or permuting them, and the two consistency conditions say exactly that all representations give the same value. Finite additivity on the algebra follows from finite additivity of each mu. The whole content is COUNTABLE additivity on the algebra, equivalently continuity at the empty set: if cylinders A_1 containing A_2 containing ... have empty intersection then P_0(A_n) -> 0. Suppose instead P_0(A_n) >= eps > 0 for every n. Each A_n is determined by finitely many coordinates and its base is a Borel subset of a finite power of a Polish space, so by inner regularity there is a COMPACT subset of the base carrying all but eps 2^{-n-1} of the measure; let K_n be the corresponding cylinder with compact base, shrunk so that the K_n are nested. Then P_0(K_n) >= eps/2 > 0, so each K_n is nonempty; picking a point from each and using compactness of the bases coordinate by coordinate, a diagonal argument produces a point lying in every K_n, hence in every A_n, contradicting that the intersection is empty. So P_0 is countably additive on the algebra, and Caratheodory's extension theorem extends it uniquely to the generated product sigma-algebra. [Proposition prop:comb-estimates of arXiv:2604.13968, 'Divisible sandpiles via random walks in random scenery'] Under the setup above, the following hold.
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
			\item \textup{(Continuation resistance)}\; For every $0\leq j\leq n{-}1$, one has $R_j\leq 2\,L_{j+1}$, and hence $V_j\leq 2\,I_{j+1}\,L_{j+1}$.
			\item \textup{(Trunk currents)}\; The trunk currents satisfy $I_1\geq 1/(4B)$ and $I_{j+1}\geq I_j/(2B)$ for every $1\leq j\leq n{-}1$. Consequently, $I_n\geq(4B)^{-n}$.
			\item \textup{(Total voltage mass)}\; There exists $C_{\mathrm{comb}}>0$ depending only on $B$ and~$\alpha$ such that
			\[
			\sum_{u\in D_{w,n}}g(u)\leq C_{\mathrm{comb}}\,I_n\,L_n^2\,.
			\]
			\item \textup{(Spike contribution)}\; Let $a\colon D_{w,n}\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $a(u)\geq -b$ for all~$u$, for some finite $b\geq 0$, and set $K\coloneqq 2+2b\,(C_{\mathrm{comb}}+1)$. If a vertex~$v$ in the first half of the terminal pipe~$P_w$ (at distance at least $L_n/2$ from the boundary) satisfies $a(v)\geq K\,L_n-b$, then
			\[
			\sum_{u\in D_{w,n}}g(u)\,a(u)\geq I_n\,L_n^2\,.
			\]
			\item \textup{(Exponential growth)}\; $I_n\,L_n^2\geq\lambda^n/4$.
		\end{enumerate}

[Proposition 1 (Exact deletion dynamics) of arXiv:2608.30261, 'Estimating Population-Risk Curves Along Nonconvex Gradient Flows from the Training Sample'] \label[proposition]{prop:exact-deletion}
Fix $i\in[n]$, $\lambda\in\Lambda$, and $T'\in[0,T]$, and suppose both
flows exist on $[0,T']$.  Suppose $F_{P_{-i},\lambda}$ is twice continuously
differentiable on the line segments joining $\theta_t^\lambda$ to
$\theta_{-i,t}^\lambda$ for every $t\in[0,T']$.  Then, for $0\leq t\leq T'$,
\begin{equation}
 \dot\Delta_{i,t}^\lambda
 =-\overline B_{i,t}^\lambda\Delta_{i,t}^\lambda
   +\frac{c_{i,t}^\lambda}{n-1},
 \qquad \Delta_{i,0}^\lambda=0,
\end{equation}
where the secant operator $\overline B_{i,t}^\lambda:\Theta\to\Theta$ is
\begin{equation}
 \overline B_{i,t}^\lambda
 =\int_0^1
   \nabla^2F_{P_{-i},\lambda}
      (\theta_t^\lambda+u\Delta_{i,t}^\lambda)\,\dd u.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Exact deletion dynamics

body: For two probability measures mu and nu on a measurable space (S, A), the total variation distance is d_TV(mu, nu) = sup over A in A of |mu(A) - nu(A)|, a number in [0, 1]. If mu and nu have densities f and g with respect to a common reference measure lambda (which always exists, for instance lambda = mu + nu), then d_TV(mu, nu) = (1/2) integral |f - g| d lambda = 1 - integral min(f, g) d lambda, and the supremum is attained at A = { f > g }. Equivalent characterisations: d_TV is half the supremum of |integral h d mu - integral h d nu| over measurable h with |h| <= 1; and by the coupling characterisation, d_TV(mu, nu) = min P(X not equal to Y) over all couplings (X, Y) with X distributed as mu and Y as nu, the minimum being attained by the maximal coupling. Convergence in total variation is strictly stronger than weak convergence (point masses at 1/n converge weakly to the point mass at 0 but stay at total variation distance 1). The normalisation matters: some texts use the un-halved integral |f - g| d lambda, which lies in [0, 2].
