body:
Let Omega be a bounded open subset of R^n with C^1 boundary (or any bounded extension domain, for instance a bounded Lipschitz domain), let 1 <= p < n and let p* = np/(n-p) be the Sobolev conjugate exponent. Then the embedding of W^{1,p}(Omega) into L^q(Omega) is COMPACT for every q strictly less than p*. At the endpoint q = p* the embedding is continuous but NOT compact. For p = n the embedding into L^q is compact for every finite q, and for p > n the embedding into C^{0,gamma}(closure of Omega) is compact for gamma < 1 - n/p. For the space W_0^{1,p}(Omega) no boundary regularity is needed: boundedness of Omega suffices.
Boundedness of Omega is essential (the embedding is never compact on R^n, by translating a fixed bump), and for W^{1,p} rather than W_0^{1,p} some boundary regularity is needed so that an extension operator exists.
Compactness FAILS at the critical exponent q = p*, which is exactly the loss of compactness behind concentration phenomena in critical problems.

[Proposition pr:tracking of arXiv:2504.11107, 'An Invariance Principle for some\\% Reaction-Diffusion Equations with a Multiplicative Ran'] For every $T>0$ let $u=u^{(T)}$ denote the solution to the parabolic Anderson model,
	\begin{equation*}\left[\begin{split}
		&\partial_t u = \partial^2_x u + \mu u  + \sigma u\dot{W}
			\hskip.95in\text{on $(T\,,\infty)\times\mathbb{T}$},\\
		&\text{subject to }u(0)=w(T)\hskip.9in\text{on $\mathbb{T}$}.
	\end{split}\right.\end{equation*}
	Then, for every $k \in (6\,,\infty)$ there exist non-random numbers
	$L=L(k\,,f\,,g)>0$ and 
	$\Delta_0=\Delta_0(k\,,f\,,g)\in(0\,,1)$ such that, independently of
	the value of $T$ and uniformly for all $\Delta(T)\in(0\,,\Delta_0)$,
	\[
		\mathrm{E}_{\mathscr{F}(T)}\left(\|w_T-u_T\|_{C([T,T+\Delta(T)]\times\mathbb{T})}^k
		\right)
		\leqslant L \left[\mathscr{E}\left({\rm e}^{-\gamma T}\right)\right]^k\|w(T)\|_{C(\mathbb{T})}^k,
	\]
	almost surely on the event $\{\tau(T)>T\}$, where
	$\mathscr{E}$ was defined in (equation R:star of the paper), and
	\[
		w_T(t\,,x) = w(t\wedge\tau(T)\,,x),\
		u_T(t\,,x) = u(t\wedge\tau(T)\,,x)\quad\forall t\geqslant T,\ x\in\mathbb{T}.
	\]

body:
[Lemma le:tightness_bdry_fl_refl of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] There exists $\zeta > 0$ such that the following is true. 
Fix $M >0$, $a_1>0$. Let $\delta^{1-a_1} \le r \le 1$, and let $h$ be a GFF on $r\mathbf{D}$ with some boundary values that are bounded by $M$ and so that the flow line $\eta_1$ from $-ir$ to $ir$ and the flow line $\overline{\eta}_2$ from $ir$ to $-ir$ in the components of $\mathbf{D} \setminus \eta_1$ to the right of $\eta_1$ (and reflected off $\eta_1$) are defined. Given $\eta_1,\overline{\eta}_2$, sample a ${\rm CLE}_{\kappa'}${} and the internal metric in the region bounded between them. Let $E_\delta$ be the event that there exist $x,y \in \eta_1 \cap \overline{\eta}_2$ such that if $U$ denotes the region bounded between the segments of $\eta_1$ and $\overline{\eta}_2$ from $x$ to $y$, then $U \subseteq B(0,3r/4)$, $\mathrm{diam}(U) \le \delta$, and
\[ D_\epsilon^{\partial U} \ge \delta^\zeta+\epsilon^{a_0} . \]
Then $\mathbf{P}[E_\delta] = o^\infty(\delta)$ as $\delta\searrow 0$.

The same is true when $\overline{\eta}_2$ is the (reflected) flow line in the components to the left of $\eta_1$.

Own-work target-partial result C008 v1, proof (unaudited); novelty unestablished. Let n>=2, m,d>=1, labels y_i in {-1,1}, z_i=y_i*x_i, ||x_i||<=1, rank{z_i}>=2, z_i dot z_l>=kappa>0 for all pairs, and a unit u satisfy u dot z_i>=gamma>0. With literal leaky ReLU phi(v)=max(v,lambda*v), 0<lambda<1, f_i=m^-1 sum_j a_j phi(w_j dot x_i), train both layers simultaneously by step m*eta on average logistic loss, any eta>0. Assume for each neuron a_j(0) and every w_j(0) dot z_i have the same strict sign. Put r_j=min_i|w_j(0) dot z_i|, H=eta*lambda^2*m^-1 sum_j r_j^2, c=H/(4+2H). This open cone is invariant: all sample branches stay fixed, neuron products increase, and every margin grows by at least H*G_t, G_t the average logistic weight. Consequently L_t<=1/(1/L_0+c*t). With epsilon_s=min(log(2)/2,1/H) and s=ceil(max(0,1/epsilon_s-1/L_0)/c), one has L_t<=8/[H*(t-s)] for every integer t>s. Under independent Gaussian initialization a_j~N(0,sigma^2), w_j~N(0,sigma^2 I_d), sigma>0, consider for each neuron the union of {a_j>0,w_j/sigma in B(u,gamma/2)} and its simultaneous negative. Independence across initial neurons gives event probability at least b^m, where b=(gamma/sqrt(2*pi*d))^d*exp(-(1+gamma/2)^2/2). On this event H>=H0=eta*lambda^2*sigma^2*gamma^2/4. Set c0=H0/(4+2H0), epsilon0=min(log(2)/2,1/H0), s0=ceil(max(0,1/epsilon0-1/log(2))/c0). Then simultaneously L_t<=1/(1/log(2)+c0*t) for t>=0 and L_t<=32/[eta*lambda^2*sigma^2*gamma^2*(t-s0)] for t>s0. The Gaussian lower bound is positive mass and decays with width: no high-probability or almost-sure generic cone-entry conclusion is claimed. Sharp Cai-type burn-in and the full target remain open. 25965 finite rational checks support selected algebra only; independent mathematical audit, analytic certification and novelty comparison remain pending.
Strictly positive signed Gram entries, rank>=2, bounded separable data and positive leakage.
Aligned initial neuron cone for deterministic theorem; explicitly specified Gaussian ball/sign event for the probability corollary.
Both layers trained simultaneously with actual step m*eta; no output-layer freezing.
Proof (unaudited), C008 v1; Gaussian positive-mass statement only, no general Gaussian entry or novelty claim.
title: T368 leaky-ReLU logistic GD: acute signed data, aligned cone and Gaussian positive mass (unaudited)

body:
[Definition def:qRacah_tilings of arXiv:2507.22011, 'Random Lozenge Waterfall:\\Dimensional Collapse of Gibbs Measures'] We put a probability measure on the set of all
	nonintersecting path ensembles. The measure depends on the
	geometry of the hexagon (parametrized by $(T,S,N)$), and
	on two parameters $q>0$ and $\kappa\in
	\mathbf{i}\mathbb{R}$.
	The
	probability weight of a nonintersecting path ensemble is
	proportional to
	\begin{equation}
		
		\prod_{\textnormal{holes in the path ensemble}} \mathsf{w}_{q,\kappa}\bigl( x-\tfrac t2+1\bigr),
		\qquad
		\mathsf{w}_{q,\kappa}(j) \coloneqq \kappa q^{j-(S+1)/2}-\frac{1}{\kappa q^{j-(S+1)/2}}.
	\end{equation}
	Here the holes are points $(t,x)$ such that $x\notin X(t)$,
	but $x$ satisfies the inequalities
	(equation eq:hexagon_constraints of the paper). In other words,
	holes are lozenges of the type
	\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline = (current bounding box.south),scale=.25]
		\draw[thick] (0,0)--++(1,1)--++(1,0)--++(-1,-1)--cycle;
	\end{tikzpicture}.
	For example, in (fig:tiling_and_path_picture of the paper), right, the holes are $(1,2),(2,1),(2,4),(3,0),(3,2),(3,5),(4,2),(4,3),(5,3)$.
	The probability weights are normalized so that the total probability of all path ensembles is $1$.
	We call the resulting probability measure the \emph{$q$-Racah measure} on nonintersecting path ensembles
	(equivalently, on lozenge tilings of the hexagon).
title: $q$-Racah measure on nonintersecting path ensembles

[Proposition 4 (Qin) of arXiv:2609.03238, 'Representation Defects and Cassels Pairings for Congruent Number Curves'] Let $n$ be a positive squarefree integer.  Define $\Delta_Q(n)$ and $\sigma_Q(n)$ by
\eqref{eq:defect}.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If $L(E_n,1)\ne0$, then
\[
|\Sha(E_n)|_{\mathrm{an}}
 =\left(\frac{\Delta_Q(n)}{2\sigma_Q(n)}\right)^2.
\]
If $L(E_n,1)=0$, then $\Delta_Q(n)=0$.
\item If $m$ is odd and $m\equiv1\pmod8$, then
\[
r_f(m)+r_g(m)=4h(-m),
\qquad
\frac{r_f(m)-r_g(m)}2=r_a(m)-h(-m).
\]
\item If $m$ is odd and $m\equiv1\pmod4$, then
\[
r_s(m)+r_t(m)=2h(-2m).
\]
\end{enumerate}

[Deffr Divisors of arXiv:2606.06187, 'How to Study Reflected Brownian Motion in a Quadrant via Kernel Functional Equations?\\ \m'] A divisor on $\mathbf{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) = \mathbb{C} \cup \{\infty\}$ is a finite formal expression of the form $\sum n_a[a]$ where each $n_a \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $a$ ranges over elements of $\mathbf{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$. The support of a divisor is the finite set of all $a$ such that $n_a \neq 0$. The divisor $\operatorname{div}(f)$ of a rational function $f \in \mathbb{C}(z)^*$ is defined as
\[
\operatorname{div}(f) := \sum_a \operatorname{ord}_a(f)[a]
\]
where $\operatorname{ord}_a(f)$ denotes the order of $f$ at the point $a$, and the sum is taken over all $a \in \mathbf{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$ and is in fact finite.
title: Divisors

body: [Definition def:disint1 of arXiv:2507.01236, 'Disintegration theorem for multifunctions, \\ with applications to empirical Wasserstein d'] Given $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $\epsilon > 0$, and $r > 0$, we declare a metric Polish probability space $(\mathfrak{X},d,\mu)$ to be $(n,\epsilon,r)$\emph{-disintegrable} if, whenever $X_1,\dots,X_n$ are i.i.d.\ with distribution $\mu$ on a probability space $(\Psi,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$, there exists a disintegration of $\mu$ along $F_{r, X_{[n]}}$ with respect to the uniform measure on $[n]$ with $\mathbb{P}$-probability at least $1-\epsilon$.

	\]

[Lemma lem2 of arXiv:2608.30848, '\huge \bf Limit Laws of the Iterated Logarithm Under Sub-linear Expectations'] Let $X\in \mathscr{H}$.
\begin{description}
  \item[\rm (i)]
 For any $\delta>0$, we have
$$ \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \mathbb V\big(|X|\ge \delta \sqrt{n\log\log n} \big)<\infty \;\; \Longleftrightarrow C_{\mathbb V}\bigg[\frac{X^2}{\log\log|X|}\bigg]<\infty.
$$
 \item[\rm (ii)]
   If $C_{\mathbb V}\bigg[\frac{X^2}{\log\log|X|}\bigg]<\infty$, then for any $\delta>0$ and $p>2$, we have
$$ \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{\widehat{\mathbb E}\big[\big(|X|\wedge (\delta \sqrt{n\log\log n})\big)^p\big]}{(n\log\log n)^{p/2}}<\infty. $$
 \item[\rm (iii)] If $C_{\mathbb V}\bigg[\frac{X^2}{\log\log|X|}\bigg]<\infty$, then for any $\delta>0$, we have
 $$ \widehat{\mathbb E}[X^2\wedge (2\delta n\log\log n)]=o(\log \log n), $$
  $$ \breve{\mathbb E}[(|X|-\delta \sqrt{2 n\log\log n})^+]=o(\sqrt{\log\log n/n}). $$
\end{description} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem2 of arXiv:2608.30848

[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2608.17562, '2608.17562'] Let $(X_{n})_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of \iid random variables whose tail distribution function $\widebar{F}$ belongs to $\SRV{-\alpha}{\rho}$ with auxiliary function~$A$, for some $\alpha > 0$ and $\rho < 0$, and set
\[
U_n \coloneq \big\lb \exists i \in \lbra 1,n \rbra,\ \forall j \in \lbra 1,n \rbra \bs \lb i \rb,\ X_{i} > X_j \big\rb.
\]
Then, for some constant $C > 0$ we have 
\[
\prob(U_{n}^{c}) \leq C\Big(\frac{1}{n} + A(a_n)\Big),
\quad n \geq 1, 
\]

body: FIRES WHEN a balls-in-boxes argument reaches for the tilted i.i.d. representation and the local limit theorem behind Janson's (18.14). THE ROUTE: write P(Y_1 = k) = w_k Z(m - k, n - 1)/Z(m, n) and union bound over the n boxes. WHERE IT BREAKS: Lemma 13.1, the local limit theorem that (18.14) rests on, is proved for FIXED lambda in (0, nu). When lambda_n = m/n -> 0 the tilted laws degenerate - the mass at 0 tends to 1 and the variance to 0 - so the Gaussian local limit theorem has to be replaced by a Poisson-regime one and glued to the Gaussian regime when m is comparable to n. That uniform statement does not appear to exist in the literature, and without it the union bound has no input at all. CONDITION OF FAILURE: m/n -> 0, which is exactly the regime the conjecture is about. The heuristic the route does give is still useful as a target: P(Y_1 >= k) is about w_k tau_n^k / Phi(tau_n) with tau_n = tau(m/n) -> 0, so n P(Y_1 >= k) -> 0 once k >= (1 + eps) log n / log(1/tau_n), and that threshold is o(log n) precisely because tau_n -> 0.

body:
In the binomial random graph G(n,p) with p = (log n + c)/n for a fixed real c, the number of isolated vertices converges in distribution to a Poisson random variable with mean e^{-c} (the method of moments: the factorial moments of the count converge to those of the Poisson law), and the probability that G(n,p) is connected tends to exp(-e^{-c}) (Erdos and Renyi 1959, 1960). The obstruction to connectivity in this window is isolated vertices alone: P(G connected) - P(G has no isolated vertex) tends to 0. Consequently p = log n / n is a sharp threshold: for p = (1 - epsilon) log n / n the graph is disconnected with probability tending to 1 (with a growing number of isolated vertices), and for p = (1 + epsilon) log n / n it is connected with probability tending to 1. Below the threshold at p = c'/n with c' > 1 the graph already has a unique giant component but is disconnected.
edges are present independently with the same probability p (the binomial model; the uniform model G(n,m) has the analogous statement with m = (n/2)(log n + c))
the statement is about the window p = (log n + c)/n with c fixed as n grows
the Poisson approximation is for the count of isolated vertices; other small components are negligible in this window
title: Erdos-Renyi connectivity threshold of G(n,p) and the Poisson paradigm for isolated vertices

body:
[Defn \cite{JamneshanMachado} of arXiv:2605.16921, '${\ASL_n}(\mathbb Z)$ invariant random subsets of $\mathbb Z^n$'] We call a \emph{bundle of nilsystems (of dimension $\leq k$) over $\Omega$} any $\mathbb{Z}^d$-system constructed from the following data:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item a standard Borel probability space $(\Omega, \nu)$;
    \item a countable Borel partition $(\Omega_n)_{n \geq 0}$ of $\Omega$ and a countable family of nilmanifolds $(N_n/\Gamma_n)_{n \geq 0}$ of dimension $\leq k$;
    \item Borel maps $\rho_n: \Omega_n \to \Hom(\mathbb{Z}^d, N_n)$ such that for $\nu$-a.e. $\omega \in \Omega_n$, the action of $\rho_n(\omega)$ on $N_n/\Gamma_n$ is ergodic.
\end{enumerate}
The space
$$ X := \bigsqcup_{n \geq 0} \Omega_n \times N_n/\Gamma_n,$$
equipped with the measure
$$\sum_{n \geq 0} \nu_{|\Omega_n} \otimes \mu_{N_n/\Gamma_n}$$
and the $\mathbb{Z}^d$-action defined for $(\omega, \overline{n}) \in \Omega_n \times (N_n/\Gamma_n)$ and $t \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ by
$$ t \cdot (\omega, \overline{n}) = (\omega, \rho_n(\omega)(t) \cdot \overline{n}),$$
is denoted
$$ \bigsqcup_{n \geq 0} \Omega_n \rtimes_{\rho_n} N_n/\Gamma_n.$$
The natural map $\bigsqcup_{n \geq 0} \Omega_n \rtimes_{\rho_n} N_n/\Gamma_n \to \Omega$ is called the \emph{bundle projection}.

CAMPAIGN RESULT [independently checked proof; E0095-FRAC v1; no novelty claim]. For the cycle C_8, with perfect matchings restricted to new edges, the maximum lambda_2(L_C8+L_M) over individual matchings is exactly 2. Maximizing lambda_2 over probability mixtures of those matching Laplacians instead has value at least (16-4sqrt(2))/5>2. Consequently minimizing the density-matrix/max-weight-matching upper bound cannot always certify the integral optimum. Divide by three to obtain the corresponding ordinary SRW gaps. [Lemma 19 of arXiv:2608.06576, 'The Resultant Distribution Method: Universality for $p$-adic Random Matrices and Polynomia'] Fix a finite set $S\subseteq\Z_{>0}$. For every $n\geq 1$, let
$A_n^{\Haar}\in\Mat_n(\Z_p)$ be additive Haar distributed. Then there
exists a random polynomial
$$
Q_{\infty}^{\Haar,S}\in\mathcal P^S
$$
such that
$$
P_{A_n^{\Haar}}^S
\overset{d}{\longrightarrow}
Q_{\infty}^{\Haar,S},
\qquad n\to\infty.
$$
Moreover, the limiting polynomial is almost surely squarefree:
$$
\mathbf{P}\left(
Q_{\infty}^{\Haar,S}\text{ is squarefree}
\right)=1.
$$

body:
[Lemma 4 (One-excursion structure) of arXiv:2605.14511, 'Clumsy and Careless:\\ Stationary-Entry Flux in Non-monotone Coupon Collectors'] Let $K_n$ be the number of standard-coupon draws before the next reset.  Then
\[
        \Pbb(K_n=k)=\rho_n q_n^k,
        \qquad k=0,1,2,\ldots.
\]
A reset-free excursion succeeds precisely when
\[
        C_n\le K_n.
\]
Consequently the one-excursion success probability is
\[
        s_n:=\Pbb(C_n\le K_n)=\Ebb q_n^{C_n}=\phi_n(q_n).
\]

[Lemma lem:uniformboundFOU of arXiv:2601.21762, 'Navier-Stokes with a fractional transport noise as a limit of multi-scale dynamics'] Let $w$ be the stationary solution of $dw_t = -Mw_t dt + Q^{\frac 12}dB^H_t$. Then:
\begin{equ}
      \sup_{t>0} \mathbb{E}\left[\left\|w_t\right\|_{H^\sigma}^2\right] = C_H \tr{M^{-2H}Q}, \qquad 
       \sup_{t>0} \mathbb{E}\left[\norm{M^{-1}w_{t}}_{H^{\sigma}}^{2}\right] = C_H\tr{M^{-2-2H}Q}.
\end{equ}
Furthermore $w$ satisfies the bounds: 
$$\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|w_{s,t}\right\|_{H^\sigma}^2\right]  \lesssim  \left(\tr{M^{2-2H}Q} +\ensuremath\trace[Q] + \tr{M^{-2H}Q} \right) |t-s|^{2H},$$
$$\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|M^{-1} w_{s,t}\right\|_{H^\sigma}^2\right]  \lesssim  
\left(\tr{M^{-2H}Q} +\tr{M^{-2}Q} + \tr{M^{-2-2H}Q}\right) |t-s|^{2H},$$
where the constants indicated by $\lesssim$ depend only on $H$.

[Definition of arXiv:2411.05534, 'Inverse problems for stochastic partial differential equations'] A measure on $ (\Omega, \mathcal{F}) $ is a function $ \mu : \mathcal{F} \rightarrow [0, +\infty] $ such that 
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item $ \mu(\emptyset) = 0 $,
        \item if $ \{E_{i}\}_{i=1}^{\infty} $ is a sequence of disjoint sets in $ \mathcal{F} $, i.e., $ E_{i} \cap E_{j}  = \emptyset$ for all $ i,j \in \mathbb{N}$ with $ i \neq j $, then $ \mu(\bigcup\limits_{i=1}^{\infty} E_{i}) = \sum\limits_{i=1}^{n} \mu(E_{i}) $.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Explicit model calculation and hypothesis obstruction Result: The obstruction to a purely topological continuation argument is already visible in R3: choose a nonzero smooth compactly supported divergence-free vector field phi and put v_n(x)=n*phi(n*x). Then ||v_n||_L3=||phi||_L3 for every n, while v_n tends to zero almost everywhere and has no strongly convergent L3 subsequence. If it had a strong subsequence, an almost-everywhere convergent subsubsequence would force its limit to zero, contradicting the constant positive norm. Check: The scaling is exact because n^3 from the cubic amplitude cancels n^-3 from the volume change. This is a sequence in the critical space, not a claimed trajectory of Navier-Stokes. Obstruction: Energy or compactness information supplied by the equation must rule out such concentration near a hypothetical blow-up time. Boundedness of the Banach-space norm alone cannot replace the source limit condition. No stochastic backward-uniqueness or concentration-compactness argument is completed.

body:
[Definition of arXiv:2608.28505, 'Quagmires and large Suslin forests'] Given two cardinals $\kappa < \lambda$, a $(\kappa, \lambda)$-forest\footnote{In Eskew's more general notation, this is a $(\kappa, \lambda, 2)$-forest [MR3326048].} is a collection $F$ of functions satisfying:
\begin{enumerate}
\item for every $f \in F$, $\mathrm{ran}(f) \subseteq \{0,1\}$,
\item $\{\mathrm{dom}(f) : f \in F\} = [\lambda]^{< \kappa}$,
\item for every $x,y \in [\lambda]^{< \kappa}$ with $x \subseteq y$,
\[
\{f \in F : \mathrm{dom}(f) = x\} = \{f \upharpoonright x : f \in F \text{ and } \mathrm{dom}(f) = y\}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2608.28505, 'Quagmires and large Suslin forests'

[Theorem thm:maincgce of arXiv:2607.05671, 'Bi-infinite systems of singularly interacting Brownian particles and the KPZ equation'] As $\varepsilon \to 0$, $\tilde \mathcal{E}^{\varepsilon}_{\theta}$ converges to $u$, in distribution, in $C([0, \infty); \mathcal{C}(\mathbb{R}))$.
Furthermore, for any $r \ge 1$, $T<\infty$ and compact $K\subset \mathbb{R}$,
\begin{equation}
   \left\|\sup_{t \in [0,T], x \in K} \left|\tilde \mathcal{E}_{\theta}^\varepsilon(t,x) - \mathcal{G}^\varepsilon(t,x) \right| \right\|_r \to 0 \text{ as } \varepsilon \to 0.
\end{equation}
Consequently, $\{\mathcal{G}^{\varepsilon}(t,x), (t,x) \in \mathbb{R}_+\times \mathbb{R}\}$ converges, uniformly on compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}_+ \times \mathbb{R}$, in distribution to the random field
$\{u(t,x), (t,x) \in \mathbb{R}_+ \times \mathbb{R}\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:maincgce of arXiv:2607.05671

[Proposition 7 (cf.~\cite{Kobayashi96}) of arXiv:2608.25785, 'Proper Actions on Homogeneous Spaces of the Upper Triangular Matrix Group via Coarse Geome'] Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group, $L$ and $H$ closed subgroups of $G$.
    The following six conditions are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item The natural $L$-action on the homogeneous space $G/H$ is proper.
        \item The natural $H$-action on the homogeneous space $G/L$ is proper.
        \item The diagonal $G$-action on the space $G/H\times G/L$ is proper.
        \item The intersection $L\cap CHC^{-1}$ is relatively compact in $G$ for any compact subset $C$ of $G$.
        \item The intersection $CLC^{-1}\cap H$ is relatively compact in $G$ for any compact subset $C$ of $G$.
        \item The intersection $CHC^{-1}\cap CLC^{-1}$ is relatively compact in $G$ for any compact subset $C$ of $G$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: cf.~\cite{Kobayashi96}

Owner draft: independently checked proof (C007 v1). Let 1<=d<=m. A spherical R^m law whose first d-coordinate projection is Unif(B_d) must have m<=d+2. Its coordinate second and fourth moments are 1/(d+2) and 3/((d+2)(d+4)), so E||Y||^2=m/(d+2) and E||Y||^4=m(m+2)/((d+2)(d+4)). Nonnegative variance of ||Y||^2 implies the ceiling. At m=d+2 the radius is one almost surely. This is a restriction on spherical extensions, not on arbitrary nonspherical constant-sum couplings. It warns against assuming the matrix-generator extension in Yin's elliptical theorem without checking it.

[Lemma of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] \label[lemma]{no_atoms_bigger_than_p}
Let $f \in \Sym$ with $\@ifstar{\oldabs}{\oldabs*}{\supp(f)} \ge 3$. 
For all $y \ne 0$, $f(y) < p$. 
\begin{proof}
We separate the proof into two cases, when $y=1$ and when $y \ne 1$. 
In the case where $y \ne 1$, 
\begin{align*}
q f(-y+2) + p f(-y)
&=  f_{X+Y}(-y+1) \\
&= f_{X+Y}(y-1) = q f(y) + p f(y-2) 
\ge qf(y). 
\end{align*}
Dividing both sides by $p$ and adding $f(y)$, 
\[
f(y) + \frac{q}{p} f(-y+2) + f(-y) \ge \frac{q}{p}f(y) + f(y) = \frac{1}{p}f(y) .
\]
Since $\frac{q}{p} < 1$ and the values $y$, $-y+2$, and $-y$ are distinct, the left-hand side of the preceding equation is strictly bounded above by $1$. 

Similarly, when $y=1$, we have 
\[
qf(-1) + pf(-3) 
= f_{X+Y}(-2) 
= f_{X+Y}(2)
= qf(3) + pf(1) 
\ge pf(1) 
\]
so that
\[
f(-1) + f(-3) \ge \frac{q}{p} f(-1) + f(-3) \ge f(1) . 
\]
Adding $f(1)$ to both sides, we see that 
\(
1 \ge f(1) + f(-1) + f(-3) \ge 2f(1)
\);
in particular $f(1) \le \frac{1}{2} < p$. 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered lemma of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'

[Theorem thm:2G_edge of arXiv:2411.16572, 'Optimal decay of eigenvector overlap for non-Hermitian random matrices'] Fix small constants $\epsilon, \tau>0$ with $0<\tau<\epsilon/10$. Then, for any deterministic matrices $\|A_i\| \lesssim 1$, the following local law  
\begin{equation}
	\Big|\langle \big(\mathrm{Im}\, G^{z_1}(\mathrm{i} \eta_1) A_1 \mathrm{Im}\, G^{z_2}(\mathrm{i} \eta_2)-\widehat M_{12}^{A_1}\big)A_2\rangle\Big|\prec
	\frac{1}{\sqrt{n\ell}}\frac{\rho_{1}\rho_{2}}{\widehat{\gamma}},
\end{equation}
holds uniformly for any $z_i \in {\mathbb C}$ and $\eta_i \in {\mathbb R }~(i=1,2)$ such that $|z_i|\le 1+n^{-1/2+\tau}$ and $\ell =\min_{i=1,2}\rho_i|\eta_i| \geq n^{-1+\epsilon}$,
with $\widehat \gamma$ given by ((parameter2 of the paper)), and the deterministic matrix $\widehat{M}_{12}^A=\widehat{M}_{12}^A(\mathrm{i}\eta_1,z_1,\mathrm{i} \eta_2,z_2)$ defined in ((Im_M_def of the paper)). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[0 2 of arXiv:2606.10058, 'Mean First Passage Times and Fundamental Tensors of Higher Order Markov Chains'] Given $m$th order tensor ${\cal A}=[a_{i_1i_2\ldots i_m}] \in \mathbb R^{u \times u \times n \times \cdots \times n}$, where $u \le n$, the $k$th power of $\cal A$ is defined recursively by 
$${\cal A}^1={\cal A}, ~{\cal A}^{k+1}={\cal A}^k \boxtimes {\cal A}, ~k=1, 2, \ldots.$$
By convention, ${\cal A}^0$ is the identity tensor ${\cal I}=[\delta_{i_1i_2\ldots i_m}] \in \mathbb R^{u \times u \times n \times \cdots \times n}$, where for any $1 \le i_1, i_2 \le u$ and $1\le i_3, \ldots, i_m \le n$,
$$\delta_{i_1i_2\ldots i_m}=\delta_{i_1i_2}=\left\{\begin{array}{cl}
1, & i_1=i_2;\\
0, & {\rm otherwise}.
\end{array}\right.$$

[Lem 11 of arXiv:2609.00723, 'An integral Hyodo--Kato isomorphism'] Let $ (\sA=(A,\alpha:L \to A),F_A)$ be a special $F$-pre-log algebra over $\sR$ such that 

$\sR\to \sA$ is log-smooth. Assume that $\sA/p$ is  of Cartier type over $\sR/p$, and that $A$ is $p$-torsion free. 

\begin{itemize}
\item[(1)]
The natural map $\omega^*_{\sA/\sR}\to \WSat(\omegaSs{\sA})$ induces a quasi-isomorphism (cf. Remark \ref{rmk;prop;omegaDAlog})
\[\omega^*_{\sA/\sR}/p^r\otimes_R \Rperf \simeq \WSat(\omegaSs{\sA})/V^r\qfor r>0,\]
where $\WSat(\omegaSs{\sA})/V^r= \WSat(\omegaSs{\sA})/\im(V^r)+\im(dV^{r})$ (cf. \cite[2.5.1]{BLM}).
\item[(2)]
The above map induces isomorphisms
\[ \omega^*_{\sA/\sR}/p\otimes_R \Rperf \simeq \widehat{\omega}_{\sA/\sR}^*/p \otimes_R \Rperf\simeq  \WSat(\omegaSshat{\sA})/V.\]

\end{itemize}

[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2608.22534, 'Entropy power inequalities in compact groups'] Let $G$ be a connected compact abelian group, let $\mu$ be its 
Haar probability measure and $Y$ be a random variable on $G$ with 
density $f_Y$. Let $S$ be a set of positive Haar measure 
and $g_S = \frac{1}{\mu(S)}\mathbb{I}_S$ be the density of a uniform 
random variable $U_S$ on $S$. For $t>0$, also define
    \begin{equation*} 
    g^t(y) = \frac{t+f_Y(y)}{1+t}, \quad y \in G.
    \end{equation*}
    Then, for all $t > 0 $
\begin{equation*} 
    \chi^2(f_Y \ast g_S \| g^t  \ast g_S) \leq \eta_S\frac{t+\|f_Y\|_{\infty}}{t}\chi^2(f_Y\|g^t),
\end{equation*}
where
$$\eta_S = \left(\frac{\sin(\pi \mu(S))}{\pi \mu(S)}\right)^2.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 19 of arXiv:2608.22534

Let $S$ be a symmetric positive semidefinite $M \times M$ matrix (a sample covariance) and consider the long-only minimum-variance problem $\min_w w^T S w$ subject to $\mathbf{1}^T w = 1$ and $w \ge 0$. Let $w^+$ be a solution and $\delta \in \mathbb{R}^M$, $\delta \ge 0$, the Lagrange multipliers of the nonnegativity constraints ($\delta_m > 0$ only where $w^+_m = 0$). THEOREM (Jagannathan and Ma, 2003). $w^+$ is also the UNCONSTRAINED minimum-variance solution (subject only to $\mathbf{1}^T w = 1$) for the modified covariance $$\tilde S = S - \delta \mathbf{1}^T - \mathbf{1}\delta^T,$$ which is symmetric, positive semidefinite on the relevant set, and differs from $S$ by lowering the covariances of the constrained (excluded) assets with every other asset by $\delta_m$ and their variances by $2\delta_m$. Imposing the no-short constraint is therefore equivalent to shrinking the large entries of the sample covariance toward zero by data-determined amounts - which is why the constraint improves out-of-sample risk even when the true covariance would not call for it ("why imposing the wrong constraints helps"): it acts as a covariance-shrinkage estimator whose amount is chosen implicitly by the optimisation, without cross-validation.
S symmetric positive semidefinite
the feasible set is nonempty (it always is: the simplex)

On the feasible directions of that problem, $v$ with $\\mathbf{1}^T v = 0$, one has $v^T\\tilde S v = v^T S v - 2(\\delta^T v)(\\mathbf{1}^T v) = v^T S v \\ge 0$, so $\\tilde S$ is positive semidefinite on the constraint hyperplane and the stationary point $w^+$ is a minimiser of the equality-constrained problem. Hence the long-only solution for $S$ is the unconstrained (sum-to-one) solution for $\\tilde S$. Reading the entries, $\\tilde S_{mk} = S_{mk} - \\delta_m - \\delta_k$: an asset whose nonnegativity constraint binds ($\\delta_m > 0$, $w^+_m = 0$) has every covariance with the other assets reduced by $\\delta_m$ and its variance reduced by $2\\delta_m$, while assets held long are untouched. body: A random variable X is sub-Gaussian with proxy sigma^2 if E exp(t(X - EX)) <= exp(sigma^2 t^2 / 2) for all real t. Equivalently, its tails satisfy P(|X - EX| > s) <= 2 exp(-s^2 / (2 sigma^2)) up to constants; bounded random variables are sub-Gaussian by Hoeffding's lemma with sigma = (b - a)/2.

[Lem rationalencodingMagee of arXiv:2412.00593, 'A new approach to strong convergence II.\\The classical ensembles'] Let $Q:=(L+M)q_0$. For every $h \in \mathcal{P}_q$, there is a rational 
function $\Psi_h:=\frac{f_h}{g_{Qq}}$ with 
$f_h,g_{Qq}\in\mathcal{P}_{\lfloor 4Qq(1+\log Qq)\rfloor}$
so that
$$
	N^{-(L+M)} \mathbf{E}[\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}} h(X^N)] = \Psi_h(\tfrac{1}{N}) =
	\Psi_h(-\tfrac{1}{N})
$$
for all $N\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $N>Qq$. Here $g_{Qq}$ is defined as in
(equation eq:defofgL of the paper).

[Definition McKean--Vlasov approximation of type 2 of arXiv:2606.13264, 'Interference Queueing Networks: A Replica Mean-Field Approach in the Symmetric Setting'] Let \(p^\star\in[0,1]\) be a solution of the fixed-point equation
\[
p^\star=\mathbb P(q^{p^\star}>0),
\]
where \(q^p\) denotes the stationary random-environment queue defined above.

For each \(i\in\{1,\dots,N\}\), let \(D_i^p\) be a Poisson random measure on
\[
\mathbb R_+\times \mathbb R_+\times \{0,1\}^{N-1}
\]
with intensity
\[
\mathrm du\,\mathrm dz\,\nu_{
p}(\mathrm d\theta),
\]
where \(\nu_{p}\) is the product measure of \(N-1\) independent Bernoulli random
variables with parameter \(p\).

For \(\theta=(\theta_m)_{m\neq i}\in\{0,1\}^{N-1}\), define
\[
\mu_i^{\mathrm{MF2}}(\theta)
=
B\log_2\left(
1+
\frac{1}{1+\sum_{m\neq i}\theta_m l(d(i,m))}
\right).
\]
The McKean--Vlasov approximation of type 2 is defined by
\begin{equation}
q_i^{\mathrm{MF2}}(t)
=
q_i^{\mathrm{MF2}}(0)
+
A_i[0,t]
-
\int_{\{0,1\}^{N-1}}\int_{\mathbb R_+}\int_0^t
\mathbf 1_{\{u\leq \mu_i^{\mathrm{MF2}}(\theta)\}}
\mathbf 1_{\{q_i^{\mathrm{MF2}}(z^-)>0\}}
\,D_i^{p^\star}(\mathrm du,\mathrm dz,\mathrm d\theta).
\end{equation}
title: McKean--Vlasov approximation of type 2

            \mathbf{1}_{U_k(r-\frac12,r)}

        \ge
        c\,\mathbb{E}\left[\bigl(X_r^{(k)}\bigr)^\lambda\right].
    \end{equation}

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2606.21394, 'McKean-Vlasov Equations for Large Networks of Neurons with Adaptive Asymmetric Edges'] For any  $b \geq T^{1/4}$, there is a constant $C_b > 0$ such that the following holds.  For any $u,\tilde{u} \in \mathcal{C}\big([0,T], \mathbb{R}^c\big)$ and $z,\tilde{z} \in \mathcal{C}\big([0,T], \mathbb{R}^d\big)$ such that 
 \begin{align}
    \sup_{h\leq 1} \sup_{0\leq t \leq T-h} \big\lbrace h^{-1/4} \norm{\tilde{u}_{t+h} - \tilde{u}_t} \big\rbrace &= b < \infty \\
   \sup_{h\leq 1} \sup_{0\leq t \leq T-h} \big\lbrace h^{-1/4} \norm{z_{t+h} - \tilde{z}_t} \big\rbrace &= b < \infty \\
 \norm{u_0}^2 &\leq b \\
  \norm{\tilde{u}_0}^2 &\leq b \\
  \norm{z_0}^2 &\leq b  \\
    \norm{\tilde{z}_0}^2 &\leq b,
 \end{align}
 it holds that
\begin{align}
\sup_{t\leq T}\big\| u(t) - \tilde{u}(t) \big\|^2 &\leq C_b\int_0^T \big\| u(t) - \tilde{u}(t) \big\|^2  dt  \\
\sup_{t\leq T}\big\| z(t) - \tilde{z}(t) \big\|^2 &\leq C_b\int_0^T \big\| z(t) - \tilde{z}(t) \big\|^2  dt  
\end{align}
title: Lemma 10 of arXiv:2606.21394

[Theorem teoScaleFnBV of arXiv:2604.08889, 'Matrix Representations for Scale Functions of Spectrally Negative Lévy Processes with Rati'] Let $X$ be a L\'evy process as in (equation eqnXTrajectories of the paper), with $\sigma=0$ and $d>0$. Then, for any $x\geq 0$ and $q\geq 0$ such that $\psi'(\Phi_q)>0$ we have
\begin{equation}
W^{(q)}(x) = \frac{1}{\psi'(\Phi_q)} \Big( \mathrm{e}^{\Phi_q x} - \bm{\Psi}\, e^{\bm{G}x}\,\bm{\nu} \Big), \qquad x \ge 0,
\end{equation}where $\bm{G}: = \bm{T} + \bm{t}\,\bm{\Psi}$, $\bm{\nu}:=(\Phi_q \bm I - \bm{T})^{-1}\bm{t}$ with $\bm I$ the identity matrix.
The matrix $\bm{\Psi}$ is a solution to 
\begin{equation}
\bm{\Psi} \big( (\lambda + q)\bm{I} - d\bm{T} - d\,\bm{t}\,\bm{\Psi} \big) = \lambda\, \bm{\alpha}.
\end{equation}Finally, $\bm{\Psi}$ can be obtained as the limit of the recursive equation
\begin{equation}
\bm{\Psi}_n
:=
\Big(\frac{\lambda}{d}\bm{\alpha} + (\bm{\Psi}_{n-1}\bm{t})\bm{\Psi}_{n-1}\Big)
\left(\frac{\lambda + q}{d}\bm I - \bm{T}\right)^{-1},
\end{equation}with  $\bm{\Psi}_0=\bm{0}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem teoScaleFnBV of arXiv:2604.08889

[Proposition 6 of arXiv:2608.22693, 'Uniformity of extremal behaviour along geodesics in Liouville quantum gravity'] Fix $\Phi \in (0,1/10)$ and $p_1 \in (0,1)$. There exists a translation and scale invariant family of deterministic points $\{u_-,u_+,v_-,v_+\}_{z \in \CC, r>0}$ satisfying $u_+,u_- \in B_{\Phi r}(z-r)$ and $v_+,v_- \in B_{\Phi r}(z+r)$ such that with $P_+,P_-$ defined by $P_+=\Gamma_{u_+,v_+}, P_-=\Gamma_{v_-,v_+}$, suppose we have a translation and scale invariant family of events $\{H_r(z)\}_{z\in \CC, r>0}$ which are measurable with respect to $\sigma(P_-\cup P_+, \cap_{\varepsilon>0}\sigma( \pi(h)\lvert_{B_{\varepsilon}(P_-\cup P_+)}))$ viewed modulo an additive constant and satisfy $\PP(H_r(z))\geq p_1$, then there exist constants $A > 1, \rho \in (0,1)$ depending only on $p_1$ and constants $c_1,c_2$ depending only on $\gamma$ such the following is true.

Let $U \subseteq \CC$ be a bounded open set. Set $\varepsilon_n = 2^{-n}$ for all $n \in \NN$. With $\mathcal{H}_n = ((\varepsilon_n / 2)^{1/c_1} \ZZ^2) \cap U$, for all $\beta >0$, there exist (random) $0<\varphi < \psi < \beta /20$ depending only on $U$ and $\beta$ such that we have the following for all $n \in \NN$ large enough. For all $\bz \in \mathcal{H}_n$ and all $w \in U$ satisfying $D_h(\bz,w) \geq \beta$, and every $D_h$-geodesic $\Gamma_{\bz,w}$ from $\bz$ to $w$, there exists $(z,r) \in \CC \times [\varepsilon_n^{1/(2c_2)} , \varepsilon_n^{1/(4c_2)}]$ satisfying the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There exists $z' \in \partial B_r(z)$ such that for the points $u_-,u_+,v_-,v_+$ corresponding to $z'$ and the radius $\rho r/A^2$, the event $\scX^{u_+,v_+}_{u_-,v_-} \cap H_{\rho r/A^2}(z')$ occurs.
    \item With $P_+ = \Gamma_{u_+,v_+}, P_- = \Gamma_{u_-,v_-}$ being the unique $D_h$-geodesics corresponding to the points $u_-,u_+,v_-,v_+$ associated to the point $z'$ and the radius $\rho r/A^2$, we have $P_-\cup P_+\subseteq B_{\rho r/(4A)}(z')$ and further there exists $\varphi<\tau^- < \tau^+<\psi$ such that $P_- \cap P_+ = \Gamma_{\bz,w}|_{[\tau^-,\tau^+]}$.
\item $P_+$ (resp.\ $P_-$) intersects $\Gamma_{\bz,w}$ on its left (resp.\ right) side.
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Thm summary of arXiv:2411.13964, 'Long-time analysis of a pair of on-lattice and continuous run-and-tumble particles with ja'] Let $\gamma_L=(L-1)/\ell$. 
\begin{enumerate}[label={\normalfont(\arabic*)}]
\item The discrete in space processes DITP (resp. DFTP) converge, with quantitative control,  when $L$ tends to infinity, in Skorohod topology towards the continuous-space piecewise deterministic Markov process CITP (resp. CFTP).
\item The processes DITP and DFTP are exponentially ergodic with invariant measures converging as $L$ tends to infinity to the unique invariant measures of the CITP and CFTP.
\item The invariant measures of CITP and CFTP have a positive mass at $\{0\}\times \{-1,0,1\}$ and  $\{\ell\}\times \{-1,0,1\}$.
\item Let us define for a Markov process with semigroup $P_t$ and invariant measure $\pi$ its mixing time as
$t_\text{\normalfont mix}(\epsilon)=\inf\left\{t\ge0\,;\, sup_\mu\|\mu P_t-\pi\|_{TV}\le \epsilon\right\}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\normalfont (a)] The mixing time $t_\text{\normalfont mix}(\epsilon)$ of CITP is of the order $C'(\epsilon)\frac 1\omega(1+\omega^2l^2)$ for some $C'(\epsilon)$.
\item[\normalfont (b)] The mixing time $t_\text{\normalfont mix}(\epsilon)$ of CFTP is of the order $C'(\epsilon)(\frac1\alpha+\frac1\beta)(1+\alpha^2l^2)$ for some $C'(\epsilon)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm summary of arXiv:2411.13964

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:607de28110cf9c534186d7ddefbcec8bb79cc50d44512d0ac6d76bdb376d7a0d","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/60/607de28110cf9c534186d7ddefbcec8bb79cc50d44512d0ac6d76bdb376d7a0d.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:4985dd569c76fe302ffa07ac79a797e033c46812b0fbc344b49bc7ff0314594a","bundle_entry_key":"portmanteau_theorem","bundle_id":"population.pivot3f-4","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"probability, weak convergence of measures","draft":"claude-pivot3f-4/bundle_pivot3f-4.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.weak_convergence:portmanteau-theorem-weak-convergence","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"(a) => (b) is trivial since bounded uniformly continuous functions are bounded continuous.

(b) => (c): for a closed set $F$ and $k \ge 1$ put $f_k(x) = \max(0, 1 - k \, d(x, F))$. Each $f_k$ is bounded and Lipschitz, $f_k \ge 1_F$, and $f_k \downarrow 1_F$ pointwise as $k \to \infty$ because $F$ is closed ($d(x,F) > 0$ off $F$). Then $\limsup_n \mu_n(F) \le \lim_n \int f_k \, d\mu_n = \int f_k \, d\mu$ for each $k$, and letting $k \to \infty$ (dominated / monotone convergence for the decreasing sequence $f_k \le 1$ under a finite measure) gives $\limsup_n \mu_n(F) \le \mu(F)$.

(c) <=> (d): complements. If $G$ is open then $F = S \setminus G$ is closed and $\mu_n(G) = 1 - \mu_n(F)$, $\mu(G) = 1 - \mu(F)$; this is where equal total mass 1 is used.

(c)+(d) => (e): for Borel $A$ with $\mu(\partial A) = 0$ one has $\mu(\mathrm{int} A) = \mu(A) = \mu(\overline{A})$, and
$\mu(\mathrm{int} A) \le \liminf \mu_n(\mathrm{int} A) \le \liminf \mu_n(A) \le \limsup \mu_n(A) \le \limsup \mu_n(\overline{A}) \le \mu(\overline{A})$, so all terms equal $\mu(A)$.

(e) => (a): let $f$ be bounded continuous; adding a constant and rescaling (allowed since the measures are probabilities) assume $0 \le f < M$. For each $t$ the set $\{f > t\}$ is open and its boundary is contained in $\{f = t\}$ (by continuity). The sets $\{f = t\}$, $t \in \mathbb{R}$, are disjoint, so $\mu(\{f = t\}) > 0$ for at most countably many $t$; hence $\{f > t\}$ is a $\mu$-continuity set for all but countably many $t$, and by (e) $\mu_n(f > t) \to \mu(f > t)$ for Lebesgue-a.e. $t \in [0, M]$. Writing $\int f \, d\nu = \int_0^M \nu(f > t) \, dt$ (layer-cake formula) and applying the bounded convergence theorem on $[0, M]$ (the integrands lie in $[0,1]$) gives $\int f \, d\mu_n \to \int f \, d\mu$.

body: In computational complexity theory, a branch of computer science, bounded-error probabilistic polynomial time (BPP) is the class of decision problems solvable by a probabilistic Turing machine in polynomial time with an error probability bounded by 1/3 for all instances. BPP is one of the largest practical classes of problems, meaning most problems of interest in BPP have efficient probabilistic algorithms that can be run quickly on real modern machines. BPP also contains P, the class of problems solvable in polynomial time with a deterministic machine, since a deterministic algorithm is a special case of a probabilistic algorithm.
title: BPP (complexity)

[Thm 3 (Varadarajan \cite{varadarajan_path_1997}) of arXiv:2605.07341, 'A Scaling Limit of Random Walks in the Rational Adeles'] The fundamental solution to the $p$-adic heat equation with diffusion coefficient $\sigma_p$ and diffusion exponent $b$ is the probability density function $f(t,x; p)$ given by
    \[ f(t,x; p) = \left(\pinvFourier \exp\left(- \sigma_p t | \cdot |_p^b \right) \right)(x). \]
    The family
    \[ \big(f(t, \cdot; p)\big)_{t \in [0,\infty)} \]
    is a convolution semigroup of probability densities on $\Qp$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 33 of arXiv:2506.20146, 'Parabolic Anderson Model in the Hyperbolic Space. Part I: Annealed Asymptotics'] Let $X$ be a locally convex, Hausdorff topological
(real) vector space and let $X^{*}$ be its topological dual. Suppose
that $F:X\rightarrow(-\infty,\infty]$ is a lower semi-continuous,
convex function. Define $G:X^{*}\rightarrow(-\infty,\infty]$ by 
\begin{equation}
G(\lambda)\triangleq\sup\big\{_{X^{*}}\langle\lambda,x\rangle_{X}-F(x):x\in X\big\},\ \ \ \lambda\in X^{*}.
\end{equation}
If $F$ is not identically equal to $\infty,$ then one has 
\[
F(x)=\sup\big\{_{X^{*}}\langle\lambda,x\rangle_{X}-G(\lambda):\lambda\in X^{*}\big\},\ \ \ x\in X.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 33 of arXiv:2506.20146

[Theorem Theorem 3 of arXiv:2607.19651, 'Metastability and phase transition in a social network model with multiple opinions'] There exists $\beta_0, C_1>0$ and  $C_2 \in (0,1/2)$, depending only on $M$ and $N$, such that for any $\beta\geq \beta_0$, for any $o\in\mathcal{O}$ and for any  $u\in \mathcal{C}^o$,
$$
\sup_{t\geq 0}\left|{\mathbb P}\left(\frac{R^{\beta,u}(\mathcal{C}^{-o})}{\mathbb{E}(R^{\beta,u}(\mathcal{C}^{-o}))}>t\right)-e^{-t}\right| \leq C_1\beta^3e^{-C_2 \beta}.
$$
Moreover, for any $u,v \in \mathcal{C}^o$,
$$
\left|\frac{\mathbb{E}(R^{\beta,u}(\mathcal{C}^{-o}))}{\mathbb{E}(R^{\beta,v}(\mathcal{C}^{-o}))}-1\right| \leq C_1\beta^3e^{-C_2 \beta}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 5 (Random environment) of arXiv:2605.04048, 'Catastrophe--dispersion models in random and varying environments across generations'] Let $(\mathcal E_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a stationary ergodic sequence.
Assume that
\[
\E[|\ell_0|]<\infty \qquad\text{and}\qquad
\E\!\Big[\bigl|\log\bigl(\p(\xi_{1,0}>0\mid\mathcal E_0)\bigr)\bigr|\Big]<+\infty,
\]
where $\xi_{1,0}$ denotes the number of offspring colonies of a single
colony given the environment $\mathcal E_0$ (see
Section~\ref{sec:branching-structure}).
Set $\Lambda=\E[\ell_0]$. Then:
\begin{itemize}
  \item[(a)] If $\Lambda>0$, survival has positive probability.
  \item[(b)] If $\Lambda<0$, extinction is almost sure.
  \item[(c)] If $\Lambda=0$ and the offspring law is non‑degenerate,
        extinction is almost sure.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:general of arXiv:2609.02123, 'Groups of Transverse Stratifications and the Hierarchy of Configuration Spaces'] Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a moduli space with a transversely nice stratification. Then there exists a natural homomorphism
\[
\pi_1(\mathcal{M}, *) \longrightarrow G(\Gamma),
\]
where $\Gamma$ is the hypergraph associated with the stratification.

In particular, for the configuration space of points on the real projective plane $\mathbb{RP}^2$, the stratification by projective constraints (collinearity, conics, etc.) yields a natural homomorphism from the spherical braid group to the corresponding group $G(\Gamma)$.

[Lem lem_meet_reduction of arXiv:2608.29914, 'Fixed points in abstract provability structures'] Let $S$ be a meet APS satisfying \textup{(C3*)} and let $x \in L$. 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item For every one-variable APS term $\triangle v$ with $d(\triangle) \geq 1$, we have $\boxtimes \triangle x = \boxtimes \Box \triangle x$. 

    \item For every one-variable APS term $\triangle v$ with $d(\triangle) \geq 1$, we have $\boxtimes \triangle x \leq \boxtimes^3 \triangle x$. 

    \item For every $k\geq 0$, we have $\boxtimes\Box^k\boxtimes x=\boxtimes^2x$.

    \item For every one-variable APS term $\triangle v$ which is of the form $\boxtimes \triangle_0 v$, we have $\triangle \boxtimes x=\boxtimes^{d(\triangle) + 1} x$.

\end{enumerate}

[Proposition l:covasymstatfindiffsobolev of arXiv:2411.08848, 'Stationary random measures: Covariance asymptotics, variance bounds and central limit theo'] Let ${\mathcal X}$ be a stationary random measure and let ${\mathcal X}_L$ denote the scaled random measure defined by ${\mathcal X}_L(A)={\mathcal X}(LA)$ for $L \geq 1$. Assume that $\int |z^{\gamma}||{\bf K}|(\mathrm{d} z) < \infty$ for $|\gamma|\le 2k+1$. Let $f,g\in L^1\cap H^k$ functions on $\mathbb{R}^d$ for some $k\ge 0$ (with the convention that $H^0=L^2$).  Then,
\begin{enumerate}
\item $L^{-d} \mathrm{Cov}({\mathcal X}_L(f),{\mathcal X}_L(g))  \to Q_0^{{\bf K}}(f,g)$ as $L\to \infty$.

\item If $\lambda_D + I(0) = 0$ and $I(\alpha)=0$ for  $1\le |\alpha|< 2k$, then
$L^{-d+2k} \mathrm{Cov}({\mathcal X}_L(f),{\mathcal X}_L(g)) \to Q_{2k}^{{\bf K}}(f,g)$.

\item If $\lambda_D + I(0)= 0$ and $I(\alpha)=0$ for  $1\le |\alpha|\le 2k$, then $\mathrm{Cov}({\mathcal X}_L(f),{\mathcal X}_L(g))=O(L^{d-2k-1})$  if one of  $f$ or $g$ is in $C_b^{2k+1}$  (functions with bounded, continuous partial derivatives of order $2k+1$).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition l:covasymstatfindiffsobolev of arXiv:2411.08848

For real Gaussian phase retrieval, rotate the fixed unit signal to e_1, so y_i=a_{i1}^2. The leave-one-out trajectory deletes observation l from the loss while retaining the denominator m and uses an initialization independent of all observations. It is independent of a_l. In a second trajectory replace each first coordinate a_{i1} by xi_i |a_{i1}| with fresh independent Rademacher signs xi_i; retain the other coordinates and labels. This random-sign trajectory is independent of the original first-coordinate signs. A third auxiliary trajectory combines both changes and has both independence properties. Bounds comparing these three trajectories with the original trajectory transfer concentration estimates to the original dependent iterates. The comparison bounds, not exact independence of the original iterates, are the essential step. Sections 4.4–4.6 establish these comparisons in the polylogarithmically oversampled setting of the main theorem.

For a measure space (X, mu) and measurable sets A, B, d_mu(A, B) = mu(A symmetric difference B), possibly infinite. For an increasing sequence E_1 in E_2 in ... with increments D_k = E_{k+1} minus E_k and union E, d_mu(E_m, E_n) = sum_{k=m}^{n-1} mu(D_k) for m <= n and d_mu(E_m, E) = sum_{k >= m} mu(D_k). Hence the following are equivalent: the sequence is d_mu-Cauchy; sum_{k >= m} mu(D_k) < infinity for some m; d_mu(E_m, E) < infinity for some m; d_mu(E_n, E) -> 0. Consecutive distances tending to zero are not enough: under the measure with weight 1/k at the point k, the chain E_n = {1, ..., n} has d(E_n, E_{n+1}) = 1/(n+1) -> 0 but is not Cauchy.

body: Let M be a compact, oriented, boundaryless smooth surface with Gaussian curvature K and area element dA. The Gauss-Bonnet theorem states that the integral over M of K dA equals 2 pi chi(M), where chi(M) is the Euler characteristic of M; for instance a topological sphere always has total curvature 4 pi, whatever its metric. If M has a piecewise-smooth boundary with geodesic curvature k_g and exterior angles theta_i at its corners, the formula generalizes to: integral of K dA over M, plus integral of k_g ds over the boundary, plus the sum of the theta_i, equals 2 pi chi(M). Due to Carl Friedrich Gauss and Pierre Ossian Bonnet.
title: Gauss-Bonnet theorem

[Definition of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] Define $\cC_\star(Q)$ to be the quasi-abelian category over $\mathbf k$ whose objects are given by:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
    \item for each $i\in Q_0$ a finite-dimensional $\bR/\Gamma$-graded vector space $V_i$ over $\mathbf k$, 
    \item for each $a\in Q_1$ an increasing $\bR$-filtration $\cF^{a^-}$ on $V_{s(a)}$, compatible with the grading,
    \item for each $a\in Q_1$ a decreasing $\bR$-filtration $\cF^{a^+}$ on $V_{t(a)}$, compatible with the grading.
\end{enumerate}
Morphisms are collections of linear maps $V_i\to V_i'$ compatible with the gradings and filtrations.

[Proposition prop:complexZero of arXiv:2608.18320, 'Asymptotics for Beta-Splitting Trees via Homogeneous Fragmentations and Meromorphic Potent'] Let $\beta>0$ be noninteger and let $      \beta=n_\beta+\theta_\beta$ with $       n_\beta=\lfloor\beta\rfloor$.

If $n_\beta$ is even, then $f_\beta$ has exactly $n_\beta$
nonreal zeros, counted with multiplicity. They occur in conjugate pairs.

Suppose that $n_\beta$ is odd. Let $q_\beta$ be the number of zeros
of $f_\beta$ in the upper half-plane, counted with multiplicity, and,
for $0\leq k\leq n_\beta+1$, let $M_k(\beta)$ be the total
multiplicity of the real zeros of $f_\beta$ in $\mathcal I_k$. Then
each $M_k(\beta)$ is odd and
\begin{equation}
        2q_\beta
        +
        \sum_{k=0}^{n_\beta+1}
        \left[M_k(\beta)-1\right]
        =
        n_\beta+1.
\end{equation}
In particular, $f_\beta$ has at most $n_\beta+1$ nonreal zeros,
counted with multiplicity.

Consequently, for every noninteger $\beta>0$, only finitely many zeros
of $f_\beta$ are nonreal or multiple. All the remaining zeros are real
and simple.

[Theorem 1 ($J$-stable criterion, see Theorem 1.1 of Song~\cite{Song}) of arXiv:2608.29736, '2608.29736'] Let $(M^n,\omega)$ be a compact K\"ahler manifold of complex
 dimension $n\geq 2$. Let $\chi$ be another K\"ahler form. Suppose that the pair $(\chi,\omega)$ is $J$-stable, that is,
  $\displaystyle\int_M \left(\chi^n-n\chi^{n-1}\wedge\omega\right)\geq 0,$ and for any $p$-dimensional subvarieties $V\subset M$ with $1\leq p\leq n-1$, \(
    \displaystyle\int_V \left(\chi^p-p\chi^{p-1}\wedge\omega\right)>0.\)
    Then there exists a smooth function $u$ such that  $\chi_u$ is a K\"ahler form and satisfies the cone condition $$\chi_u^{n-1}-(n-1)\chi_u^{n-2}\wedge\omega>0.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: $J$-stable criterion, see Theorem 1.1 of Song~\cite{Song}

[Lem 251 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] If $\bX:\R^{N'}\to\R^N$ is $L$-Lipschitz, and $\bg$ is a standard gaussian in $\R^{N'}$, then $\bX(\bg)-\E[\bX(\bg)]$ is subgaussian with variance proxy $2L^2$.
(As a result, Lemma~\ref{l:sg.norm.bound} applies with $\sigma^2=2L^2$.)

\begin{proof}
Recall from \cite[Thm.~1.3.4]{MR2731561} that if the function $F: \R^N\to\R$ is $L$-Lipschitz, and $\bg$ is a standard gaussian in $\R^N$, then
    \[
    \E \exp\bigg\{
     s\Big( F(\bg)-\E f(\bg)\Big)\bigg\}
    \le \exp(s^2 L^2)
    \]
for all $s\in\R$, i.e., the random variable $F(g)-\E F(g)$ is subgaussian
with variance proxy $2L^2$. As a consequence we have the subgaussian tail bound
    \beq
    \P\bigg(
    \Big|  F(\bg)-\E f(\bg) \Big| \ge t
    \bigg)
    \le 2 \exp\bigg\{ -\frac{t^2}{4L^2}
    \bigg\}
    \eeq
for all $t\ge0$. Now suppose $\bX:\R^{N'}\to\R^N$ is $L$-Lipschitz. If $\theta$ is a unit vector in $\R^N$, then it is easily seen that $\bg\mapsto (\theta,\bX(\bg))$ is $L$-Lipschitz. It follows from \eqref{e:lip.subgaus} that the scalar random variable $(\theta,X(\bg)-\E[X(\bg)])$ is subgaussian with variance proxy $2L^2$, as claimed.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 251 of arXiv:2608.29416

		$\widehat S$ satisfies
		\[
		\left|\|\widehat S\|_*-d\right|,
		\ |\Tr\widehat S-d|,
		\ \|\widehat S_-\|_*
		\le\frac{\delta d}{1-\delta}.

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2607.02434, 'A Topological Formula for \\ Potts Lattice Gauge Theory Correlations'] Let $\Lambda\subset \Z^d$ be a box and let $q\in\N+1,\,$$\beta \in [0,\infty),$ and $p = 1-e^{-\beta}.$ Consider the couplings on $C^{i}\paren{\Lambda;\Z\paren{q}}\times \set{0,1}^{X^{\paren{i+1}}}$ by
\[K^{\mathbf{f}}\paren{f,P} \propto \prod_{\sigma \in X^{\paren{i+1}}}\brac{\paren{1-p}I_{\set{\sigma \notin P}} + p I_{\set{\sigma \in P,\delta f\paren{\sigma}=1}}}\]
and
\[K^{\mathbf{w}}\paren{f,P} \propto I_{\delta f\mid_{\partial \Lambda} =1}\prod_{\sigma \in X^{\paren{i+1}}}\brac{\paren{1-p}I_{\set{\sigma \notin P}} + p I_{\set{\sigma \in P,\delta f\paren{\sigma}=1}}}\,.\]

Then for $\#\in\set{\mathbf{f},\mathbf{w}},$ 
\begin{itemize}
    \item The first marginal of $K^{\#}$ is
    $\nu^{\#}_{\Lambda,\beta,q,i}.$ 
    \item The second marginal of $K^{\#}$ is
    $\mu^{\#}_{\Lambda,p,\Z_q,i+1}.$ 
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:topo of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Let $z_1, \dots, z_n$ be distinct points in $D$. Let $A \subseteq D$ be a closed connected set not containing any of the $z_j$, such that $D \setminus A$ has countably many connected components,  the boundary of each connected component is a Jordan curve, and for every $\varepsilon > 0$ only finitely many of these curves have diameter more than 
$\varepsilon$. 

Let $\widehat A$ be the set obtained as follows: we take the connected components $O_j$ of $z_j$ in $D \setminus A$, the connected component $O_0$ whose boundary is $\partial D$ and set 
$\widehat A := \overline{D \setminus \bigcup_{j=0}^n O_j}$.

Then there exists a closed path $\gamma \subseteq A$ with $\sum_{j=1}^{n}
\indx_{\gamma}(z_j) \text{ odd}$ if and only if there exists a closed path $\widehat \gamma \subseteq \widehat A$ with $\sum_{j=1}^{n}
\indx_{\widehat \gamma}(z_j) \text{ odd}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:topo of arXiv:2604.15146

[Theorem 6 (Output-space deletion bound) of arXiv:2608.30261, 'Estimating Population-Risk Curves Along Nonconvex Gradient Flows from the Training Sample'] Fix a realized sample, $\cH\subset[0,T]\times\Lambda$, and a nonempty set of
evaluation inputs $\varnothing\ne\mathcal X_{\rm ev}\subseteq\mathcal X$.
Suppose the identities in \cref{thm:kernel-mismatch} hold for every
$i\in[n]$, $(t,\lambda)\in\cH$, and $x\in\mathcal X_{\rm ev}$.
Suppose there are finite nonnegative constants $A_{\rm tr}$ and
$D_{\rm dyn}$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\substack{1\leq i\leq n,\ (t,\lambda)\in\cH\\0\leq s\leq t}}
 \operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{z\in\mathsf Z}^{|h_i|}
 \|a_s^\lambda(z)\|\leq A_{\rm tr},
 \qquad
 \|\mathcal K^{\rm ch,\lambda}-\mathcal K^{\rm res,\lambda}\|
       _{\infty,\op;\mathcal X_{\rm ev},\mathbf h}\leq D_{\rm dyn}.
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\substack{1\leq i\leq n,\ (t,\lambda)\in\cH\\x\in\mathcal X_{\rm ev}}}
 \|f_{\theta_{-i,t}^\lambda}(x)
     -f_{\theta_t^\lambda+d_{i,t}^\lambda}(x)\|
 \leq\frac{2T}{n}A_{\rm tr}D_{\rm dyn}.
\end{equation}
If $x_i\in\mathcal X_{\rm ev}$ for every $i\in[n]$ and
$\varphi(\cdot,y_i)$ is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of the
line segment joining $f_{\theta_t^\lambda+d_{i,t}^\lambda}(x_i)$ and
$f_{\theta_{-i,t}^\lambda}(x_i)$ for every $i$ and $(t,\lambda)\in\cH$, define
\[
 \bar a_{i,t}^{\rm out,\lambda}
 =\int_0^1\nabla_f\varphi\!\left(
 f_{\theta_t^\lambda+d_{i,t}^\lambda}(x_i)
 +u\{f_{\theta_{-i,t}^\lambda}(x_i)
      -f_{\theta_t^\lambda+d_{i,t}^\lambda}(x_i)\},y_i
 \right)\,\dd u.
\]
If, for a finite $A_{\rm ev}\geq0$,
$\|\bar a_{i,t}^{\rm out,\lambda}\|\leq A_{\rm ev}$ uniformly over
$1\leq i\leq n$ and $(t,\lambda)\in\cH$, then
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{(t,\lambda)\in\cH}
 |\Score_n^{\LOO}(t,\lambda)-\widetilde\Score_n(t,\lambda)|
 \leq\frac{2T}{n}A_{\rm ev}A_{\rm tr}D_{\rm dyn}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Output-space deletion bound

D_{\Sr} \stackrel{d}{=} |\BP_{\ve}(T_1)|,
\] 
where $T_1 \sim \exp(1)$ is independent of $\BP_{\ve}$.

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.26692, 'Many Facets in Random Polytopes from Product and Log-Concave Measures'] There exists
\[
 0<\eta<\min\{1,x^*/4\}
\]
with the following property.  For every fixed $0<a<b<r^*$ there are constants
$c,C>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$ and every
$x\in[-\eta,\eta]^n$ satisfying
\[
 an\leq\Lambda_{\mu_n}^*(x)\leq bn,
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 q_n(x)\geq c\frac{e^{-\Lambda_{\mu_n}^*(x)}}{\sqrt n}.
\end{equation}
Moreover, if
\[
 H_x^+=\{y:\ip{\nabla\Lambda_{\mu_n}^*(x)}{y-x}\geq0\},
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 \mu_n(H_x^+)\leq C\frac{e^{-\Lambda_{\mu_n}^*(x)}}{\sqrt n}.
\end{equation}

On Z^4 let p_n be the full-space discrete-time nearest-neighbor SRW kernel, g_T(x)=sum_{n=0}^T p_n(x), sigma_T^2=sum_x g_T(x)^2, and let xi_z be independent standard Gaussians. Define Y_T(x)=sum_z g_T(x-z)xi_z/sigma_T and H_T(x)=1{Y_T(x)>=sqrt(2 log T)}, h_T=E H_T(0). For every fixed a>0, with graph radius R_T=floor(a h_T^(-1/4)), liminf_{T->infinity} log[sum_{0<|x|<=R_T} E(H_T(0)H_T(x))/h_T]/log T >= 2/3. Thus this comparison field violates bounded Palm clustering at mean spacing. It is not a parking process and has no active-particle field. Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty: UNCHECKED exact comparison statement;
KNOWN Gaussian density method and SRW kernel estimates. This is not a
claim about the actual parking field.

Let p_n be the full-space, discrete-time, uniform nearest-neighbor SRW
kernel on Z^4. For integer T>=2 put g_T(x)=sum_{n=0}^T p_n(x). Let
(xi_z) be independent standard real Gaussian variables, and define

    Y_T(x) = sum_z g_T(x-z) xi_z / sigma_T,
    sigma_T^2 = sum_z g_T(z)^2.

The sums are finite. Each Y_T(x) is standard normal, and the field is
stationary. Define H_T(x)=1{Y_T(x)>=sqrt(2 log T)}, h_T=E H_T(0), and
R_T=floor(a h_T^(-1/4)) for a fixed a>0. Then

    liminf_{T->infinity} log[ sum_{0<|x|_1<=R_T}
                  E(H_T(0)H_T(x))/h_T ] / log T >= 2/3.

In particular this field violates C9's bounded Palm clustering hypothesis
for every a>0. There is no active-particle field or parking dynamics in
this construction; it does not refute any claim concerning that dynamics.

## Covariance and the graph-ball scale

By symmetry and the semigroup property,

    C_T(x):=sum_z g_T(z)g_T(z-x)
           =sum_{n=0}^{2T} w_{T,n} p_n(x),

where w_{T,n}=n+1 for n<=T and w_{T,n}=2T-n+1 for T<n<=2T.
The uniform heat-kernel bound p_n(x)<=C n^(-2) shows that the tail
T<n<=2T contributes O(1), uniformly in x. The first part is exactly
the kernel of I0005-C1 v1. Consequently, with c=4/pi^2,

    C_T(x)=c log_+(T/(1+|x|_2^2))+O(1),
    sigma_T^2=c log T+O(1).

All constants are independent of x and T. The positive covariance kernel
here is the convolution square of g_T; no assertion of positive
definiteness for an arbitrary truncated semigroup polynomial is needed.

Mills' estimate follows directly by integrating the normal density: for
v>0, phi(v) v/(v^2+1)<=P(Z>=v)<=phi(v)/v. Thus

    h_T=(1+o(1))/(2 sqrt(pi log T) T).

It follows that R_T=T^(1/4+o(1)). In the annulus
R_T/2<=|x|_1<=R_T, norm equivalence gives |x|_2=T^(1/4+o(1)), uniformly.
Therefore

    rho_T(x):=E[Y_T(0)Y_T(x)]=1/2+o(1)

uniformly on this annulus. In particular rho lies in [1/3,2/3] eventually.

## Uniform bivariate tail estimate

Let (Z,W) be standard jointly Gaussian with correlation rho in [1/3,2/3]
and put v=sqrt(2 log T). The implication Z,W>=v => Z+W>=2v and the
Gaussian exponential-moment bound give

    P(Z,W>=v)<=exp(-v^2/(1+rho)).

For a matching logarithmic lower bound, integrate the joint density over
[v,v+1/v]^2. Its area is 1/v^2. On that rectangle the density exponent is

    (z^2-2rho zw+w^2)/(2(1-rho^2))
                  <=v^2/(1+rho)+C,

with one uniform C because rho stays in the stated compact interval.
The density prefactor is uniformly bounded below by a positive constant.
Hence

    P(Z,W>=v)>=c v^(-2) exp(-v^2/(1+rho)).

For rho_T(x)=1/2+o(1), these bounds imply

    E[H_T(0)H_T(x)]=T^(-4/3+o(1))

uniformly throughout the annulus.

## Palm summation

The number of annulus sites is a positive constant times R_T^4,
up to a lower-order boundary error, hence T^(1+o(1)). Also
h_T^(-1)=T^(1+o(1)). Keeping only this annulus in the nonnegative sum
gives

    sum_{0<|x|_1<=R_T} E[H_T(0)H_T(x)]/h_T
                    >=T^(1+1-4/3+o(1))=T^(2/3+o(1)).

This proves the claimed liminf and divergence.

## What the comparison excludes

The full-space G*G obstruction in the parking source resembles the
logarithmic covariance used here. By contrast the interlacement benchmark
C10 uses a single Green function and has bounded Palm counts. Neither
comparison identifies the actual parking field. They show that decay of
the one-hole intensity and a reference to random-walk Green functions do
not, by themselves, imply C9's Palm bound. The stopping dynamics must be
used in any valid transfer theorem.

\[
  \Ball{a}{t}\subseteq\{p_1,\dots,p_{t+1}\}\cup c^{-1}\bigl([\,c(a)-t-1,\ c(a)-1\,]\bigr),

$\Ball{b}{t}\subseteq\{p_m,\dots,p_{m-t}\}\cup c^{-1}([\,c(b)+1,\ c(b)+t+1\,])$
and $|\Ball{b}{t}|\le 2t+2$.

For B in R^(m x w), A in R^(w x n), and differentiable convex loss C on m-by-n matrices, set U=[B;A^T], Z=UU^T and F(Z)=C(Z12)+C(Z21^T) on (m+n)-square matrices. Then F(UU^T)/2=C(BA). At symmetric Z, with G=grad C(Z12), grad F(Z)=[[0,G],[G^T,0]]. Thus Uprime=-grad F(UU^T)U is exactly the asymmetric gradient flow Bprime=-GA^T, Aprime=-B^T G; the Gram matrix solves Zprime=-Z grad F(Z)-grad F(Z)Z. No whitening, data commutation, or initial balance is required. With a simple positive top residual singular value s, the conditional Gram escape theorem uses rate 2s and requires (v^T Zalpha v)/||Zalpha-Zbar||_F to have a strictly positive liminf; nonzero projection alone is insufficient. Section 3 of arXiv:2012.09839, PDF p.3 explicitly gives the square asymmetric-to-symmetric reduction; these formulas spell out arbitrary rectangular block sizes and the exact gradient-flow normalization. Applying Theorem G.2 requires all its hypotheses; for quadratic regression its all-real-time convention requires a local complete extension, since quadratic flow need not be backward complete. This is an existing reduction and conditional local theorem, not an unconditional Gaussian second-step result.

body:
[Cor 190 (quenched first moment bounds on $Q^\sigma$ and $Q^{\sigma,\frozen}$) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For $Q$ as in Definition~\ref{d:Q}, we have
	$\bE[\Delta Q^\RomI(q_d)]
	\le L^{O(1)}(\MAX_N)^2\delta^2$
with $\MAX_N$ as in Proposition~\ref{p:Y.kolmogorov}. We also have
	\[
	\sum_{\sigma\in\{\RomII,\RomIII,\Ising\}}
	\bE\Delta Q^\sigma(q_d)
	\le L^{O(1)}\bigg\{
	(\MAX_N)^2
	+ \frac{(\SMAX_N)^2 \BUCKETS}{N}
	\bigg\} \delta
	\]
with $\SMAX_N$ as in Proposition~\ref{p:drift.quenched}. The same bound holds for the $Q^{\frozen,\sigma}$ processes.
	
\begin{proof}
Recall that $Q^\sigma=E^\sigma+\tilde{Q}^\sigma$. It follows from Lemma~\ref{l:qv.simplification} that
	\[
	\Big|\Delta E^\sigma(q_d)\Big| 
	\le O\bigg(
	\eta^2
	+\eta\Big(\Delta\tilde{Q}^\sigma(q_d)\Big)^{1/2}
	+\Big( \Delta \bar{D}^\sigma(q_d)\Big)^2\bigg)\,.
	\]
For $\sigma=\RomI$, it follows by combining Lemma~\ref{l:barD.I.second.quenched} with Lemma~\ref{l:tQ.first.quenched} that
	\[
	\bE\Delta Q^\RomI(q_d)
	\le \bE\Delta \tilde{Q}^\RomI(q_d)
		+\bE\Big|\Delta E^\RomI(q_d)\Big|
	\le
	L^{O(1)} \bigg\{
	\eta^2 + (\MAX_N)^2\delta^2 \bigg\}\,.
	\]
For $\sigma\in\{\RomII,\RomIII,\Ising\}$,
it follows by combining Lemmas~\ref{l:barD.II.second.quenched}--\ref{l:barD.Ising.second.quenched} with Lemma~\ref{l:tQ.first.quenched} that
	\[
	\bE\Delta Q^\sigma(q_d)
	\le\bE\Delta \tilde{Q}^\sigma(q_d)+ \bE\Big|\Delta E^\sigma(q_d)\Big| 
	\le L^{O(1)}\bigg\{
	\eta^2
	+(\MAX_N)^2\delta
	+ \frac{(\SMAX_N)^2 \BUCKETS\delta}{N}
	\bigg\}\,.\]
This proves the claim for the $Q^\sigma$ processes,
using that $\MAX_N\ge1$ and $\eta\ll\delta$. The analogous bound for the $Q^{\frozen,\sigma}$ processes follows by the same argument.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: quenched first moment bounds on $Q^\sigma$ and $Q^{\sigma,\frozen}$

[Thm 84 of arXiv:2605.23308, 'Convergence rate estimates for semigroups and heat kernels associated with resistance form'] \quad\par
  Suppose that $\alpha$ and $\kappa\in (1/2,1]$ satisfy $\alpha>\frac{\kappa}{3\kappa+4}+5\kappa+\frac{7}{2}$.
  Then it holds for any $f\in\BL^{\kappa},K\in(0,\infty),K\in (0,\infty)$ and $E<\frac{\kappa}{2(3\kappa+4)}$ that

\end{equation}

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2511.14740, 'Marking and re-marking'] Let $X$ be a random variable taking values in $\mathbb N$, $\mathbf a \in [0,1]^c$ with $|\mathbf a| \leq 1$, and let $\mathbf Y = \mathbf a \circ X$ be the multinomial marking of $X$ with parameters $\mathbf a$. Then we have the following.
\begin{enumerate}

\item $\mathbb EY_i = a_i \, \mathbb EX$.
\item $\Disp(Y_i) = a_i^2 \Disp(X)$.
\item $\Cov(Y_i, Y_j) = a_i a_j \Disp(X)$ for $i \neq j$.
\item ${\displaystyle \operatorname{\mathbb E} \mathbf Y^{\ff{\mathbf k}} = \left(\prod_{i=1}^d a_i^{k_i}\!\right) \operatorname{\mathbb E} X^{\ff{| \mathbf k|}}}$.
\item $\Phi_{\mathbf Y}(\mathbf t) = \Phi_X\big(\mathbf a ^\top \mathbf t\big)$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\[

=
p_{n}^{[\kappa]}\boxast_n^{(\kappa)} \left( p_{n}^{[\kappa-1]}\boxast_n^{(\kappa-1)}\left(\cdots p_n^{[2]}\boxast_n^{(2)}\left( p_{n}^{[1]}\boxast_n^{(1)} p_n^{[0]}\right)\cdots \right)\right),
\]
where \(p_m^{[i]}\in \pols_m(\R_{\geq 0})\) for \(i=0,\ldots,\kappa\) and for $m\in\N$, 
\[
\boxast_m^{(i)} =
\begin{cases}
  \boxtimes_m,       & \text{if } i \in\mathcal{I}, \\
  \boxplus_m,      & \text{if } i \notin \mathcal{I}.
\end{cases}
\]
Assume that
\[
\meas{p_n^{[i]}}\weak \mu_i, \qquad i=0,\ldots,\kappa,
\]
for some \(\mu_i\in \MM(\R_{\geq 0})\). Then
\[
\meas{q_n}\weak \mu_\kappa\boxast^{(\kappa)} \left( \mu_{\kappa-1}\boxast^{(\kappa-1)}\left(\cdots \mu_2 \boxast^{(2)}\left( \mu_1\boxast^{(1)} \mu_0\right)\cdots \right)\right),
\]
where
\[
\boxast^{(i)} =
\begin{cases}
  \boxtimes,       & \text{if } i \in\mathcal{I}, \\
  \boxplus,      & \text{if } i \notin \mathcal{I}.
\end{cases}
\]

body: In mathematics, the axiom of choice, abbreviated AC or AoC, is an axiom of set theory. Informally put, the axiom of choice says that given any collection of non-empty sets, one can identify another set containing one element chosen from each set, even if the collection is infinite. Formally, the axiom establishes existence rather than a construction; it states that for every set and every -indexed family of nonempty sets, there exists an -indexed set of elements of such that for every . The axiom of choice was formulated in 1904 by Ernst Zermelo in order to formalize his proof of the well-ordering theorem.

[Theorem thm:Huang-moment-extraction of arXiv:2609.03532, 'Airy limit for the Jack process and topological expansion'] [Huang]

For $m\geq1$ and
$k_1,\ldots,k_m\geq1$,
\begin{align*}
  \prod_{p=1}^m
  \left(
    \frac{I^{(k_p)}}{N^{k_p}}
    +\frac{I^{(k_p+1)}}{N^{k_p+1}}
  \right)
  \mathcal J_{\lambda}(\boldsymbol p;\theta)
  \notag=
  \left[
    \prod_{p=1}^m
    \int x^{k_p}\,\mathrm d\mu_{\mathrm{PP}}[\lambda](x)
  \right]J_{\lambda}(\boldsymbol{p};\theta).
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Ren-Nichani-Wu-Lee population MSE identity. Let X~N(0,I_d), let v_star,1,...,v_star,P be orthonormal, and let a_p>=0 with sum_p a_p^2=1. Let sigma be a real even link with sigma=sum_{i>=I} c_2i h_2i in L2(N(0,1)), I>=1, and sum_i c_2i^2=1, in the normalized probabilists Hermite basis. Let all student vectors v_k be nonzero and finite in number, and set f_v(x)=sum_k b_k sigma(u_k dot x), u_k=v_k/||v_k||_2, b_k=||v_k||_2^2, and f_star(x)=sum_p a_p sigma(v_star,p dot x). Define C(r)=sum_{i>=I} c_2i^2*r^(2i), -1<=r<=1. Then L=(1/2)E[(f_star(X)-f_v(X))^2]=(1/2)sum_p a_p^2-sum_{p,k}a_p*b_k*C(v_star,p dot u_k)+(1/2)sum_{k,l}b_k*b_l*C(u_k dot u_l). Equivalently, L=(1/2)sum_{i>=I}c_2i^2*||sum_p a_p*v_star,p^(tensor 2i)-sum_k b_k*u_k^(tensor 2i)||_F^2. Both series are finite-valued and converge absolutely. This deterministic identity is the source equation4; it needs no SGD convergence, sample independence across training steps, or neuron-initialization assumption. It is valid under the weaker link hypotheses displayed here, in particular without the differentiability assumptions needed to run SGD.
Finite orthonormal teacher family and finitely many nonzero student vectors.
Shared centered even normalized L2 Gaussian link; displayed Hermite expansion.
Squared loss with factor one half; coefficients and directions as displayed.

gluing of (prop:closed-gates of the paper).

[Prob 112 of arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy'] When $\phi$ is unital, Theorem~\ref{thm:pre-LDP} says that the value $E_n$ gives the rate function in the large deviations principle obeyed by the random element
\[(\Phi^\pi_V)[B_n] \in \S^\rm{u}_k(B_n).\]
The values $E_n'$ should have an analogous interpretation, but this time for the random $S$-tuples
\begin{equation}
\big((\Phi^\pi_V)[B_n\cup sB_n]:\ s \in S\big)
\end{equation}
taking values in the space
\[\Big\{(Q_s:\ s \in S) \in \prod_{s \in S}\S^\rm{u}_k(B_n\cup sB_n):\ (Q_s)[B_n]\ \hbox{is the same for all $s$}\Big\}.\]
If this is true, then both inequalities in Lemma~\ref{lem:1-2-ineqs} become instances of the contraction principle.

I believe one can prove this along the same lines as Theorem~\ref{thm:pre-LDP} without any really new ideas, but working with the the tuples in~\eqref{eq:tuple-of-Phis} is sure to be more complicated than working with $(\Phi^\pi_V)[B_n$ alone. (Stated as a problem by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Problem 112 of arXiv:2507.08909

[Lemma 17 of arXiv:2511.06414, 'Non-uniform Edgeworth expansions for weakly dependent random variables and their applicati'] There are polynomials $\bar H_j$ whose coefficients are rational functions of  $p_k$ and $q_k$ for $k\leq 3j$ so that with 
$$
\bar\Phi_{n,m}(x)=\Phi(x)-\varphi(x)\sum_{j=1}^{m-2}n^{-j/2}\bar H_{j}(x)
$$
uniformly in $x$ we have 
\begin{equation}
\tilde\Phi_{n,m}(x)=\bar\Phi_{n,m}(x)+R_n(x)e^{-x^2/4}O(n^{-m/2})
\end{equation}
where $R_n$ is a polynomial with bounded coefficients whose degree does not depend on $n$.

[Lemma 13 (Uniform boundary decay) of arXiv:2608.30211, '2608.30211'] Let $G_j$ be domains whose boundaries in $B_{2r}(p_j)$ are given by
uniformly $C^{1,1}$ graphs, and let
$h_j\in L^\infty(G_j\cap B_{2r}(p_j))$.  Suppose that
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 w_j\in H^1(G_j\cap B_{2r}(p_j))
 \cap C(\overline{G_j\cap B_{2r}(p_j)}),\\
 -\Delta w_j=h_j\quad\hbox{in }G_j\cap B_{2r}(p_j),\\
 \|w_j\|_\infty\leq M,\qquad \|h_j\|_\infty\leq M_1.
 \end{gathered}
\]
There are $\eta\in(0,1)$ and $C>0$, depending only on the dimension and
the uniform graph bounds, such that, for $0<\delta<r/8$,
\begin{align}
 \sup_{\substack{x\in G_j\cap B_{r/2}(p_j)\\
                  \dist(x,\partial G_j)\leq\delta}}
 |w_j(x)|
 &\leq \sup_{\partial G_j\cap B_r(p_j)}|w_j|
 \notag\\
 &\quad+C(M+M_1r^2)\left(\frac{\delta}{r}\right)^\eta .
 
\end{align}
The constants are uniform over the family $G_j$.

body: The Fourier entropy-influence conjecture is equivalent to its restriction to Boolean functions all of whose influences are below any fixed tau: a coordinate of influence at least tau has restriction drop Delta_i <= (2/ln 2 + log2(e/tau)) Inf_i, so a violation localizes to a subcube on which every influence is small and the restriction step fails at every coordinate. On self-compositions of Numaro's record function the restriction-step constant rho_0 = min_i Delta_i/Inf_i is 6.3290, 6.8901 and 7.0519 at 324, 5832 and 104976 variables (limit about 7.1116), so no potential-free coordinate induction can give a constant below 7.05. The XOR gate inequality is certified, so read-once formulas over AND, OR, XOR and NOT satisfy H <= 6.4573 I; a prime monotone 7-input gate breaks the read-once potential behind that bound; the five prime 3-input classes (one-hot, MAJ3, EQ3, MUX, Q3) are proved, while fan-in 3 at 6.4573 in general is numerical only. Per-coordinate erasure bounds fail even for monotone functions (majority with one flipped point gives ratio at least (n - 3 log2 n)/2). The full conjecture remains open.

[Definition 6 of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] Let $U : \T^d \to \R^d$ with $U \in C^0(\T^d)$ and $y \in \T^d$. Define
    \[R_t(y) := \sup_{X^1,\ X^2 \text{ solutions to~\eqref{eq:main ODE autonomous data}}}  d_{\T^d}(X^1_t, X^2_t).\]
    If, for some $t_0 >0,$ $R_t(y) = 0$ for all $t \in [0,t_0]$, then we say that $U$ is \textit{effectively regular at $y$}.
    Otherwise, we define
    \[E(y) := 1-\limsup_{t \to 0^+} \frac{\log t}{\log R_t(y)}.\]
    We then say that $U$ has \textit{effective Lagrangian regularity} $E(y)$ at $y$.

[Lem 38 of arXiv:2609.03821, 'Condensation and Metastability in the Supercritical Two-Species Zero-Range Process via Res'] Fix positive real numbers $x_{1},y_{1},\dots,x_{k},y_{k}>0$.
Then for any integers $N,n,p_{1},\dots,p_{k}\ge0$ such that $p_{1}+\cdots+p_{k}=N$
and $0\le n\le N$,
\[
\frac{1}{\binom{N}{n}}\sum_{\substack{q_{1},\dots,q_{k}\ge0:\\
q_{1}+\cdots+q_{k}=n
}
}\prod^{k}_{j=1}\left[{p_{j} \choose q_{j}}x^{q_{j}}_{j}y^{p_{j}-q_{j}}_{j}\right]\le c\prod^{k}_{j=1}\left(\frac{nx_{j}+(N-n)y_{j}}{N}\right)^{p_{j}},
\]
where $c>0$ depends only on the fixed constants $x_{1},y_{1},\dots,x_{k},y_{k}$.

body:
[Definition 7 of arXiv:2606.31287, '\bf Heat kernel lower bound estimates for symmetric pure jump processes via averaged jump '] \begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm (i)]  We say that ${\rm J}_{\phi, \leq}$ holds if there is some constant $c_{\ref{e:1.2}} > 0$ so that 
\be 
  J(x, y) \le \frac{c_{\ref{e:1.2}}}{V(x,d(x, y)) \phi (d(x, y))}
\ee 
for any $x, y \in \sX$.
 

 \item[\rm (ii)]\,\,Let $D$ be an open subset of $\sX$. Define
\[
\sF_D := \{ u : u \in \sF, u = 0 \,\,\text{for $\sE$-quasi everywhere on $D^c$}\}
\]
and
\[
\lambda_1(D) = \inf \left\{ \sE(f,f):  \,  f \in \sF_D \hbox{ with }  \|f\|_2 =1 \right\},
\]
where $\| u\|_2$ is the $L^2$-norm of $u \in L^2(K, \mu)$. Note that $\lambda_1(D)$ is the bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum for the generator of the subprocess $X^D$ of $X$ killed upon leaving $D$.

\item[\rm (iii)]\,\,
 We say that an MMD space $(\sX,d,m,\sE, \sF)$  satisfies the {\em Faber-Krahn
inequality} ${\rm FK}(\phi)$, if there exist constants $c_{\ref{e:fki}} > 0$, $\sigma_{\ref{e:fki}} \in (0, 1/2)$ and
$\theta > 0$ such that for any $r \in (0, {\sigma_{\ref{e:fki}}}\,\diam{\sX})$, any ball $B(x, r)$ and any open set $D \subseteq B(x, r)$, 
\be 
 \lambda_1(D) \ge \frac{c_{\ref{e:fki}}}{\phi(r)} \Big(\frac{V(x,r)}{m(D)}\Big)^{\theta}.
\ee

 \item[\rm (iv)]\,\, Let $\sF_b = \sF\cap L^\infty(\sX, m)$. We say that an MMD space $(\sX,d,m,\sE, \sF)$   satisfies the 
 {\em weak Poincar\'e inequality}
(${\rm PI} (\phi)$)
  if there exist constants $c_{\ref{eq:PIn}} > 0 $, $\sigma_{\ref{eq:PIn}} \in (0, 1/2)$ and $\delta \ge 1$ such that
for any $r \in (0, \sigma_{\ref{eq:PIn}}\,\diam{\sX})$, any $x \in \sX$ and $f \in \sF_b$,
\begin{equation}
\int_{B_r} (f(x) - \bar{f}_{B_r})^2m(dx) \le c_{\ref{eq:PIn}}\phi(r)\int_{{B_{\delta r}}\times {B_{\delta r}}} (f(y)-f(x))^2\,J(dx,dy),
\end{equation}
 where $B_r = B(x, r)$ and $\bar{f}_{B_r}= \frac{1}{m({B_r})}\int_{B_r} f(x)m(dx)$ is the average value of $f$ on $B_r$.
\end{enumerate}
